dossier.arm: Paper (record-282 manuscript): paper/current/main.tex + closed numeric insert + figure data v5 + prior-art collision matrix + current experiment index
dossier.purpose: Integrate the program's two accepted measurement arms into one ICASSP 2027 manuscript: (1) a probability-sampled audit estimating how often public SER GitHub code exposes speaker-nonexclusivity RISK at an active train/validation or train/test boundary (S1 D2 endpoint), and (2) a controlled same-implementation study quantifying Random vs GroupKFold vs LOSO protocol effects on RAVDESS and CREMA-D (P1), with S0/S2/S3 as representation-stack, split-draw, and third-corpus robustness supplements. The manuscript explicitly disclaims first discovery of the protocol effect or of the RAVDESS>CREMA-D direction (Ibrahim et al. 2026 already report it) and positions its contribution as the LINKAGE of probability sampling + byte-level repository evidence + complete OOF predictions + speaker-paired inference + frozen SSL probes + repeated draws + a third acted-corpus panel. Record-282 specifically adds a reader-visible erratum disclosure (the D2 decision brief undercounted threshold-crossing lineage pairs) and four hygiene fixes; all scientific values are unchanged from record-279.
dossier.design_summary:
MANUSCRIPT: spconf article, \ninept, title 'SPEAKER-NONEXCLUSIVITY RISK IN PUBLIC SER CODE: A PROBABILITY AUDIT AND CONTROLLED STUDY OF PROTOCOL EFFECTS'; author/affiliation are placeholders ('AUTHOR METADATA REQUIRED BEFORE SUBMISSION'); template verification pending; header comment says 'NOT A SUBMISSION PDF'. All S1/S0/S2/S3 numbers are LaTeX macros pulled via \InputIfFileExists{numeric_insert_closed.tex} (generated from closed_numeric_insert_manifest_record279.json; compile errors if absent, with a note 'do not reuse run-5 or provisional numbers'). P1 table numbers are hard-coded in the tex. Sections: Abstract, Intro, Relation to Prior Work, Methods (audit / controlled / SSL+draw supplements), Results (audit prevalence; controlled effects w/ Table 1 and Fig. 1; frozen-feature & partition-draw robustness), Discussion, Limitations, Conclusion, Reproducibility & AI-use statement, 13 references.

AUDIT (S1 D2): Frame = public GitHub implementations evaluating SER on >=1 of RAVDESS, CREMA-D, IEMOCAP, EmoDB, discoverable via bounded GitHub+arXiv searches by 2026-08-10 cutoff. Candidate log 383 normalized URLs before screening; exclusions: non-SER, no target-corpus evaluation, no relevant code, unavailable, duplicate/materially-unchanged fork lineages. Papers with Code contributed zero (redirected). Original literal frame 291 entries; historical N282 branch; after M4 red-team found copy lineages, author adopted D2 lineage rule (outcome-VISIBLE but outcome-agnostic: uses provenance + pinned content metadata with Y/N/U masked; declared executable extensions = code; notebook = one blob; extensionless excluded; vendor/LFS/submodule retained; no containment edge from empty code set; unique code-blob hashes per repo). D2 frame N=286. Deterministic beacon-seeded priority order (fixed pre-outcome) selected n=60. Endpoint: positive if >=1 active train-val/model-selection or train-test path permits same-speaker on both sides; negative only if all active paths verified speaker-exclusive AND path enumeration closed; unresolved if decisive membership unavailable / resource cap / no applicable split. Static review only, no execution. Y/N have byte-verified entry-to-split chains + fragment hashes + hash-bound receipts; U have receipts + reasons only. Second AI-assisted adversarial pass; separate-code-path replay; explicitly NOT independent human replication. No public immutable pre-registration; local pre-outcome freeze only. Statistics: confirmed fraction Y/n; sample partial-identification interval [Y/n, (Y+U)/n]; frame-level envelope = two one-sided 97.5% exact hypergeometric bounds Bonferroni-combined -> joint >=95% coverage under partial classification (explicitly 'not a CI centered on the confirmed fraction'). Sensitivity branches D1 (original rule), D3, literal 291-entry frame, N282 are retained but NO numbers from them appear in the main text.

P1 CONTROLLED STUDY: RAVDESS speech 1,440 utt / 8 classes / 24 speakers; CREMA-D 7,442 utt / 6 classes / 91 speakers. 22.05 kHz mono, 30 dB trim; 64-bin log-mel (FFT 1024, hop 512, fmax 11,025 Hz, 128 frames), per-utterance standardization, SpecAugment train-only. Four from-scratch probes: CNN, ResNet-SE, Transformer, FNO; fixed architecture/optimization across protocols; AdamW, batch 64, <=100 epochs, early-stop patience 15, seeds 0/1/2; test never guides selection. Protocols: Random = 5-fold StratifiedKFold no grouping; Grouped = 5-fold GroupKFold by speaker; LOSO. Inner validation mirrors outer (ungrouped under Random, grouped under strict) -> Random-minus-Grouped is a pipeline-level contrast, not outer-overlap-only causal estimate. ONE frozen split per protocol. 72 corpus x model x protocol x seed cells; 1,620 fits (= 4 models x 3 seeds x [(5+5+24) RAVDESS + (5+5+91) CREMA-D] — checks out). Full OOF predictions retained. UAR primary; speaker = paired unit, averaged over seeds, 10,000 whole-speaker bootstrap replicates; two-sided Wilcoxon, Holm within prespecified 24-test UAR family (2 corpora x 4 models x 3 pairwise contrasts). Accuracy/macro-F1 descriptive only. No corpus-interaction test.

S0: outcome-visible 'corrective reproduction' (v2 authoritative, v1 historical) with pinned wav2vec 2.0 / HuBERT / WavLM frozen-feature linear probes on both corpora; 180/180 units; own 6-test Holm family. S2: fixed StandardScaler+Ridge head on frozen S0-v2 features, Random vs speaker-grouped outer folds, 20 prespecified partition draws; 240 units / 1,200 CPU fits; endpoint = empirical draw distribution of the outer-grouping contrast (no inner validation, no early stopping). S3: S2 head+draw contract on a repetition-clean SUBESCO (acted Bangla) panel: 20 speakers, 7 emotions, 7 prompts, 980 utterances after within-cell duplicate-component selection; 120 scientific units + 600 audit replay refits (verification only); release_v10 accepted via cross-agent exact-byte acceptance. B (SUBESCO allocation, 2,880 fits) prespecified but manuscript-routing chosen post-outcome -> descriptive supplement only, excluded from title/abstract/claims/figure/conclusion.

FIGURE (figure_data_record279_v5.json): figure* at 178 mm (7.0079 x 3.28 in), panel ratio 47:53, min text 7.2 pt, panel titles 8.6 pt. Panel A: D2 sample Y/N/U composition + partial-ID interval + frame envelope, labelled 'outcome-visible revised-primary/exploratory', not_sample_ci=true. Panel B: eight speaker-paired Random-minus-Grouped UAR deltas with bootstrap intervals, sourced from p1_run5/paper_facts_07.json (sha 0bcae6f1...) and S1_INSERT_SOURCE_RECORD277_V1.json (sha 1273a279...). v5 = v4 with compacted Y/N/U labels after a source-QA collision; scientific payload unchanged.

dossier.outcome: A complete, compile-ready (given the closed insert) record-282 manuscript exists with all scientific values frozen from record-279 and an added reader-visible erratum on the D2 decision brief. MAIN TEXT carries: the S1 D2 audit (44/9/7 of 60 from 286; 73.3%; 73.3-85.0%; 61.9-92.0%) as Panel A and the Results/Conclusion headline; the P1 8-row UAR table plus Panel B forest of Random-minus-Grouped deltas; S0 as a two-range sentence (2.76-6.21 / 0.87-1.83; 6/6); S2 as a two-corpus sentence (13.90 / 1.58; 20/20 both); S3 as two sentences (primary 3.10 +- 1.46, 19/0/1; WavLM 1.26 +- 1.66, 16/0/4). ROUTED TO SUPPLEMENT/REPOSITORY: lineage-rule sensitivity branches D1/D3/literal-291/N282 (named but no numbers), experiment B (allocation, named as excluded), S3 probe-specific rows and per-draw data. NOT MENTIONED AT ALL in main.tex: experiment D1 (Speech-Song, 792 fits), A (factorial, 240 fits), C/P5 (mechanism salvage), S4 (no-go). The audit is labelled 'revised-primary/exploratory', explicitly 'not preregistered or confirmatory'; S0 is 'outcome-visible corrective reproduction'. Status per index (2026-08-30): the frozen plan's required experiment set is complete; no further fits allowed. Manuscript still lacks author metadata, official-template verification, artifact DOI/URL, and the human-review sign-off its own AI-use statement says is required; it is a 'closed-asset candidate', not a submission.
limitations: STATED: audit frame is GitHub/arXiv-dominated, four target corpora, bounded retrieval; not representative of all SER papers/software.

STATED: D2 lineage definition selected after initial audit outcomes were visible (outcome-visible), though its predicate excludes outcome fields and was applied uniformly; no public immutable pre-registration; sensitivity branches 'essential to interpretation' but none of their numbers appear in the paper.
STATED: decision brief behind D2 undercounted threshold-crossing pairs (7 of 11); erratum-documented correction leaves frame and inferences unchanged.

STATED: static evidence shows what a path permits, not actual membership used for a reported run unless memberships are committed; only Y/N have decisive byte-verified chains; 7 unknowns stay in denominator; C218 resource-cap decision made after seeing repo size.
STATED: AI-assisted adjudication and adversarial pass share context; not independent human replication; no inter-rater reliability reported.

STATED: controlled study = two acted English corpora, four from-scratch probes, three seeds, ONE frozen split per protocol; speaker-cluster intervals do not cover alternative split draws or recording-design superpopulations; hyperparameters fixed (no per-protocol tuning); Random-Grouped also changes inner-validation grouping; no corpus-interaction estimate; nonoverlapping marginal intervals are not an interaction test; speaker count/recording design/acted content/within-speaker structure remain confounded moderators.

STATED: S0 outcome-visible corrective reproduction (no formal SSL-vs-scratch comparison); S2 = 20 draws from fixed generators/deterministic heads, not population interval; S3 = frozen 20-speaker Bangla panel, no language effect; B descriptive only because routing chosen post-outcome.
STATED: neither result licenses prevalence x effect-size multiplication, a universal correction, or attribution to speaker identity alone.

UNSTATED but visible in files: the abstract contains no effect sizes in plain text (only 'descriptively larger') and spends a sentence on governance (red-team/copy lineages) rather than results; frame envelope is ~30 points wide (61.9-92.0), limiting usefulness of the headline prevalence.

UNSTATED: 'D1' is used for two different things in the same manuscript — the original lineage rule (Methods/caption) and the RAVDESS Speech-Song experiment ('B ... to replace D1', line 143) — a name collision a reader cannot resolve from the text.
UNSTATED: S3 numbers are typeset to five decimals (3.09864 +- 1.45597, -1.59694) while every other number is two decimals; inconsistent precision in a 9-pt paper.

UNSTATED: figure Panel B facts are sourced from a 'p1_run5 ... final_candidate_v2_run5/paper_facts_07.json' file while the tex guard says 'do not reuse run-5 or provisional numbers' — probably scoped to S1 only, but the provenance labels invite a consistency question.
wasted_or_low_value: Experiment B (2,880 fits, SUBESCO allocation) — numerically complete, prespecified, but excluded from every claim, the figure, and the conclusion because its manuscript routing was chosen post-outcome; it contributes zero to the paper.

Experiment A (240 fits, outer/inner factorial) — the ONE experiment that could decompose the outer-overlap vs inner-selection confound the paper repeatedly flags, but it is not cited in main.tex at all because its verifier was corrected after outcome visibility.
Experiment D1 Speech-Song diagnostic (792 fits) and C/P5 mechanism salvage (144 checkpoints, 6,336 scored occurrences) — complete, never referenced in the manuscript.
S3's 600 audit replay refits and S0 v1 (superseded by v2, 180 units) — verification/retry effort that does not change any reported value.

Governance churn embedded in the paper: the record-279 -> record-282 lineage exists solely to add an erratum sentence about a decision brief that described 7 of 11 pairs, with all numbers unchanged; the erratum now occupies space in Methods AND Limitations of a 4-page paper. Figure v4 -> v5 was a label-spacing repair only.

Lineage-rule sensitivity branches (D1, D3, literal 291-entry frame, N282) are named three times (Methods, caption, Limitations) as 'essential to interpretation' but no number from any of them is reported, so they consume text without informing the reader.

Redundancy: S2 (RAVDESS 13.90, CREMA-D 1.58; 20/20 both) and P1 (15-20 / 2-3) carry essentially the same directional information for the two anchor corpora; S0's RAVDESS range (2.76-6.21) is the only SSL number that is NOT redundant, and it is the one the paper does not explain.

Prior-art matrix carried two author-name errors (Wagner->Wu for Open-Emotion; Arora->Scheidwasser-Clow for SERAB) that required a dated correction note; main.tex references were already correct, so this was audit overhead only.

Supporting infrastructure disproportionate to output: a 107 KB number-checker script, 352 KB numbercheck JSON, 30 KB insert manifest, multiple validators and QA JSONs for a manuscript whose macro insert has 38 numbers.
dossier.contribution_to_paper_claim: This arm IS the paper; every claim lives here. Claim 1 (audit prevalence: 44 positive / 9 negative / 7 unresolved of 60 sampled from a 286-lineage frame; 73.3%; partial-ID 73.3-85.0%; frame envelope 61.9-92.0%) depends entirely on the S1 D2 macros in numeric_insert_closed.tex and Panel A of the figure — the paper's title and first half of the abstract rest on it. Claim 2 (Random > Grouped in 8/8 corpus-model pairs; RAVDESS 15.39-19.68 vs CREMA-D 1.82-3.06 pts; 8/8 and 19/24 Holm survivors) rests on the hard-coded P1 table and Panel B. Claim 3 (direction 'not confined to the original probes') rests on the S0/S2 macros (6/6; 20/20 + 20/20). Claim 4 (third acted-corpus panel positive but WavLM fragile) rests on the S3 macros (19/0/1; 16/0/4). The operational recommendation (enforce speaker exclusivity at all active boundaries; publish grouping information) is argued from Claims 1-2 jointly. Per the prior-art matrix, none of the protocol-effect findings is novel; the defensible novelty is the audit plus the combined-evidence package, so Claim 1 carries the paper's distinctiveness while Claims 2-4 are replication/extension.
untested_gaps: Why does the same frozen-SSL feature stack give a RAVDESS Random-minus-Grouped premium of 2.76-6.21 pts in S0 (linear probes, one split) but 13.90 pts (5th pct 12.65, 20/20) in S2 (Ridge head, 20 draws)? A 2-5x disagreement between the paper's own SSL supplements on the same corpus is unexplained; CREMA-D is consistent (0.87-1.83 vs 1.58), which makes the RAVDESS gap more conspicuous. A reviewer will ask whether head choice or partition family drives the premium.

Why is the SUBESCO premium (~3.1 pts with the S2 head; 20 speakers, acted, fully crossed 7x7) an order of magnitude smaller than RAVDESS (13.9 with the same head; 24 speakers, acted)? This directly undercuts 'speaker count' as the moderator and is not discussed; the paper never compares S3 to S2 numerically.

The outer-overlap vs inner-model-selection confound is flagged four times but never decomposed in the paper, even though experiment A (240 fits) was designed for exactly that and S2 (no inner validation) already isolates outer grouping; no sentence relates S2's outer-only premium to P1's pipeline-level premium.

Which 5 of the 24 Holm contrasts failed to reject? Presumably LOSO-related, but the main text does not say, and the LOSO > GroupKFold pattern in all 8 rows (up to +6.64 on RAVDESS CNN) is attributed to fold count/training size without evidence.

No corpus-by-protocol interaction test, no per-protocol hyperparameter tuning, and one frozen split per protocol in P1 — the reviewer's obvious 'is the RAVDESS-CREMA-D gap real or a split artifact' question is answered only indirectly by S2.

Audit construct validity: what fraction of the 44 positives are the leakage of a validation/model-selection boundary vs the test boundary? Which corpus? What fraction of the 286 lineages accompany a published paper vs hobby/student code? None reported, so the prevalence cannot be related to the literature the reader cares about.
No sensitivity numbers under D1/D3/literal-291/N282 despite calling them essential; a reviewer cannot judge how much the outcome-visible D2 choice moved the estimate.
No inter-rater or human-vs-AI agreement statistic for the Y/N/U adjudications; no execution of any pipeline to confirm that a 'permitted' path is the one actually run.

Absolute grouped UAR on RAVDESS is only 39-46% (8 classes) — whether the large premium is partly a small-data/underfit artefact of from-scratch probes, and whether it shrinks with stronger models, is not tested (the S0 range hints it does, but the paper declines a between-stack comparison).

Untouched in the paper: IEMOCAP and EmoDB are in the audit frame definition but absent from every experiment; accuracy/macro-F1 are called descriptive but never shown; no Random-vs-LOSO or Grouped-vs-LOSO effect sizes are tabulated as deltas.

dossier.arm: P0 / P0.5 / S1 audit lineage (probability audit of public SER repositories for speaker-nonexclusivity risk)
dossier.purpose: Estimate how often publicly discoverable SER code (evaluating on RAVDESS, CREMA-D, IEMOCAP, or EmoDB) contains an active train/validation or train/test boundary that permits the same speaker on both sides ("speaker-nonexclusivity risk"), with an explicit denominator (a frozen public-code candidate frame) and honest handling of unresolved cases. In the program logic this is the "practice prevalence" half of the paper; the controlled P1 study supplies the "effect size" half, and the paper explicitly refuses to multiply the two. P0 originally also audited four other leakage/reporting risks (normalization leakage, test-set-driven selection, augmentation into test, single-split/no-variance reporting); only the speaker-split risk survives into the current paper.
dossier.design_summary:
FRAME CONSTRUCTION (P0, protocol frozen 2026-08-10 14:48 ET). Sources: GitHub repo search, two query families per dataset (`<DATASET> "speech emotion recognition"`, `<DATASET> emotion recognition`) x 4 datasets, top-100 "Best match" each; arXiv API `all:"<DATASET>" AND (all:"speech emotion recognition" OR all:"speech emotion classification")`, top 100 per dataset; supplementary `site:github.com` web queries; snowball from included READMEs/papers (tagged discovery_source=snowball). Papers with Code was pre-registered but its dataset/task pages redirected to an unrelated Hugging Face trending page on the search date (0 candidates); the fallback Semantic Scholar Graph API returned HTTP 429 on 16/16 attempts (P0.6). Effective frame = GitHub + arXiv only. URLs canonicalized to https://github.com/{owner}/{repo} (casefold, strip .git/trailing slash/params). Dedup order: identical URL > explicit fork w/o substantive change (keep upstream) > rename/transfer > content mirror > same model name but independent code (not merged). Inclusion: public, SER evaluation on >=1 target corpus, at least some data-prep/split/train/eval code, freezable to a commit; exclusions E1_not_SER, E2_target_not_evaluated, E3_no_relevant_code, E4_unavailable, E5_duplicate_or_fork, E6_not_repository, E7_non_target_modality, E8_other; no exclusion for low accuracy, bad protocol, or suspected leakage. candidate_log.csv (verified): 383 unique canonical URLs = 32 include (purposive P0 audit), 20 exclude, 331 pending. Unit = unique repository; per-dataset judgments kept as DATASET=value maps. P0 purposive audit: 38-field static audit, 5 risk dimensions coded into 7 binary outcomes, evidence must cite path:Lx-Ly at frozen commit and cover definition AND call/scope; `no` requires positive evidence; evidence_strength high/medium/low with low demoted to unknown in main stats; second-pass cross-review of 32/32 (21 fully agreed, 30 fields in 11 repos revised, unresolvable no/direct downgraded to unknown). Reviews are different passes of the same automated agent system, not two human coders (disclosed).

P0.5 RANDOM SAMPLE (protocol frozen 2026-08-10 17:52 ET, before any draw). Frame = the 331 pending records (SHA-256 of candidate_log pinned). Seed 202608101744; order = ascending SHA256("P0.5|202608101744|" + casefolded canonical URL); full 331-row order written before any Stage-B check. Sequential Stage-B eligibility screening until 30 eligible unique repos. Verified draw log: ranks 1-34 checked -> 30 include, 4 exclude (E1=1, E2=2, E3=1), 297 not_reached. Same 38-field audit, 30/30 full cross-review, adjudication to p0_5_adjudications.csv, IDs P05R001-P05R030. Sample composition (verified from p0_5_random_survey.csv): repo_relation supplemental_code 19 / third_party_reproduction 8 / author_linked_paper 2 / author_official 1; target corpora RAVDESS-only 12, IEMOCAP-only 7, RAVDESS|CREMA-D 4, CREMA-D-only 3, others 4; publication_year 2026:9, 2025:7, 2024:3, 2022:3, 2021:3, 2020:2, 2019:2, 2023:1; evidence_strength high 19 / medium 9 / low 2; split_category random 19 / unknown 4 / speaker_independent 3 / predefined_speaker_independent 2 / mixed 1 / LOSO 1. Estimands preregistered: primary = yes/n with unknown kept in denominator as non-risk; upper = (yes+unknown)/n; decidable subset yes/(yes+no); Wilson 95% on each; purposive-vs-random comparison via Newcombe hybrid score-10 difference, two-sided Fisher (yes vs no+unknown), Holm over the 7-outcome family; no finite-population correction; purposive and random samples never pooled.

P0.5 EXECUTION VALIDATION (results/execution_validation, .venv_p0_8, then section-12 closure 2026-08-13). Synthetic manifest 4,444 rows (RAVDESS 1,440; CREMA-D 2,184; IEMOCAP 400; EmoDB 420) with corpus-prefixed speaker IDs; 265 candidate code/text files byte-read and SHA-256'd; candidate_code_executed=false for all. Tier1 (final definition): the decisive split AST statement(s) parsed from the frozen .py/.ipynb and executed in an isolated namespace (no module import, no whole-repo run) on the full manifest plus 15 fixed row-order permutations = 16 cases/repo; ordered train/test indices compared with an independently written adapter, 384/384 (24x16) matches. Tier2 = static execution inference (P05R025, fastai valid_pct=0.2, fastai not installable). Tier3 = unknown. Final tiers 24/1/5; final split risk 20 yes / 5 no / 5 unknown.

S1 RISK ADJUDICATION (Aug 2026). A separate, fuller screening of the whole 383-URL candidate log to eligibility produced the "p0_full_frame_precision_v1_release_v67" frame of N=291 IDs (releases v63-v66 superseded as checker development; the manifest itself is only in the private Release asset, not this tree). n=60 drawn by a beacon-seeded priority order (seed a72da303..., pulse 2026-08-23T12:01Z) fixed independently of outcomes. Verified: all 60 IDs exist in candidate_log (56 were pending, 4 were P0 purposive includes: C214, C231, C343, C365); only 2 of the 60 overlap the P0.5 30. Endpoint dictionary (S1_RISK_ENDPOINT_CONTRACT_V4, not in tree; wording from paper/current/main.tex L92-94 and C203 record): Y = at least one active training-validation/model-selection or training-test/evaluation path permits same-speaker membership on both sides; N = every active path verified speaker-exclusive AND path enumeration closed; U = decisive membership unavailable, bounded resource cap prevented acquisition (C218: 20,652 files > 20,000-file cap), or no applicable split. Evidence is STATIC: byte-verified entry-to-split chains with per-line SHA-256 fragment hashes at a pinned commit (e.g., C203: four StratifiedKFold/KFold paths with group_argument=false; whole-tree scan for GroupKFold/LeaveOneGroupOut/groups= = 0 hits). Review = "second AI-assisted adversarial pass" over frozen evidence plus hash-bound review/adjudication/commit receipts per record; tools s1_acquire_batch_v5, s1_audit_repo_fetch_v5, s1_risk_adjudicator_v3/v4/v4b, s1_audit_finalize_v4, s1_risk_stats_v1. Effective 60 = 12 corrected_v5 + 4 corrected_v4 (C192/C280/C287/C358) + 44 carried; C292 Y->U in corrected_v5 (records 259/260). Statistic: confirmed fraction Y/n; sample partial-identification interval [Y/n, (Y+U)/n]; frame envelope by exhaustive exact hypergeometric inversion over K=0..N with rational arithmetic, two one-sided 97.5% bounds Bonferroni-combined (alpha 1/40 per tail) for joint >=95% coverage under partial classification, dual independent implementations.

S1 D2 FRAME REPAIR (2026-08-29, outcome-visible). Trigger: M4 red-team review found copy lineages (near-duplicate repos) in the 291 frame; author ruling (dialogue record 271) chose D2. D2 predicate: executable-code blobs = closed suffix set (.py .ipynb .m .sh .r .jl .js .ts .java .cpp .cc .c .h .hpp .cu .scala .lua .pl .bat .ps1), notebook = one blob, dedup by git blob SHA within repo, containment(A,B)=|A∩B|/min(|A|,|B|) >= 0.90 plus a frozen corroborator (same project name, identical root README blob, or owner lineage); plus original rules (explicit fork lineage, identical top-level tree SHA, identical full content-blob set). Canonical keeper: unique explicit upstream > earliest creation time > URL lexical order. Beacon permutation re-derived and filtered, not reseeded; outcome columns masked. Result N*=286; sample = 58 survivors + entrants C135, C203; dropped noncanonical C299 (->C303) and C103 (->C049). Only new entrants were re-audited (C203 via evidence v1 -> record-274 exact-byte review -> review v2 -> audit v3 -> commit v2; earlier same-transaction artifacts invalidated). replay_v1 rehashed 61 acquisition manifests, 22,799 files, 6,024,696,807 bytes. Sensitivity branches kept: D1 (N=289), D3 (N=287), original 291, historical N=282.

dossier.outcome: Two different headline numbers exist in the tree, and the program has demoted one. (1) The older paper lineage (paper/main.tex, paper/build/*, title 'A PREREGISTERED AUDIT ...') reports the P0.5 execution-validated result: 30 repos, 20 positive / 5 negative / 5 unresolved, 66.7% (Wilson 48.8-80.8%), sensitivity 83.3% (66.4-92.7%). (2) The authoritative record-282 lineage (paper/current/main.tex, per SUPERSESSION_MAP and DECISION_LOG, title 'A PROBABILITY AUDIT ...') reports S1 D2: frame of 286 lineages, 60 sampled, 44/9/7, sample partial-identification interval 73.3-85.0%, joint >=95% frame envelope 61.9-92.0%, in abstract (L25-26), Results (L151-154), Fig. 1 panel A, and Conclusion (L245-246). CURRENT_EXPERIMENT_INDEX labels P0/P0.5 'Historical basis for the current probability audit; the original frame is not the final D2 endpoint' and S1 D2 'Accepted revised-primary/exploratory endpoint. It is explicitly not preregistered or confirmatory' (dialogue record 277). The 'preregistered' wording was dropped: the paper now says contracts were 'locally frozen before audit outcomes, but no public immutable pre-outcome registration exists' (L81). Of P0's seven outcomes, only speaker-split risk reaches the paper; normalization/test-selection/augmentation/repetition/variance results and the purposive-vs-random comparison appear in no paper lineage. The 32-repo purposive P0 audit is 'deep case layer' only. P0_5_REPORT.md was never updated after the 21->20 correction. The D2 completion receipt is still 'pending an append-only dialogue external anchor'; the dialogue receipt chain formally ends at record 282 (two unidentified bytes deleted from an older prefix; record 283 adopted unreceipted).
limitations: Estimand is a bounded GitHub+arXiv-discoverable candidate frame (four corpora, top-100 best-match cutoffs, 2026-08-10), not SER papers or software in general; frame coverage is unquantified because Papers with Code and Semantic Scholar both returned nothing usable.

Construct: Y means an active path PERMITS same-speaker membership on both sides; it does not establish realized overlap in the authors' data, that a model used speaker identity, or what membership was used for a paper's reported run ('Static evidence shows what an inspected path permits', L229). P0.5 synthetic-manifest intersections confirm program mechanism only, not real-data overlap counts.

Frame is dominated by non-paper code: P0.5 sample is 19/30 supplemental_code (no paper) + 8 third-party reproductions, only 3 author-linked; S1 sample has 56/60 repo_relation=unknown. Claims about 'public SER implementations' therefore describe mostly student/hobby notebooks plus some paper code, not the published literature.

S1 (the paper's headline) is static evidence with hash-bound receipts; it lacks the execution-on-synthetic-manifest tier that P0.5 had. The more rigorous P0.5 evidence covers a nearly disjoint set of repos (2/60 overlap) and is now historical.

D2 lineage rule was chosen after outcomes were visible (author ruling record 271); mitigations are outcome-masked uniform application and retained D1/D3/291/282 sensitivity branches. No public pre-outcome registration exists for any part of the audit.

All inter-rater checks are different passes of the same automated agent system or an 'AI-assisted adversarial pass'; the planned human blind coding of 8-10 repos was prepared then revoked ('实验包.zip' invalidated); no human inter-rater reliability was ever computed.

Unresolved rate: 5/30 (P0.5) and 7/60 (S1). Unknowns may be informative (e.g., C218 unresolved because of a 20,000-file cap adopted after size visibility; P05R008 unresolved because external Kaggle directories are absent).

Hypergeometric frame envelope ([61.9, 92.0]%) is a joint bound under partial classification, not a CI centred on the confirmed fraction; the paper is careful about this but the width (30 pp) is large and the two intervals are easily conflated by readers.
Eligibility/accessibility could be correlated with risk outcome (acknowledged), which would bias the random sample despite the seeded order.

Frame manifest (frame_freeze_manifest_v6p7, 291 IDs), the S1 endpoint contract, and the per-record S1 audit JSONs for the 60 are not in this tree (private Release asset only); the panel cannot inspect per-record S1 evidence from here except C203.

dossier.contribution_to_paper_claim: This arm is the sole basis for the first half of the title ('A Probability Audit'), the first contribution, abstract sentences 3-5, Results 'Audit prevalence', Fig. 1 panel A, and the first sentence of the Conclusion in the authoritative record-282 paper: 'In the revised D2 frame of 286 public SER repository lineages, a probability sample of 60 contained 44 positive, 9 negative, and 7 unresolved ... partial-identification interval 73.3-85.0% ... joint >=95% confidence envelope 61.9-92.0%.' P0 contributes the search protocol, exclusion codes, and the 383-URL candidate log that the Methods (L75-79) cite as the frame origin; P0.5 contributes no number to the current paper (its 20/30, 66.7% appears only in the superseded paper/main.tex and paper/build lineage). The audit is deliberately decoupled from P1: the paper states the audit and experiment have separate estimands and forbids multiplying prevalence by effect size (L55-56, L212). Dependence is therefore total for the prevalence claim but zero for the protocol-effect claims; if the S1 D2 endpoint were withdrawn, the paper would fall back to P0.5's 20/30 with a different frame definition and different evidence standard.
untested_gaps: No human coder ever coded any repository; inter-rater reliability between the automated passes and a human is unmeasured (the planned 8-10-repo author blind coding was revoked).
The 2 repos in both P0.5 and S1 samples, and the 4 P0 purposive includes in S1, are natural cross-lineage agreement checks (execution-validated vs static; purposive vs random) that were not reported.

S1's Y conflates validation/model-selection-boundary nonexclusivity with test-boundary nonexclusivity; how many of the 44 Y are test-boundary overlaps versus validation-only is not reported, though the two have very different implications for reported test scores.
No stratification of the 44/9/7 by repo_relation (paper-linked vs student project), corpus, or year, so the reader cannot tell whether risk is concentrated in non-paper code.

No link from code risk to reported numbers: the P0 field paper_code_discrepancy and reported_results were collected but never summarized; whether 'risky' repos report higher accuracy than 'clean' ones within the same corpus is untested (P1 answers this only for the authors' own implementation).
Realized speaker overlap under the authors' actual data (rather than the synthetic manifest) was never estimated, even for the 24 tier-1 P0.5 repos where the split fragment is executable.

Informativeness of unknowns: whether U/unknown repos differ systematically (size, framework, notebook vs script) from resolved ones is not examined, so the partial-identification interval's realism is unassessed.
Frame coverage: no estimate of what fraction of arXiv/GitHub SER code the top-100 best-match cutoffs and four-corpus restriction miss; P0.6's alternative-source check produced zero usable data.

Temporal trend (2019-2026 publication years are present in P0.5) is not analyzed, though a recent-year concentration (16/30 from 2025-2026) suggests the frame may be dominated by very recent, low-effort repositories.
Whether the D2 containment threshold (0.90) and corroborator rule are sensitive: only the D1/D3 variants were computed, not a threshold sweep.

dossier.arm: P1 controlled study (RAVDESS + CREMA-D protocol comparison; "protocol premium" measurement)
dossier.purpose: Isolate, under fully fixed model/input/optimizer/augmentation/evaluation-sample conditions, how much switching the evaluation protocol of the same corpus from speaker-independent (GroupKFold, LOSO) to utterance-level random splitting optimistically inflates UAR (primary), accuracy and macro-F1 (secondary). The preregistration (frozen 2026-08-10 18:02:55 UTC-04:00, before any P1 training) states explicitly that P1 does not reproduce papers, does not compare others' code, and does not tune for the best-looking model; it only measures the premium. A prior sister-project observation of 0.555 -> 0.736 (~18.1 pp) is declared a hypothesis-forming prior, not part of P1 inference. This arm is the "Controlled Study of Protocol Effects" half of the paper title; the listed files themselves do not state where in the paper the results are placed.
dossier.design_summary:
CORPORA (fixed analysis population, all readable WAVs, no exclusions): RAVDESS speech, 1,440 utterances, 24 actors, 8 emotions (label order neutral, calm, happy, sad, angry, fearful, disgust, surprised; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; song subset excluded); CREMA-D, 7,442 utterances, 91 actors, 6 emotions (angry, disgust, fearful, happy, neutral, sad; ODbL 1.0 / DbCL 1.0). Known data quirks retained on purpose: RAVDESS 1 exact-duplicate pair (same actor/label) and 5 stereo files; CREMA-D 3 exact-duplicate groups with conflicting labels, 1 renamed variant (1040_ITH_SAD_X.wav), and 1076_MTI_SAD_XX.wav (manifest index 6187) is readable but all-zero audio (only zero-variance spectrogram). Byte-level manifests (relative path, bytes, SHA-256, label, speaker) hashed: RAVDESS 259b453c..., CREMA-D 8b628265....

FEATURES (one shared cache for all models/protocols/seeds): librosa.load sr=22050 mono; trim top_db=30; zero-pad if <0.1 s; 64 mel bins, n_fft=1024, hop=512, fmax=11025; power_to_db(ref=max); fixed 128 frames (~2.97 s; pad right with spectrogram minimum, truncate to first 128); per-utterance z-score (single mean/SD per spectrogram, eps=1e-6, no cross-utterance statistics). Train-only online SpecAugment: 2 time masks (<=16 frames), 2 freq masks (<=8 bins), Gaussian noise sigma=0.1. No augmentation on validation/test. Cache SHA-256s RAVDESS 0e73160e..., CREMA-D c4913616...; preprocessing code hash 33bc3b5e....

MODELS (4 small architectures, all built by sister-project advanced_models.build_neural_model at git commit d11768ed..., config = candidate_configs(model)[2], fully expanded in the prereg): CNN (width 48, 3 blocks, kernel 5, dilation base 1, dropout 0.1; AdamW lr 1e-3, wd 1e-4); ResNet-SE (width 48, 4 blocks, kernel 5, max dilation 4, SE reduction 4, dropout 0.1; AdamW lr 1e-3, wd 1e-4); Transformer (d_model 96, 4 heads, 2 layers, FF x2, normalized sinusoidal position, attentive pooling, dropout 0.1; AdamW lr 3e-4, wd 1e-4); FNO (width 48, 16 Fourier modes, 4 layers, dropout 0.1; AdamW lr 1e-3, wd 1e-4). Input [B,64,128].

TRAINING: class-balanced cross-entropy (weights computed from the current fit subset only), batch 64, max 100 epochs, CosineAnnealingLR T_max=100, early stopping on full-validation weighted CE loss (sum weighted per-sample CE / sum target class weights) with patience 15, checkpoint updated only on strict < improvement, restore best-loss checkpoint, outer test touched exactly once after restore. float32, no AMP, TF32 off, torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True), cuDNN deterministic, num_workers=0. Seeds {0,1,2}. Model/loader/augment RNG key = first 32 bits (big-endian) of SHA256("P1-train|corpus|protocol|outer_fold|seed") (no model token, so the same corpus/protocol/fold/seed reuses identical splits/batch order across models). Fixed run order corpus ravdess->cremad, model cnn->resnet_se->transformer->fno, protocol random->groupkfold->loso, seed 0->1->2, folds ascending; no result-dependent stopping.

OUTER PROTOCOLS (generated once, hashed, identical for all 4 models x 3 seeds; each gives exactly-once OOF coverage): (1) Random utterance-level: StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42) stratified by emotion only, speaker not passed (the leakage control arm); (2) Speaker-independent GroupKFold(n_splits=5, groups=speaker_id), hard failure on any train/test speaker overlap; (3) LOSO by ascending canonical speaker ID: 24 folds RAVDESS, 91 folds CREMA-D. INNER VALIDATION (~25% of outer train): random arm train_test_split(test_size=0.25, stratify=emotion) allowing speaker overlap (by design); grouped arms GroupShuffleSplit(n_splits=1, test_size=0.25) by speaker with fit/val speaker disjointness enforced; inner random_state = first 32 bits of SHA256("P1-inner|corpus|protocol|outer_fold|seed"), retry base+1..+99 if any class missing (all 405 inner splits succeeded at offset 0); infeasible would be recorded as inner_split_infeasible, never borrowing outer test.

UNITS: run_plan.csv fixed at 1,620 fits = RAVDESS 4 models x 3 seeds x (5+5+24)=408 and CREMA-D 4 x 3 x (5+5+91)=1,212; LOSO alone is 1,380 of 1,620 fits (85%). Each fit writes config.json, history.csv, per-utterance predictions.csv (all logits), run.json with SHAs. One retry allowed only for failures before outer-test access.

ESTIMAND: Delta_RG = UAR(random) - UAR(GroupKFold); Delta_RL = UAR(random) - UAR(LOSO); Delta_GL = UAR(GroupKFold) - UAR(LOSO); positive = looser protocol scores higher; negatives never clipped to zero. Two reporting layers: (a) OOF layer: for each corpus x model x protocol x seed concatenate all outer-fold test predictions into one OOF prediction, compute UAR/accuracy/macro-F1, report mean +/- sample SD over 3 seeds (outer folds never treated as replicates); (b) PAIRED layer (the confirmatory one): for each speaker x protocol x model x corpus x seed compute UAR on that speaker's own utterances (identical utterance set across protocols), average within speaker over 3 seeds, then take the per-speaker difference. Point estimate = mean speaker difference; 95% CI = 10,000-replicate speaker-cluster percentile bootstrap (whole speakers resampled), fixed seed 202608101744, numpy linear percentile 2.5/97.5. Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank (zero_method="wilcox", correction=False, method="auto"; all-zero -> p=1; exact sign test only as sensitivity if SciPy fails). Confirmatory family fixed at 2 corpora x 4 models x 3 UAR contrasts = 24 tests, Holm alpha=0.05 (missing tests would be p=1 placeholders keeping family=24). Accuracy and macro-F1 paired differences with cluster-bootstrap CIs are descriptive only, no significance. Random-arm per-fold speaker overlap (n_train/n_test/n_overlap/fraction) reported plus zero-overlap assertions for grouped arms. Any missing/failed/invalid outer fold invalidates the whole corpus-model-protocol-seed cell and every dependent contrast (written "not conclusive").

BUDGET CAPS: 200 single-GPU hours, 14 days wall, 20 GiB artifacts, checked before each unit and at epoch boundaries. ENVIRONMENT: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070, Windows 11 (10.0.26200), Python 3.13.9 (Anaconda), torch 2.11.0+cu128, CUDA 12.8, numpy 2.4.6, scipy 1.18.0, sklearn 1.9.0, librosa 0.11.0, soundfile 0.14.0.

dossier.outcome: Completed in full with no missing cells (72/72 cells, 1,620/1,620 fits, both the internal verifier and an independent re-implementation report pass with 0.0 numeric error). Findings: (1) the Random-vs-GroupKFold premium is positive and Holm-significant for all 4 architectures on both corpora, but its magnitude is strongly corpus-dependent: +15.4 to +19.7 UAR points on RAVDESS (24 speakers) versus only +1.8 to +3.1 points on CREMA-D (91 speakers); (2) Random-vs-LOSO is +11.1 to +15.3 points on RAVDESS (all significant) but near zero on CREMA-D (-0.5 to +1.1 points; only CNN significant); (3) LOSO scores higher than GroupKFold in every one of the 8 cells (GL negative, significant in 6 of 8), contradicting the prior expectation that LOSO is the stricter protocol, and explainable by LOSO's larger per-fold training-speaker count; (4) absolute UARs are well below the preregistered prior points on both corpora, and the CREMA-D premia are 3-10x smaller than the priors. Of 24 confirmatory tests, 19 rejected under Holm and 5 did not (RAVDESS Transformer GL, RAVDESS FNO GL, CREMA-D ResNet-SE RL, CREMA-D Transformer RL, CREMA-D FNO RL). The listed files do not record how the paper places these results (main vs supplement); given the title, this is the controlled-study half of the main paper. No result was demoted or declared no-go in the files read.
limitations: Only 2 corpora, both acted, scripted, English, studio-recorded; no spontaneous/podcast/multilingual corpora, so the premium's generality is unknown.

RAVDESS has only 2 lexically matched sentences (and 60 utterances per actor, 8 classes with neutral at half count), so per-speaker UARs are noisy (speaker-difference SD 0.07-0.10 on n=24) and the corpus is atypically small; CREMA-D has 12 sentences and ~82 utterances per speaker. The files never discuss sentence count as a factor.

Handcrafted log-mel input (64 mel, 128 frames ~ 2.97 s, longer utterances truncated to the first 128 frames, per-utterance z-score); no pretrained self-supervised or fine-tuned front-ends (wav2vec2/HuBERT/WavLM), which dominate current SER practice.

Small, untuned models fixed at the sister project's candidate_configs[2] (width 48 / d_model 96, 2-4 blocks/layers), max 100 epochs, batch 64; speaker-independent absolute UARs (RAVDESS GroupKFold 0.39-0.46, CREMA-D 0.49-0.59) are below commonly reported values, so the premium at higher capacity is untested.
The Random arm's inner validation also allows speaker overlap by design, so Delta_RG/Delta_RL bundle outer-test leakage with leaky early-stopping selection; the two sources are not separated.
Random arm = 100% speaker overlap in every fold (overlap fraction 1.0); no partial-overlap or dose-response condition, so the study cannot say how much premium arises from, e.g., 20% shared speakers.

Delta_GL (GroupKFold - LOSO) is confounded with training-set size (LOSO trains on 23/24 or 90/91 speakers vs 19-20/24 or 72-73/91), so the negative GL cannot be attributed to protocol strictness per se; the preregistration did not anticipate this and no control (e.g., LOSO with train subsampled to GroupKFold size) exists.

LOSO cost: 1,380 of 1,620 fits (85%) and presumably most of the 25 GPU-hours go to LOSO; on CREMA-D (1,092 LOSO fits) LOSO essentially matches Random, so Delta_RL there is uninformative about leakage.
Only 3 seeds; seed SDs are small (0.001-0.025) relative to premia on RAVDESS but comparable to premia on CREMA-D LOSO contrasts.
Fixed hyperparameters with no per-protocol HPO; the premium under hyperparameter search on leaky splits (the realistic failure mode in public code) is not measured.

Duplicates retained by rule (RAVDESS 1 exact-duplicate pair; CREMA-D 3 duplicate groups with conflicting labels) and one all-zero CREMA-D file retained; exact duplicates split across train/test in the Random arm are a second, tiny leakage source not separated from speaker leakage.

Wilcoxon signed-rank with speaker-level ties/zeros (up to 3 zero differences dropped under zero_method='wilcox') on n=24 for RAVDESS; the RAVDESS FNO GL case shows bootstrap CI and Wilcoxon disagreeing at the margin.

Absolute UARs and CREMA-D premia fall well outside the preregistered prior intervals; the preregistration mandates an implementation audit in that case, but no audit document is among the listed files (only the two verification JSONs, which check pipeline integrity, not modeling adequacy).
Deterministic single-GPU Windows environment (RTX 5070, torch 2.11.0+cu128, Python 3.13.9); reproducibility elsewhere unverified.

dossier.contribution_to_paper_claim: The paper's title makes two claims: (i) speaker-nonexclusivity risk is prevalent in public SER code (the probability-audit arm) and (ii) protocol choice causally inflates reported numbers (this controlled-study arm). This arm is the sole causal evidence for (ii) and supplies the effect sizes the paper can attach to the audit's risk estimates: under identical models/features/seeds, utterance-level random splitting inflates UAR by +15 to +20 points on RAVDESS and +2 to +3 points on CREMA-D relative to speaker-independent GroupKFold, with 19/24 Holm-corrected paired tests significant and all 8 RG contrasts significant. It also supplies the secondary, unexpected finding that LOSO reports higher UAR than 5-fold GroupKFold on every architecture and both corpora, which matters for any claim that LOSO is the 'strictest' protocol. The claim's weight depends heavily on this arm: without it the paper has prevalence but no magnitude. Conversely, the arm shows the magnitude is corpus-dependent (RAVDESS vs CREMA-D differ by ~6x), so a paper-level claim of a single 'inflation figure' would not be supported; the arm supports a range and a mechanism (fewer speakers, fewer sentences -> larger premium) only qualitatively.
untested_gaps: Why is the premium ~6x larger on RAVDESS than CREMA-D? Speaker count (24 vs 91), utterances per speaker, sentence count (2 vs 12), class count (8 vs 6) and recording conditions are all confounded; no subsampling experiment (e.g., CREMA-D restricted to 24 speakers or 2 sentences) isolates the driver.
Does the premium survive with pretrained SSL front-ends (wav2vec2/WavLM/HuBERT) or fine-tuned large models, i.e., the pipelines actually found in public SER code?
Dose-response: premium as a function of the fraction of test speakers seen in training (0%, 10%, 50%, 100%); only 0% and 100% were measured.
Decomposition of the Random-arm premium into outer-test leakage vs leaky inner validation/early stopping (crossed designs: random outer + grouped inner, grouped outer + random inner).
Is negative Delta_GL a training-set-size effect? Test LOSO with training speakers subsampled to GroupKFold size, or GroupKFold with 24/91 folds.
Does the premium interact with hyperparameter search performed on leaky validation data (the realistic failure mode)?
Per-class effects: which emotions absorb the inflation (per-class recall/confusions are not in the listed summary tables).
Other leakage channels beyond speaker: sentence/text identity, session, gender balance across folds; the study measures speaker only.
Additional corpora (IEMOCAP, MSP-Podcast, EmoDB, non-English, spontaneous speech) to test generality; only two acted English corpora were used.
Effect of the 128-frame (~3 s) truncation and of the retained duplicates / all-zero file on the premia (no sensitivity analysis).
Calibration/confidence effects of leakage (only point metrics measured; logits were saved but not analyzed in the listed files).
Reconciling the large miss between preregistered priors and outcomes: the mandated implementation audit for out-of-interval results is not among the listed files.
How the controlled premia map onto the audit arm's risk probabilities (e.g., expected inflation per repository) is not computed here.

dossier.arm: C / P5 mechanism-exposure salvage (post-exposure protocol-deviation finite-panel descriptive pilot; CNN-only; RAVDESS vs CREMA-D cross-prompt target-actor exposure-substitution)
dossier.purpose: Original question (P5 plan §1.1): why, under the unified P1 pipeline, is the RAVDESS Random-minus-GroupKFold UAR gap (+15.39 to +19.68 pp) so much larger than CREMA-D's (+1.82 to +3.06 pp)? P1 cannot answer this because Random vs GroupKFold changes both the outer test split and the inner validation grouping at once. P5 narrows it to (§1.2): holding the test utterances, validation set, training size, training-speaker count, and per-corpus label x text-cell counts fixed, does replacing a matched donor actor's utterances with the TEST actor's OTHER (different-text, i.e. cross-prompt) utterances raise test UAR more in RAVDESS than in CREMA-D? The pre-frozen directional prediction is delta_panel > 0. IMPORTANT for the panel: "mechanism exposure" here means target-actor training EXPOSURE (the actor's own cross-prompt speech in the training set), NOT a speaker-identity probe of the model. No representational probing of checkpoints for speaker identity is performed anywhere in this arm; the plan (§13 item 3) explicitly forbids writing "the SER model uses voiceprint / memorized actor identity". "Checkpoint" = one trained CNN fit (144 of them); "occurrences" (a term used only in docs/CURRENT_EXPERIMENT_INDEX.md and README.md) = the 6,336 utterance-level scoring rows = 144 checkpoints x 44 fixed test utterances (T_s + T_d) each, which the salvage verifier hard-asserts (len(raw) == 6336). The estimand is explicitly an "actor/session/expression exposure substitution effect" (§1.4), not a pure voiceprint effect, not a causal effect of speaker count, not a mediation decomposition of the P1 gap, and not a same-text repetition test. In the program logic (PLAN §12) it is the third, complementary leg after (1) the probability audit of public code and (2) P1/P4 protocol sensitivity, but it was frozen at G0 as NOT a fourth contribution and (presentation option B) at most one pre-written sentence in the main text.
dossier.design_summary:
DATA/PANELS (plan §3-4). Two corpora, 24 actors each. RAVDESS: all 24 actors (12F/12M), calm and surprised excluded. CREMA-D: 24-actor panel (12F+12M) drawn from 91 eligible actors by sorting SHA256("ICASSP2027-P5-v1|"+actor_id) within sex and taking the first 12 per stratum, after outcome-blind eligibility (actors 1006 and 1017 excluded for cross-label identical hashes among selected files; 1013 and 1076 anomalies only informational). Six shared classes with frozen label map angry=0, disgust=1, fearful=2, happy=3, neutral=4, sad=5. Exactly 44 utterances per actor: neutral 4, each other class 8. RAVDESS: neutral 1 intensity x 2 statements x 2 reps; others 2 intensities x 2 statements x 2 reps. CREMA-D: intensity=XX only; non-neutral sentences DFA, IOM, ITS, IWL, IWW, TAI, TIE, TSI; neutral DFA, IOM, IWL, IWW. Each actor's 44 files split before training into exposure-half E_s (22) and test-half T_s (22), prompt-disjoint within corpus: RAVDESS Half-A = statement 01, Half-B = statement 02; CREMA-D Half-A = {DFA, IOM, ITS, IWL} + neutral {DFA, IOM}, Half-B = {IWW, TAI, TIE, TSI} + neutral {IWL, IWW}. Every half has neutral 2 and 4 per other class. Actors paired within sex by hash order into 12 pairs per corpus (M0-M5, F0-F5); both members of a pair use the same half direction; 3 pairs per sex use E=A/T=B and 3 use E=B/T=A. RAVDESS Actor 07 has two byte-identical happy files in statement 02, so its pair is frozen at E=Half-B(st02) and a pre-specified sensitivity drops the entire Actor-07 pair (recompute on 11 pairs). Actor 20 has two stereo source files, kept with the frozen mono=True downmix.

UNITS/ARMS (§5). For target pair (s,d): validation V is a deterministic rotation (target Mi -> V = M(i+1 mod 6) U Fi; target Fi -> V = F(i+1 mod 6) U Mi), so V = 4 actors (2F+2M) = 176 utterances and every pair serves as V exactly twice. Base B = remaining 18 actors x 44 = 792 utterances. Arm M_s trains on B + E_s = 814 utterances, 19 speakers; arm M_d trains on B + E_d = 814 utterances, 19 speakers. Fixed test = T_s + T_d = 44 utterances. Training label counts identical across arms (neutral 74, others 148 each), as are test/validation files and order, optimizer, scheduler, epoch cap, early-stop rule, init seed, and slot-level minibatch/augmentation random streams. For T_s, M_s is "exposed" and M_d "unexposed"; for T_d the roles reverse, so each pair yields two opposite-direction counterfactuals. Features: P1's frozen per-utterance z-scored log-mel cache, no additional cross-utterance scaler; BatchNorm running stats, internal normalization and all learned weights still vary with E_s/E_d (plan §5.4 says this must not be described as "all normalization paths excluded").

MODEL/SEEDS/FITS (§6). CNN only (P1 implementation and frozen hyperparameters; RAVDESS head changed 8->6 classes; salvage inference via BUILD_MODEL("cnn", 64, 6, config), CPU-only, argmax). Seeds 0, 1, 2; train_seed = stable_u32("p5|{corpus}|{pair_id}|{seed}"), arm-independent. Total = 12 pairs x 2 arms x 3 seeds x 2 corpora = 144 fits. Transformer sensitivity (a further 144 fits) was frozen OUT at G0 and may not be added by result. Budget hard cap 3.0 charged GPU-h (CNN-only estimate 0.4-1.0 GPU-h). Interleaving pair -> RAVDESS CNN -> CREMA-D CNN so a hard stop (frozen 2026-08-22 23:59:59 UTC-4) would not leave one corpus only.

ESTIMAND/STATISTICS (§7). Actor-level UAR = unweighted mean of six class recalls over the actor's 22 fixed test items (neutral 2, others 4; no empty class allowed). tau_{c,s} = mean over 3 seeds of [UAR(T_s; M_{E_s,k}) - UAR(T_s; M_{E_d,k})]. Symmetric pair contrast g_{c,i} = 1/2(tau_a + tau_b). Delta_c = mean of 12 g_{c,i}. Sole primary endpoint delta_panel = Delta_RAVDESS - Delta_CREMA-D as a finite-panel POINT ESTIMATE. Inference level frozen at G0: finite-panel descriptive pilot, no CI, no p-value; leave-one-pair-out (12 x 2 recomputations) reported only as a "stability range"; seeds are not n; no corpus-label permutation, no sign-flip test; percentile pair-bootstrap explicitly forbidden as a population CI because every pair's model reuses the other 22 actors as base/validation, so the 12 g_{c,i} are not independent clusters. SESOI = 5 UAR pp (about one third of the P1 12-18 pp RG gap), used only to classify the observed magnitude: delta > +5 positive-substantive; 0 < delta <= +5 positive-below-threshold; -5 <= delta <= 0 no-substantive-difference; delta < -5 reversed-substantive (SESOI_PP = 5.0 pinned, strict >/>= boundaries as in score_p5_v3.py sha 3fb7acb1...). A confirmatory path (§8.2 CI-boundary table, §9 coverage simulation with 1x/1.5x/2x SD inflation, within-pair and between-pair correlation) was drafted but never activated. Blind protocol: runner receives only opaque test IDs + feature tensors; sealed opaque_id->label key; single batch scoring after a completion-and-scoring manifest.

SALVAGE PROTOCOL (contract v1 + errata v1.1-v1.3; PLAN revisions 8-9). Triggered by INCIDENT-P5KEY-20260821 (see limitations). Author chose option B "downgraded salvage" (record 186, 2026-08-21 21:06 -04) over Codex's option A (terminate C as incomplete). Immutables: all 144/144 v3 checkpoints, both panels, test keys, splits, roles, packages, cache read-only; no retraining, model change, panel/split/endpoint change, exposed-row deletion, or key resealing. Analysis functions (actor_uar/analyze/classify_sesoi/LOPO/actor07_sensitivity) reused verbatim from score_p5_v3.py; a new isolated launcher/scorer/verifier was built with: authentication chain (author unlock -> completion manifest -> design/run-plan -> self-hash -> 144 checkpoint + package sha -> cache/roles/input roots) BEFORE any import/checkpoint load/key parse; read-once same-bytes hashing; two persistent state machines (salvage_v1/launch_attempt.json: absent->authenticating->authenticated; salvage_v1/scoring_claim.json: absent->claimed->committed, terminal states committed/consumed/failed_consumed/aborted_consumed, never reset to absent; shared attempt_id UUID and digests bound across FSMs; tmp-file + fsync + os.replace + re-read on every write); key bytes read exactly once only after a durable re-read-verified claim; fail-closed propagation actor x seed -> pair -> corpus -> delta_panel with no available-case analysis; disclosure block (incident ID, not blind, CNN-only, repo/arXiv-only) constructed in memory before the first atomic write; independent-code-path post-score recomputation. Executed once by Codex after taking over C (PLAN rev 9) with a one-time author waiver of personnel review. Output: one salvage_scoring_report.json (O_EXCL) with actor x seed, pair x seed, 3-seed means/SD, Delta_c, delta_panel, all LOPO, Actor-07 sensitivity, boundary classification; plus claim registry, correction receipt, and immutable hashes.

dossier.outcome: FOUND: in the two frozen 24-actor panels, cross-prompt target-actor exposure produced a larger positive point estimate in RAVDESS (+6.42 pp) than in CREMA-D (+1.85 pp); the corpus difference delta_panel = +4.57 pp is positive but BELOW the pre-specified 5 pp substantive threshold. All 12 RAVDESS pair contrasts were positive; CREMA-D had 9 positive, 1 zero, 2 negative. LOPO kept the positive direction everywhere (+3.58 to +5.09) but straddled the 5 pp line, so the magnitude classification is not stable. Since delta_panel > 0 AND Delta_RAVDESS > 0, the plan's narrower permitted reading applies: the direction is consistent with RAVDESS having stronger positive cross-prompt exposure sensitivity, as a mechanism clue only. PROGRAM TREATMENT: status "complete_post_exposure_protocol_deviation_finite_panel_descriptive_pilot". Per G0 presentation option B and PLAN §24 rule C, the result goes to repo/arXiv/supplement only, with at most one pre-written sentence in the ICASSP main text; it is explicitly not promoted on effect size, and PLAN revision 10 (outcome-visible editorial routing of B into the main text) leaves C's repo/arXiv routing unchanged. Because the direction agrees with the main-text interpretation, the only lever C had on the main text (forcing a weakening if it contradicted) was not triggered. Deliverables: results/experiment_summaries/c_mechanism_salvage/ (summary, claim registry, correction receipt) and the supplement-ledgers Release asset; CURRENT_EXPERIMENT_INDEX records it as "Complete under the salvage contract" with governance deviations and proxy limits kept visible; no retraining, panel change, or second scoring pass allowed.
limitations: No population inference at all: no CI, no p-value; delta_panel is a point estimate over two fixed 24-actor panels. The 12 pair contrasts per corpus are not independent because each pair's models reuse the other 22 actors as base (18) and validation (4); the plan says a pair bootstrap cannot repair this and must not be reported as a CI.

Not blind and not preregistered: INCIDENT-P5KEY-20260821 (executor read one CREMA-D key row and both key line counts before the authentication/sentinel gate); a second disclosed deviation (one real no-label checkpoint+cache forward pass before the final authentication entry, logits/argmax only); a third post-score verifier tolerance correction that is outcome-visible. The arm may not be described as fully blind, sealed-throughout, preregistered, or deviation-free. Even before the incident, the absence of a public timestamp limited it to 'prospectively frozen'.

Personnel independent review was waived by the author (independent_review='waived'; personnel_independent_review=false). The post-score recomputation is code-path independent only, written by the same program participants. Codex, the intended reviewer, was permission-blocked from all P5 key/split/mechanism artifacts until it was instead made the executor.

Estimand proxy limits: the manipulation swaps 22 utterances of a target actor for 22 cell-matched utterances of a donor actor, so actor identity, recording session, and performance/expression style change together; the effect cannot be attributed to biological voice identity, speaker count, language, text count, or recording condition, and it is not a mediation share of the P1 Random-GroupKFold gap. The plan forbids any 'explains X% of P1' statement.

Cross-prompt only: E and T halves are prompt-disjoint (RAVDESS statement 01 vs 02; CREMA-D two disjoint sentence sets). The same-speaker x same-emotion x same-text repetition pathway, which an unaccepted structural count suggested is more common in RAVDESS random splits, is untested by design; a null here would not have refuted it and the positive result does not rank the two pathways.

Corpus asymmetry in what 'exposure' contains: RAVDESS halves include both intensity levels while CREMA-D uses only intensity=XX; RAVDESS test items are the other scripted statement whereas CREMA-D test items are four different sentences. The two panels are therefore matched on counts, not on prompt diversity.
CNN only. The Transformer sensitivity arm was frozen out, so dependence of the direction on convolutional inductive bias is unknown.
The CREMA-D panel is one hash-selected 24-of-91 sample (12F/12M); the plan forbids treating it as representative of all 91 actors or all CREMA-D usage. No replication panel.

Actor-level UAR granularity (derived, not in the files): each actor's class recall is computed on 2 (neutral) or 4 (other) test items, so a single test-item flip moves actor UAR by 4.17 pp (non-neutral) or 8.33 pp (neutral). The 5 pp SESOI is of the same order as one item flip at the actor level; only averaging over 24 actors x 3 seeds provides finer resolution.
Seed variability is substantial relative to the SESOI: seed-specific delta_panel spans +2.95 to +5.90 pp, i.e. the classification would differ by seed; seeds are frozen as training noise, not n.

The result summary reports only aggregates (Delta_c, delta_panel, sign counts, LOPO range, seed values); per-actor tau values, per-pair g values with seed SDs, per-class recalls, accuracy/macro-F1, and half-direction/sex diagnostics are said to be in the full scoring report but are not in the files read here.

Actor 07's byte-duplicate happy files sit in its exposure half; the prescribed whole-pair exclusion lowers delta_panel from 4.57 to 4.21, and the implied pair contrast (~+10.4 pp) is well above the RAVDESS mean, so one pair with a known data anomaly contributes disproportionately.

dossier.contribution_to_paper_claim: Which claim: the paper's interpretive claim that the Random-vs-GroupKFold protocol gap is corpus-dependent (RAVDESS >> CREMA-D) and that target-speaker exposure in training is a plausible pathway (PLAN §12 leg 3: "do the two anchor corpora show pre-frozen differential target-actor exposure sensitivity"). How much: very little by design. G0 presentation option B and PLAN §24 rule C cap the main text at one pre-written pilot sentence of the form "in two pre-defined, size- and label-matched finite actor panels we observed / did not observe the pre-specified direction and magnitude of the cross-prompt target-actor exposure-substitution difference; this point estimate is a mechanism screening clue, not a population test". The observed result fills that sentence with "positive direction, below the 5 pp threshold". It cannot be cited as explaining or mediating the P1 gap, as evidence of speaker-identity memorization, or with a CI/p-value (registry forbidden_claims). Its only structural influence on the main text would have been negative (a contradiction would force weakening main-text wording), and that did not occur. The main contributions (probability audit; P1/P4 protocol effects) do not depend on this arm numerically or logically; C is a supplement/arXiv item with a permanently disclosed deviation record.
untested_gaps: Same-text pathway: no arm exposes the model to the SAME speaker x emotion x text as the test item, so the effect of literal repetition (the structural-count observation about RAVDESS random splits) versus cross-prompt speaker/session exposure is unseparated.

No representational test of speaker identity: no speaker-ID probe, embedding similarity, or identity-classifier on the exposed vs unexposed checkpoints, so 'exposure substitution effect' cannot be upgraded to 'speaker-identity information in the emotion model'.
Dose-response: exposure is fixed at 22 utterances; nothing tests whether Delta scales with the number of exposed utterances, which is what a bridge to the P1 gap would require.

Linking to the P1 gap: no design puts exposure into the actual Random split (e.g., stratified removal of test-speaker utterances from Random-split training with the outer split fixed), so the fraction of the +15-20 pp RAVDESS gap attributable to exposure remains unknown and the plan forbids estimating it.
Architecture dependence: CNN only; no Transformer, ResNet-SE, or self-supervised front-end.

Decomposition of the manipulated bundle: actor identity vs recording session vs performance style vs intensity coverage (RAVDESS two intensities vs CREMA-D XX only) are confounded within the substitution.

Per-class and per-actor heterogeneity: which emotions carry the +6.42 pp RAVDESS effect, why two CREMA-D pairs are negative and one is zero, and which pair drives the LOPO minimum (+3.58) are not reported in the files read.
Panel replication: only one CREMA-D 24-actor panel; the remaining 67 actors and alternative hash seeds are untested; no second RAVDESS-like corpus.

Dependence-aware inference: what a design with independent base/validation per pair, or the §9 coverage simulation (1x/1.5x/2x SD inflation, within-pair and between-pair correlation, seed variance), would say about the precision of delta_panel was never run.

Clean re-execution: what a fresh, publicly timestamped, key-custody-separated, personnel-reviewed run would need: (a) a public pre-registration commit/OSF stamp; (b) key custody held by a non-executor with sentinel-gated access; (c) a named independent reviewer with P5 permissions completed before scoring; (d) an inference design that either avoids shared base/validation or models the dependence with pre-approved coverage simulation; (e) a same-text arm and a Transformer arm; (f) a speaker-ID probe on penultimate features; (g) an exposure-dose ladder; (h) at least one outcome-blind replication panel for CREMA-D. None of these were done.

dossier.arm: S0 / S2 / S3 / S4 SSL probe series (ssl_probe_v2_repro; ssl_split_stability_v1; SUBESCO release_v10; wavlm_layer_weighting_v1 NO-GO)
dossier.purpose: The series asks whether the speaker-nonexclusivity "protocol premium" P_RG = UAR(random split) - UAR(speaker-grouped split) that the paper measures on trained-from-scratch stacks (P1, 1,620 fits) also appears when the representation is a modern frozen self-supervised encoder, i.e. whether the effect is an artifact of small from-scratch models. S0 answers this on RAVDESS and CREMA-D with formal per-speaker tests. S2 asks whether the sign of that contrast is stable to the partition draw (an uncertainty source S0's bootstrap explicitly excludes). S3 asks the same partition-stability question on a non-English (Bangla, SUBESCO) repetition-clean panel. S4 (WavLM layer-weighting) would have probed whether WavLM's small/fragile premium is a final-layer artifact; it was never run.
dossier.design_summary:
S0 (ssl_probe_v2_repro, 2026-08-22): outcome-visible corrective reproducibility re-run of ssl_probe_v1; science identical to v1, changes are provenance-only (matched torch/torchaudio 2.10.0+cu128, pinned weights/tools/env, per-row cache identity, exact-rational rank statistics). Probes: torchaudio.pipelines HUBERT_BASE, WAV2VEC2_BASE, WAVLM_BASE_PLUS, frozen pretrained, no fine-tuning; weight SHAs pinned (~377 MB each). Frontend: librosa load sr=16000 mono, trim top_db=30, pad min 1600 samples, float32, FINAL hidden layer, time-mean pooling, 768-d. Head: single linear 768->n_classes, class-balanced CE, AdamW lr=1e-3 wd=1e-4, batch 64, max 100 epochs, patience 15, checkpoint = strict min validation weighted CE, no augmentation; seed contract stable_u32('SSL-train|corpus|protocol|fold|seed') shared across probes. Corpora: RAVDESS (24 speakers), CREMA-D (91 speakers). Splits: P1 frozen inner-split npz, byte-pinned, 60 pins = 2 corpora x 2 protocols (random, groupkfold) x 5 folds x 3 seeds; 180 units = 60 x 3 probes; GPU RTX 5070, Windows 11, Python 3.13.9, sklearn 1.9.0. Estimand chain: per-speaker OOF UAR -> mean over 3 seeds -> per-probe speaker-equal P_RG = UAR_random - UAR_groupkfold, all as exact rationals. Interval: paired whole-speaker bootstrap on float64 deltas, 10,000 replicates, 95%, seed 2812276266, percentile-linear; reported strictly as a conditional whole-speaker interval (no split-realization or training-pipeline uncertainty). Test: Wilcoxon signed-rank with zero removal, exact-rational ties/average ranks, frozen normal approximation with tie correction, no continuity correction, two-sided, for all 6 contrasts regardless of n; Holm family fixed at 6 (2 corpora x 3 probes). Readout rule: v2 numbers reported as-is whether equal/smaller/larger/reversed vs v1; after PASS v2 is sole authoritative SSL version.

S2 (ssl_split_stability_v1, 2026-08-22): frozen S0-v2 feature caches (same 6 npz files, SHA-pinned) with a fixed deterministic CPU head: StandardScaler fit on outer-train fold only + RidgeClassifier(alpha=1.0, fit_intercept, solver='cholesky', class_weight='balanced'). Generators: random = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle, random_state=seed); grouped = StratifiedGroupKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle, random_state=seed, groups=speaker). 20 prespecified draws, seed_r = uint32 of sha256('ICASSP2027|SSL_SPLIT_STABILITY_V1|DRAW|r')[:8] (e.g. draw 0 = 4121830118). Units: 2 corpora x 3 probes x 20 draws x 2 generators = 240 units; x 5 folds = 1,200 CPU fits. Per draw: Delta_cmr = speaker-equal OOF UAR(random) - speaker-equal OOF UAR(grouped). Primary series D_cr = equal-weight mean over 3 probes per draw (one 20-draw series per corpus); secondary = per-probe series, all reported, no selection. Prespecified readout: direction_stable_positive = >=18/20 positive AND empirical 5th pct > 0; direction_stable_negative symmetric; fragile = min < 0 < max; else not_conclusive. Gates: class-complete every fold train/test, grouped speaker overlap zero, OOF exactly once, fail-closed. Summaries: 20 raw values, mean, SD (ddof=1), median, IQR, min/max, linear p5/p95, sign counts, MC SE = SD/sqrt(20). Explicitly "partition-generator stability summaries, not population CIs"; no t-test headline.

S3 (SUBESCO release_v10, 2026-08-30): the S2 design transplanted to SUBESCO (Bangla). Finite population: 20 speakers x 7 emotions x 7 prompts = 980 utterances (prompts 1,2,3,6,8,9,10 of SUBESCO's 10). Same three frozen S0-v2 encoders, same final-layer time-mean prep-v2 features (torchaudio 2.10.0+cu128), same Ridge head, same 20-draw seed rule and StratifiedKFold/StratifiedGroupKFold(5) generators. 120 scientific units = 3 probes x 20 draws x 2 protocols; 600 folds. Primary = fixed equal-weight mean of the three probe deltas per draw. release_v10 adds no feature extraction, no GPU, no new units; its independent verifier performs 600 CPU audit-replay refits of the frozen 120x5 grid (verify only), a CPU metadata cache repack with bitwise X-identity assertion, a 78-case mutation battery (78/78 PASS) and 19/19 production-entry cases, then activates claim_registry.json only after verification (00:24:19) and mutation (00:24:45) PASS, registry at 00:24:56 with backward SHA pins. Outcome visibility disclosed: built after S3 outcomes were known; not preregistered. "Repetition-clean": the listed files do not define the term or the prompt-selection rule (that lives in the pinned but unlisted selected_manifest_v1.json / s3_subesco_manifest.py); the population label implies repetitions collapsed to one utterance per speaker x emotion x prompt so near-duplicate takes cannot straddle folds, and 3 of 10 prompts excluded for an unstated reason.

S4 (wavlm_layer_weighting_v1): 0 units. Per DECISION_LOG record 271 and CURRENT_EXPERIMENT_INDEX: "Permanent NO-GO because the conditional start gate was missed before the hard stop." The gate condition itself is not stated in any released doc. By its name it would have replaced WavLM's final-layer time-mean feature with a weighted combination of hidden layers.

Which are the same experiment: S3 is S2 on a different corpus (identical head, generators, seed rule, readout rules, summaries). S0 shares corpora and feature caches with S2 but differs in head (trained linear probe with early stopping vs Ridge), splits (P1 frozen 5-fold x 3-seed vs 20 fresh StratifiedKFold draws), aggregation (per-speaker paired test + bootstrap vs per-draw sign counts), and statistics (Holm/Wilcoxon vs none).

Treated as supplement/supporting evidence (primary-ledgers asset). S2: PASS; every series (2 primary + 6 secondary) is 20/20 positive, direction_stable_positive; allowed claim capped at "direction stable across 20 prespecified partition draws"; routed to at most one main-text sentence, full table in supplement. S3: release_v10 accepted (records 278-279) after nine failed/incomplete release iterations; wav2vec2, HuBERT and the equal-weight primary are direction-stable positive, WavLM-base+ is fragile (range crosses zero, q05 negative); per record 271 a compact finite-panel S3 result is routed into the paper slot formerly occupied by arm B, with full detail in the SSL supplement; forbidden to say Bengali causes the contrast, to give population CIs, or to call WavLM stable.
