limitations: All probes are base-size (~95M) encoders with frozen FINAL-layer time-mean features and no fine-tuning; claim registries explicitly forbid extrapolation to fine-tuned SSL / SOTA / modern SER.

S0 intervals are conditional whole-speaker bootstrap intervals only: they exclude split-realization and training-pipeline uncertainty; S2/S3 summaries are partition-generator stability descriptors on finite frozen corpora, not population CIs.

S0 is an outcome-visible corrective re-run of v1 (v1 failed independent verification); S3 release_v10 is an outcome-visible corrective release built after results were known. Neither is preregistered or outcome-blind, and the S3 claim spec was written after the numbers existed.

Small speaker panels: RAVDESS 24 speakers, SUBESCO 20 speakers (4 test speakers per grouped fold); SUBESCO per-draw deltas are coarse rationals (denominators 980/490/196), so single-utterance flips move a draw by ~0.1 pp.

S2/S3 use a different head (StandardScaler+Ridge, no validation/early stopping) than S0 (trained linear probe); the RAVDESS premium magnitude differs 2-5x between heads and this is not reconciled anywhere in the artifact.

S3's primary equal-weight mean folds a fragile WavLM series into two stable ones; the primary passes the >=18/20 gate at exactly 19/20 with q05 = 0.95 pp, so the headline depends on the aggregation choice. 'All draws positive' is a forbidden claim for good reason.
S0 CREMA-D WavLM: 37/91 speakers have non-positive P_RG; S0 tests are on per-speaker deltas averaged over only 3 seeds.
S3 'repetition-clean' and the exclusion of prompts 4, 5, 7 are not defined or justified in the listed files; the selection tooling is pinned but not included in the summary.
S3 historical campaign runner did not emit 'failed' ledger states or enforce the one-retry ceiling (the ledger happens to contain zero failures); only the release verifier enforces it prospectively.

S3's earlier recompute receipt (s3_closure_recompute_v1.json) stores only a match flag and one exact score per row despite declaring a three-field comparison; release_v10's own fold_audit.json is the actual 600-fold evidence.
No formal test of SSL vs from-scratch stacks; the 'attenuation' reading is descriptive only.
Grouping is by speaker only; prompt/sentence overlap across folds (SUBESCO 7 shared prompts, RAVDESS 2 sentences) is a second nonexclusivity axis that is untested.
wasted_or_low_value: S0 v1 -> v2: a full 180-unit GPU re-run whose science is declared identical to v1; all changes are provenance/pinning fixes. The reported numbers exist only because v1 failed independent verification on provenance, not on results.

S3 release_v1 through v9: nine release iterations (v3 predeclared PASS before verifier ran; v4 mutation battery stalled 61/62 on a fixture alias; v5 self-derived cache expectations; v6 misread receipt rows; v7 trusted under-validated mutation report; v8 stale 'releasev6' filename token; v9 basename gate not independently derived). Zero scientific change across all ten versions; the README devotes ~40% of its text to this history.

S3 release_v10's 600 CPU audit-replay refits and 78-case mutation battery verify existing outcomes only; they are correctly labelled non-scientific but represent substantial effort with no claim change.
S2 run_plan_derivation_note.json: a post-outcome packaging correction confirming 240/240 rows already matched the frozen plan.

S2 secondary per-probe series are informationally redundant with the S2 primary and with S0's direction result on the same features/corpora: every one of the 8 S2 series is 20/20 positive, and S0 had already rejected all six nulls with p < 0.003; the paper takes at most one sentence from S2.
Holm correction over 6 in S0 changes no decision (smallest raw p = 2.77e-3 survives unchanged); the exact-rational Wilcoxon machinery is precision beyond what the decision needs.

S2 governance forbids 'probe selection among secondary series' and 't-test headline statistics', yet the most informative feature of the S2 data, the head-dependent RAVDESS magnitude gap versus S0, is never examined.
S4 exists only as a name in three docs; no design, gate condition, or rationale is released, so its NO-GO cannot be evaluated by a reader.
dossier.contribution_to_paper_claim: The paper's controlled-study claim (protocol premium from speaker-nonexclusive splitting) rests primarily on P1 (1,620 fits, trained-from-scratch stacks) and the S1 repository audit. The SSL series is the generalization defense: S0 lets the paper say the premium is also present, though smaller (RAVDESS 2.8-6.2 pp vs the four stacks; CREMA-D 0.9-1.8 pp), with three widely used frozen SSL encoders, blocking the objection that the effect is a small-CNN artifact; it is supplement-grade, with descriptive-only SSL-vs-stack comparison. S2 contributes one main-text sentence that direction is stable across 20 partition draws. S3 is the only arm that earned a main-paper slot from this series: record 271 routes the compact SUBESCO result (primary +3.10 pp, 19/20; WavLM fragile) into the slot previously held by arm B, giving the paper its only non-English corpus and a cross-language robustness statement carefully bounded to 'finite panel, specified generator, not language-causal'. S4 contributes nothing. Dependence is moderate: removing S0/S2/S3 would not undercut the audit or P1 numbers, but would remove the 'modern representations' and 'other language' generalization sentences.
untested_gaps: Fine-tuning any encoder (partial or full) - the registries forbid extrapolating, and no fine-tuned run exists.

Larger/other encoders: WavLM-Large, HuBERT-Large, wav2vec2-XLSR/XLS-R, data2vec, Whisper encoder, emotion-specialized models (e.g. emotion2vec); all locked out by the 'no additional SSL encoders' completion judgment.

Layer selection or learned layer weighting (the S4 question): all results use the final hidden layer, which for WavLM-base+ is the layer least expected to carry paralinguistic/speaker information; whether WavLM's small (0.87 pp) and fragile (16/4) premium is a final-layer artifact is exactly what was not run.

Pooling alternatives (mean+std, attentive pooling) and head choice: S0 trained linear probe vs S2 Ridge give RAVDESS contrasts of ~4-6 pp vs ~12-15 pp on identical features; the head-dependence of the premium magnitude is unaddressed, and no run puts the Ridge head on the P1 frozen splits or the trained probe on the 20 draws.
Other languages and corpora: only Bangla (SUBESCO) beyond English acted corpora; no IEMOCAP, MSP-Podcast, EmoDB, spontaneous speech, or cross-corpus evaluation.

Effect of the repetition-clean reduction itself: the premium on the full 7,000-utterance SUBESCO (with 5 repetitions) versus the 980-utterance panel is not measured, so the contribution of near-duplicate takes to leakage is unknown.
Prompt/text nonexclusivity: grouped folds isolate speakers but not prompts; a StratifiedGroupKFold on speaker x prompt or a prompt-disjoint protocol is untested.
Why prompts 4, 5, 7 were excluded from SUBESCO and whether results depend on that selection.
Whether per-speaker P_RG is correlated across probes (same speakers driving the premium under all three encoders) - per-speaker deltas exist but no cross-probe analysis is reported.
Sensitivity to fold count / speakers per test fold (5-fold on 20 or 24 speakers gives 4-5 test speakers), and to more than 20 draws.
Formal comparison of SSL versus from-scratch premium (only descriptive 'lower').

dossier.arm: Governance history, plan, deviations, excluded work
dossier.purpose: This is not a scientific arm; it is the control layer of the program. It answers: what was the original plan and schedule, which experiments were authorized/cut and when, which hard-stop and gating rules bounded execution, what deviations occurred and why, and which of the resulting numbers are allowed into the main text versus repo/supplement. In the program logic it underwrites the paper's honesty claims (what is 'prospectively frozen' versus 'outcome-visible revised', why nothing is called 'preregistered', why A/B/C/D1 are supplement-only) and the completeness judgment that zero further experiments were scientifically defensible after 2026-08-30.
dossier.design_summary:
SOURCE SHAPE: PLAN.md is a Chinese-language, append-only author/Claude/Codex ruling file with a base plan (2026-08-15) plus 12 numbered revisions (two are both labelled '修订四'; the second, dated 2026-08-24, is really revision 13). The supplement task package (2026-08-22 07:24 UTC-4) is the S0-S4 executable contract. DEVIATION_REGISTRY records one named incident. DECISION_LOG/SUPERSESSION_MAP/SCOPE_AND_EXCLUSIONS/README are the 2026-08-30 release-time distillations.

ORIGINAL PLAN (2026-08-15, author ruling): Topic 07 chosen from 12 topics as the only one with 'no residual hard gates or quality gaps', frozen commits, file:line evidence, and a working paper toolchain (topic 04: 6 tables, 2,531 traceable facts, 42/42 regressions). Constraints: deadline 2026-09-16, 4 pages incl. figures/refs (+ optional 5th page refs-only), non-blind, 32 days. One-sentence claim: 'protocol-induced score differences can exceed model-improvement differences and have no universal discount factor'. In-list: 30-repo audit 20/30 risk (Wilson 95% CI 48.8-80.8%), P1 controlled replication 2 corpora x 4 models x 3 splits x 3 seeds = 1,620 training units, RAVDESS +15.39 to +19.68 pp vs CREMA-D +1.82 to +3.06 pp, 19/24 preregistered comparisons Holm-rejected. Compressed to a sentence: voiceprint check (Random split puts RAVDESS 24/24 and CREMA-D 91/91 actors in both train and test; Resemblyzer EER detectable, explicitly 'not proof the SER model uses it'), evidence tiers 24 tier-1 / 1 static-inference / 5 unknown; 384/384 finite-equivalence cases. Out-list (cut): P2 stratified conditional intervals and Theta scenario quantity; P0.5 process history; purposive deep sample 16/32 (footnote only, never pooled); topic 03 sampling-rate contract results; every other topic. Overflow deletion order: 3.2 items -> limitation detail -> compress methods; four untouchables: claim, 20/30, two-corpus contrast, Holm result. Milestones: M1 freeze 8/15-18; M2 figures+skeleton 8/19-25; M3 full draft 8/26-9/1; M4 independent Codex review 9/2-8; M5 finalize 9/9-13; M6 submit 9/14-15 (never on 9/16). Buffer 1-2 days; 'if a milestone slips, cut content, don't extend'. Hard constraints: no new large experiment (exception: <3 GPU-h AND reviewer-must AND author-approved); frozen results never changed ('fix the paper, not the result'); zero overclaiming; other 11 topics frozen (four pending Codex items frozen too); toolchain 04 mandatory. Reviewer questions pre-answered: 30 repos not representative (lower bound in a discoverable frame); no named papers; voiceprint use unproven.

REV 1 (2026-08-15, author): P4 multi-corpus extension added because related-work search showed 'speaker leakage inflates SER scores' is not new (cites arXiv 2304.00860; arXiv 2604.14354). Contributions re-stated: (1) prevalence 20/30 [claimed novel], (2) non-portability of premium across corpora [main]. n=2 corpora insufficient for a universal negative, hence P4. Three iron rules: queue order frozen before running (availability x cost x language diversity, result-independent); stop rule is the clock (2026-08-22), not results; every started corpus is reported (download failures, license refusals, timeouts, near-zero premiums). Four fixed steps per corpus: license check before download; download to E: only; loader with unit tests (speaker-ID uniqueness, label-map completeness, zero train/test speaker crossing); run identical frozen protocol 4 models x 3 seeds x (Random/GroupKFold/LOSO). Frozen queue with GPU estimates: 1 RAVDESS-Song ~1 h; 2 EmoDB ~0.5 h; 3 ESD (EN+ZH) ~2 h; 4 CaFE ~1 h; 5 URDU ~2 h; 6 SUBESCO ~5 h; 7 ShEMO ~15-20 h; 8 EMOVO ~0.5 h (application form). Speaker floor >=8 (SAVEE 4, TESS 2 excluded). Statistics: original 24-comparison family untouched; new corpora form a separate Holm family; RG-UAR = Random - GroupKFold UAR (pp) plus RL-UAR; no pooling, no 'what predicts premium' model. Budget: preregistered cap 200 GPU-h, P1 used 25.09 h, ~175 h left, P4 <30 h; single GPU job at a time; write PROGRESS.md after each corpus. Schedule: M1 compressed to 8/15-17; P4 8/16-22 hard stop; M2 8/18-25 with main figure changed to per-corpus premium dot-interval plot.

REV 2 (2026-08-15, Claude, from Codex PRIOR_ART_COLLISION_MATRIX of 10 papers): Collision confirmed with Ibrahim, Ghoraba & Ghoraba (Sci. Rep. 16:19584, 2026-06-25): RAVDESS 95.83% random vs 48.06 +/- 9.76% LOSO (~47.8 pt gap); CREMA-D 73.54% vs 53.12 +/- 2.65% 5-fold subject-exclusive (~20.4 pt); and Zielonka et al. Electronics 2022 (RAVDESS/CREMA-D, actor-disjoint, CNN/ResNet). The Rev-1 'non-portability' headline is void. New working title 'Speaker-Nonexclusive Evaluation in Public SER Code: A Preregistered Audit and Controlled Study of Protocol Effects'. Contribution order: (1) probability-sampled prevalence [main, still novel: none of the 10 papers did it]; (2) multilingual sensitivity [only novel with P4; SERAB (ICASSP 2022) has no random-split control]; (3) same-implementation 4-architecture 3-protocol comparison, written as an independent replication of Ibrahim/Zielonka. Five claims deleted, including 'Random-GroupKFold difference comes entirely from outer test-set speaker overlap' because the inner validation grouping also changes (found by Codex, not Claude; must go in limitations). Codex's unauthorized 5-page demo (bypassed M1 author gate) accepted as M2 starting point: 5 pages US Letter, page 5 refs-only, 102 numeric matches / 0 red / 0 uncited; workspace migrated to E:\科研\ICASSP2027\.

proposals.angle: Confirmatory minimalist: the smallest publicly preregistered, single-family program that supports the paper's four claims with clean speaker-paired inference; ~22 GPU-h (hard cap 30) on one RTX 5070.
proposals.thesis: Keep the thesis (speaker-nonexclusive evaluation is common in public SER code and inflates reported performance), but earn each half with exactly one instrument: a single preregistered probability audit with an execution-verified endpoint and a human agreement check, and a single unified outer x inner protocol factorial (RR/RG/GR/GG) run on three corpora and four representations with partition draws crossed with training seeds. Everything the frozen program routed to 'supplement/descriptive' (LOSO, D1, B, C/P5, S2 Ridge, S3 as a separate release, purposive audit, six non-speaker outcomes, lineage sensitivity branches) is cut because the dossier shows it changed no claim or was redundant with P1; the two genuinely missing pieces (outer/inner decomposition in the main family; a fine-tuned SSL pipeline) are folded in as levels of the same paired design under one 16-test Holm family.

program.name: PREREG-0: public preregistration + verifier-first synthetic dry run
program.rationale: Every arm in the dossier is labelled 'not preregistered'/'outcome-visible' because no public immutable timestamp existed and verifiers were written after scoring (A: 2 min after; B: 43 s after; C: tolerance corrected post-score; S3: ten release iterations). That governance churn consumed more effort than any experiment and demoted A (the only decomposition) and B (10.25 GPU-h) out of the paper. With hindsight the fix costs ~1.5 GPU-h: freeze every analysis script and verifier on synthetic outputs before any real fit, then publish the hash.
program.design: One repository commit containing: (i) this protocol; (ii) the frozen split generator, training engine (P1's, unchanged), probe/fine-tune configs, scorer and an independently written verifier; (iii) the audit frame-construction script, lineage predicate, endpoint dictionary and adjudication form. Dry run: synthetic audio manifest (3 fake corpora with the real speaker/class cardinalities) pushed through the full pipeline for 1 replicate x 4 cells x 5 folds x all 4 model levels plus 2 fine-tune fits; scorer and verifier must reproduce each other to 1e-12 on the synthetic outputs and pass a 20-case mutation battery (row drop, label swap, fold overlap injection, seed drift). Then: OSF registration of the protocol PDF, git tag, and the SHA-256 of the tag recorded; the NIST Randomness Beacon pulse used for the audit draw is the first pulse after the OSF timestamp. No real audio is touched before the tag.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: No scientific estimand. Gate: verifier==scorer on synthetic data and 20/20 mutation cases rejected; if the gate fails the tag is not created and the program does not start.

program.name: AUDIT-1: single preregistered probability audit of public SER code (execution-verified endpoint, boundary stratification, human agreement check)
merged_from: P0 frame construction (383-URL candidate log, E1-E8 codes)
P0.5 execution validation tier (synthetic 4,444-row manifest, 16-permutation AST-fragment execution)
S1 beacon-seeded sample and exact hypergeometric envelope
program.rationale: The audit is the paper's only non-replicated contribution (prior-art matrix: none of 10 collision papers did probability sampling), yet its headline rests on static evidence for 60 repos (44/9/7) while the stronger execution-tier evidence (P0.5, 384/384 index matches) sits on a nearly disjoint 30 (2 overlap) and is now 'historical'. The 30-pp envelope (61.9-92.0%) is driven by 7 unresolved cases and n=60; the lineage rule was chosen after outcomes and spawned D1/D3/291/282 branches that moved the bound by <=0.3 pp. No human ever coded a repo. Redesign: one frame, one preregistered lineage rule (the D2 predicate, fixed a priori so no sensitivity branches exist), one sample of up to 80, execution tier applied to every resolvable repo, endpoint split into any-boundary vs test-boundary, and a 20-repo human blind-coding kappa.
program.design: Frame: rerun the frozen P0 query families (GitHub top-100 best match x 2 query forms x 4 corpora RAVDESS/CREMA-D/IEMOCAP/EmoDB; arXiv API top-100 per corpus; snowball from included READMEs) at cutoff T0 = OSF timestamp date; union with the existing 383-URL log; canonicalize; apply the D2 lineage predicate (explicit fork; identical tree SHA; identical blob set; executable-blob containment >=0.90 with corroborator; keeper = upstream > earliest > URL order) and E1-E5 eligibility to the FULL candidate list before the draw. Sample: n = min(80, N) in order SHA256(beacon_pulse || canonical_id); sequential adjudication in that order; stop at 80 or at the 60 CPU-review-hour cap (truncated n is still a probability sample and is reported as such). Unit: one repository lineage at a pinned commit; static, no whole-repo execution. Coding (pre-verdict, outcome-masked): repo_relation (paper-linked = README/arXiv link or citation present vs other), corpus set, notebook vs script, year. Endpoint per repo: Y_any = at least one active train/validation-or-model-selection OR train/test path permits same-speaker membership on both sides; Y_test = the same restricted to train/test paths; N requires all active paths verified speaker-exclusive with closed path enumeration; U otherwise. Evidence tiers: tier-1 = byte-verified entry-to-split chain AND isolated execution of the decisive split statement(s) on the synthetic 4-corpus manifest with 16 fixed permutations, compared to an independent adapter; tier-2 = static chain only; U if neither closes within 1.5 review-hours (cap fixed a priori, not after seeing repo size). Human check: the author blind-codes the first 20 repos in beacon order using the same form before the AI verdicts are unmasked; Cohen's kappa on Y/N/U. Statistics: confirmed fraction Y/n; partial-identification interval [Y/n, (Y+U)/n]; frame-level joint >=95% envelope by two one-sided 97.5% exact hypergeometric bounds (unchanged from S1); the same three quantities for Y_test; Wilson intervals per stratum (descriptive). No sensitivity branches.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Primary estimand: the finite-frame proportion of eligible public SER repository lineages whose active pipeline permits speaker-nonexclusive membership at any train/validation or train/test boundary (K/N), reported as sample partial-identification interval and frame envelope. Preregistered directional hypothesis H_A: the confirmed fraction Y/n exceeds 0.5 (one-sided exact hypergeometric test of K/N > 0.5 using Y as the count, alpha = 0.025, unknowns counted as non-positive; this is the single test outside the controlled-study Holm family because it has a different estimand). Secondary (estimate + interval, no test): Y_test/n; kappa between human and AI coding on 20 repos with preregistered rule: kappa >= 0.60 -> AI verdicts are the primary; kappa < 0.60 -> headline reported as AI-assisted with the full disagreement table and the human-coded 20 reported alongside.

program.name: CTRL-1: unified outer x inner protocol factorial (RR/RG/GR/GG) x 3 corpora x 4 representation levels x 5 partition-draw/seed replicates
merged_from: P1 (Random/GroupKFold cells, engine, features, speaker-paired inference)
A (RG and GR cells; O_G/I_G decomposition)
S0 (frozen HuBERT/WavLM linear probes on the same splits)
program.rationale: P1 (25.09 GPU-h) spent 85% of its fits on LOSO, whose only new message (LOSO > GroupKFold in 8/8 cells) is a training-size confound not tied to the thesis, and 3 of 4 CREMA-D Random-LOSO tests did not reject. A (2.67 GPU-h) is the ONE arm that decomposes the pipeline premium the paper flags four times as a confound (RAVDESS O_G +9.99, I_G +5.13, interaction +2.15; CREMA-D O_G +1.89, I_G +0.68) but never entered the paper because its verifier was post-outcome. S0's six probe contrasts were all Holm-significant on P1's own splits, so probes belong as model levels in the same design rather than a separate 6-test family; S2's 20 Ridge draws were 20/20 positive everywhere and their RAVDESS magnitude (13.9 pp) is irreconcilable with S0's (2.8-6.2 pp) because the head differs, so one head is fixed and draws are crossed with seeds inside the main design. S3 is S2 on SUBESCO and is folded in as a corpus level under the full protocol, giving the paper its only non-English corpus with the same four representations (never done: the frozen program tested SUBESCO only with Ridge probes and with the allocation design). Transformer and FNO added no sign or decision beyond CNN/ResNet-SE in any of the 24 P1 tests and are cut. One replicate = one partition draw + one training seed, so the reported replicate SD covers both sources S0's bootstrap excluded.
program.design: Corpora (in hand): RAVDESS speech (1,440 utt, 24 spk, 8 classes; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); CREMA-D (7,442 utt, 91 spk, 6 classes; ODbL 1.0/DbCL 1.0); SUBESCO as released (7,000 utt, 20 spk, 7 emotions, 10 sentences x 5 takes; CC BY 4.0) because the estimand is the premium a practitioner using the corpus as released would obtain. Preregistered hygiene (applied before any fit, no sensitivity runs): drop files with zero-variance audio (CREMA-D 1076_MTI_SAD_XX); collapse exact-byte duplicate groups to one file (RAVDESS 1 pair, CREMA-D 3 groups; label conflicts -> drop the group); log counts. Features: P1 log-mel contract unchanged (22.05 kHz, 30 dB trim, 64 mel, n_fft 1024, hop 512, 128 frames, per-utterance z-score, train-only SpecAugment) for scratch models; frozen torchaudio HUBERT_BASE and WAVLM_BASE_PLUS final-layer time-mean 768-d features (16 kHz, 30 dB trim) cached once with pinned weight SHAs (extraction ~1 GPU-h). Model levels (4): CNN and ResNet-SE at P1 frozen configs; linear probe 768->C for HuBERT-base and WavLM-base+. Engine (all levels): class-balanced CE, AdamW (lr 1e-3, wd 1e-4), batch 64, <=100 epochs, cosine T_max 100, early stop patience 15 on inner-validation weighted CE, strict-min checkpoint, deterministic, float32. Replicates r = 1..5: seed_r = first 32 bits of SHA256('SER-ONESHOT|draw|r'). Outer folds per r: Random = StratifiedKFold(5, shuffle, random_state=seed_r) ignoring speaker; Grouped = StratifiedGroupKFold(5, shuffle, random_state=seed_r, groups=speaker) with zero-overlap assertion. Inner (25% of outer train) per r: random = stratified train_test_split(seed_r); grouped = GroupShuffleSplit(0.25, seed_r) by speaker. Cells: RR, RG, GR, GG (outer letter first). Training RNG key = SHA256('SER-ONESHOT-train|corpus|fold|r') WITHOUT protocol tokens, so all four cells of a (corpus, fold, r) share initialization and batch-order streams (removes the 'protocol-specific seed streams' caveat A carried). Fits: 3 corpora x 2 scratch models x 4 cells x 5 folds x 5 r = 600 scratch fits (~10 GPU-h at the P1-measured ~0.015 s per training utterance per fit) + 600 probe units (~1 GPU-h). Fixed run order corpus -> model -> r -> fold -> cell; one retry only for failures before outer-test access; a missing outer fold voids the (corpus, model, cell, r) cell and its dependent contrasts (p=1 placeholders keep the family size). Outputs per fit: predictions.csv with all logits for every OOF utterance, history, config, hashes. Per-speaker OOF UAR is computed on each speaker's own utterances for each (corpus, model, cell, r); accuracy and macro-F1 are computed, released in the repository, and receive no inference and no text.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: All estimands are speaker-paired UAR differences (unit = speaker; n = 24 / 91 / 20), averaged within speaker over the 5 replicates and over the model levels named, with 10,000-replicate whole-speaker percentile bootstrap 95% CIs (seed fixed) and two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (zero_method='wilcox'). Per corpus c in {RAVDESS, CREMA-D, SUBESCO}: (1) Delta_pipe^scratch(c) = mean over CNN, ResNet-SE of [UAR(RR) - UAR(GG)] > 0; (2) Delta_pipe^probe(c) = mean over HuBERT, WavLM probes of [UAR(RR) - UAR(GG)] > 0; (3) Delta_outer(c) = mean over all 4 levels of [UAR(RG) - UAR(GG)] > 0; (4) Delta_inner(c) = mean over all 4 levels of [UAR(GR) - UAR(GG)] > 0. Corpus dependence (replication of the direction reported by Ibrahim et al. 2026 and Zielonka et al. 2022, so it is a legitimate a priori hypothesis): (5) Delta_pipe^all(RAVDESS) - Delta_pipe^all(CREMA-D) > 0, two-sample Mann-Whitney U on the speaker-level pipeline deltas (24 vs 91) with a two-sample speaker bootstrap CI for the difference. These 12 + 1 tests plus the 3 CTRL-2 tests form the single 16-test Holm family (alpha 0.05). Secondary estimates with CIs but no tests: per-model-level cells (12 corpus x level pipeline deltas), the interaction (RR - RG) - (GR - GG) per corpus, SUBESCO-vs-others differences, replicate-level sign counts (x/5) and SD for every contrast.

program.name: CTRL-2: partially fine-tuned WavLM-base+ pipeline contrast (RR vs GG) on 3 corpora
program.rationale: The audit frame is dominated by code that fine-tunes or trains pretrained encoders, but every controlled number in the paper comes from small from-scratch models (RAVDESS grouped UAR only 39-46%) or frozen probes whose RAVDESS premium shrank to 2.8-6.2 pp; the claim registries explicitly forbid extrapolation to fine-tuned models and the NO-GO list barred 'full fine-tuning'. A reviewer's obvious objection is that the premium vanishes under the pipelines people actually run. One representation level, two cells, one replicate on shared splits answers this at ~8 GPU-h within the 12 GB budget and adds exactly three tests to the family.
program.design: Encoder: WavLM-base+ (pinned weights); unfreeze the top 4 transformer layers and a mean-pool + linear head; the rest frozen. fp16 autocast, batch 16, random 3 s crops for training and full utterance at evaluation, AdamW (encoder lr 5e-5, head lr 1e-3, wd 1e-2), <=15 epochs, early stop patience 3 on inner-validation weighted CE, strict-min checkpoint, gradient checkpointing off (fits in 12 GB at 3 s x 16). Splits: replicate r=1 outer/inner partitions from CTRL-1, cells RR and GG only (inner mirrors outer, as in P1), so the fine-tuned model is directly speaker-paired with the other four levels on identical folds. Fits: 3 corpora x 2 cells x 5 folds = 30 (estimated 1.5 h RAVDESS, 3.5 h CREMA-D, 3 h SUBESCO). Hard cap 12 GPU-h checked at fold boundaries; if hit, the remaining corpus is reported incomplete and its test enters the family as p=1 (no design shrinkage). Determinism is not guaranteed under fp16; seeds recorded and disclosed. Outputs identical in schema to CTRL-1.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Per corpus: Delta_pipe^ft(c) = speaker-mean of [UAR(RR) - UAR(GG)] for the fine-tuned WavLM level (r=1) > 0; two-sided Wilcoxon on speaker-level differences (n = 24/91/20) and 10,000-replicate whole-speaker bootstrap CI. Three tests, members of the 16-test Holm family. Secondary estimate (no test): Delta_pipe^ft(c) minus Delta_pipe^probe(c) with speaker-paired CI, i.e. whether fine-tuning widens or narrows the premium relative to the frozen probe on the same speakers.

program.name: STAT-1: one-shot scoring under a single 16-test Holm family + independent verifier replay
program.rationale: The frozen program ran separate multiplicity families (P1 24, S0 6, A 4) and descriptive readouts (S2/S3 sign counts, B t-intervals, C SESOI classes) with routing decided after outcomes (Rev 10 B-for-D1, record 271 S3-for-B). One family, one scorer, one verifier frozen in PREREG-0, and a fixed routing rule (every family result and the audit envelope enter the main text regardless of direction) remove the outcome-visible editorial layer that generated most of the dossier's governance churn.
program.design: Executed once after CTRL-1, CTRL-2 and AUDIT-1 ledgers are locked and hashed. Inputs: run plan, manifests, split files, all predictions.csv, audit adjudication CSV. Scorer produces: per-speaker cell table, the 16 family contrasts with CIs, Holm-adjusted p, replicate sign counts, secondary estimates, audit fractions/intervals/envelope, kappa. Verifier (independent code path, no shared modules, frozen in PREREG-0) reproduces every reported number to 1e-12 from raw predictions; any mismatch is reported as-is, never patched post hoc. Main-text routing fixed a priori: one table (3 corpora x 4 contrasts + fine-tune row), one two-panel figure (Panel A audit composition + intervals; Panel B forest of the 16 contrasts), one audit paragraph, one limitations list (already drafted with blanks).
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: No new estimand; implements Holm over the 16 controlled-study tests and the single audit test. Gate: verifier replay exact; otherwise the discrepancy itself is reported.

program.name: LOSO protocol arm (P1: 1,380 of 1,620 fits)
program.rationale: 85% of P1's fits and most of its 25 GPU-h. Its content: Random-LOSO on CREMA-D was non-significant for 3 of 4 models (FNO LOSO 53.86 > Random 53.37), and GroupKFold-LOSO was negative in 8/8 cells because LOSO trains on 23/24 or 90/91 speakers versus 19-20/24 or 72-73/91, a training-size confound the preregistration did not anticipate. Neither fact bears on the thesis (Random vs speaker-exclusive); the thesis needs one speaker-exclusive comparator, and 5-fold StratifiedGroupKFold is the cheaper, less confounded one.
program.design: Not run. The paper states explicitly that LOSO was not compared and cites the P1 archive for the LOSO > GroupKFold observation.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

program.name: Transformer and FNO model levels (P1/A/D1/B)
program.rationale: Across P1's 24 tests, A's per-model strata and D1, Transformer and FNO never changed a sign or a Holm decision relative to CNN/ResNet-SE (P1 RG premia: RAVDESS 16.34/15.39 vs 17.71/19.68; CREMA-D 3.06/1.82 vs 2.80/2.46). FNO is an atypical SER architecture that needed a justification sentence. Two from-scratch levels plus two SSL levels plus one fine-tuned level give five representations, which is more representation diversity than P1's four convolution/attention variants at half the fit count.
program.design: Not run.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

program.name: P0 purposive 32-repo audit, six non-speaker outcomes, purposive-vs-random comparison, and D1/D3/291/N282 lineage sensitivity branches
program.rationale: The purposive audit (32 x 38 fields, full cross-review) produced only a 'working-model diagnostic' with nothing surviving Holm and appears in no paper lineage. The six other outcomes (normalization leakage 10.0%, test-set selection 36.7%, augmentation 20.0%, single split 83.3%, no variance 83.3%) were coded, cross-reviewed and never used. The four lineage branches all yield 44/9/7 with envelopes within 0.3 pp, so they inform nothing once the lineage rule is preregistered. All are zero-GPU but they consumed the review hours that AUDIT-1 now spends on execution tiers and human coding.
program.design: Not run. AUDIT-1 codes only the speaker endpoint (any/test boundary) plus four pre-verdict strata.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

program.name: D1 RAVDESS speech-song matched panel (792 fits)
program.rationale: 70% of its fits were LOSO for a secondary endpoint that was not conclusive for all four models; the speech half re-ran P1 on a 23-actor / 6-class subset; the channel difference (-1 to -6 pp, CNN not conclusive) supports no claim and was removed from the manuscript by Rev 10. Vocal channel is not a moderator the thesis needs.
program.design: Not run.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

program.name: B SUBESCO speaker-concentration allocation diagnostic (2,880 fits, 10.25 GPU-h)
program.rationale: Largest compute item in the frozen program, yet its design binds speaker count to repeat density under a fixed budget (cannot say which drives the premium), uses one seed per block, and was barred from explaining the RAVDESS-CREMA-D gap; it ended as a routing sentence. Its most interpretable observation (c20r1 -> c20r2 triples the premium) was not a registered endpoint. CTRL-1 uses SUBESCO as released (all 5 takes), so the practice-relevant premium on that corpus is measured directly instead.
program.design: Not run.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

program.name: C/P5 cross-prompt target-actor exposure substitution (144 fits + salvage)
program.rationale: A mechanism pilot frozen at G0 as 'at most one sentence' with no CI or p-value by construction (dependent pairs sharing 22 base/validation actors), delivered delta_panel = +4.57 pp below its own 5 pp threshold after a key-exposure incident, three errata and a review waiver. It supports no claim the paper makes and cannot by design. The mechanism question stays out of a confirmatory minimalist paper.
program.design: Not run.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

program.name: S2 Ridge-head split-stability draws and S3 as a separate SUBESCO release; S4 WavLM layer weighting
program.rationale: S2's eight series were 20/20 positive everywhere, duplicating S0's six rejections on the same features, and introduced an unexplained head-dependent magnitude (RAVDESS 13.9 pp Ridge vs 2.8-6.2 pp trained probe); S3 was S2 transplanted to SUBESCO and went through ten release builds with zero scientific change. Both are absorbed by CTRL-1 (one head, draws crossed with seeds, SUBESCO as a corpus level). S4 never ran and its gate condition was never published; the layer question is out of scope for the claims and is replaced by CTRL-2, which tests the practice-relevant regime (fine-tuning) rather than a pooling variant.
program.design: Not run.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

program.name: P4 multi-corpus queue (EmoDB, ESD, CaFE, URDU, ShEMO, EMOVO) and licensed corpora (IEMOCAP, MSP-Podcast)
program.rationale: Rev 1/2 promised a multilingual contribution and delivered none of the eight corpora under the P1 protocol. With hindsight the minimalist program takes exactly one non-English corpus already in hand (SUBESCO, CC BY 4.0) into the main factorial and stops. EmoDB (10 speakers, 535 utterances) gives 2-speaker test folds and ~7 utterances per class per speaker, too coarse for speaker-paired inference; ESD (10 EN + 10 ZH speakers, 5 emotions, 350 parallel utterances each) is research-only and requires a signed license emailed to the authors (https://hltsingapore.github.io/ESD/download.html, https://github.com/HLTSingapore/Emotional-Speech-Data); IEMOCAP (10 speakers) requires a USC agreement; MSP-Podcast requires an institution-signed FDP data-transfer agreement and its test sets have known speaker overlap (https://lab-msp.com/MSP/MSP-Podcast.html). TESS (2) and SAVEE (4), EmoV-DB (4-5), EMOVO (6), CASIA (4, not openly distributed) fall below any usable speaker floor; MELD speaker labels are TV characters and its audio licensing is unclear. Any of these would add family tests, license latency and a new loader to a one-shot run without changing the thesis; the paper states the acted-corpus limitation instead.
program.design: Not run. Limitations paragraph names the licensed spontaneous corpora as the natural next study.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

pipeline_order: PREREG-0: freeze code, scorer, verifier; synthetic dry run and mutation battery; OSF registration + git tag; record NIST beacon pulse

AUDIT-1 (CPU, runs in parallel with all GPU steps): frame rebuild at T0 -> D2 lineage predicate + E1-E5 eligibility on the full candidate list -> beacon-ordered draw -> author blind-codes first 20 -> sequential AI adjudication with execution tier to n=80 or 60 review-hours
Data hygiene + manifests for RAVDESS, CREMA-D, SUBESCO (hash-pinned); log-mel cache; HuBERT-base and WavLM-base+ feature extraction (~1 GPU-h)
CTRL-1 scratch fits: corpus -> model -> replicate -> fold -> cell (600 fits, ~10 GPU-h)
CTRL-1 probe units on cached features (600 units, ~1 GPU-h)
CTRL-2 WavLM partial fine-tuning, r=1 splits, RR/GG x 5 folds x 3 corpora (30 fits, ~8 GPU-h, cap 12)
Ledger lock and hash of all predictions and the audit adjudication CSV
STAT-1 one-shot scoring (16-test Holm family + audit test) and independent verifier replay
Manuscript fill-in under the pre-fixed routing rule; release of code, predictions, audit receipts
proposals.preregistration_notes: Registered before any real fit or adjudication, with an OSF timestamp and a git tag hash: (1) the exact 16-test family (12 corpus x contrast tests, 1 corpus-difference test, 3 fine-tune tests) and the single audit test; Holm at alpha 0.05 within the family; missing tests enter as p=1 with the family size unchanged. (2) All directional hypotheses point to positive premia and to RAVDESS > CREMA-D; the latter is registered as a replication of a published direction (Ibrahim et al. 2026; Zielonka et al. 2022), not derived from this program's data. (3) Unit of inference = speaker; per-speaker OOF UAR; averaging over replicates and named model levels precedes differencing; whole-speaker percentile bootstrap (10,000, fixed seed) and two-sided Wilcoxon; replicate sign counts and SD are descriptors, never tests. (4) Hygiene exclusions (zero-variance audio, exact-byte duplicate groups) are fixed here and produce no sensitivity runs. (5) No LOSO, no accuracy/macro-F1 inference, no per-model-level tests, no post-hoc heads, no additional encoders, no additional corpora, no dose-response or mechanism arms; the interaction (RR-RG)-(GR-GG), the per-level cells and the SUBESCO comparisons are estimates with CIs and no tests. (6) Audit: lineage predicate, eligibility codes, endpoint dictionary (Y_any primary, Y_test secondary), tier definitions, 1.5 review-hour per-repo cap, 60-hour total cap, n = min(80, N), kappa rule (>=0.60 -> AI verdicts primary) are all fixed; no sensitivity branches will be computed. (7) Stop rules: program GPU cap 30 h; CTRL-2 cap 12 h; a cap hit yields an 'incomplete' arm reported with p=1 placeholders, never a shrunken design. (8) Routing is fixed: every family contrast and the audit intervals appear in the main table/figure regardless of sign or significance; forbidden claims are listed now (no prevalence x effect multiplication, no universal correction factor, no 'speaker identity alone', no extrapolation beyond the five representation levels, no language-causal statement for SUBESCO). (9) The verifier is frozen before outcomes; any scorer/verifier disagreement after the real run is reported verbatim and not corrected.
risks: CTRL-2 time/VRAM overrun: the ~8 GPU-h estimate for partial fine-tuning is extrapolated, not measured; the 12-h cap and p=1 placeholders protect the family but could leave the fine-tune row incomplete for one corpus.

Audit unresolved rate: if the execution tier cannot close many notebooks or external-data repos, U may stay near 10% and the frame envelope will remain ~25 pp wide even at n=80; the partial-identification interval is still valid but the headline stays imprecise.
Human-AI kappa on 20 repos may fall below 0.60, which by the preregistered rule demotes the AI verdicts to 'AI-assisted'; this is a feature, but it weakens the prevalence headline.

SUBESCO as released contains 5 takes per speaker x emotion x sentence; the Random-split premium there bundles same-speaker leakage with near-duplicate-take leakage (B showed repeats roughly triple the premium). The estimand is stated as 'as-released practice premium' and must not be read as a speaker-only effect.

Only 20 speakers on SUBESCO and 24 on RAVDESS: Wilcoxon power is adequate for premia of the size seen (15-20 pp; 3-6 pp for probes) but a CREMA-D-sized probe premium (~1 pp) on SUBESCO could fail to reject after Holm; that outcome is reported as such.

The WavLM-base+ probe premium on CREMA-D was 0.87 pp (S0); the probe-level contrast averages HuBERT and WavLM, so a small WavLM effect is not tested alone and the paper must not claim WavLM-specific stability.
Dropping LOSO forfeits any statement about LOSO practice; readers who equate 'speaker-independent' with LOSO get only 5-fold StratifiedGroupKFold.

Prior-art collision persists: the protocol effect is a replication; the novelty rests on the audit plus decomposition; if Ibrahim et al. or others publish an audit before submission the contribution shrinks to the execution-verified endpoint and the outer/inner decomposition.

Corpus-difference test compares different speaker populations (24 vs 91); it estimates corpus dependence, not its cause; speaker count, sentence count, class count and recording design remain confounded and the paper must say so.
Deterministic execution is not guaranteed for fp16 fine-tuning; exact replay of CTRL-2 by others may differ at the third decimal.
Frame rebuild at a new cutoff changes N relative to the 286 lineages; results are not directly poolable with the frozen program's 44/60 and must not be presented as an update of it.
resulting_paper_claims: In a preregistered probability sample of up to 80 lineages from a frozen frame of public GitHub/arXiv SER implementations evaluating on RAVDESS, CREMA-D, IEMOCAP or EmoDB, the confirmed fraction with an active speaker-nonexclusive train/validation or train/test boundary exceeds one half (exact test), with a partial-identification interval, a frame-level >=95% envelope, the test-boundary-only fraction, and human-AI agreement (kappa on 20 repos) reported.

Under identical implementation, features, seeds and partitions, speaker-nonexclusive splitting at both boundaries (RR vs GG) inflates UAR on RAVDESS, CREMA-D and SUBESCO for from-scratch models (CNN, ResNet-SE) and for frozen HuBERT-base/WavLM-base+ linear probes, with speaker-paired CIs and Holm-adjusted tests in a single 16-test family.

The pipeline premium decomposes into a positive outer-test component (RG-GG) and a positive inner model-selection component (GR-GG) on each corpus, with the interaction reported as an estimate; the paper states which component dominates per corpus instead of flagging the confound.

The premium is corpus-dependent: RAVDESS exceeds CREMA-D by a tested, speaker-bootstrapped margin; SUBESCO is placed on the same scale with CIs and no causal attribution to language, speaker count or repetition structure.

The premium persists (or does not, reported either way) under a partially fine-tuned WavLM-base+ pipeline on the same speaker-paired folds, and its magnitude relative to the frozen-probe premium is reported with a paired CI.

Operational recommendation, argued from claims 1-3 jointly: enforce speaker exclusivity at every active boundary including inner validation, and publish grouping information; no prevalence x effect multiplication, no universal correction factor.

proposals.angle: Reviewer-proof generality: close the four standard attacks (two English acted corpora; handcrafted-feature toy models; frozen probes instead of fine-tuning; no dose-response and no tie to real public repositories) with a single multi-corpus, multi-regime panel plus mechanism arms, while cutting the 70% of past compute that was redundant (LOSO, three of four from-scratch architectures, speech-song, purposive audit, duplicated SSL supplements).
proposals.thesis: Speaker-nonexclusive evaluation is both common in public SER code and materially inflating, and the inflation is not an artifact of small models, English, acted speech, or one partition: the same speaker-paired Random-minus-Grouped premium is measured on one frozen partition set across 7-9 corpora (5-7 languages, acted and spontaneous) and three representation regimes (log-mel CNN, frozen large SSL/emotion-specialised probes with practice-typical layer/head selection, full fine-tuning of WavLM-base+). The magnitude is shown to be a monotone function of the fraction of test-speaker speech seen in training and of corpus structure (speakers, utterances per speaker, repeated takes), and it is tied to practice by replaying the splits that audited public repositories actually produce. The audit is redone once, with a pre-outcome frame rule, public timestamp, human double coding, and a test-boundary vs validation-boundary distinction.

program.name: AUD: probability audit v2 (frame + sample + adjudication + execution tier + human kappa)
program.rationale: S1 D2 is the paper's only distinctive contribution but it is labelled outcome-visible/exploratory, has a 30-pp envelope, no human reliability, no test-vs-validation boundary split, and no link to reported numbers; P0.5's execution tier (the tree's strongest evidence) covers a nearly disjoint 30 repos and is unused. All five sensitivity branches (D1/D2/D3/291/282) moved the envelope by <=0.3 pp, so the dedup rule can be fixed a priori at no risk. P0 purposive (32 repos x 38 fields) and six of seven P0 outcomes never reached any paper lineage: cut. Doing the audit once, larger, with the rule and endpoint hierarchy frozen before the draw, converts it from exploratory to confirmatory.
program.design: Frame: GitHub repo search + arXiv API + Semantic Scholar (retry with backoff) + Papers with Code if reachable, for 6 target corpora (RAVDESS, CREMA-D, IEMOCAP, EmoDB, MSP-Podcast, SUBESCO), two query families each, top-100 best-match, snowball one hop; canonical URL dedup plus the D2 executable-blob containment rule (>=0.90 + corroborator) FIXED in the preregistration before any repo is opened. Eligibility E1-E8 as before. Sample: n=100 by NIST beacon-seeded SHA order (pulse time named in the registration), sequential screening to 100 eligible. Endpoint hierarchy per repo (static, byte-hashed evidence at pinned commit): Y_test (an active train/test path permits same-speaker on both sides), Y_val (only a train/validation or model-selection path does), N (all active paths verified speaker-exclusive, enumeration closed), U (unresolved; reasons coded). Recorded stratifiers: paper-linked (arXiv/DOI in README) vs not, corpus, year, feature/model family, reported metric on target corpus. Execution tier: for repos whose split statement is AST-isolable, execute it on the real corpus manifest (not synthetic) and record realized train/test speaker-overlap fraction and test size; these realized splits feed REPLAY. Human double coding: author codes 25 beacon-selected repos blind to AI verdict; Cohen's kappa on Y/N/U and on Y_test. Adjudication: two independent AI passes with different prompts + author tie-break; 2 CPU-h cap per unknown. No purposive sample. Registration on OSF with protocol hash; git commit hash of tooling in the registration.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Primary: proportion of frame lineages with Y_test (test-boundary risk). Point = Y_test/n; partial-identification [Y_test/n, (Y_test+U)/n]; frame envelope = Bonferroni-combined two one-sided 97.5% exact hypergeometric bounds (joint >=95%). H1: lower confirmed bound > 50% (one-sided exact binomial on Y_test/n vs 0.5, alpha 0.05). Secondary (descriptive, prespecified): Y_test+Y_val prevalence; prevalence by paper-linked vs not (Newcombe CI on difference); kappa (human vs AI) with 95% CI; among paper-linked repos reporting accuracy on the same corpus, Mann-Whitney of reported accuracy Y_test vs N (descriptive, n expected <20).

program.name: DATA: corpus panel, hygiene, subsampling, shared partition-draw set
program.rationale: The multilingual/spontaneous contribution promised in Rev 1-2 was abandoned; only two acted English corpora reached the controlled study. Every downstream arm must evaluate on identical speaker-paired partitions so that regime comparisons are paired at speaker level; P1 (one split), S0 (P1 split), S2 (20 fresh draws) could not be reconciled precisely because they used different partitions. One frozen draw set per corpus, shared by all regimes, removes that ambiguity and makes the S0-vs-S2 head disagreement testable.
program.design: Corpora (speaker floor >=10; licensing stated): in hand: RAVDESS speech (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; 24 spk, 8 cls, 1,440), CREMA-D (ODbL; 91 spk, 6 cls, 7,442), SUBESCO (Bangla, Zenodo CC BY 4.0; 20 spk, 7 cls, 7,000 full). Free download: EmoDB (German; 10 spk, 7 cls, 535; no formal license, academic use customary), ShEMO (Persian; 87 spk, 6 cls, 3,000 semi-natural radio-play speech; free for academic use per authors), ESD-EN and ESD-ZH (10 spk each, 5 cls; requires the ESD license form emailed to NUS, non-commercial research only; hash-selected 50 utt per speaker x emotion = 2,500 per language). License-gated (request on day 0; included only if received by day 14, else reported 'not obtained'): IEMOCAP (USC academic license; 10 spk, 4-class neu/hap+exc/ang/sad, 5,531), MSP-Podcast v1.11+ (UTD academic license; speaker IDs for most segments; hash-selected panel of 300 speakers with >=20 segments in A/H/N/S, 20 each = 6,000 spontaneous segments). Excluded with reason: TESS (2 spk), SAVEE (4), EMOVO (6), CaFE (12, redundant with EmoDB role), MELD (speaker labels incomplete). Hygiene (preregistered, differs from P1): exact byte-duplicates collapsed to one, all-zero files removed, stereo downmixed, label-conflicting duplicates removed; manifests SHA-256 hashed. Partition-draw set: for each corpus, draws r=0..9 with seed = uint32(sha256('SER-PANEL|corpus|draw|r')); Random = StratifiedKFold(5, shuffle) by emotion; Grouped = StratifiedGroupKFold(5, groups=speaker); inner validation (where a regime uses one) = 25% of outer train, ungrouped under Random, grouped under Grouped, fixed sizes. Draw 0 is the 'anchor draw' used by every regime; draws 1-9 by cheap regimes only. Cross-corpus 4-class map (angry/happy/neutral/sad) fixed here.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: No hypothesis; validity gates: zero train/test speaker overlap in every Grouped fold (hard fail), every class present in every fold, OOF exactly once per draw. Reports panel descriptors used as moderators later: n_speakers, mean utterances/speaker, repeated-text density (share of utterances sharing speaker x text x emotion with another utterance), acted vs spontaneous.

program.name: FEAT: frozen feature extraction, 5 encoders x all layers x all corpora
program.rationale: S0 used only three base encoders and only the final layer (the layer least expected to carry paralinguistic cues in WavLM), which is exactly the reviewer objection ('base models, final layer, no emotion-specialised encoder') and the S4 question that was never answered. Extracting every hidden layer once makes layer policy a free CPU factor. wav2vec2-base and HuBERT-base are dropped: S0/S2 show them tracking WavLM-base+ in direction, and they add nothing a reviewer asks for.
program.design: Encoders (pinned weights, SHA recorded): WavLM-base+ (continuity anchor), WavLM-Large, HuBERT-Large, Whisper-medium encoder (Apache-2.0), emotion2vec+ large (FunASR model-license; research use; stated in paper). 16 kHz mono, trim 30 dB, cap 10 s, fp16 forward, time-mean of every transformer layer stored as float16 [n_layers x d] per utterance plus final-layer mean+std. Cache key includes encoder SHA, layer, pooling, sr, trim, manifest SHA. ~36k utterances total.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None (infrastructure). Gate: 1% re-extraction bitwise identical.

program.name: PROBE: frozen-representation panel with practice-typical layer and head selection
merged_from: LOSO/GroupKFold fold-count contrast from P1 (as CPU sensitivity)
program.rationale: S0, S2 and S3 answer the same question (does the premium survive frozen SSL features) three times on overlapping corpora with different heads and partitions, and produced an unexplained 2-5x disagreement on RAVDESS (S0 trained linear probe 2.8-6.2 pp vs S2 Ridge 13.9 pp). One arm on shared draws with head and layer as explicit factors resolves that, extends to 9 corpora and 5 encoders including large and emotion-specialised models, and replaces S4. LOSO-vs-GroupKFold (85% of P1 compute) is reduced to a CPU fold-count sensitivity because Delta_GL was a training-size effect, not a leakage effect.
program.design: Corpora: all obtained. Encoders: 5 (FEAT). Layer policy: L-final; L-sel = layer chosen by inner CV that mirrors the outer protocol (grouped inner under Grouped, ungrouped under Random), i.e. selection is part of the pipeline under test. Heads: H-ridge (StandardScaler on outer-train + RidgeClassifier alpha=1, balanced; S2's head), H-logreg (L2 logistic, C in {0.01,0.1,1,10} by the same mirrored inner CV), H-esp (S0's early-stopped linear probe, AdamW, patience 15; run on GPU in batches). Draws 0-9, protocols Random/Grouped, 5 folds. Primary pipeline (fixed a priori): WavLM-Large + L-sel + H-logreg. All other cells are sensitivity, reported in full. Fold-count sensitivity on primary pipeline: Grouped with k in {5, 10, LOSO} (CPU). Per-speaker OOF UAR per draw; speaker-paired Delta_RG per draw; average over draws for the confirmatory test; draw SD reported.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Delta_RG(corpus) = mean over speakers of [UAR_Random - UAR_Grouped] (primary pipeline, mean over 10 draws). H1: Delta_RG > 0 in every obtained corpus; per-corpus two-sided Wilcoxon on speaker deltas + 10,000-rep whole-speaker bootstrap CI, Holm within the PROBE family (n_corpora tests); panel-level H1: exact binomial on the number of corpora with positive point estimate (all-positive; p=2^-k). H2 (head disagreement, two-sided): on RAVDESS, Delta_RG(H-ridge) != Delta_RG(H-esp) on identical draws; Wilcoxon on per-speaker difference-of-differences. H3: Delta_RG(L-sel) >= Delta_RG(L-final) in the majority of corpus x encoder cells (sign test), i.e. practice-typical layer selection does not shrink the premium. H4 (fold count): Delta_RG(k=5) - Delta_RG(LOSO) has no consistent sign across corpora (equivalence framing: |difference| < 2 pp in >= 2/3 of corpora).

program.name: SCRATCH: from-scratch log-mel CNN panel (the public-code-typical regime)
program.rationale: P1's four architectures agreed in direction and within 4 pp in magnitude on both corpora; ResNet-SE/Transformer/FNO tripled the cost without changing any claim, and LOSO consumed 85% of fits. The audit shows most public code is a small from-scratch model on handcrafted features, so this regime must stay, but one architecture across nine corpora is worth far more to a reviewer than four architectures on two. Accuracy/macro-F1 become supplement-descriptive only (P1 showed them tracking UAR sign-for-sign).
program.design: P1 CNN (width 48, 3 blocks, k=5, dropout 0.1), P1 log-mel front-end (22.05 kHz, 64 mel, 128 frames, per-utterance z-score, train-only SpecAugment), AdamW 1e-3, batch 64, <=100 epochs, patience 15 on mirrored inner validation, deterministic. All obtained corpora (class count per corpus), protocols Random/Grouped, 5 folds, draws 0-2 with seed = draw (3 replicates per corpus); RAVDESS and CREMA-D additionally seeds 1-2 on each of draws 0-2 (for a draw-vs-seed variance decomposition). ~270 + 120 = 390 fits at ~40-60 s each (P1 average was 56 s including LOSO fits).
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Delta_RG(corpus) speaker-paired, averaged over replicates. H1: Delta_RG > 0 in every corpus (Wilcoxon + whole-speaker bootstrap, Holm within SCRATCH family). H2 (regime contrast, paired on draw 0): Delta_RG(SCRATCH) > Delta_RG(PROBE primary) in the majority of corpora (sign test over corpora; per-corpus Wilcoxon on speaker-level difference-of-differences), replicating the S0<P1 observation as a preregistered claim. Variance decomposition (descriptive): draw SD vs seed SD on the two anchors.

program.name: FT: full fine-tuning of WavLM-base+ across the panel
program.rationale: The single most damaging reviewer line is 'nobody trains log-mel CNNs or frozen probes any more; modern SER fine-tunes a pretrained encoder'. No arm in the program touched fine-tuning; the claim registries explicitly forbid extrapolating to it. On a 12 GB consumer GPU, WavLM-base+ full fine-tuning at fp16, batch 8x2, 4 s crops is feasible at roughly 2 GPU-min per 1,000 training utterances per fit, so a 2-protocol x 5-fold x 3-seed design across the panel costs ~31 GPU-h — the largest line item, and the one that converts the paper from 'toy models' to 'the regime practitioners use'.
program.design: WavLM-base+ (95M), CNN feature encoder frozen, transformer fully trainable, mean-pool + linear head; AdamW, lr 5e-5 encoder / 1e-3 head, 10% warmup, fp16 autocast, batch 8 x grad-accum 2, random 4.0 s crop in training, full utterance (cap 10 s) at eval, <=12 epochs, early stop patience 3 on mirrored inner validation (ungrouped under Random, grouped under Grouped), 3 seeds, anchor draw 0 only (so speaker pairing with PROBE and SCRATCH is exact). Corpora in fixed order: RAVDESS (1.5 h), CREMA-D (6), SUBESCO (7), EmoDB (0.5), ESD-EN (2.5), ESD-ZH (2.5), ShEMO (3), then IEMOCAP (3.7, 2 seeds) and MSP-Podcast panel (4, 2 seeds) if obtained. Checkpoints of Grouped folds retained for XCORP. Validity anchor (not a hypothesis): Grouped UAR on IEMOCAP 4-class within 60-72%, the literature range for session-independent WavLM-base fine-tuning; a miss triggers an implementation audit, not exclusion.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Delta_RG_FT(corpus) speaker-paired on draw 0, mean over seeds. H1: Delta_RG_FT > 0 in every obtained corpus (Wilcoxon + whole-speaker bootstrap; Holm within the FT family). H2 (paired with PROBE primary on identical partitions): Delta_RG_FT >= Delta_RG_PROBE in the majority of corpora (sign test), directional prior that end-to-end training absorbs more speaker information than a frozen probe. H3 (descriptive, prespecified): random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian-Laird, corpus as unit) of Delta_RG_FT with I^2; heterogeneity expected to be high; meta-regression on n_speakers, utterances/speaker, repeated-text density, acted/spontaneous is descriptive only (k<=9).

program.name: FACT: outer x inner 2x2 decomposition with matched allocation sizes
merged_from: A outer/inner factorial (240 fits, never cited)
program.rationale: The paper flags four times that Random-minus-Grouped bundles outer-test leakage with leaky inner model selection, and A (which decomposes it: RAVDESS outer ~10 pp, inner ~5 pp, interaction +2) was excluded only because its verifier was corrected after outcome visibility. A's own confounds (unequal fit/val sizes across inner arms, protocol-specific seed streams) are fixable for free. Re-run once, inside the prereg, on the anchor corpora, and extend to the fine-tuned regime on RAVDESS so the decomposition is not a CNN-only fact.
program.design: Cells RR (reuse), RG, GR, GG (reuse) where first letter = outer protocol, second = inner validation grouping; fit/val sizes fixed at exactly 75/25 of outer-train for both inner arms; seed streams keyed on (corpus, fold, seed) only, shared across all four cells. SCRATCH CNN: RAVDESS + CREMA-D, draw 0, 3 seeds -> 2 new cells x 2 corpora x 5 folds x 3 seeds = 60 fits. FT WavLM-base+: RAVDESS only, 2 new cells x 5 x 3 = 30 fits (~1.5 h). PROBE H-logreg/H-esp inherit the crossing on CPU/negligible GPU.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: O_G = Y(RG) - Y(GG) (outer contrast under grouped inner), I_G = Y(GR) - Y(GG) (inner contrast under grouped outer), interaction = [Y(RR)-Y(GR)] - O_G; speaker-paired, whole-speaker bootstrap, Wilcoxon, Holm over the 4 primaries (O_G, I_G for RAVDESS CNN and RAVDESS FT). H1: O_G > 0 and I_G > 0 in both regimes on RAVDESS; H2: O_G > I_G (Wilcoxon on per-speaker O_G - I_G). CREMA-D CNN cells reported with +/-2 pp practical band, descriptive.

program.name: DOSE: dose-response of test-speaker exposure with fixed test set and fixed training size
merged_from: C/P5 mechanism-exposure salvage (144 fits, 0/1 exposure, cross-prompt only)
program.rationale: P1 measured only 0% and 100% overlap; C/P5 measured one 22-utterance exposure step, cross-prompt, CNN-only, ended below its own threshold, and could not be blind. Reviewers ask 'how much leakage does it take' — a monotone dose curve is the answer, and the only close precedent is in depression detection (arXiv 2604.14354, shared test set with optional target-subject training inclusion), not SER. The same design with two exposure-pool rules separates the same-text repetition pathway from cross-prompt speaker exposure, the gap C could not close.
program.design: Start from the draw-0 Grouped partition. For each fold, test speakers' utterances are hash-split within speaker (stratified by emotion) into T (always evaluated) and E (exposure pool). Dose d in {0, .25, .5, .75, 1}: a fraction d of each test speaker's E is moved into training and an equal number of training-speaker utterances with matching emotion labels is removed (hash-selected), so training size and label counts are constant; d=0 is speaker-exclusive, d=1 is full exposure. Two E/T rules on RAVDESS: prompt-disjoint (E = statement 1, T = statement 2, as in P5) and prompt-shared (hash split ignoring statement); other corpora prompt-shared only. SCRATCH CNN: RAVDESS (2 rules), CREMA-D, SUBESCO-full x 5 doses x 5 folds x 3 seeds = 300 fits (~4 h). FT WavLM-base+: RAVDESS prompt-shared, 5 doses x 5 folds x 3 seeds = 75 fits (~3.75 h). PROBE primary pipeline at every dose on all corpora (CPU).
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Per speaker: UAR on T as a function of d; slope b_s from OLS over the five doses. H1: median slope > 0 in each corpus and regime (Wilcoxon on b_s; Page's L trend test with speakers as blocks as confirmatory ordered test; Holm over corpus x regime cells). H2: slope(RAVDESS) > slope(CREMA-D) (Mann-Whitney on speaker slopes; descriptive because corpora differ in many ways). H3 (same-text pathway): on RAVDESS at d=1, UAR(prompt-shared) - UAR(prompt-disjoint) > 0 (Wilcoxon over speakers), i.e. literal text repetition adds inflation beyond cross-prompt speaker exposure. Reported: fraction of the d=1 premium reached at d=.25 (descriptive).

program.name: STRUCT: corpus-structure moderators by budget-varying subsampling (speaker count, utterances per speaker, repeated takes)
merged_from: B SUBESCO allocation (2,880 fits, fixed budget, count/repeat confounded)
program.rationale: B is the largest past compute item and is paper-invisible; its fixed-budget design algebraically confounds speaker count with repeat density, and the most interpretable comparison (c20r1 vs c20r2: premium ~6 -> ~16 pp) was never a registered endpoint. The RAVDESS-vs-CREMA-D 6x gap is the paper's most obvious unanswered question. A budget-varying ladder on CREMA-D (91 speakers, ~82 utt each — the natural finite population) plus a takes ladder on SUBESCO separates the two moderators at one-third of B's cost.
program.design: CREMA-D (SCRATCH CNN and PROBE primary): speaker-count ladder n_spk in {12, 24, 48, 91} at 40 utt/speaker (hash-stratified by emotion); density ladder utt/speaker in {20, 41, 82} at 24 speakers; shared cell counted once -> 6 conditions; 4 outcome-blind hash panels per non-full condition (10 for PROBE); Random vs Grouped 5-fold, 1 seed per panel (panel is the replication unit). SUBESCO: takes ladder t in {1, 2, 3, 5} per speaker x emotion x prompt cell (980/1,960/2,940/4,900 utterances; t=1 is the S3 'repetition-clean' panel), 20 speakers, 3 hash panels for t<5, CNN + PROBE. CNN fits: 240 (CREMA-D) + 120 (SUBESCO) at ~40-60 s.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Delta_RG per condition and panel (speaker-paired within panel, then panel mean). H1: Delta_RG decreases with speaker count at fixed density (Page's L / Jonckheere over the 4 levels, panels as blocks; one-sided). H2: Delta_RG increases with utterances per speaker at fixed speaker count (same test, 3 levels). H3: Delta_RG increases with takes per cell on SUBESCO (4 levels). Tests run for CNN and PROBE separately; Holm over the 6 ordered tests. Descriptive: whether the 24-speaker/41-utt CREMA-D cell approaches the RAVDESS premium (a direct check on the 'speaker count' explanation).

program.name: REPLAY: realized-split premium under the splits public repositories actually produce
program.rationale: The paper forbids multiplying prevalence by effect size and therefore never connects the two halves; a reviewer will say the controlled premium is 'your split, your model'. Executing the audited repos' own split code on the real manifest (P0.5 already proved 24/30 fragments are AST-executable) and training our fixed pipelines on the realized split versus a size-matched speaker-exclusive counterfactual gives a per-repository premium with no multiplication and no extrapolation. It also replaces the abandoned P2 scenario analysis with an empirical quantity.
program.design: From AUD: every Y_test repo whose split fragment executed on the real RAVDESS or CREMA-D manifest (expected 15-25). For each: realized train/test index sets (single split as the repo does it, or its k folds), realized overlap fraction, test size. Counterfactual: 3 GroupShuffleSplit draws matched on test-utterance count and class proportions, zero speaker overlap. SCRATCH CNN: (1 realized + 3 counterfactual) x 3 seeds per repo (~240 fits, 3.3 h). PROBE primary on the same index sets (CPU). FT WavLM-base+: first 8 repos in beacon order, realized vs 1 counterfactual x 2 seeds (~4.3 h). Our pipeline, not theirs, is trained; their split is the treatment.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Delta_repo = UAR(realized split) - mean UAR(counterfactual splits), per repo, per regime. H1: Delta_repo > 0 for the majority of repos (exact sign test across repos, per regime); report median Delta_repo per corpus with a repo-level bootstrap CI. H2 (descriptive): Delta_repo increases with realized overlap fraction (Spearman). Reported alongside, never multiplied with, the AUD prevalence.

program.name: XCORP: cross-corpus ladder from Grouped-fold checkpoints and frozen probes
program.rationale: Cross-corpus evaluation is the reviewer's 'real' speaker-independent benchmark and has been established since Schuller et al. 2010; the paper cannot ignore it, but it does not need new training: FT's Grouped-fold checkpoints and PROBE's features already exist. A zero-training arm places Random, within-corpus Grouped, and cross-corpus UAR on one ladder under the 4-class map, at ~0.5 GPU-h of inference.
program.design: 4-class map (angry/happy/neutral/sad) fixed in DATA. For every ordered corpus pair (source, target): FT Grouped-fold checkpoints (all 5 folds x seeds) scored on the full target corpus with argmax restricted to the mapped classes; PROBE primary pipeline trained on all of source, tested on all of target. Within-corpus Random and Grouped 4-class UARs recomputed from existing OOF predictions on the same class subset.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Per target corpus: UAR_random_within, UAR_grouped_within, mean UAR_cross (over sources). H1: UAR_random_within > UAR_grouped_within > UAR_cross in every target corpus (ordered; Page's L over targets, FT regime primary). Descriptive: cross-corpus matrix, within-language vs cross-language pairs (ESD-EN/ESD-ZH is the controlled pair).

program.name: CUT: LOSO protocol in every trained regime
program.rationale: LOSO was 85% of P1 compute and 70% of D1; its only finding (LOSO > GroupKFold in 8/8 cells) is a training-set-size effect, Delta_RL on CREMA-D was non-significant in 3/4 cells, and it contributed nothing to the leakage claim. Retained only as a CPU fold-count sensitivity in PROBE (k in {5,10,LOSO}).
program.design: None.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

program.name: CUT: ResNet-SE, Transformer, FNO from-scratch architectures
program.rationale: All four P1 architectures agreed in direction with premia within 4 pp on both corpora; architecture is not a moderator worth 75% of the from-scratch budget when corpus, language, regime and dose are untested. FNO in particular invites 'why FNO' questions with no payoff. The regime factor (CNN vs frozen large probe vs fine-tuned WavLM) replaces architecture as the capacity axis.
program.design: None.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

program.name: CUT: D1 RAVDESS speech-song matched panel
program.rationale: Vocal channel is not a leakage question; all five endpoints were not conclusive; the result was removed from every manuscript lineage; RAVDESS-Song adds no language, no speakers, no regime. The information it carries (the premium persists on the same actors in another channel) is subsumed by nine corpora.
program.design: None.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

program.name: CUT: P0 purposive audit, six non-speaker P0 outcomes, P0.5-vs-purposive comparison, P2 scenario burden
program.rationale: None of these reached any paper lineage; the purposive-vs-random comparison was reclassified as a 'working-model diagnostic' by its own protocol; the six non-speaker outcomes dilute coding effort that AUD needs for n=100 and human double coding. P2's scenario multiplication is replaced by REPLAY's empirical per-repo premium.
program.design: None.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

program.name: CUT: S0 v1/v2, S2, S3 as separate arms; S4 as a separate arm
program.rationale: Merged into PROBE and DATA. S0 v2 existed only for provenance; S2 and S3 were the same Ridge design on different corpora; S3 needed ten release iterations for zero scientific change; S4 never ran. In the redesign SUBESCO is an ordinary panel corpus in all three regimes (the four P1-style models were never run on any non-English corpus, which was the abandoned Rev-2 contribution), and layer policy is a CPU factor.
program.design: None.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

pipeline_order: Day 0: file IEMOCAP and MSP-Podcast license requests; email ESD license form; publish OSF preregistration (protocol hash, tooling commit hash, named NIST beacon pulse time for AUD sampling and hash seeds for all subsampling/draws)
AUD frame construction and beacon-seeded sample draw (CPU, runs in parallel with everything below; adjudication proceeds throughout)
DATA: acquire in-hand + free corpora, hygiene, hash subsampling (ESD, later MSP-Podcast), manifests, 10-draw partition set per corpus, validity gates
FEAT: extract all-layer features for 5 encoders on all obtained corpora (5 GPU-h)
PROBE: full CPU panel (heads x layers x encoders x draws x corpora) + fold-count sensitivity; H-esp head batched on GPU (1 GPU-h)
SCRATCH: CNN panel, corpus order RAVDESS, CREMA-D, SUBESCO, EmoDB, ESD-EN, ESD-ZH, ShEMO, then IEMOCAP/MSP-Podcast if obtained (5.5 GPU-h)
FT: WavLM-base+ fine-tuning in the same fixed corpus order (31 GPU-h); day-14 cutoff decides whether IEMOCAP/MSP-Podcast enter
FACT: RG/GR cells for CNN (RAVDESS, CREMA-D) and FT (RAVDESS) (2.3 GPU-h)
DOSE: CNN on RAVDESS (two E/T rules), CREMA-D, SUBESCO; FT on RAVDESS; PROBE at all doses on CPU (8 GPU-h)
STRUCT: CREMA-D speaker/density ladders and SUBESCO takes ladder, CNN + PROBE (5 GPU-h)
AUD execution tier on real manifests -> REPLAY: realized vs counterfactual splits, CNN + PROBE + FT subset (7.5 GPU-h)
XCORP: inference only from FT Grouped checkpoints and PROBE features (0.5 GPU-h)

Locked analysis scripts run once on the complete ledger; independent re-implementation of every table; ~10 GPU-h reserve for result-independent retries only; hard cap 100 GPU-h, arms later in this order are reported incomplete if the cap is hit
proposals.preregistration_notes: Registration: one OSF preregistration before any corpus is downloaded, containing the full protocol, SHA-256 of the tooling commit, every hash seed string, the AUD dedup rule and endpoint hierarchy, the fixed corpus order, the day-14 license cutoff rule, and the exact test list below; the NIST beacon pulse used for the audit order is named by time in advance. Test families (Holm within each, families fixed now): AUD (1 confirmatory test); PROBE (n_corpora + 3 secondary); SCRATCH (n_corpora); FT (n_corpora); regime contrasts (2 sign tests over corpora); FACT (4); DOSE (corpus x regime slope tests + H3); STRUCT (6); REPLAY (2); XCORP (1). Speaker is the paired unit everywhere; 10,000-replicate whole-speaker percentile bootstrap with fixed seed; two-sided Wilcoxon unless a direction is stated; partition draws and seeds are replication of the pipeline, never n. Primary pipelines are fixed a priori: SCRATCH = P1 CNN; PROBE = WavLM-Large + inner-CV layer + logistic; FT = WavLM-base+ full fine-tune; every other cell is sensitivity and is reported in full regardless of direction. Routing is result-independent: main text carries one forest figure (Delta_RG per corpus x regime), one audit panel, one dose curve; everything else is supplement. Data hygiene (duplicate removal, all-zero removal) is fixed before extraction. Preregistered validity anchors (IEMOCAP 4-class Grouped UAR range; zero overlap gates) trigger implementation audits, not exclusions. Prior-art positioning fixed now: the protocol effect on RAVDESS/CREMA-D is a replication of Ibrahim et al. 2026 and Zielonka et al. 2022; the novelty claims are the probability audit with human reliability and test-boundary distinction, the multi-corpus/multi-regime/fine-tuned generality, the dose curve, and the realized-split replay. Verification: an independent re-implementation of all statistics from raw prediction files is written and tested on synthetic data before any real result exists; verifiers are frozen before scoring, not after. No number is changed after the ledger lock; any deviation is logged with timestamp and disclosed. Licenses stated in the paper: RAVDESS CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; CREMA-D ODbL; SUBESCO CC BY 4.0; EmoDB academic custom; ShEMO free for academic use; ESD NUS non-commercial research license (signed form); IEMOCAP USC academic license; MSP-Podcast UTD institutional academic license; emotion2vec+ FunASR model-license; Whisper Apache-2.0; WavLM/HuBERT MIT.
risks: IEMOCAP and/or MSP-Podcast licenses may not arrive by day 14; the panel then has 7 corpora and no spontaneous English corpus (ShEMO semi-natural Persian is the only non-acted corpus), which weakens but does not void the generality claim; the rule is fixed in advance so this is reported, not silently absorbed.
ESD requires a signed license returned by email to NUS; if refused or delayed, both ESD languages drop and the controlled within-design language contrast (EN vs ZH) is lost.

Fine-tuning cost is estimated at ~2 GPU-min per 1,000 training utterances per fit on an RTX 5070; if the real figure is 2x, FT alone reaches ~60 GPU-h and the reserve is consumed; the fixed corpus order and the 100 GPU-h hard cap mean late corpora (ShEMO, IEMOCAP, MSP-Podcast) would be reported incomplete rather than the design being shrunk mid-run.

12 GB VRAM: WavLM-base+ full fine-tuning at batch 8 x 4 s fp16 fits, but MSP-Podcast segments up to 10 s at eval and any attempt to fine-tune a Large model do not; the design deliberately fine-tunes only the base model.

EmoDB, IEMOCAP and ESD have 10 speakers, giving 2 test speakers per grouped fold; per-corpus Wilcoxon on n=10 speakers has low power and those corpora contribute mainly to the panel-level sign tests and meta-analysis, which must be said in the paper.

AUD n=100 with ~10% unresolved still yields a partial-identification width of ~10 pp and a frame envelope of ~20-25 pp; human double coding on 25 repos gives a kappa CI that may be wide; both are preregistered as reported quantities, not as claims.

REPLAY depends on AUD adjudication finishing and on enough Y_test repos having AST-executable split fragments on RAVDESS/CREMA-D; if fewer than 10 qualify, REPLAY is reported as descriptive only (rule fixed in advance).

emotion2vec+ is itself fine-tuned on pseudo-labelled emotion data whose provenance may overlap the panel corpora; its frozen-probe results are flagged as potentially contaminated and excluded from the primary PROBE pipeline for that reason.

The DOSE design keeps training size constant by removing training-speaker utterances, so at high dose the training speaker set is slightly reduced; the effect is bounded (<=2% of training utterances at d=1 for CREMA-D, higher for RAVDESS) and is reported alongside the curve.

Governance overhead was the program's largest hidden cost last time (13 plan revisions, ten S3 releases, three moved hard stops); the single preregistration, fixed order, frozen verifiers and result-independent routing are the mitigation, but they require the author to refuse mid-run scope changes.
resulting_paper_claims: In a beacon-sampled probability sample of 100 public SER repository lineages (frame rule and endpoint fixed before sampling), X% (partial-identification [X, X+U]%, frame envelope [L, H]%) permit the same speaker in training and the reported test set; human-vs-AI agreement on the verdict is kappa = K; risk is/is not concentrated in non-paper-linked code.

Under identical speaker-paired partitions, utterance-level random splitting inflates UAR relative to speaker-grouped splitting in every one of 7-9 corpora spanning 5-7 languages, acted and semi-natural/spontaneous speech, and in all three regimes: log-mel CNN, frozen large SSL/emotion-specialised probes with practice-typical layer and head selection, and full fine-tuning of WavLM-base+; the premium is largest for end-to-end regimes and smallest for frozen probes (paired regime contrasts), so it is not a small-model artifact.

The premium is heterogeneous across corpora (I^2 reported) and is moderated in preregistered directions by speaker count, utterances per speaker, and repeated takes, shown by budget-varying subsampling of CREMA-D and SUBESCO rather than by cross-corpus comparison.

Inflation is a monotone dose-response in the fraction of test-speaker speech present in training, with a substantial share of the full-exposure premium reached at 25% exposure; on RAVDESS, same-text repetition adds a measurable increment over cross-prompt speaker exposure.

On RAVDESS the pipeline-level premium decomposes into an outer test-leakage component and an inner model-selection component, both positive, in both the CNN and fine-tuned regimes; enforcing speaker exclusivity at the validation boundary alone recovers only part of the gap.
