When the split code of audited repositories is executed on the real corpora and our fixed pipelines are trained on the resulting partitions, the majority of repositories' splits produce a positive premium over size-matched speaker-exclusive counterfactuals (median reported per corpus and regime), tying prevalence to magnitude without multiplying the two.

Within-corpus grouped UAR remains well above cross-corpus UAR in every target corpus, placing the leakage premium on a ladder random > grouped > cross-corpus; the recommendation is speaker exclusivity at every active boundary plus publication of grouping metadata, with cross-corpus evaluation as the stricter complement.

proposals.angle: Mechanism-first: decompose the speaker-nonexclusive inflation into separable leakage channels (same-speaker cross-prompt exposure, same-sentence exposure, near-duplicate sibling takes, and model-selection/validation leakage), and test whether corpus structure (sentences per speaker, takes per cell, speaker count) rather than speaker count per se sets the size of the premium. The public-code audit stays as the prevalence half, refined so its outcome fields map onto the same channels.
proposals.thesis: Speaker-nonexclusive evaluation is common in public SER code (probability audit with a public pre-registration, human double-coding, and channel-specific outcome fields) and it inflates reported scores through three separable outer-boundary channels plus one model-selection channel. On an identical held-out test block with training-set size held constant, we measure each channel directly: exposure to the test speaker's other sentences, exposure to the test sentence from other speakers, and exposure to near-duplicate sibling takes (same speaker x sentence x emotion, different take/intensity), plus leaky inner validation and hyperparameter selection. The claim the paper would make is that the RAVDESS-vs-CREMA-D gap (15-20 vs 2-3 pp) is predominantly a sibling-take-density and sentence-count effect, not a speaker-count effect, that the speaker channel is identity-specific (it accrues only to exposed speakers, dose-linearly) and is the only channel attenuated by per-speaker normalization or speaker-adversarial training, and that these conclusions hold for frozen SSL representations and across six acted corpora in four languages.

program.name: AUD (probability audit of public SER code, channel-resolved)
program.rationale: The audit is the paper's only non-collided contribution (prior-art matrix: Ibrahim 2026, Zielonka 2022 already report the protocol effect), so it stays as the prevalence half. The dossier shows three fixable weaknesses: (1) no public pre-outcome registration; (2) no human coding at all (planned 8-10 repo blind coding revoked), so no inter-rater statistic; (3) the Y endpoint conflates validation-only with test-boundary nonexclusivity and reports no stratification by repo_relation or corpus, so prevalence cannot be related to the literature. It also wastes effort on duplicate estimation (P0.5 n=30 and S1 n=60 on overlapping frames with 2 shared repos, never reconciled) and on six extra P0 outcomes never used. One audit only; keep the P0.5 execution tier (the tree's strongest evidence, 384/384 AST-fragment matches) and apply it to every Y/N unit. Add channel-specific fields so audit outcomes map onto the M1 channels: sentence/prompt exclusivity (predicted near-zero in the wild) and sibling-take handling. Lineage rule (D2) fixed before any outcome; sensitivity branches dropped because the dossier shows all five branches move the envelope by <=0.3 pp.
program.design: Frame: rebuild the 383-URL candidate log with the D2 executable-blob lineage rule fixed in the pre-registration (containment >=0.90 + corroborator), eligibility E1-E5, four target corpora (RAVDESS, CREMA-D, IEMOCAP, EmoDB) plus SUBESCO/ESD hits, cutoff date fixed. Sample n=80 by NIST-beacon-seeded order (pulse after the OSF timestamp); ~57 needed for 12 pp half-width, 80 gives ~10 pp and room for U. Per unit (static + AST-fragment execution tier on a synthetic 4-corpus manifest, as P0.5): endpoint Y/N/U as before, PLUS fields: boundary_type in {test, validation-only, both}; sentence_exclusive Y/N/U; sibling_handling (any dedup of same speaker-sentence-emotion takes) Y/N/U; test_set_used_for_selection Y/N/U (feeds M3-HPO); repo_relation {author-official, author-linked, third-party reproduction, supplemental/student}; corpus set; year. Human coding: two human coders blind-code 20 beacon-selected units on the Y/N/U endpoint and boundary_type before seeing AI verdicts; Cohen's kappa reported; disagreements adjudicated by a third pass. Statistics unchanged: confirmed fraction, partial-identification interval, exact hypergeometric joint >=95% envelope (two one-sided 97.5% bounds), plus the same envelope for the stratum test-boundary-Y and for paper-linked repos. 0 GPU; ~120 CPU-review hours.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Primary: frame prevalence of test-boundary speaker-nonexclusivity risk (Y with boundary_type in {test, both}) in the frozen frame, reported as confirmed fraction, partial-ID interval and joint >=95% hypergeometric envelope. H1 (directional): confirmed test-boundary prevalence > 50% (lower envelope bound above 0.50). Secondary preregistered: sentence-exclusive fraction < 10%; paper-linked stratum prevalence not lower than the supplemental stratum (two-sided Fisher on Y vs N+U, reported, no Holm); human-AI kappa >= 0.6 on the 20 double-coded units (report point estimate and bootstrap CI; if kappa < 0.6 the audit is labelled AI-coded exploratory).

program.name: M0 (shared data, split and feature infrastructure; SSL all-layer caches)
program.rationale: Every mechanism arm needs the same objects: per-corpus manifests with speaker, sentence/prompt, emotion, take/intensity keys; a single test-block generator; size-matched training-pool samplers per exposure level; and cached features. Extracting all hidden layers once (not final-layer only) revives S4 at zero marginal cost and enables the layer-wise speaker-vs-emotion probe. The dossier shows S0 v1 had to be fully re-run for provenance (env mismatch, no pins) and S3 needed ten releases for cache-identity reasons, so cache identity (SHA of audio manifest + preprocessing config + weight SHA in the filename) is fixed here once. Corpus set is chosen to span the structural corners the mechanism predicts: RAVDESS (24 spk, 2 sentences, 2 takes x 2 intensities = 4 siblings per cell), CREMA-D (91 spk, 12 sentences, siblings only in IWW), SUBESCO full (20 spk, 10 sentences, 5 takes; CC BY 4.0), ESD English and ESD Chinese subsampled to 70 sentences x 10 speakers x 5 emotions = 3,500 each (10 spk, many sentences, no siblings; research-only license form e-mailed to the authors per the HLTSingapore GitHub page, obtainable but not yet in hand), EmoDB (10 spk, 10 sentences, 535 utt, free). IEMOCAP is dropped (license, dyadic partner leakage confounds the channel decomposition; EMO-SUPERB arXiv:2402.13018 documents that partner speech leaks into segmented turns). TESS/SAVEE excluded (2/4 speakers).
program.design: Manifests: byte-level SHA-256 per file; keys (speaker, sentence_id, emotion, take, intensity); exact-duplicate and all-zero files removed by rule before any split (unlike P1, which kept them) with the removal list frozen; near-duplicate audio detection (chromaprint/ MFCC-hash) reported but not used for exclusion. Log-mel features exactly as P1 (22.05 kHz, 64 mel, 128 frames, per-utterance z-score). SSL: torchaudio HUBERT_BASE, WAV2VEC2_BASE, WAVLM_BASE_PLUS frozen, 16 kHz, time-mean of EVERY hidden layer (13 x 768) stored as float16 npz named by manifest SHA + weight SHA. Test-block generator: for each corpus, 5 speaker folds (StratifiedGroupKFold by speaker, seed fixed) crossed with one sentence fold per speaker fold (sentence fold j = k mod n_sentence_folds; RAVDESS 2, CREMA-D 4, SUBESCO 5, ESD 5, EmoDB 5), so test block k = speakers S_k x sentences T_k, identical across all exposure levels. Training-pool samplers for levels L0-L4 (see M1) with N_train fixed to |(non-S_k) x (non-T_k)| minus emotion-stratified rounding. Models: CNN and ResNet-SE with P1 hyperparameters (Transformer/FNO cut), AdamW, batch 64, <=100 epochs, patience 15, deterministic; inner validation ALWAYS speaker- and sentence-exclusive within the training pool (25%) except in M3. Seeds: 3 everywhere, 5 on RAVDESS and EmoDB (seed SD 1-3 pp in D1/P1 is comparable to the smaller channel effects there). Independent scorer and verifier written and hash-frozen BEFORE the first production fit; smoke test on 2% of run_plan. Compute: SSL extraction ~24k utterances x 3 encoders ~1.5 GPU-h; log-mel CPU; smoke tests and verification refits ~2.5 GPU-h.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: No scientific estimand. Gate: all caches bitwise reproducible on re-extraction of a 2% sample; zero speaker or sentence overlap between test block and L0 pool asserted per fold; N_train identical across levels within a fold (hard assertion).

program.name: M1 (exposure-channel factorial on identical test blocks, size-matched)
merged_from: C/P5 mechanism exposure (cross-prompt target-actor exposure = level L1)
D1 speech-song (RAVDESS sibling structure now manipulated directly)
S0/S2/S3 direction results (SSL heads run on the same levels)
program.rationale: This is the arm that discriminates mechanisms. P1 varies outer split and inner grouping together and cannot say whether the RAVDESS premium comes from speaker identity, from the two shared sentences, or from the 4 sibling takes per speaker x sentence x emotion cell; C/P5 measured only the cross-prompt speaker channel, only on CNN, with a 24-actor CREMA-D subpanel and no inference; B's unregistered c20r1 -> c20r2 comparison (premium ~6 -> ~16 pp when a second take is added) is the strongest hint in the whole dossier that sibling takes drive the RAVDESS-type premium, and CREMA-D has almost no siblings. Holding the test block and N_train fixed and varying only what the training pool may contain turns P1's 'protocol package' into a channel decomposition with paired per-speaker inference, and the corpus corners (ESD: few speakers, many sentences, no siblings; EmoDB: few speakers, 10 sentences) separate 'speaker count' from 'sibling density' as the moderator. Prior work shows speaker information is linearly extractable from emotion embeddings (arXiv:2202.01252) and content leakage is a known artefact in TTS/VC evaluation, but no SER study decomposes the leakage premium by channel.
program.design: Per corpus (RAVDESS, CREMA-D, SUBESCO-full, ESD-EN, ESD-ZH, EmoDB), per test block k (5), five training-pool levels, each sampled to the same N_train, emotion-stratified: L0 = neither test speakers nor test sentences (fully exclusive); L1 = test speakers' OTHER sentences allowed (cross-prompt speaker exposure), test sentences from other speakers excluded; L2 = test sentences from OTHER speakers allowed, test speakers excluded; L3 = same speaker AND same sentence allowed but only with a DIFFERENT emotion (no same-emotion siblings); L4 = everything outside the test block allowed uniformly (siblings included; this is what a random split does). Models CNN, ResNet-SE (from scratch, log-mel), plus two frozen-SSL heads (HuBERT-base, WavLM-base+; trained linear probe on the M0 caches, layer per M6 rule) per level. Inner validation speaker+sentence exclusive within pool, 25%. Seeds 3 (5 on RAVDESS/EmoDB). Fits (scratch): 5 levels x 5 blocks x 2 models x seeds = 150 per corpus (250 RAVDESS/EmoDB); ~1,100 scratch fits; SSL heads ~1,100 cheap fits. Per-fit cost from dossier: RAVDESS ~15 s, CREMA-D ~65 s, SUBESCO-7000 ~60 s, ESD-3500 ~35 s, EmoDB ~8 s (size-matched pools are smaller than P1's, so these are upper bounds). Outputs: per-utterance logits for every fit; penultimate embeddings saved for M4.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Per corpus and model, speaker-paired UAR contrasts on the identical test utterances, averaged over seeds: D_spk = L1-L0, D_sent = L2-L0, D_lex = L3-L2 (same speaker+sentence, other emotion, beyond sentence-only), D_sib = L4-L3, and total T = L4-L0. Inference: whole-speaker cluster bootstrap (10,000, percentile) + two-sided Wilcoxon; Holm family per corpus = 4 contrasts x 2 scratch models = 8; SSL heads a separate 8-test family. Directional hypotheses: H1 D_spk > 0 in every corpus (universal speaker channel). H2 D_sib > 0 in RAVDESS and SUBESCO-full (siblings present) and |D_sib| < 1 pp (TOST equivalence, speaker-cluster) in CREMA-D, ESD, EmoDB (siblings absent/rare). H3 D_sent > 0 but D_sent < D_spk in every corpus. H4 (cross-corpus, the RAVDESS-vs-CREMA-D question): total premium T orders RAVDESS > SUBESCO-full > CREMA-D ~ EmoDB ~ ESD-EN ~ ESD-ZH, i.e. corpora with 10 speakers but many sentences and no siblings (ESD) show T < 0.5 x T(RAVDESS); the competing speaker-count account predicts T(ESD) >= T(RAVDESS). Tested with a two-sample speaker-cluster bootstrap of T(RAVDESS) - T(ESD-EN) > 0 and a preregistered rank prediction (Spearman between corpus sibling-density index and T, all 6 corpora). H5 SSL heads show the same sign pattern with smaller D_sib (descriptive, no cross-stack test).

program.name: M1b (practice-mirroring headline: Random vs speaker-GroupKFold at full size on six corpora)
program.rationale: The thesis needs one number in the practitioner's configuration (full training size, inner validation mirroring the outer protocol, 5-fold), because that is what an audited repository's Y maps onto and what M1's size-matched decomposition deliberately does not measure. P1 provided this for two corpora only; Rev 1/2's promised multilingual contribution (8-corpus queue) was never delivered. Running it on the same six corpora as M1 with 2 models and 3 seeds costs ~4 GPU-h, replaces P1's 1,620 fits (85% of which were LOSO), and gives the per-corpus dot-interval figure originally planned for M2. LOSO is cut: P1 showed LOSO > GroupKFold in 8/8 cells purely through training-size (23/24 vs 19/24 speakers), so it carries no leakage information and M1 removes the size confound by design. Split-draw stability (S2) is folded in by using 5 partition draws instead of one frozen split.
program.design: Per corpus: 5 partition draws (seed_r from SHA of a fixed string, as S2) x {Random StratifiedKFold(5), StratifiedGroupKFold(5) by speaker}, inner validation mirrors outer (25%), full training size, CNN + ResNet-SE, seeds 3 (5 RAVDESS/EmoDB), plus HuBERT/WavLM frozen probes. Scratch fits: 5 draws x 2 protocols x 5 folds x 2 models x 3 seeds = 300 per corpus (500 RAVDESS/EmoDB); many corpora are small so total ~4 GPU-h. Report per-corpus Random-minus-Grouped UAR with speaker-cluster bootstrap on draw 0 (paired, same speakers) and the empirical 5-draw range.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: P_RG(corpus, model) = speaker-equal OOF UAR(Random) - UAR(GroupKFold), seed-averaged, draw 0 confirmatory, draws 1-4 stability. H: P_RG > 0 in all 6 corpora x 2 models (Holm family 12, Wilcoxon + cluster bootstrap); H (moderator): P_RG(corpus) rank-correlates with the corpus sibling-density index (siblings per speaker x sentence x emotion cell) more strongly than with speaker count (preregistered Spearman on 6 corpora; descriptive with n=6, reported with CI, no p-value headline).

program.name: M2 (speaker-exposure dose-response and identity specificity)
program.rationale: P1 measured only 0% and 100% speaker overlap; the audit finds repositories that leak all speakers, but the mechanism question is whether the premium is identity-specific (accrues only to the exposed speakers, no spillover) and linear in the fraction of test speakers exposed. This cannot be inferred from M1 because L1 exposes all test speakers. A within-fold exposed-vs-unexposed contrast at partial dose is the cleanest identity-specificity test available and it reuses M1's L0 and L1 cells as dose 0 and dose 100.
program.design: Corpora RAVDESS, CREMA-D, SUBESCO-full. Same test blocks and N_train as M1. Doses 25/50/75% of the test speakers in block k exposed cross-prompt (L1 rule), the rest unexposed (L0 rule); exposed subset chosen by hash order fixed before outcomes and rotated so each speaker is exposed in exactly one of the three partial doses. CNN + ResNet-SE, seeds 3 (5 RAVDESS). Fits: 3 doses x 5 blocks x 2 models x seeds = 90 per corpus (150 RAVDESS). Per-speaker UAR from per-utterance logits.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: (a) Identity specificity at dose 50: speaker-paired contrast E = UAR(exposed speakers at dose 50) - UAR(same speakers at dose 0) vs U = UAR(unexposed speakers at dose 50) - UAR(same speakers at dose 0). H: E > 0 (Wilcoxon, cluster bootstrap) and U equivalent to 0 within +/-1.5 pp (TOST). (b) Dose linearity: mean block UAR as a function of dose in {0,25,50,75,100}; H: slope > 0 and the quadratic term's 95% cluster-bootstrap CI includes 0. Holm family 4 per corpus (E, U-equivalence not Holm-adjusted, slope; 2 models).

program.name: M3 (model-selection leakage: inner-validation grouping and hyperparameter search on leaky validation)
merged_from: P0 outcome 'explicit test-set selection' (36.7% in P0.5)
program.rationale: A is the only arm in the dossier that decomposed outer from inner leakage (RAVDESS O_G +9.99, I_G +5.13, interaction +2.15; CREMA-D O_G +1.89, I_G +0.68) and it never entered the paper because its verifier was corrected post-outcome; its design also confounded fit-set size (+0..+66 items) and seed streams across outer protocols. M1 fixes inner validation to the exclusive rule everywhere, so the inner channel is isolated by adding only leaky-inner variants of L0 and L4 with matched sizes and shared init seeds. The HPO sub-arm measures the realistic failure mode the audit records (selection on a speaker-nonexclusive or test set): how much does selecting a configuration on a leaky validation set inflate the reported validation number relative to the exclusive-test number, and does it hurt exclusive-test performance.
program.design: (i) Inner-grouping factorial: corpora RAVDESS, CREMA-D, SUBESCO-full; outer levels L0 and L4 from M1; inner validation rule {exclusive (already in M1), random utterance-level (leaky)}; identical N_fit and N_val (leaky inner draws the same counts), identical init seed within (corpus, block, seed) across all four cells. New fits: 2 x 5 x 2 models x seeds = 60 per corpus (100 RAVDESS). (ii) HPO sub-arm: CNN only, RAVDESS and CREMA-D, outer L0 test blocks; random search over 8 preregistered configurations (width {32,48,64}, lr {3e-4,1e-3}, dropout {0.1,0.3}, subset of 8 fixed by hash); each config trained once per block with (a) leaky random inner validation and (b) exclusive inner validation; selection rule = best validation UAR; 8 x 2 x 5 = 80 fits per corpus, 1 seed. Report selected-config leaky-validation UAR, its exclusive-test UAR, and the exclusive-test UAR of the config selected under (b).
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: (i) I = UAR(outer L0, leaky inner) - UAR(outer L0, exclusive inner) per speaker; O = UAR(L4, exclusive inner) - UAR(L0, exclusive inner) (= M1's T); interaction = [UAR(L4, leaky) - UAR(L4, excl)] - I. H: I > 0 in RAVDESS and SUBESCO-full (Holm over 3 corpora x 2 models); descriptive shares O/(O+I+interaction) reported with cluster-bootstrap CIs, no mediation language. (ii) HPO: G_report = leaky-val UAR of the leaky-selected config minus its exclusive-test UAR. H: G_report > 5 pp on RAVDESS and > 1 pp on CREMA-D (block-level paired bootstrap); H2: exclusive-test UAR of leaky-selected config <= that of exclusive-selected config (one-sided, reported; equivalence within 1 pp also acceptable and preregistered as 'selection does not help').

program.name: M4 (representational probes: speaker identity in emotion embeddings and sibling nearest-neighbour analysis)
merged_from: C/P5 gap 'no representational test of speaker identity'
program.rationale: The dossier explicitly forbade writing that the SER model uses speaker identity because nothing tested it. Speaker information being linearly recoverable from emotion embeddings is established (arXiv:2202.01252), so the probe alone is confirmatory of known work; the new, mechanism-discriminating piece is the sibling nearest-neighbour analysis: if the L4 premium works through near-duplicate memorisation, a test utterance whose nearest training embedding is its own sibling should be classified correctly far more often than one whose nearest neighbour is not, and this should hold in RAVDESS/SUBESCO and be absent in CREMA-D. Runs on checkpoints and embeddings saved by M1; inference only.
program.design: From M1 (L0 and L4 checkpoints, CNN and ResNet-SE, all corpora): penultimate embeddings for all training-pool and test-block utterances. (a) Speaker-ID linear probe: within the training pool speakers, logistic regression on a 50/50 utterance split by sentence, accuracy vs chance (1/n_speakers), for L0- and L4-trained checkpoints; paired over (block, seed). (b) Sibling-NN: for each L4 test utterance, cosine nearest neighbour in the L4 training pool; categorise NN as sibling / same speaker non-sibling / same sentence other speaker / other; conditional accuracy per category; speaker-cluster bootstrap. (c) Layer-wise on SSL caches (M0): per layer l of each encoder, linear speaker-ID probe accuracy (speaker-exclusive by sentence halves) and the M1-style L4-L0 premium of a linear emotion head on layer l; correlation across 13 layers x 3 encoders x 6 corpora. CPU except embedding extraction (~0.5 GPU-h).
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: (a) H: speaker-ID probe accuracy > 5 x chance for both L0 and L4 checkpoints, and L4 > L0 (paired Wilcoxon over block x seed, Holm over corpora). (b) H: P(correct | NN is sibling) - P(correct | NN is other) > 10 pp in RAVDESS and SUBESCO-full; in CREMA-D/ESD/EmoDB fewer than 5% of test items have a sibling NN (reported, no test). (c) H: Spearman correlation between layer-wise speaker-probe accuracy and layer-wise L4-L0 premium > 0 (per encoder, pooled over corpora, bootstrap CI over layers).

program.name: M5 (interventions: per-speaker normalisation and speaker-adversarial training)
merged_from: S4 (representation-side fix, replaced by an intervention with a directional prediction)
program.rationale: Channel decomposition (M1) is observational within the training pool; an intervention that targets the speaker channel and leaves the others alone gives the causal signature. Per-speaker feature normalisation and adversarial speaker removal are standard SER tools (arXiv:2202.01252 reports gains for SSL SER; iterative feature normalisation, gradient-reversal speaker normalisation are older). Prediction: they attenuate D_spk (L1-L0) but not D_sent (L2) and not D_sib (L4-L3), because sibling takes remain near-duplicates after per-speaker standardisation. If instead they attenuate D_sib as well, the speaker-identity account of the sibling channel wins. This is also the paper's only constructive recommendation beyond 'group by speaker'.
program.design: Corpora RAVDESS, CREMA-D, SUBESCO-full; levels L0, L1, L2, L4 (L3 omitted); interventions: (a) per-speaker z-normalisation of log-mel statistics using each speaker's own utterances (transductive at test, as in common practice); (b) gradient-reversal speaker classifier on the penultimate layer (lambda 0.1 fixed, preregistered, speaker labels from the training pool only). CNN + ResNet-SE, seeds 3 (5 RAVDESS). Fits: 2 interventions x 4 levels x 5 blocks x 2 models x seeds = 240 per corpus (400 RAVDESS). Same test blocks, N_train and inner rule as M1.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: For each intervention I and channel c in {spk, sent, sib-proxy = L4-L2}, attenuation A_c = D_c(baseline) - D_c(I), speaker-paired. H1: A_spk > 0 and > 0.5 x D_spk(baseline) for both interventions in all three corpora (Holm family 6 per corpus). H2: A_sent equivalent to 0 within +/-1.5 pp (TOST). H3 (discriminating): A_sib-proxy < 0.25 x D_sib-proxy(baseline) under per-speaker normalisation in RAVDESS (sibling channel is not a speaker-identity effect); reported with CI. H4: exclusive-level UAR (L0) rises under per-speaker normalisation (replicating the literature; one-sided).

program.name: M6 (SSL head and split-family reconciliation, layer selection)
program.rationale: The dossier's most conspicuous unexplained number is that the same frozen RAVDESS features give a 2.8-6.2 pp premium in S0 (trained linear probe, P1 frozen splits) and 12.4-15.4 pp in S2 (Ridge, 20 fresh StratifiedKFold/StratifiedGroupKFold draws), while CREMA-D agrees across heads. A reviewer will ask whether head or partition family drives the premium; no run in the artifact crosses them. S3 is S2 on SUBESCO and is absorbed by M1/M1b running SSL heads on all six corpora. S4 (layer weighting) was a permanent NO-GO because of a missed calendar gate, not science; with all-layer caches from M0 it costs minutes. All on cached features; near-zero GPU.
program.design: (a) 2x2x2 on RAVDESS and CREMA-D HuBERT/WavLM/wav2vec2 caches: head {trained linear probe w/ early stopping on inner val, RidgeClassifier(alpha=1, balanced)} x split family {P1-style GroupKFold unshuffled vs StratifiedGroupKFold shuffled, 5 draws} x sibling handling {as-is, siblings of the test cell removed from the random-split train fold}; premium per cell. (b) Layer rule for M1/M1b SSL heads fixed in advance: layer chosen by exclusive-inner-validation UAR on L0 of draw 0 only, per encoder per corpus (no outcome peeking at test); (c) learned layer-weighted (softmax weights) head vs final-layer vs best-single-layer under L0 and L4.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: (a) Premium difference attributable to head vs to split family vs to sibling removal (three main effects in a 2x2x2 on speaker-paired deltas, cluster bootstrap). H: the sibling-removal main effect explains > 50% of the S0-S2 discrepancy on RAVDESS (i.e. the Ridge premium collapses toward the probe premium once same-cell siblings are removed), and all three effects are < 1 pp on CREMA-D. (c) H: layer-weighted WavLM has a larger L4-L0 premium than final-layer WavLM (final layer suppresses speaker information; cf. layer analyses of wav2vec2-family models), one-sided, family 3 encoders x 2 corpora.

program.name: M7 (corpus-structure manipulation on SUBESCO: takes per cell, sentences, speaker count, one factor at a time)
merged_from: D1 speech-song (its 'restricted vs P1 premium' puzzle)
program.rationale: B is the dossier's largest single compute item (10.25 GPU-h) and its fixed-budget design algebraically bound speaker count to repeat density, so it could not answer the question it was built for and was barred from explaining the RAVDESS-CREMA-D gap. Its unregistered c20r1 -> c20r2 comparison (premium ~6 -> ~16 pp) is nonetheless the key hint. SUBESCO's full 20 x 7 x 10 x 5 grid allows each structural factor to be varied alone with the others fixed. Combined with M1's cross-corpus corners this gives a within-corpus causal test of the moderator. One seed per block (B's confound) is replaced by 3 seeds.
program.design: SUBESCO full grid. Cells (speakers x sentences x takes): T1 20x10x1, T2 20x10x2, T5 20x10x5 (takes ladder); S2 20x2x2, S5 20x5x2 (sentence ladder; T2 shared as 20x10x2); K10a, K10b two complementary 10-speaker panels x10 sentences x2 takes (speaker ladder vs T2). Takes and sentences chosen by hash order fixed before outcomes. Protocols: Random StratifiedKFold(5) and StratifiedGroupKFold(5) by speaker, inner mirrors outer (practice-mirroring, full size; total budget varies by design and the exclusive-protocol UAR is reported alongside). CNN + ResNet-SE, 3 seeds. Fits: 7 cells x 2 protocols x 5 folds x 2 models x 3 seeds = 420, sizes 560-7,000 utterances.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: P_RG per cell (speaker-equal OOF, seed-averaged, speaker-cluster bootstrap on the 20 speakers; K10 cells on 10). H1: P_RG(T1) < P_RG(T2) < P_RG(T5) (monotone takes effect; Jonckheere-type ordered test via bootstrap of the two adjacent differences, both > 0). H2: P_RG(S2) > P_RG(S5) > P_RG(T2=S10) (fewer sentences, larger premium). H3: mean P_RG(K10a,K10b) - P_RG(T2) is smaller than P_RG(T5) - P_RG(T1) (speaker count is a weaker moderator than take density; reported as a difference with CI, one-sided). Holm family 4 per model.

program.name: M8 (naturalistic corpus check: MSP-Podcast, license-gated)
program.rationale: Every corpus in the program is acted and scripted, so the sibling and sentence channels cannot exist in naturalistic speech and the audit frame includes IEMOCAP-style corpora. MSP-Podcast (academic license free of charge, requires an institutional signature; v1.7+ has speaker IDs for >1,100 speakers and CC-licensed sources per lab-msp.com) is the right naturalistic contrast: it has only the speaker channel. Prediction from the mechanism account: a small but positive speaker-only premium comparable to CREMA-D's, not RAVDESS's. Because the license may not arrive, the arm is preregistered as conditional with a fixed decision date; if not obtained by the M0 freeze it is reported as not run and nothing else changes.
program.design: If licensed: 4-class (angry, happy, neutral, sad) subset, speakers with >= 20 utterances, subsampled to 6,000 utterances balanced by speaker cap; test blocks = 5 speaker folds; levels L0 (speaker-exclusive) and L1 (same speakers' other utterances, size-matched) only; CNN + ResNet-SE + HuBERT/WavLM heads; 3 seeds; 60 scratch fits (~45 s each) + heads.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: D_spk (L1-L0) speaker-paired. H: D_spk > 0 (Wilcoxon, cluster bootstrap over speakers) and D_spk < 0.5 x D_spk(RAVDESS) (one-sided two-sample bootstrap). Not part of any Holm family; reported as a single preregistered conditional test.

program.name: CUT: LOSO protocol arms (P1 LOSO 1,380 fits; D1 LOSO 552 fits)
program.rationale: ~21 GPU-h of the recorded 40 went to LOSO. Its only finding (LOSO > GroupKFold in 8/8 cells, Delta_GL negative) is a training-size artefact (23/24 vs 19/24 training speakers) that P1 itself could not disentangle and D1's LOSO secondaries were not conclusive in 4/4. M1's size-matched pools make the question moot; the practice-mirroring arm M1b uses 5-fold grouping, which is what the audited repositories that do group use. Information redundant.
program.design: None.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

program.name: CUT: Transformer and FNO from-scratch stacks
program.rationale: In every arm of the dossier (P1 8/8, A, B, D1, C) all four architectures gave the same sign and the same corpus ordering; the architecture factor never changed a decision and B's per-model interaction disagreement was itself unusable. Two stacks (simplest CNN, strongest ResNet-SE) plus two frozen SSL heads cover the 'not a small-CNN artefact' objection at half the cost, and the mechanism angle needs levels and interventions, not an architecture survey.
program.design: None.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

program.name: CUT: D1 RAVDESS speech-song channel contrast
program.rationale: 792 fits produced a song-minus-speech premium difference of -1 to -6 pp that was not conclusive for CNN and changed no claim; the speech half re-ran P1 on a 23x6 subset. Vocal channel is not a leakage mechanism. The RAVDESS structure it depended on (siblings, 2 sentences) is manipulated directly in M1 and M7.
program.design: None.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

program.name: CUT: P0 purposive 32-repo audit, its 6 non-split outcomes, P0.5 separate sample, and D1/D3/291/282 lineage sensitivity branches
program.rationale: Two audits estimated the same construct on overlapping frames with nearly disjoint samples and were never reconciled; the purposive-vs-random comparison was demoted to a 'working-model diagnostic' and never published; the five lineage branches all give 44/9/7 and envelopes within 0.3 pp. One audit with the lineage rule fixed in the public preregistration replaces all of them. The single retained extra field is test-set selection, which now links to M3-HPO.

program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

program.name: CUT: verification-only refits and corrective re-runs (S0 v1->v2 180 fits, S3 600 replay refits, C/P5 salvage machinery)
program.rationale: These consumed compute and weeks of governance without changing any number; they existed because provenance, cache identity, key custody and verifier timing were not fixed before the first fit. M0 fixes cache identity and the scorer/verifier freeze up front; the preregistration notes below replace the state-machine and receipt apparatus with a public timestamp and one independent recomputation.

program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

pipeline_order: PRE: write and publicly timestamp the preregistration (OSF + git tag); e-mail ESD license form; file MSP-Podcast institutional license request; fix license decision date
AUD: rebuild candidate frame, apply lineage rule, obtain NIST beacon pulse after the OSF timestamp, draw n=80; start CPU/human coding in parallel with all GPU arms
M0: manifests, duplicate/all-zero removal list, test-block generator, level samplers, log-mel + all-layer SSL caches for 6 corpora, freeze scorer + independent verifier, 2% smoke test
M1b: practice-mirroring Random vs GroupKFold on 6 corpora (headline figure)
M1: five-level exposure factorial on identical size-matched test blocks (saves checkpoints and embeddings)
M2: partial-dose speaker exposure (25/50/75%)
M3: leaky-inner variants and HPO-on-leaky-validation
M5: per-speaker normalisation and gradient-reversal interventions
M7: SUBESCO structure ladders (takes, sentences, speaker count)
M6: SSL head/split/sibling reconciliation and layer rule (cached features, light)
M4: speaker-ID probes, sibling nearest-neighbour analysis, layer-wise probe correlation (inference only)
M8: MSP-Podcast conditional arm if license obtained by the decision date; otherwise record 'not run'
SCORE: single one-shot scoring run with the frozen scorer; independent recomputation from raw per-utterance logits; AUD human-coding kappa; write-up
proposals.preregistration_notes: Public, immutable timestamp before any outcome: OSF registration plus a signed git tag of the frozen protocols, run_plan.csv, level samplers, scorer and verifier; the dossier's central credibility problem was that nothing could be called preregistered. Fixed before outcomes: corpus list, duplicate-removal list, test-block assignments (speaker folds x sentence folds), N_train per fold, the five exposure levels, model set (CNN, ResNet-SE, HuBERT-base, WavLM-base+), seeds, the SSL layer rule (chosen on L0 inner validation of draw 0 only), all Holm families (M1: 8 per corpus; M1b: 12; M2: 4 per corpus; M3: 6 + HPO 2; M5: 6 per corpus; M6: 6; M7: 4 per model; M8: 1 conditional), the equivalence margins (1 pp sibling, 1.5 pp spillover/sentence), and the SESOI language ('substantive' = >= 5 pp). Analysis unit is always the speaker (paired within identical test blocks); intervals are whole-speaker percentile bootstraps (10,000, fixed seed) and explicitly conditional on the frozen partition; draw ranges are reported separately. Every started fit enters a public ledger; a missing cell invalidates the dependent contrast (no available-case analysis). Verifier and scorer are hash-frozen before the first production fit and must not be edited after; any post-outcome correction demotes the affected arm to exploratory, so the verifier is exercised on synthetic fixtures (including rounded fields) during the smoke test. No LOSO, no additional architectures, no additional corpora after the tag; MSP-Podcast is the only conditional arm and its condition is a calendar date, not a result. Routing of every arm into main text vs supplement is fixed now: AUD + M1b headline figure; M1 channel table (all 6 corpora); M2/M3/M5 one row each in a mechanism table; M4(b), M6, M7, M8 supplement with one sentence each. Accuracy/macro-F1 are repository-only. Budget: 52 GPU-h planned (43 h of arms + ~20% for smoke tests, verification refits and one retry per failed unit), hard cap 70 GPU-h and 21 calendar days; if the cap is reached the arms are dropped in the reverse of the pipeline order (M8, M4 stays because it is inference-only, then M6, M7, M5, M3, M2), never by shrinking an arm's design.
risks: ESD license (research-only form by e-mail to the authors) or MSP-Podcast institutional agreement may not arrive before the M0 freeze; the program then loses its 'many sentences, few speakers' corner (ESD) or its naturalistic check (M8). Mitigation: EmoDB provides a weaker few-speaker corner; the preregistration states both corpora as calendar-conditional.

Size-matching in M1 shrinks training pools (RAVDESS 2-sentence blocks leave ~570 training items), lowering absolute UAR and possibly compressing all channel effects; M1b at full size is retained so the headline is not affected, but M1 channel shares may not transfer to full-size pipelines.

Level L3 vs L4 differ in both sibling presence and same-emotion labelling of the shared speaker-sentence cell, so D_sib is 'same-emotion near-duplicate exposure' and cannot separate acoustic near-duplication from label memorisation; M4(b) partly addresses this.

Gradient-reversal training can be unstable at a fixed lambda; a preregistered fixed lambda avoids tuning on outcomes but may under- or over-remove speaker information, weakening M5's discriminating test.

Cross-corpus ordering (H4) rests on n=6 corpora that differ in language, class set and recording conditions; the rank test is descriptive and a single corpus (e.g. ESD-ZH) behaving unexpectedly would not falsify the account.
Human double-coding of 20 audit units depends on two available coders and may yield kappa < 0.6, in which case the audit must be labelled AI-coded exploratory as preregistered.

Prior-art collision: the protocol effect itself (Ibrahim 2026, Zielonka 2022) and the speaker-in-emotion-embedding fact (arXiv:2202.01252) are established; the paper's novelty must rest on the audit plus the channel decomposition and the sibling-density explanation, and a reviewer may still judge the decomposition incremental.

Per-fit timings are extrapolated from A/B/D1 (RAVDESS ~15 s, CREMA-D ~65 s, SUBESCO-7000 ~60 s, ESD-3500 ~35 s); ESD and SUBESCO-full timings are untested on this GPU, so the 20% contingency and the 70 GPU-h cap matter.

Seed variability on small corpora (D1 seed SD 1-3 pp) is comparable to the sentence channel; 5 seeds on RAVDESS/EmoDB may still leave D_sent underpowered, in which case the preregistered result is 'not conclusive' rather than a null.
resulting_paper_claims: Claim 1 (audit): in a beacon-sampled probability sample of 80 public SER repositories from a frozen, publicly preregistered frame, the confirmed fraction with test-boundary speaker-nonexclusivity risk exceeds 50% (joint >=95% hypergeometric envelope reported), sentence-exclusive evaluation is essentially absent, and human-AI agreement on the endpoint is reported as kappa.

Claim 2 (headline effect, six corpora, four languages): Random-vs-speaker-grouped 5-fold evaluation inflates UAR in all six acted corpora for both from-scratch stacks and frozen SSL probes, with per-corpus premia that track sibling-take density rather than speaker count (RAVDESS and SUBESCO-full large; CREMA-D, EmoDB, ESD-EN, ESD-ZH small).

Claim 3 (channel decomposition): on identical test blocks with training size held constant, the nonexclusive premium separates into a universal cross-prompt speaker channel, a smaller same-sentence channel, and a sibling-take channel that is large in RAVDESS/SUBESCO and equivalent to zero in corpora without repeated takes; the RAVDESS-vs-CREMA-D gap is accounted for by the sibling and sentence channels.

Claim 4 (identity specificity and dose): the speaker channel accrues only to speakers actually exposed (no spillover to unexposed speakers in the same fold) and grows linearly with the fraction of test speakers exposed.

Claim 5 (model selection): leaky inner validation adds a further premium beyond outer leakage, and selecting hyperparameters on speaker-nonexclusive validation inflates the reported validation number by a stated margin without improving speaker-exclusive test performance.

Claim 6 (intervention): per-speaker normalisation and speaker-adversarial training attenuate the speaker channel by at least half but leave the sentence and sibling channels, so 'speaker normalisation' is not a substitute for speaker- and take-exclusive splitting.

Claim 7 (representation): emotion-model embeddings encode speaker identity well above chance; under nonexclusive training, test utterances whose nearest training neighbour is a sibling take are classified far more often correctly, and in SSL encoders the layer-wise premium co-varies with layer-wise speaker-probe accuracy; the head/split-family/sibling reconciliation explains the discrepancy between frozen-probe and Ridge premia.

Recommendation: enforce speaker exclusivity at every active boundary (test and validation), deduplicate repeated takes across boundaries, report sentence/prompt overlap, and publish grouping keys; corpus-specific expected inflation is given by the channel table rather than a universal discount.

proposals.angle: One-shot pipeline engineer: the whole program as one deterministic, resumable pipeline (one corpus stage, one feature/SSL cache, one seed table and split generator, one training harness, one scoring module, one number-checked insert), with every existing arm folded into a small number of unified factorials.
proposals.thesis: Speaker-nonexclusive evaluation is common in public SER code and inflates reported scores; the paper keeps that thesis but changes how it is evidenced. The redesigned program treats the prevalence audit and the effect study as two halves of one preregistered pipeline, and replaces the fragmented supplements (P1/A/B/C/D1/S0/S2/S3) with three factorials that share one data cache and one split table: a core outer-by-inner protocol factorial across seven corpora (subsuming P1 and A), a frozen-SSL probe factorial across encoder, layer, head, fold count and 20 partition draws (subsuming S0/S2/S3/S4 and the LOSO question), and a moderator block (speaker-count, repetition and prompt ladders plus a leakage dose-response ladder) that subsumes B and C. Two additions never run before, a fine-tuned wav2vec2 arm and a leaky-HPO arm, close the 'small-model artifact' and 'realistic failure mode' objections. The paper would then claim: prevalence with boundary type and human-verified reliability, a corpus-resolved premium with its outer/inner decomposition, the moderators that make RAVDESS-type corpora six times more inflatable than CREMA-D-type corpora, a monotone dose-response, and persistence of the premium under fine-tuned modern encoders.

program.name: INFRA: corpus preparation, shared caches, seed table, split generator
program.rationale: Every arm in the dossier rebuilt its own manifests, caches and split logic (P1 mel cache, S0 v1/v2 SSL caches with identity defects that forced a full re-run, S3 v1-v10 cache-name churn, D1 split manifest v1 rejected, B hygiene tooling). One shared stage with content-addressed caches and a single seed table removes that churn, and makes every later factorial cell comparable by construction (same audio bytes, same features, same folds). Seven corpora are prepared once: RAVDESS speech (24 spk, 8 cls, 1,440; CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, in hand), CREMA-D (91, 6, 7,442; ODbL/DbCL, in hand), SUBESCO full (20 spk x 7 emo x 10 prompts x 5 reps = 7,000; CC BY 4.0 on Zenodo, in hand), EmoDB (10, 7, 535; CC0 via audb: https://github.com/audeering/emodb), ESD-EN and ESD-ZH (10 spk x 5 emo each; research-only license form emailed to the maintainers, Google Drive download: https://github.com/HLTSingapore/Emotional-Speech-Data ), IEMOCAP (10 spk, standard 4-class 5,531 utt; USC release form https://sail.usc.edu/iemocap/ , academic only, conditional on the form being returned before the pipeline freeze). MSP-Podcast is not used: its academic license needs an institutional signatory (https://lab-msp.com/MSP/MSP-Podcast.html), it ships a fixed speaker-independent partition that is not the practice being audited, and its 400 h of audio would consume most of the SSL-cache budget.
program.design: (1) License check and byte manifest per corpus (relative path, bytes, SHA-256, speaker, label, prompt/sentence id, repetition, sex). Preregistered exclusions, applied uniformly: exact byte-duplicates keep the lexically first path; zero-variance audio dropped; stereo downmixed; all recorded in anomaly_registry.csv. ESD: fixed subset of 100 of the 350 parallel sentence ids per language chosen by SHA256('SER26|esd|'+sentence_id) order (5,000 utt per language, keeps the parallel-text structure, matches CREMA-D scale). IEMOCAP: standard 4-class merge (neu/hap+exc/ang/sad), improvised+scripted, speaker = session x gender (10 speakers). Native class sets are kept per corpus (no cross-corpus mapping). (2) Log-mel cache exactly as P1 (22.05 kHz mono, trim 30 dB, 64 mel, FFT 1024, hop 512, 128 frames, per-utterance z-score; SpecAugment train-only at fit time). (3) SSL cache: 16 kHz, torchaudio bundles WAV2VEC2_BASE, HUBERT_BASE, WAVLM_BASE_PLUS (weights SHA-pinned), all 13 hidden states time-mean pooled, stored float16 [N,13,768] per corpus x encoder, cache file name = SHA of (manifest SHA, bundle SHA, sr, trim, pooling, code SHA). (4) Seed table: split_seed(c,family,d) = u32(SHA256('SER26|split|c|family|d')); train_seed(c,model,d,fold) = u32(SHA256('SER26|train|c|model|d|fold')) so initialization is identical across all outer/inner cells and HPO configs (removes A's protocol-specific seed-stream confound); panel_seed(c,level,p) = u32(SHA256('SER26|panel|c|level|p')). (5) Split table (one CSV per corpus, hashed): outer Random = StratifiedKFold(5, shuffle, split_seed) ignoring speaker; outer Group = StratifiedGroupKFold(5, shuffle, split_seed, groups=speaker); LOSO deterministic by speaker id; inner random = train_test_split(0.25, stratify=label) allowing speaker overlap; inner grouped = GroupShuffleSplit(0.25) by speaker; draws d in 0..19 for the probe arm, d in 0..2 for training arms (draw index doubles as training seed, so seed SD now covers partition variability); plus DOSE halves and LADDER panels (see those arms). Assertions: zero speaker overlap for every grouped path, exactly-once OOF coverage, class-complete folds; failure aborts the pipeline before any fit.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: No estimand; gate stage. Preregistered acceptance: all overlap/coverage assertions pass; cache SHAs recorded in the frozen manifest; any corpus whose license is not in hand by the freeze date is recorded as 'not run' and every dependent cell is reported as missing (no re-planning).

program.name: PREREG: public pre-outcome registration and pipeline freeze
program.rationale: The dossier's single largest credibility loss is that nothing can be called preregistered: every arm relied on local mtime+hash freezes, the receipt chain broke at record 282, and routing of A/B/C/D1/S3 into the paper was decided after outcomes. One public, immutable freeze of run_plan.csv, the seed table, the analysis code and the manuscript slot of every arm, made before any audio is downloaded, is zero-cost and makes every downstream number confirmatory or exploratory by rule rather than by ruling.
program.design: OSF registration containing: this program document, run_plan.csv (every unit id = SHA256 of its config), seed table, split-generator code SHA, scoring-module code SHA, audit codebook and endpoint dictionary, Holm families F1-F7, SESOIs, GPU caps per arm, the fixed manuscript slot of every arm (main text: AUDIT, CORE table+decomposition, DOSE figure, FINETUNE line, LADDER slopes; supplement: SSLPROBE tables, HPO, per-model strata, accuracy/macro-F1), and the missingness rule (a unit that fails after one retry stays missing; its contrast is reported with the cell dropped, never re-planned). GitHub tag of the same tree; tag hash anchored with OpenTimestamps. Any later change goes in an append-only deviation file that the paper must cite.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None. Acceptance: registration timestamp precedes the first cache write (verified by the INFRA ledger).

program.name: AUDIT: probability audit of speaker-nonexclusivity risk in public SER code
merged_from: P0 candidate frame and search protocol
program.rationale: This arm is the paper's only novel contribution (the prior-art matrix shows the protocol effect itself is already published by Ibrahim et al. 2026 and Zielonka 2022), yet in the dossier it exists as three partially overlapping estimates (P0.5 20/30 execution-validated; S1 44/60 static; D2 44/60 on a repaired frame) with 2/60 sample overlap, no human coder, no boundary-type breakdown and no strata. One pass fixes all four: the lineage rule is fixed before any outcome, the sample is drawn once, every Y/N gets the P0.5 execution-validation tier, boundary type (test vs validation-only) is coded, strata are recorded, and a human blind-codes a subsample for kappa. The purposive 32-repo audit and the six non-speaker outcomes are cut: they reached no paper lineage and the purposive-vs-random comparison was self-classified as a working-model diagnostic.
program.design: Frame: rerun the P0 search protocol (GitHub best-match top-100 x 2 query families x 4 corpora; arXiv API top-100 per corpus; snowball) at a new fixed cutoff date, canonicalise URLs, apply the D2 lineage rule (executable-blob containment >= 0.90 with corroborator; fork/tree/blob-set identity; keeper = upstream > earliest > URL) with outcome columns absent by construction (screening happens before any adjudication). Eligibility E1-E8 as P0. Sample: n = 80 (up from 60; gives a 10.9 pp half-width at p = 0.5 with FPC on N ~ 290) by NIST beacon seed, hash-ordered priority list, sequential screening. Endpoint dictionary: Y_test (an active train/test path permits same-speaker on both sides), Y_val (only a train/validation or model-selection path permits it), N (all active paths verified speaker-exclusive and enumeration closed), U (undecidable/resource cap 20,000 files fixed in advance/no split). Evidence: static byte-verified entry-to-split chain with fragment hashes at a pinned commit AND the P0.5 tier-1 execution of the decisive split statement on a 4,444-row synthetic manifest with 16 row-order permutations, for every Y/N. Strata recorded per unit: repo_relation (paper-linked/official vs third-party vs no paper), target corpus, year, notebook vs script, framework, whether reported accuracy on RAVDESS/CREMA-D is stated. Reliability: a human coder blind-codes a hash-selected 25-unit subsample against the same codebook; Cohen's kappa vs the AI-assisted verdict is reported; preregistered rule: kappa < 0.6 relabels the audit 'exploratory'. Review budget: 2 CPU-review hours per unit, cap 200 h.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Primary: frame prevalence pi of Y = Y_test or Y_val, reported as confirmed fraction Y/n, partial-identification interval [Y/n, (Y+U)/n], and the exact hypergeometric joint >= 95% envelope (two one-sided 97.5% bounds, Bonferroni). Secondary: pi_test alone with the same machinery; prevalence by repo_relation stratum (paper-linked vs not) with Newcombe difference CI; exploratory: among paper-linked repos reporting RAVDESS or CREMA-D accuracy, reported accuracy for Y vs N (Mann-Whitney, descriptive). Directional expectation (not a test): pi >= 0.5 (lower confidence bound above 50%) and pi_test > pi_val; prevalence higher in non-paper code. No prevalence x effect multiplication.

program.name: CORE: outer x inner protocol factorial across seven corpora
merged_from: P1 controlled study (RR and GG cells, LOSO cut, FNO cut)
A outer/inner factorial (RG and GR cells)
program.rationale: P1 and A are the same experiment: A added the two missing cells (RG, GR) of a 2x2 that P1 had only sampled at RR and GG, and the identity O_R + I_G = P1 delta held to 0.0 pp on all 8 cells. Running the full 2x2 once, on every corpus, makes the decomposition (RAVDESS outer +9.99 vs inner +5.13 pp) a preregistered main-text result instead of a withdrawn supplement. LOSO from-scratch training (1,380 of P1's 1,620 fits, 85% of its 25 GPU-h) is cut: its only finding (LOSO > GroupKFold in 8/8 cells) is confounded with training-set size and is answered cheaply and without confound in SSLPROBE (E4). FNO is cut (same sign and magnitude as CNN in every cell; a non-standard choice needing justification). The multilingual contribution promised in plan revision 2 is delivered by adding EmoDB, ESD-EN, ESD-ZH, SUBESCO and IEMOCAP under the same protocol, which also puts IEMOCAP and EmoDB, which are in the audit frame definition, into the effect study. Tying the partition draw to the training seed removes the one-frozen-split limitation at zero cost.
program.design: Factors: corpus {RAVDESS, CREMA-D, SUBESCO-full, EmoDB, ESD-EN, ESD-ZH, IEMOCAP (conditional)} x model {CNN, ResNet-SE, Transformer; P1 frozen configs} x outer {Random, Group5} x inner {random, grouped} x draw/seed d in {0,1,2} x 5 folds = 7 x 3 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 5 = 1,260 fits. Training exactly as P1 (AdamW, batch 64, <= 100 epochs, cosine, early stop on inner weighted CE with patience 15, class weights from the fit subset, SpecAugment train-only, float32 deterministic). train_seed identical across the four outer x inner cells. Per-fit cost from the dossier (A: 40 s/fit average on RAVDESS+CREMA-D; B: 13 s/fit at 1-2k utterances): RAVDESS 20 s, CREMA-D 60 s, SUBESCO 55 s, EmoDB 8 s, ESD 45 s each, IEMOCAP 45 s -> 180 fits per corpus -> ~14 GPU-h; cap 20 GPU-h. Outputs per fit: predictions.csv with logits for every outer-test utterance, history.csv, run.json with SHAs; unit_id = SHA256(config).
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Unit = speaker; per speaker and cell, OOF UAR on that speaker's utterances, averaged over 3 draws and equal-weighted over 3 models. F1 (7 tests, Holm): Delta_pkg(c) = UAR(RR) - UAR(GG) > 0 for each corpus; paired two-sided Wilcoxon on speaker differences, 10,000 whole-speaker bootstrap percentile CI. F2 (14 tests, Holm): O_G(c) = RG - GG > 0 and I_G(c) = GR - GG > 0; interaction O_R - O_G reported with CI. F3 (1 test): between-corpus moderator, speaker-level Delta_pkg RAVDESS vs CREMA-D by 10,000-permutation cluster test; H: RAVDESS > CREMA-D. Descriptive: per-model strata, corpus-level Delta_pkg against speaker count, utterances/speaker and prompts/speaker across the 7 corpora (n = 7, no test), accuracy/macro-F1 in supplement. SESOI for 'practically meaningful' = 2 pp (preregistered).

program.name: HPO: hyperparameter search on leaky vs grouped inner validation
program.rationale: The dossier flags 'premium under hyperparameter search on leaky validation' as the realistic failure mode found in public code, never measured (P1 used fixed configs). It is a cheap extension of CORE: the same harness, one model, a small grid, and selection by inner validation. It tests whether the inflation is amplified when the practitioner tunes on a speaker-overlapping validation set, which is exactly what a Y_val repo in the audit does.
program.design: ResNet-SE only; RAVDESS and CREMA-D; cells RR and GG; draw d = 0; grid of 8 configs (lr {3e-4, 1e-3} x weight decay {1e-4, 1e-3} x dropout {0.1, 0.3}); each config trained on each of the 5 outer folds with the cell's inner split; per fold the config with the highest inner-validation UAR is selected and its outer-test predictions are used (no refit). 2 corpora x 2 cells x 8 configs x 5 folds = 160 fits, ~1.8 GPU-h; cap 3 GPU-h. The fixed-config comparator is the CORE d = 0 ResNet-SE cell (no extra fits).
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: F4 (2 tests, Holm): Delta_HPO(c) = [UAR(RR,hpo) - UAR(GG,hpo)] - [UAR(RR,fixed) - UAR(GG,fixed)] on speaker-paired UAR; H: Delta_HPO > 0 (tuning on a leaky validation set enlarges the premium); paired Wilcoxon + whole-speaker bootstrap CI. Secondary descriptive: distribution of selected configs under RR vs GG.

program.name: SSLPROBE: frozen-SSL probe factorial (encoder x layer x head x fold count x 20 partition draws)
merged_from: S0 v2 (trained linear probes on P1 splits)
program.rationale: S0, S2 and S3 are one design run three times with one factor changed each time (head, corpus), which is why the paper carries an unexplained 2-5x disagreement on RAVDESS between S0 (2.8-6.2 pp, trained probe, P1 split) and S2 (13.9 pp, Ridge, 20 draws) and never compares S3 to S2. Crossing head x split family inside one factorial resolves the discrepancy by design. Adding a layer factor answers S4's question (WavLM's small, fragile final-layer premium) at zero GPU cost because all 13 layers are already cached. Because Ridge has no early stopping, LOSO vs Group5 on identical features isolates the fold-count/training-size effect that P1 could not; a training-size-matched LOSO control closes it. All Ridge fits are CPU; the only GPU cost is the trained-probe head.
program.design: Corpora: all 7. Encoders: wav2vec2-base, HuBERT-base, WavLM-base+. Layer: {final (12), mid (6), mean of layers 1-12}. Head A: StandardScaler(train fold) + RidgeClassifier(alpha 1, cholesky, balanced), no inner validation. Head B: trained linear probe as S0 (AdamW 1e-3, batch 64, patience 15 on inner weighted CE, inner split mirrors outer). Protocols: Random5, Group5 for draws d in 0..19 (Head A) and d in 0..4 (Head B, final layer only); LOSO (one deterministic pass, Head A, all layers) plus LOSO-sub, in which the LOSO training set is subsampled to the mean Group5 training-speaker fraction (80%) by hash order. Ridge fits: 7 x 3 x 3 x 2 x 20 x 5 = 12,600 (~0.1 s each) + LOSO/LOSO-sub 7 x 3 x 3 x 2 x N_spk (175 speakers total) = 3,150; trained probes 7 x 3 x 2 x 5 x 5 = 1,050 fits at ~4 s = ~1.2 GPU-h; cap 2 GPU-h.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: E1 (F5a, 7 tests, Holm): per corpus, 3-encoder equal-weight Ridge-final Delta_RG > 0 on speaker-paired, draw-averaged UAR (Wilcoxon + whole-speaker bootstrap); plus S2's direction-stability descriptor (>= 18/20 positive and q05 > 0). E2 head effect (F5b, 7 tests): Delta_RG(trained probe) - Delta_RG(Ridge) on the same 5 draws, two-sided; preregistered reading: |E2| > 3 pp on RAVDESS attributes the S0/S2 discrepancy to head choice, otherwise to the split family. E3 layer effect (F5c, 21 tests = 7 corpora x 3 encoders): Delta_RG(mid) - Delta_RG(final) > 0 (speaker information is concentrated in early-mid SSL layers, so mid-layer probes should be more inflatable). E4 fold count (F5d, 7 tests): UAR(LOSO) - UAR(Group5) > 0 and UAR(LOSO-sub) - UAR(Group5) within a +/-1 pp equivalence band (TOST), which would attribute P1's LOSO > GroupKFold finding to training-set size, not protocol strictness.

program.name: LADDER: within-corpus moderator ladders (speaker count, repetition density, prompt diversity)
merged_from: B SUBESCO allocation diagnostic (cut: fixed-budget design binds speaker count to repeats)
program.rationale: The 6x RAVDESS-vs-CREMA-D gap is the paper's most interesting number and its least explained: speaker count (24 vs 91), utterances per speaker, prompts (2 vs 12) and classes are confounded, and B could not separate speaker count from repeats because its utterance budget was fixed. A budget-varying design on the two corpora that already have the needed structure separates the three moderators. CREMA-D (91 speakers) supports a speaker-count ladder at full per-speaker content; SUBESCO-full (5 repetitions x 10 prompts per speaker-emotion) supports repetition and prompt ladders at fixed speaker count. B's most interpretable comparison (c20r1 -> c20r2 tripled the premium) becomes a registered endpoint. D1 is cut: its channel contrast was not conclusive and changed no claim.
program.design: (a) CREMA-D speaker ladder: n_spk in {12, 24, 48, 91}, all utterances of each selected speaker; 3 sex-balanced hash-ordered panel draws per subsampled level, 1 at 91; ResNet-SE; cells RR and GG (the pipeline-level contrast the audit measures); draws d in {0,1,2}; 5 folds -> 10 panels x 2 x 3 x 5 = 300 fits (~2.9 GPU-h). (b) SUBESCO repetition ladder: reps/cell in {1, 2, 5} at 10 prompts and 20 speakers; prompt ladder: prompts in {2, 5, 10} at 5 reps and 20 speakers -> 5 distinct cells, 2 subset draws where subsetting occurs -> 9 panels x 2 cells x 3 draws x 5 folds = 270 fits (~2.3 GPU-h). Nested subsets by hash order so smaller levels are contained in larger ones. Ridge on cached SSL features is run on every panel at zero GPU cost as a replication with a second representation. Cap 7 GPU-h.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Panel-level Delta_pkg = UAR(RR) - UAR(GG), speaker-equal. F6 (3 tests, Holm), Jonckheere-Terpstra monotone trend with panel x draw as units: H1 Delta_pkg decreases with speaker count; H2 Delta_pkg increases with repetitions per cell; H3 Delta_pkg decreases with prompt diversity. Slopes with bootstrap CIs over panel draws x seeds. Descriptive: whether the ladder reproduces the observed RAVDESS premium when CREMA-D is reduced to 24 speakers (preregistered readout: CREMA-D-24 premium within the RAVDESS 95% CI counts as 'speaker count sufficient', otherwise 'not sufficient').

program.name: DOSE: leakage dose-response with a fixed prompt-disjoint test set
merged_from: C/P5 mechanism-exposure salvage (cut; its q = 1 case is one rung of this ladder)
program.rationale: P1 measured only 0% and 100% speaker overlap; C measured a single 22-utterance cross-prompt exposure with no inference and a key-exposure incident. A controlled-overlap ladder with a shared, fixed test set is an established design in the neighbouring depression-detection literature (arXiv 2604.14354 uses size-matched splits with a shared test set and an optionally included same-speaker subset) but has not been reported for SER; it turns C's descriptive pilot into a monotone-trend test and gives the paper the 'how much overlap is how bad' curve reviewers ask for.
program.design: RAVDESS and CREMA-D; CNN and ResNet-SE; outer Group5 folds for draws d in {0,1,2}. Each speaker's utterances are split into prompt-disjoint halves A/B (RAVDESS statement 01/02; CREMA-D the P5 sentence sets). Fixed test = half B of the test-fold speakers. Training = all utterances of train-fold speakers + a fraction q in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0} of half A of the test-fold speakers, selected by hash order within speaker x class so doses are nested. Inner validation grouped, drawn from train-fold speakers only, identical across doses. Class weights recomputed. 2 x 2 x 4 x 3 x 5 = 240 fits (~2.7 GPU-h); cap 4 GPU-h.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Per speaker, UAR on its half-B test items at each dose q, averaged over draws and both models. F7 (2 tests, Holm): Page's trend test across q with speakers as blocks, per corpus; H: UAR increases monotonically with q. Secondary (1 test): slope(RAVDESS) > slope(CREMA-D) by speaker-level permutation. Descriptive: q = 1 minus q = 0 compared with C's +6.42 / +1.85 pp point estimates; per-class recall shifts.

program.name: FINETUNE: fine-tuned wav2vec2-base under Random vs Grouped pipelines
program.rationale: Every claim registry in the dossier forbids extrapolating to fine-tuned SSL models, so the paper cannot answer the obvious objection that the premium is a from-scratch small-model artifact (grouped RAVDESS UAR was only 39-46%). Fine-tuning wav2vec2-base is the most common recipe in public SER code (Hugging Face tutorials; Wang et al. 2021 arXiv 2111.02735 report speaker-dependent 79.6% vs speaker-independent 73.0% WA on IEMOCAP, but from different data splits, not a same-pipeline contrast). A 12 GB GPU handles base-size fine-tuning with 3 s crops and batch 16. This is the most expensive addition and is scheduled late so a budget overrun only truncates it.
program.design: wav2vec2-base (torchaudio bundle, SHA-pinned), CNN feature encoder frozen, transformer layers and a mean-pool + linear head fine-tuned; lr 2e-5 encoder / 1e-3 head, AdamW, batch 16 of 3 s random crops, bf16 autocast (disclosed as non-bitwise-deterministic), max 15 epochs, patience 4 on inner weighted CE, gradient checkpointing. Cells RR and GG (inner mirrors outer). RAVDESS: 2 cells x 5 folds x 3 draws = 30 fits at ~6 min = 3 GPU-h; CREMA-D: 2 x 5 x 2 draws = 20 fits at ~25 min = 8.3 GPU-h. Per-epoch checkpoints for mid-fit resume. Cap 14 GPU-h; if the cap is hit, CREMA-D draw 1 is the first unit dropped (preregistered order).
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: F8 (2 tests, Holm): speaker-paired Delta_pkg = UAR(RR) - UAR(GG) > 0 per corpus (Wilcoxon + whole-speaker bootstrap). Secondary (2 tests): Delta_pkg(fine-tuned) - Delta_pkg(Ridge, final layer, same draws) on the same speakers, two-sided; preregistered reading: a positive difference means fine-tuning re-exposes speaker information that frozen final-layer features attenuate. Descriptive: absolute grouped UAR versus CORE's ResNet-SE.

program.name: SCORE: single scoring/statistics module, replay verification, number-checked insert
merged_from: S0/S2/S3 scoring reports and claim registries
paper numeric insert manifest and number checker

program.rationale: The dossier has at least seven scorers and verifiers written per arm, several after outcomes (A verifier 2 min after scoring; B 43 s after; C tolerance corrected post-score), plus a 107 KB number checker and 352 KB of check JSON for 38 macros. One scoring module that consumes the uniform predictions.csv layout of every arm, frozen and hashed at PREREG, computes every preregistered estimand from raw utterance predictions, and one independent re-implementation (as P1's, which achieved 0.0 numeric error) run once at the end replaces all of that. Replay of a 2% hash-selected subset of fits confirms bitwise determinism instead of S3's 600 audit refits.
program.design: Inputs: run_plan.csv, split table, manifests, every unit's predictions.csv. Pipeline: utterance predictions -> per-speaker OOF UAR per (arm, corpus, cell, model, draw) -> draw/model averaging as preregistered -> paired contrasts -> 10,000 whole-speaker percentile bootstrap (fixed seed) -> Wilcoxon (SciPy, zero_method wilcox) -> Holm within each of F1-F8 -> trend tests (Jonckheere, Page) -> TOST for E4. Missing units propagate to 'cell dropped' with the family size unchanged (p = 1 placeholder). Output: one results.json, one numeric_insert.tex of LaTeX macros, figure data JSON (Panel A audit composition; Panel B corpus-resolved Delta_pkg forest with O_G/I_G stacked; Panel C dose-response curves; Panel D ladder slopes), and a number-checker that verifies every macro in the manuscript against results.json. Independent re-implementation: a second script that imports nothing from the pipeline, reads only run_plan, splits, manifests and predictions, and must match every table to 1e-9. Replay: 2% of fits (hash-selected, all arms except FINETUNE) re-trained and compared bitwise.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: No new estimand. Acceptance: independent re-implementation max absolute error <= 1e-9 on every table; replay bitwise identical for float32 arms; number checker red = 0 before the manuscript is frozen.
