pipeline_order: PREREG: write run_plan.csv, seed table, split-generator and scoring code; OSF registration + GitHub tag + OpenTimestamps anchor (checkpoint: stages/prereg.done with tag hash)

INFRA-1 acquire: license checks (ESD form, IEMOCAP form, EmoDB audb, others in hand); byte manifests, anomaly registry, ESD sentence subset (checkpoint: manifests/*.sha256; a corpus without license by this point is marked not_run and never revisited)
INFRA-2 caches: log-mel cache on CPU; SSL all-layer cache on GPU, 3 encoders x 7 corpora, ~4 GPU-h (checkpoint per corpus x encoder file with content SHA; resumable per file)

INFRA-3 splits: generate the full split table for every arm and draw; run overlap/coverage/class-complete assertions; hash (checkpoint: splits/table.sha256; pipeline aborts here on any assertion failure)

AUDIT (CPU + human, runs in parallel with all GPU stages from here on): frame rebuild -> D2 lineage rule -> beacon-seeded n=80 sample -> static + execution-validation adjudication -> 25-unit human blind subsample -> stats (checkpoint per unit JSON with hash-bound receipt)
SSLPROBE-Ridge (CPU, parallel with GPU stages): 12,600 draw fits + LOSO/LOSO-sub (checkpoint per unit)

GPU-1 CORE: 1,260 fits in fixed order corpus -> model -> draw -> fold -> cell (RR,RG,GR,GG), ~15 GPU-h (checkpoint per fit: results/units/<unit_id>/DONE holding predictions SHA; the runner skips verified DONE units on restart)
GPU-2 DOSE: 240 fits, ~3 GPU-h (per-fit checkpoints)
GPU-3 LADDER: 570 fits, ~5 GPU-h (per-fit checkpoints); Ridge replication on the same panels on CPU
GPU-4 HPO: 160 fits, ~2 GPU-h (per-fit checkpoints)
GPU-5 FINETUNE: 50 fits, ~11 GPU-h, per-epoch checkpoints for mid-fit resume; preregistered drop order if the 14 GPU-h cap is hit
GPU-6 SSLPROBE trained probes: 1,050 fits, ~1.5 GPU-h (per-fit checkpoints)
GPU-7 replay verification: 2% hash-selected subset of float32 fits re-trained and compared bitwise, ~0.5 GPU-h
SCORE-1: single scoring module over all arms -> results.json, figure data, numeric_insert.tex
SCORE-2: independent re-implementation (no shared code) must match every table to 1e-9; number checker red = 0
PAPER: compile manuscript from the frozen slot map; any deviation cited from the append-only deviation file; artifact bundle (manifests, splits, predictions, code) published with the tag
proposals.preregistration_notes: Register before any download: run_plan.csv (unit ids = SHA256 of config; 1,260 CORE + 160 HPO + 1,050 probe + 570 LADDER + 240 DOSE + 50 FINETUNE = 3,330 GPU fits plus 15,750 CPU Ridge fits), the seed table strings, split-generator and scoring code SHAs, the audit codebook (Y_test/Y_val/N/U), and the fixed manuscript slot of every arm. Holm families are closed and named: F1 core premium (7), F2 decomposition (14), F3 corpus contrast (1), F4 HPO (2), F5a-d SSL probe (7/7/21/7), F6 ladder trends (3), F7 dose trends (2), F8 fine-tune (2); tests are two-sided Wilcoxon or trend tests at alpha 0.05 within family; directional hypotheses are stated but a significant reversal is reported as a reversal. SESOI: 2 pp for premiums, +/-1 pp equivalence band for E4. Unit of inference is the speaker for every paired contrast; whole-speaker percentile bootstrap with 10,000 replicates and fixed seed; draws and models are averaged within speaker, never treated as replicates. Missingness: one retry per fit for pre-test failures; a unit still missing stays missing, its cell is dropped, family sizes are unchanged (p = 1 placeholder); no re-planning. Budget: total cap 60 GPU-h, per-arm caps (CORE 20, DOSE 4, LADDER 7, HPO 3, FINETUNE 14, probes 2, INFRA 5, replay 1); the GPU stage order is fixed so overruns truncate the last arms, and the truncation order inside FINETUNE is preregistered. Corpus contingencies: IEMOCAP and ESD are 'conditional' units; if the license is not in hand at INFRA-1 the units are marked not_run and reported as such in the paper. Exclusion rules (exact duplicates, zero-variance audio, ESD 100-sentence subset, IEMOCAP 4-class merge) are fixed here. Audit: the lineage rule, the endpoint dictionary, the 20,000-file resource cap, n = 80, the beacon pulse time, the 25-unit human subsample and the kappa >= 0.6 rule are all fixed before screening. Non-determinism: FINETUNE uses bf16 autocast and is declared non-bitwise-reproducible; all other arms are float32 deterministic and replay-verified. No prevalence x effect-size product is computed. Any change after registration is written to an append-only deviation file that the paper must cite by entry number.
risks: License timing: ESD (email form) and IEMOCAP (USC release form) may not arrive before the freeze; the plan degrades to 5 corpora with the missing corpora reported as not_run, weakening the multilingual claim.

Per-fit cost estimates are extrapolated from A (40 s/fit) and B (13 s/fit); ESD, SUBESCO-full and IEMOCAP could cost 1.5-2x more, which the 60 GPU-h cap and truncation order absorb but at the expense of FINETUNE draws.
EmoDB (10 speakers) and ESD/IEMOCAP (10 speakers each) give only 2 test speakers per Group5 fold and n = 10 for the paired Wilcoxon; those corpora will have wide CIs and mainly contribute direction.

Fine-tuning on a 12 GB consumer GPU with bf16 is not bitwise deterministic and may hit OOM on longer CREMA-D batches; per-epoch checkpoints and a fixed 3 s crop mitigate but the arm is the most likely to be truncated.
The audit still measures what a code path permits, not what a reported number used; execution validation on a synthetic manifest confirms mechanism only, and the human-kappa subsample is small (25).

Prior art: the protocol effect on RAVDESS/CREMA-D is already published (Ibrahim et al. 2026; Zielonka 2022); the paper's novelty must rest on the audit, the decomposition, the moderator ladders, the dose curve and the fine-tune line, so a null in LADDER or DOSE removes a headline rather than the thesis.
Human coder availability for the audit subsample and 200 CPU-review hours are the wall-clock bottleneck, not GPU time; the audit must start on day one.
Merging heads and layers into one probe factorial raises the number of secondary tests (F5c has 21); results there are supplement-grade and must not be promoted post hoc.

SUBESCO-full contains near-duplicate takes; the repetition ladder deliberately includes them, so the r = 5 premium partly measures near-duplicate leakage, which is the intended construct but must be stated.
resulting_paper_claims: In a probability sample of n = 80 from a frame of ~290 public SER repository lineages, the confirmed fraction whose active train/test or train/validation path permits same-speaker membership is X% (partial-identification and exact hypergeometric envelope reported), with Y% at the test boundary specifically, higher in non-paper code than in paper-linked code, and human-AI coding agreement kappa = Z on a blind subsample.

Under one implementation, one feature cache and one split table, utterance-level random splitting inflates speaker-paired UAR relative to speaker-grouped splitting on every corpus tested (7 corpora, 3 architectures, 3 partition draws), with corpus-specific magnitudes from ~2 pp (CREMA-D) to ~15-20 pp (RAVDESS).

The inflation decomposes into an outer test-boundary component and an inner model-selection component (both positive, RAVDESS ~10 and ~5 pp), so validation-only nonexclusivity is itself inflationary; hyperparameter search on a speaker-overlapping validation set enlarges the premium further.

Corpus composition moderates the inflation: within CREMA-D the premium rises as speaker count falls, and within SUBESCO it rises with repeated takes and falls with prompt diversity, which accounts for (or fails to account for, preregistered readout) the RAVDESS-CREMA-D gap.

Inflation is dose-dependent: with a fixed prompt-disjoint test set, test-speaker UAR rises monotonically with the fraction of the speaker's other utterances placed in training, more steeply on RAVDESS than on CREMA-D.

The premium persists with frozen self-supervised features (three encoders, direction stable across 20 partition draws on all corpora), is larger for mid-layer than final-layer features, depends on head choice by a measured amount, and survives full fine-tuning of wav2vec2-base; the LOSO-over-GroupKFold advantage is a training-set-size effect, not protocol strictness.

Operational recommendation: enforce speaker exclusivity at every active boundary including validation, publish grouping information, and report corpus structure (speakers, takes, prompts) because it predicts how much a nonexclusive split will inflate.

proposals.angle: Audit-to-practice bridge: re-execute audited risk-positive repositories under their own split and under a speaker-exclusive split to measure the real-world premium distribution; make the audit cheaper and more defensible (frozen frame, stratified beacon sample, two blinded raters + adjudication, fixed n, public prereg); keep a trimmed controlled study that decomposes and moderates the premium; fold all SSL supplements into one draw-based arm.
proposals.thesis: The paper keeps its thesis (speaker-nonexclusive evaluation is common in public SER code and inflates reported performance) but closes the gap the current manuscript refuses to bridge: prevalence (audit) and effect size (controlled study) are joined by a third leg that measures inflation IN THE AUDITED CODE ITSELF, by minimally editing each runnable risk-positive repository to a speaker-exclusive split and re-running it on the same corpus with the same hyperparameters. The audit is rebuilt around one preregistered dedup rule, a stratified (paper-linked vs other) beacon-ordered sample of fixed size n=60, two blinded raters with kappa, and a separated test-boundary vs validation-only endpoint, so it can be called confirmatory. The controlled study is trimmed to what the thesis needs (Random vs speaker-grouped, outer x inner 2x2, three corpora, three probes, seed-plus-draw replicates) and extended by two cheap moderator arms (speaker count x sentence count; overlap dose-response) and one unified SSL arm (two heads, 13 layers, partial fine-tuning) that resolves the program's own unexplained S0-vs-S2 head discrepancy. Everything runs once, in a fixed order, with pre-frozen scorers and pre-assigned paper slots, under a 59 GPU-h target (70 GPU-h hard cap).

program.name: AUDIT-R (probability audit, redesigned)
program.rationale: The dossier shows the current headline (44/9/7 of 60 from N=286; envelope 61.9-92.0%) is sound in direction but indefensible in process: the lineage rule was chosen after outcomes were visible, five sensitivity branches move the envelope by <=0.3 pp yet consume text three times, no human ever coded a repository, no inter-rater statistic exists, 56/60 sampled repos have unknown paper linkage, and the Y endpoint conflates validation-only with test-boundary leakage. Governance (v4 acquisition discard, v63-v67 closure, D2 repair, erratum lineage) consumed weeks and moved the estimate by nothing measurable. The fix is to decide every rule before the draw and to publicly timestamp it, to stratify on the one covariate readers care about (paper-linked vs not), to separate the endpoint, and to replace the Bonferroni hypergeometric envelope with plain Wilson intervals on the confirmed and upper-bound fractions. Papers with Code cannot be a source (sunset 24 Jul 2025, redirects to Hugging Face; confirmed by search), so the frame is GitHub-only by design and stated as such. The EMO-SUPERB report that >80% of SER papers release no code (arXiv 2402.13018) motivates the paper-linked stratum: it is the part of the frame that speaks to the literature.
program.design: FRAME (frozen day 0, one pass, hash + OSF-registered): GitHub repository search (4 corpora x 2 query templates, top 100 best-match each, as before) PLUS GitHub code search on corpus-specific filename tokens that only a loader would contain (RAVDESS '03-01-0', CREMA-D '_DFA_', '_IEO_', IEMOCAP 'Ses01F_impro', EmoDB '03a01Fa'); union, canonicalize URL, snapshot default-branch commit SHA for every candidate on freeze day. DEDUP RULE fixed before screening and never revised: (i) GitHub fork/parent relation, (ii) identical top-level tree SHA, (iii) executable-blob containment >= 0.90 (blob-SHA set, closed suffix list) -> one lineage, keeper = earliest created_at. Count of merges reported once; no sensitivity branches. STRATUM (automated regex on snapshot README/description/description field): paper-linked = contains arxiv.org, doi.org, ieeexplore, aclanthology, or 'Interspeech'/'ICASSP' plus a title string; else other. SAMPLE: NIST beacon pulse at a preregistered UTC minute; order = SHA256(seed||candidate_id) within stratum; screen sequentially per stratum (eligibility E1-E5, 10-min cap per screen) until 30 eligible per stratum (n=60); if a stratum has <30 eligible, take all and record. Stopping is fixed: n=60, no extension, no replacement after rating starts. RATING: two independent, mutually blinded raters per repo: Rater A = human (author), Rater B = LLM agent with a frozen prompt and a byte-pinned evidence template; both must cite path:Lstart-Lend at the pinned commit for the decisive split statement(s) and the entry point that calls it; 60-min cap per rater per repo, cap exceeded -> U for that rater. ENDPOINTS coded per repo: Y_test (an active train->test/eval boundary permits same-speaker membership), Y_val (validation/model-selection only), N (all active paths verified speaker-exclusive), U; plus three secondary binary fields reused from P0 (test set used for checkpoint/hyperparameter selection; single split with no variance reported; augmentation applied before splitting) and the repo's top-line reported number (metric, value, corpus) if any. ADJUDICATION: disagreements on Y_test/N/U resolved by a third rater (second human) using only the two evidence records; all three records published. Reported: Cohen's kappa (A vs B) on the 4-level endpoint and on Y_test-vs-not. STATISTICS: primary = Y_test/n with Wilson 95% CI; partial-identification upper bound (Y_test+U)/n with Wilson CI; stratum-specific estimates and a stratum-weighted frame estimate using eligible-count weights; no finite-population correction beyond noting N; no Bonferroni envelope. Human budget ~60 h rating + 15 h screening + 10 h adjudication; 0 GPU.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Estimand: proportion of eligible public GitHub SER repository lineages (frame as defined, 4 corpora, freeze date) whose active train->test boundary permits same-speaker membership (Y_test), overall and by stratum. H1 (directional, preregistered): Y_test/n > 0.50 in the whole sample AND in the paper-linked stratum, treating U as non-positive (conservative); one-sided exact binomial test at alpha 0.05 for each (Holm over 2). Power at n=60, true 0.70 with 12% U: ~0.85. Secondary (descriptive, no test): Y_val-only fraction; kappa >= 0.6 is the preregistered reliability threshold below which the paper reports the human rater's verdicts as primary and flags the LLM pass as unreliable; within-corpus comparison of reported top-line accuracy between Y_test and N repos (Mann-Whitney, exploratory).

program.name: BRIDGE (re-execution of audited risk-positive repositories)
merged_from: P0.5 execution validation (synthetic manifest, AST fragment execution)
program.rationale: This is the missing leg. The manuscript explicitly forbids multiplying prevalence by effect size because nothing measures inflation in the audited code; P1 measures it only in the authors' own pipeline. The P0.5 execution-validation tier (4,444-row synthetic manifest, 384/384 adapter matches) was the tree's strongest evidence for the audit construct but established program mechanism only, never realized overlap or realized inflation, and is now historical. A real re-execution on the real corpus does three things at once: (a) yields the realized speaker overlap under the repo's native split (superseding the synthetic tier), (b) validates the static Y_test verdict (a static Y with zero realized overlap is a recorded false positive), and (c) gives the real-world premium distribution the thesis needs. My searches found no prior study that re-executes public SER repositories under corrected splits (EMO-SUPERB documents partition heterogeneity and non-reproducibility but does not re-run code), so this is a defensible novelty claim. Selection cannot be random with respect to runnability; the estimand is therefore stated over the runnable subset with full accounting of non-runnable cases.
program.design: POPULATION: Y_test repos from AUDIT-R (expected ~40). ORDER: the beacon order already fixed by AUDIT-R, alternating strata (paper-linked first). PER-REPO RUNNABILITY PROTOCOL (all pre-specified): (1) corpus in hand: RAVDESS, CREMA-D (in hand), EmoDB (CC0 on Zenodo, download day 0), IEMOCAP only if the USC SAIL academic license is granted by the preregistered freeze date (request submitted day 0; if not granted, IEMOCAP-only repos are logged 'not runnable: data license' and reported); (2) engineering cap 4 h to obtain one complete native-split training+evaluation run (environment pinning, data path edits, notebook -> script via nbconvert, no model/hyperparameter/epoch changes; every edit is a published diff); (3) compute cap: a 1-epoch timing probe x declared epochs must be <= 1.0 GPU-h per run, else logged 'not runnable: compute'; (4) stop when 12 runnable repos are obtained or 24 attempts are exhausted, whichever first (~100 engineering hours max). ARMS per runnable repo: NATIVE = repo's own split exactly as shipped; EXCLUSIVE = the minimal edit replacing the decisive split call with the speaker-grouped analogue that preserves fold count/test fraction (train_test_split -> GroupShuffleSplit; (Stratified)KFold -> StratifiedGroupKFold; fixed lists -> speaker-disjoint lists of the same size), speaker parsed from the corpus filename convention; if the repo also selects on the test set, that behaviour is kept identical in both arms (documented as 'protocol-only counterfactual'). 3 replicates per arm (replicate = repo's split seed and training seed, where exposed; else 3 training seeds). Both arms write per-utterance predictions so UAR can be recomputed uniformly. Recorded per repo: metric as the repo computes it, UAR from predictions, realized train/test speaker overlap fraction under NATIVE (must be >0 to confirm Y_test), reported top-line number from README/paper, wall/GPU seconds. GPU: 12 repos x 2 arms x 3 reps = 72 runs at ~0.4 GPU-h mean (cap 1.0) ~29 GPU-h + ~3 GPU-h for timing probes and abandoned attempts; hard cap 34 GPU-h.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Primary estimand: over runnable Y_test repos, the per-repo real-world premium Delta_j = M_native - M_exclusive in the repo's own primary metric (3-replicate mean), summarized by median and IQR; secondary Delta_j in UAR. H1 (directional): median Delta_j > 0, one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank across repos (n >= 10 required; if n < 10 the arm is reported descriptively with sign counts only). Pre-specified descriptive targets: fraction of repos with Delta_j >= 5 pp; reproducibility gap R_j = reported - M_native (median, sign count); construct check = number of static-Y_test repos with realized overlap 0 (expected 0). Pre-specified moderator prediction: Delta_j is larger for RAVDESS-only repos than CREMA-D-only repos (Mann-Whitney, one-sided, exploratory because cell sizes are uncontrolled). Comparison to P1-T: each Delta_j is plotted against the P1-T premium for the same corpus; no formal test.

program.name: P1-T (controlled study, trimmed and decomposed)
program.rationale: P1 is the paper's only prospectively frozen confirmatory content and must stay, but 1,380 of its 1,620 fits (85%, ~21 GPU-h) are LOSO, whose only new message (LOSO scores above GroupKFold because it trains on more speakers) is a training-size confound irrelevant to the thesis and already known. FNO is a non-standard probe found in no audited repo; dropping it costs nothing. Experiment A (240 fits) is the one arm that decomposes outer-test leakage from leaky inner model selection (RAVDESS O_G +9.99, I_G +5.13; CREMA-D O_G +1.89, I_G +0.68) and was excluded from the paper only because its verifier was corrected after outcome visibility; folding it into the main 2x2 design removes the 'inner validation also changes' caveat that the paper flags four times. Using one frozen split per protocol left the 'split artifact' question to S2; pairing each replicate with a fresh draw makes the 3-replicate SD honestly include partition variance. EmoDB (10 speakers, 535 utterances, CC0) is in the audit frame and is nearly free to add; it gives a third anchor corpus with the smallest speaker count.
program.design: Corpora: RAVDESS speech (1,440 utt, 24 spk, 8 classes), CREMA-D (7,442 utt, 91 spk, 6 classes), EmoDB (535 utt, 10 spk, 7 classes; CC0). Features: P1 frozen recipe (22.05 kHz, 30 dB trim, 64 log-mel, 128 frames, per-utterance z-score, train-only SpecAugment). Models: CNN, ResNet-SE, Transformer (P1 configs, unchanged; FNO dropped). Design: outer split {Random StratifiedKFold(5), Grouped StratifiedGroupKFold(5) by speaker} x inner validation {random 25% with overlap, grouped GroupShuffleSplit 25%} = 4 cells (RR, RG, GR, GG). Replicates r=0,1,2: replicate r uses outer/inner draw seed r AND training seed r, shared across models and cells within corpus (so cells are paired on identical outer test folds within a replicate). Training exactly as P1 (AdamW, batch 64, <=100 epochs, patience 15 on weighted val CE, restore best, test touched once). Fits: 3 corpora x 3 models x 4 cells x 5 folds x 3 reps = 540 fits; ~330 s/fit weighted mean for CREMA-D, ~25 s RAVDESS, ~8 s EmoDB -> ~6.5 GPU-h. Duplicates and the all-zero CREMA-D file are removed by a preregistered hygiene rule (exact-duplicate groups collapsed to one file, all-zero file dropped) with counts reported. Outputs: per-utterance logits, OOF predictions per cell.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Speaker-paired UAR contrasts, each per-speaker value averaged over 3 replicates and equal-weighted over the 3 models (per-model values reported descriptively): RR-GG (pipeline premium), RG-GG (outer-test leakage under grouped inner, O_G), GR-GG (inner-selection leakage under grouped outer, I_G). H1 per corpus: all three > 0 (one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank on speaker differences; whole-speaker percentile bootstrap 10,000 reps for 95% CI). Confirmatory family = 3 corpora x 3 contrasts = 9 tests, Holm alpha 0.05. Corpus-interaction (preregistered, replaces the missing test): RR-GG(RAVDESS) - RR-GG(CREMA-D) with a two-sample speaker-cluster bootstrap CI; H1: difference > 5 pp. Prior points from the frozen artifact: RAVDESS RR-GG ~17 pp, CREMA-D ~2.5 pp, O_G ~10/1.9, I_G ~5/0.7; EmoDB unknown, predicted RR-GG > 10 pp.

program.name: MOD (speaker-count x sentence-count moderator on CREMA-D)
program.rationale: The reviewer's obvious question, why RAVDESS inflates ~6x more than CREMA-D, is unanswered; speaker count (24 vs 91), sentences per speaker (2 vs 12), classes, and recording design are confounded. B spent 10.25 GPU-h on SUBESCO showing the premium roughly triples from 20x1 to 20x2 takes and reaches 31-41 pp at 10x4, but its fixed-budget design bound speaker count to repeats, it was on a third corpus, and it was barred from explaining the RAVDESS-CREMA-D gap. C/P5 spent 144 fits and a key-exposure incident on a +4.57 pp descriptive pilot with no inference. Replacing both with a small factorial on CREMA-D itself, varying speakers and sentences separately, directly tests the two candidate moderators on the corpus whose gap motivated them, for ~3 GPU-h.
program.design: Corpus: CREMA-D after P1-T hygiene, intensity XX plus other levels as in P1 (all files retained). Factor S (speakers): 91 (all) vs 24 (12F+12M panel, hash-selected; three disjoint-as-possible panels, one per replicate). Factor T (sentences): 12 (all) vs 3 (a fixed 3-sentence subset {IEO, TIE, DFA}, hash-chosen day 0; one subset per replicate). Four conditions: (91,12) = P1-T CREMA-D (reused, not refit), (24,12), (91,3), (24,3). Protocol: RR vs GG cells only (Random outer+inner vs grouped outer+inner; 5 folds). Models: CNN, ResNet-SE. Replicates 3 (panel/subset draw + split draw + training seed). Fits: 3 new conditions x 2 protocols x 5 folds x 3 reps x 2 models = 180 fits on smaller data (~2.5 GPU-h; 3 with buffer). Estimator per condition: speaker-paired RR-GG premium, averaged over models and replicates.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Estimand: RR-GG premium P(S,T) per condition, and the two marginal moderator effects M_S = P(24,·) - P(91,·) and M_T = P(·,3) - P(·,12) (each averaged over the other factor). H1 (directional): M_S > 0 and M_T > 0; test = speaker-cluster bootstrap CI of each difference (10,000 reps; for the 24-speaker conditions the bootstrap resamples panels' speakers; conditions sharing speakers are paired, others independent); reject if the one-sided 95% bound excludes 0 AND the point estimate exceeds 2 pp. Prediction (from B and RAVDESS): M_T is the larger of the two; P(24,3) approaches the RAVDESS premium (>10 pp). Interaction reported descriptively.

program.name: DOSE (fraction of test speakers exposed in training)
program.rationale: The audit endpoint is 'permits overlap', which in practice ranges from a few shared speakers to 100%; P1 measured only 0% and 100%. BRIDGE repos will show intermediate realized overlap, so the paper needs a within-pipeline dose curve to interpret them, and this is the cleanest exposure manipulation (outer test fixed, inner grouped) that C/P5 attempted with a far more fragile substitution design.
program.design: Corpora: RAVDESS, CREMA-D. Outer: StratifiedGroupKFold(5) by speaker; each test-fold speaker contributes only a fixed emotion-stratified half of their utterances to the test set (the same half at every dose, so the test set is constant across doses). Dose d in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0} = fraction of test-fold speakers (hash-ordered) whose OTHER half is added to the training set; inner validation always grouped (speaker-disjoint from test). Models: CNN, ResNet-SE. Replicates 3 (draw + seed). Fits: 2 corpora x 4 doses x 5 folds x 3 reps x 2 models = 240 fits (~3.5-4 GPU-h). Per-speaker UAR on the fixed half-test-set per dose.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Estimand: per-corpus dose curve U(d) of speaker-paired UAR, and slope beta from a per-speaker regression of UAR on d with speaker-cluster bootstrap CI. H1: beta > 0 in both corpora (one-sided, bootstrap 95% lower bound > 0), and U(0.25) - U(0) > 0 (speaker-paired Wilcoxon, one-sided; Holm over the 4 tests). Secondary: linearity check (U(0.5) vs midpoint of U(0), U(1)); RAVDESS slope > CREMA-D slope (two-sample cluster bootstrap, descriptive).

program.name: SSL-U (unified frozen-representation and fine-tuning arm)
program.rationale: S0, S2 and S3 answer the same question (does the premium survive frozen SSL features) with two different heads and two split families, and they disagree by 2-5x on RAVDESS (S0 linear probe 2.8-6.2 pp vs S2 Ridge 12.4-15.4 pp on identical features) without anyone examining why; S3 transplants S2 to SUBESCO; S4 (layer question) was never run although WavLM's fragile 0.9 pp / 16-of-20 premium is exactly the final-layer-artifact case. One arm that extracts all 13 hidden layers once (same forward pass, mean-pooled, ~400 MB per corpus) and runs both heads on the same 20 draws resolves the head puzzle, answers the layer question, and adds the one thing the claim registries forbade extrapolating to: a (partial) fine-tuned encoder. SUBESCO full (7,000 utt, 5 takes) vs the 980-utterance repetition-clean panel is included because the pair isolates the near-duplicate-take pathway for free.
program.design: Encoders: wav2vec2-base, HuBERT-base, WavLM-base+ (torchaudio bundles, weights SHA-pinned). Extraction: 16 kHz, 30 dB trim, all 13 hidden layers, time-mean (and mean+std for the final layer as a pooling secondary). Corpora: RAVDESS, CREMA-D, EmoDB, SUBESCO-980 (repetition-clean panel), SUBESCO-full (7,000 utt with all 5 takes); ~2 GPU-h extraction. Splits: 20 preregistered draws, StratifiedKFold(5) vs StratifiedGroupKFold(5) by speaker (S2 seed rule). Heads: H-Ridge = StandardScaler+RidgeClassifier(alpha=1, balanced) on every layer (CPU, ~40k fits, ~15 CPU-h); H-Probe = early-stopped linear probe (S0 contract: AdamW, class-balanced CE, grouped/random inner val mirroring outer) on the final layer only (3,000 fits, ~2.5 GPU-h). FT arm: WavLM-base+ with top 4 transformer layers + attentive-pool head trainable, fp16, 3 s crops, batch 16, 8 epochs, early stop on inner val (grouped under grouped outer, random under random outer); RAVDESS, CREMA-D, EmoDB; outer Random vs Grouped x 5 folds x 3 replicates = 90 fits (~9 GPU-h, cap 12). Per-draw speaker-equal OOF UAR contrast Delta = UAR_random - UAR_grouped.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: (1) Primary per corpus: equal-weight 3-encoder Ridge final-layer Delta series over 20 draws; readout direction-stable positive iff >= 18/20 positive and empirical 5th percentile > 0 (S2 rule); H1: stable positive on all five corpus panels. (2) Head effect (resolves S0 vs S2): per draw, Delta(Ridge) - Delta(Probe) on RAVDESS and CREMA-D; H1: > 0 on RAVDESS (paired Wilcoxon over 20 draws, one-sided; Holm over 2 corpora). (3) Layer effect: Spearman correlation between layer index and mean Delta per encoder x corpus; H1: negative for WavLM-base+ on both anchor corpora (premium concentrated below the final layer). (4) Repeats: Delta(SUBESCO-full) - Delta(SUBESCO-980), paired by draw; H1: > 0. (5) Fine-tuning: speaker-paired premium under FT vs H-Probe frozen, same folds; H1: FT premium > frozen-probe premium on RAVDESS (speaker-cluster bootstrap 95% lower bound > 0); CREMA-D and EmoDB reported. Families: tests (2)-(5) form one Holm family of 6.

program.name: P1 LOSO arm (1,380 fits)
program.rationale: 85% of P1's compute (~21 GPU-h) for a secondary contrast that is confounded with training-set size (LOSO trains on 23/24 or 90/91 speakers vs 19-20 or 72-73), yields 5 of the paper's 5 non-rejections, and adds nothing to the thesis of nonexclusive vs exclusive evaluation. The single sentence 'LOSO is not stricter than 5-fold GroupKFold' can cite the frozen 2026 artifact if wanted; it does not need to be re-run.
program.design: None.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

program.name: D1 RAVDESS speech-song matched panel (792 fits)
program.rationale: Its speech half is a P1 sub-replication on a 23-actor x 6-class subset; its song-minus-speech contrast (-1 to -6 pp) was not conclusive for CNN and all four Random-LOSO secondaries were not conclusive; 70% of its fits were LOSO; the final manuscript dropped it. Vocal channel is orthogonal to the thesis.
program.design: None.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

program.name: B SUBESCO allocation (2,880 fits) and C/P5 mechanism salvage (144 checkpoints)
program.rationale: B: largest compute item (10.25 GPU-h), fixed-budget design binds speaker count to repeats so the two moderators cannot be separated, one seed per block, on a corpus different from the one whose gap it was meant to explain; ended as a routing sentence. C/P5: substitution design with no admissible inference (shared base/validation across pairs), CNN-only, key-exposure incident, +4.57 pp below its own 5 pp threshold. Both are superseded by MOD (moderators varied separately on CREMA-D) and DOSE (exposure with fixed test set and admissible cluster inference). SUBESCO is retained only inside SSL-U where the full-vs-repetition-clean pair measures the repeat pathway.

program.name: P0 purposive audit (32 repos x 38 fields), 7-outcome risk battery, purposive-vs-random comparison
program.rationale: The purposive layer was reclassified as a 'working-model diagnostic' with no design-based inference and appears in no paper lineage; 6 of the 7 coded outcomes never reached any manuscript; the Newcombe/Fisher/Holm apparatus over 7 outcomes was unused. Three of the secondary fields (test-set selection, single split no variance, augmentation before split) are cheap and are retained as descriptive columns inside AUDIT-R; the rest is dropped.

program.name: P0.5 synthetic-manifest execution validation and S1 lineage sensitivity branches (D1/D3/291/N282)
program.rationale: The synthetic-manifest tier verified only that split code behaves as read (384/384 matches) and is fully subsumed by BRIDGE, which runs the real split on real data and records realized overlap. The four lineage branches all give 44/9/7 and envelopes within 0.3 pp; AUDIT-R fixes one dedup rule before the draw, so there is nothing to be sensitive about and no erratum lineage to maintain.

program.name: P4 multi-corpus queue (ESD, CaFE, URDU, ShEMO, EMOVO, EmoDB-v2.5 under the P1 protocol)
program.rationale: The multilingual-sensitivity contribution was abandoned in the original program and is not needed by the thesis; running 5 more corpora under the 4-model P1 protocol would cost 20-30 GPU-h and produce a per-corpus premium table that cannot be modelled (n<=8 corpora) and that Ibrahim et al. 2026 / Zielonka 2022 / SERAB already partially cover. Only EmoDB (CC0, tiny, in the audit frame) enters P1-T and SSL-U; SUBESCO enters SSL-U only. ESD (license by e-mail to the NUS authors, research-only) and MSP-Podcast (free academic license, but podcast speech with hundreds of speakers is outside the audit frame) are noted as out of scope; IEMOCAP (USC license) is requested only to make IEMOCAP repos runnable in BRIDGE.

pipeline_order: Day 0: request IEMOCAP academic license (USC SAIL); download EmoDB (Zenodo, CC0) and SUBESCO-full; write and freeze the single protocol document covering all six arms (frame rules, dedup rule, strata, endpoints, rater prompts, runnability caps, scorer code with synthetic-fixture tests for every arm); register it on OSF with the candidate-frame hash; obtain the NIST beacon pulse and derive the AUDIT-R sample order.

Week 1: build shared feature caches (P1 log-mel recipe for RAVDESS/CREMA-D/EmoDB after the hygiene rule; SSL-U all-layer extraction for the five corpus panels, ~2 GPU-h); hash and freeze caches; start AUDIT-R sequential screening (human) and blinded rating (Rater A human, Rater B LLM) in beacon order.

Weeks 1-3 (GPU queue, fixed order, no result-dependent stopping): P1-T (540 fits) -> DOSE (240 fits) -> MOD (180 fits) -> SSL-U probes (3,000 fits) -> SSL-U fine-tune (90 fits); SSL-U Ridge layer sweep on CPU in parallel; AUDIT-R rating continues on the human/CPU side.
Week 4: AUDIT-R adjudication by the third rater; freeze Y_test set and kappa; write the BRIDGE attempt order (beacon order, strata alternated).

Weeks 4-8: BRIDGE runnability attempts in order (4 engineering-hour cap each, 1-epoch timing probe, 1.0 GPU-h per-run cap) until 12 runnable repos or 24 attempts; run NATIVE and EXCLUSIVE arms x 3 replicates for each; publish diffs.

Week 9: one-shot scoring of every arm with the frozen scorers in the order AUDIT-R, P1-T, DOSE, MOD, SSL-U, BRIDGE; independent re-implementation check on committed prediction files only; fill the pre-assigned paper slots (Fig. 1A audit by stratum; Fig. 1B BRIDGE real-world premium distribution overlaid on P1-T premiums; Table 1 P1-T 2x2 by corpus; one paragraph each for MOD, DOSE, SSL-U); no arm is re-routed after outcomes.
proposals.preregistration_notes: One public, timestamped registration (OSF) covers all arms before any draw or fit; internal freeze receipts are replaced by that timestamp plus a git tag. Fixed decisions that may not be revisited after outcomes: the dedup rule and stratum regex; n=60 with 30 per stratum and no extension; the Y_test/Y_val/N/U endpoint dictionary; the 60-minute rater cap; kappa threshold 0.6; BRIDGE runnability caps (4 engineering h, 1.0 GPU-h per run, 12 repos or 24 attempts) and the minimal-edit rule (splitter substitution only, preserve fold count/test fraction, keep any test-set selection identical in both arms); replicate seeds and draw seeds (SHA256 of fixed strings); the hygiene rule for duplicates and the all-zero file; SESOI 5 pp for corpus interaction and 2 pp for moderator effects; every Holm family listed above with its size; the paper slot of every arm regardless of direction (no promotion or demotion on effect size). Scorers and verifiers for all arms are written, tested on synthetic fixtures (including rounded-field tolerance cases), and hashed before the first fit; a verifier written after a score report is not a verifier. Any deviation goes into one deviation log with a timestamp; no sensitivity branches are created post hoc. Reporting rules: BRIDGE reports every attempted repo (runnable, not runnable with reason, excluded for compute) and every diff; AUDIT-R reports all three rater records per repo; the prevalence-times-effect multiplication remains forbidden, but the paper may now state the measured real-world premium distribution in risk-positive code directly. Compute: 59 GPU-h target, 70 GPU-h hard cap checked before each unit; if the cap is reached the remaining units are reported as incomplete, in queue order, with no design shrinkage.
risks: BRIDGE runnability may be low: P0.5 found 19/30 repos are student/hobby code, often Kaggle-path notebooks with missing dependencies; if fewer than 10 runnable repos are obtained within 24 attempts the primary Wilcoxon is not run and the arm becomes descriptive, which weakens the bridge claim (mitigation: the 24-attempt cap and stratum alternation are fixed in advance so the shortfall is itself a reportable finding about runnability).

IEMOCAP license may not arrive by the freeze date; IEMOCAP-only repos (7/30 in the P0.5 sample) then fall out of BRIDGE as 'not runnable: data license', biasing the runnable subset toward RAVDESS/CREMA-D code.

Selection into BRIDGE is not random with respect to code quality or compute size (1.0 GPU-h cap excludes heavy fine-tuning repos), so the premium distribution is over 'runnable, cheap, risk-positive' code only; the paper must state this estimand explicitly.

Minimal-edit ambiguity: some repos have several split sites or hard-coded speaker lists; the rule 'substitute the decisive splitter only' may need judgment, and every such judgment must be logged and diffed before the exclusive run.
Two-rater design still uses an LLM as Rater B; if kappa < 0.6 the LLM pass is discarded per protocol and the audit rests on one human rater plus adjudication, reducing the reliability claim.

The partial fine-tuning arm may not fit or may be slow on a 12 GB RTX 5070 for CREMA-D (batch 16, fp16, 3 s crops); its 12 GPU-h cap could truncate CREMA-D replicates, in which case they are reported incomplete in queue order.

Human time (~85 h audit + ~100 h BRIDGE engineering) is the binding constraint, not GPU; a single author cannot both rate and engineer in parallel, so the 9-week calendar assumes at least one additional human for adjudication and part of the engineering.

Prior-art risk: Ibrahim et al. 2026 and Zielonka 2022 already report the protocol effect on the same corpora; the controlled arms are replication/extension, and the paper's novelty rests on AUDIT-R (stratified, rated, public prereg) and BRIDGE (re-execution of audited code). If a re-execution study appears before submission, the contribution narrows to the linkage.
resulting_paper_claims: Claim 1 (audit, confirmatory): in a preregistered, stratified probability sample of 60 eligible public GitHub SER repository lineages evaluating on RAVDESS/CREMA-D/IEMOCAP/EmoDB, the fraction whose active train-test boundary permits same-speaker membership exceeds 50% overall and in the paper-linked stratum (Wilson CIs reported; inter-rater kappa reported; validation-only leakage reported separately).

Claim 2 (bridge, new): among runnable risk-positive repositories re-executed on their own corpus with only the splitter replaced by a speaker-exclusive one, the median real-world premium in the repo's own metric is positive (distribution, IQR, fraction >= 5 pp, and reproducibility gap reported), realized speaker overlap under the native split confirms the static verdicts, and RAVDESS repos inflate more than CREMA-D repos.

Claim 3 (controlled, confirmatory): under a fixed pipeline on RAVDESS, CREMA-D and EmoDB, the Random-minus-Grouped premium is positive and decomposes into a positive outer-test component and a positive inner-selection component (2x2), with a corpus interaction (RAVDESS minus CREMA-D > 5 pp) that is not a split artifact (replicates include partition draws).

Claim 4 (moderators): on CREMA-D itself, reducing speakers to 24 and sentences to 3 raises the premium toward the RAVDESS level, with sentence count the stronger moderator; the premium rises monotonically with the fraction of test speakers exposed in training, already positive at 25% exposure.

Claim 5 (representations): the premium persists across frozen wav2vec2/HuBERT/WavLM features on five corpus panels, is head-dependent (Ridge > early-stopped probe on RAVDESS, explaining the earlier S0/S2 discrepancy), is concentrated below the final WavLM layer, is amplified by repeated takes (SUBESCO full vs repetition-clean), and persists under partial fine-tuning.

Operational recommendation, now backed by all three legs: enforce speaker exclusivity at both the test and the model-selection boundary, publish grouping information, and treat unreported protocol as a risk factor whose typical cost is the measured real-world premium distribution rather than a single universal correction.

judgements.lens: Senior SER researcher / ICASSP area chair: will the program yield a 4-page paper that is accepted and cited; are the claims the right claims given that the Random-vs-speaker-independent effect on RAVDESS/CREMA-D is already published (Ibrahim, Ghoraba & Ghoraba, Sci. Rep. 16:19584, 2026, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-58836-w; Zielonka et al. 2022); are the additions novel relative to the literature (checked: no prior SER study re-executes public repositories under corrected splits; the only controlled-overlap/dose precedent is depression detection, arXiv 2604.14354; EMO-SUPERB arXiv 2402.13018 standardises partitions but does not re-run code); and do the cuts remove anything reviewers would demand.

scores.angle: Confirmatory minimalist (22 GPU-h): one preregistered audit + one RR/RG/GR/GG factorial on 3 corpora x 4 representations + partial WavLM fine-tune, single 16-test Holm family
scores.comments: Cleanest statistics in the set: one family, speaker as unit, draws crossed with seeds, verifier frozen on synthetic data before any real fit (PREREG-0) directly fixes the failure mode that demoted A/B/C. Folding A into the main design and giving SUBESCO the full protocol are the right moves and the paper fits 4 pages. Weaknesses from the AC chair: novelty is thin — after the audit the rest is a replication of Ibrahim 2026/Zielonka 2022 plus a decomposition; cutting Transformer entirely leaves only two convolutional from-scratch levels, which a reviewer will notice; CTRL-2 has one replicate; the corpus-difference test (24 vs 91 speakers, different class sets) is a descriptive contrast dressed as a test; SUBESCO 'as released' with 5 takes conflates near-duplicate leakage with speaker leakage and the paper would have to explain a very large SUBESCO premium it cannot decompose. Likely accepted as a solid methods-hygiene paper; unlikely to be highly cited.

scores.angle: Reviewer-proof generality (76 GPU-h): 7-9 corpora, 3 regimes incl. full WavLM fine-tune, dose, structure ladders, realized-split replay, cross-corpus ladder, n=100 audit
scores.comments: Anticipates every standard reviewer attack and contains the single best de-risked bridge idea (REPLAY: execute the audited repo's split code on the real manifest, then train OUR fixed pipelines on that realized split vs size-matched counterfactual — avoids running other people's environments). But as a program it is a journal-scale campaign, not an ICASSP paper: 11 arms, ~10 test families, 9 corpora with three license-gated ones, n=100 audit with 25 human-coded repos, 31 GPU-h of full fine-tuning on a 12 GB card with an untested per-fit cost, plus DerSimonian-Laird meta-regression on k<=9 corpora (descriptive at best). Ten-speaker corpora (EmoDB, ESD, IEMOCAP) give n=10 for Wilcoxon and 2 test speakers per fold, so most of the 'every corpus' claims are underpowered. emotion2vec+ contamination is acknowledged but still consumes extraction budget. Seven headline claims cannot be reported verifiably in 4 pages; the AC would expect either a journal submission or a heavy cut. High risk of the same governance collapse as the original program because the scope invites mid-run changes.

scores.angle: Mechanism-first (52 GPU-h): five-level exposure factorial on size-matched identical test blocks (speaker / sentence / sibling-take channels), dose, inner leakage + HPO, normalisation/adversarial interventions, representational probes, SUBESCO ladders, conditional MSP-Podcast
scores.comments: Scientifically the most interesting hypothesis in the set (RAVDESS-type inflation is a sibling-take/sentence-count effect, not a speaker-count effect; B's unregistered c20r1->c20r2 jump is exactly the right clue) and the channel decomposition on identical test blocks is genuinely novel. But it re-centres the paper on mechanism, leaving the audit — the only non-collided contribution — as a preamble, and the claim list (7 claims + recommendation) is a journal article. Validity concerns: size-matching to the L0 pool on RAVDESS (2 sentences) means training on ONE sentence with ~570 items, a regime nobody uses, so channel shares may not transfer to full-size pipelines (acknowledged, but it means M1 does not measure what the audit measures); L3 vs L4 confounds sibling presence with same-emotion labelling; per-speaker normalisation 'transductive at test' is itself a form of test-time speaker information; gradient reversal at one fixed lambda is a weak intervention; H4 rank prediction over n=6 corpora that differ in language and class set is not a test. ESD and MSP-Podcast licensing and two human coders are calendar risks. Excellent follow-up journal program; as an ICASSP program it is over-scoped and diluted.

scores.angle: One-shot pipeline engineer (42 GPU-h): shared caches/seed table/split table; CORE 2x2 on 7 corpora x 3 models; HPO-on-leaky-validation; SSL probe factorial (encoder x layer x head x fold count x 20 draws) with size-matched LOSO control; CREMA-D/SUBESCO moderator ladders; dose; wav2vec2 fine-tune
scores.comments: The most disciplined engineering redesign: content-addressed caches, one seed table so all four outer/inner cells share initialisation (removes A's seed-stream confound), a single scoring module plus independent re-implementation (the P1 pattern that actually worked), OpenTimestamps anchor, preregistered truncation order. Keeps Transformer (sensible), cuts FNO and LOSO, and answers the LOSO>GroupKFold puzzle with a size-matched LOSO on frozen features for CPU minutes — a clever, cheap closure of an open reviewer question. The HPO-on-leaky-validation arm is the realistic failure mode and is cheap. Concerns: 7 corpora with IEMOCAP/ESD conditional again yields 10-speaker Wilcoxon tests; F5c's 21 layer tests are supplement filler; the paper would still carry 7 claims; no arm ties effect size back to the audited code, so the 'linkage' novelty stays the same as the frozen manuscript's. Absolute grouped UAR validity anchors are missing (Proposal 1 has them). A safe, publishable, moderately cited paper; the AC would accept it but it does not change what the paper is about.

scores.angle: Audit-to-practice bridge (59 GPU-h): stratified two-rater audit with test-vs-validation endpoint; BRIDGE re-execution of runnable risk-positive repos under native vs minimally-edited speaker-exclusive split; trimmed 2x2 on 3 corpora; CREMA-D speaker x sentence moderator; dose; unified all-layer SSL arm with head contrast, SUBESCO full vs repetition-clean, partial FT
scores.comments: This is the program that produces the paper people cite: 'X% of public SER code leaks speakers, and when we re-ran that code with only the splitter fixed, its reported score fell by a median of Y points.' Searches confirm no SER study has re-executed public repositories under corrected splits (EMO-SUPERB standardises partitions but does not re-run code), so BRIDGE is a defensible first, and it finally lets the paper connect prevalence and magnitude without the forbidden multiplication. The audit redesign is the most reviewer-literate: paper-linked stratum, test-vs-validation endpoint, human rater A blinded from LLM rater B, third-rater adjudication, published evidence records; dropping the Bonferroni hypergeometric envelope for Wilson intervals loses a little (no FPC on N~290) but removes the 30-pp headline that readers misread. MOD is the best-designed moderator arm in the set because it varies speakers and sentences on the corpus whose gap is in question rather than on a third corpus. SSL-U resolves the S0/S2 head discrepancy and the layer question with one all-layer extraction. Feasibility is the real risk: ~100 engineering hours on hobby/Kaggle-path notebooks, 32 GPU-h of other people's code with unknown determinism, IEMOCAP-only repos falling out, and a runnable-subset estimand that is honestly non-random — but the 24-attempt/12-repo caps and 'runnability is itself a finding' framing make failure reportable. Wilcoxon over ~12 repos is weak inference, and the regex 'paper-linked' stratum will be noisy; some P1-T timing numbers (330 s/fit CREMA-D) look inconsistent with the dossier's ~60 s. Still five claims is one or two too many for 4 pages; drop MOD or DOSE to supplement and the paper is a clear accept.

graft_ideas: [1] REPLAY as the fallback/complement to BRIDGE: execute each Y_test repo's split code (AST-isolated, as P0.5 did) on the real RAVDESS/CREMA-D manifest to obtain its realized train/test index sets, then train the program's OWN fixed pipeline on the realized split vs a size-matched GroupShuffleSplit counterfactual. Costs ~3 GPU-h, needs no repo environment, covers the many repos BRIDGE cannot make runnable, and makes the 'not runnable' shortfall far less damaging.

[0] PREREG-0 verifier-first synthetic dry run: freeze scorer AND an independently written verifier, prove they agree to 1e-12 on synthetic outputs including rounded-field fixtures, pass a 20-case mutation battery, then tag/OSF-register before any real fit — this is the single cheapest fix for the failure that demoted A, B, C and produced ten S3 releases.

[0] Single Holm family with p=1 placeholders and a routing rule fixed a priori ('every family contrast appears in the main table regardless of sign'); Proposal 4 has per-arm families but no explicit anti-re-routing rule for BRIDGE's descriptive fallback.

[3] Size-matched LOSO control on frozen features (LOSO vs Group5 vs LOSO-sub at 80% of training speakers, Ridge head, CPU minutes) to close the LOSO>GroupKFold question cheaply instead of cutting LOSO with a bare citation to the 2026 artifact.

[3] HPO-on-leaky-validation arm (8 preregistered configs, select on inner validation, RR vs GG, ~2 GPU-h): the realistic failure mode that Y_val repositories represent; Proposal 4 codes 'test set used for selection' in the audit but never measures its effect.

[3] Content-addressed cache naming (manifest SHA + weight SHA + sr/trim/pooling + code SHA) and one shared seed table with train_seed keyed on (corpus, draw, fold) only, so all outer/inner cells share initialisation; plus OpenTimestamps anchoring of the git tag.

[2] Sibling nearest-neighbour analysis on saved penultimate embeddings (inference only): P(correct | nearest training neighbour is a same speaker-sentence-emotion sibling take) vs other — a cheap, direct mechanism readout that would explain the SUBESCO-full vs repetition-clean contrast Proposal 4 already measures.
[2] Preregistered TOST equivalence margins for the 'no spillover to unexposed speakers' claim in the dose arm, so a null is interpretable rather than 'not conclusive'.

[1] Preregistered validity anchor for the fine-tuned regime (e.g. grouped UAR range from the literature) that triggers an implementation audit rather than exclusion — P1's priors were 3-10x wrong on CREMA-D and no audit ever happened.
universal_objections: Page budget: every proposal ends with 5-8 headline claims, but ICASSP is 4 pages plus references; none allocates space or names which one figure/table each claim gets, so all would ship as a thin main text pointing at a supplement reviewers cannot check — the same problem the record-282 manuscript has.

Calendar: all proposals implicitly abandon the 2026-09-16 ICASSP deadline (weeks of audit coding, license requests, 22-76 GPU-h, BRIDGE engineering) without saying so; the honest framing is 'next cycle or journal', and none states which.

Human reliability is still weak everywhere: the 'human' coder is the author who also designed the LLM prompt and rubric (Proposals 0, 3, 4) or two unnamed coders (1, 2); kappa on 20-25 units has a CI roughly +/-0.25, so the kappa>=0.6 gate is close to a coin flip and reviewers who demand independent human double coding are not satisfied by any proposal.

Prior-art positioning is asserted, not written: all say the protocol effect is a replication of Ibrahim 2026 / Zielonka 2022, but none drafts the one paragraph that explains why a same-implementation contrast is needed when the published gaps (95.8 vs 48.1% on RAVDESS) already exist; an AC will ask for it.

Small-speaker corpora (EmoDB 10, ESD 10, IEMOCAP 10, SUBESCO 20) are used for per-corpus Wilcoxon tests in every multi-corpus proposal; n=10 speakers with 2 test speakers per fold gives near-zero power and coarse UAR granularity, and no proposal reports a power calculation.

Comparability with the frozen program is broken silently: every proposal changes hygiene (drops duplicates, all-zero file), fold family (StratifiedGroupKFold shuffled vs P1's GroupKFold), and model set, so none of the 2026 P1/S0/S2/S3 numbers can be reused or presented as an update, yet several proposals still cite them as priors/overlays without saying the estimand changed.

Fine-tuning cost on a 12 GB RTX 5070 is extrapolated in every proposal that includes it (0, 1, 3, 4); none reports a measured timing probe, and fp16/bf16 non-determinism is disclosed but not reconciled with the 'bitwise replay' verification story used elsewhere.

Audit frame coverage remains unquantified: all rebuild a GitHub(+arXiv) best-match frame with top-100 cutoffs; none proposes a capture-recapture or second-search overlap estimate, so 'prevalence in public SER code' still means 'prevalence in a bounded discoverable frame'.

Governance risk is addressed by prose ('the author must refuse mid-run scope changes') rather than mechanism; only Proposal 0's verifier-first dry run and Proposal 3's preregistered truncation order are concrete, and no proposal budgets the CPU-review and engineering wall-clock hours against a named number of people.

judgements.lens: Statistician / preregistration methodologist: estimand clarity, paired-design validity, multiplicity control, whether merges preserve pairing, falsifiable prespecified hypotheses, soundness of audit sampling and interval logic, and whether the program can be executed once without post-hoc changes.

scores.angle: Confirmatory minimalist: single 16-test Holm family, one audit test, 22 GPU-h
scores.comments: Cleanest estimand set in the batch: every controlled contrast is a per-speaker OOF UAR difference, averaged within speaker over replicates and over named model levels BEFORE differencing, so pairing survives every merge (P1+A+S0+S2+S3 collapse into one RR/RG/GR/GG design without breaking the speaker unit). Training RNG keyed without protocol tokens gives shared initialization across the four cells, which fixes A's seed-stream confound. Family is closed and countable (3 corpora x 4 contrasts + 1 corpus difference + 3 fine-tune = 16), missing tests enter as p=1, per-level cells and interaction are estimates only. The corpus-difference test is honestly framed as an a priori replication of a published direction and uses an unpaired speaker-level Mann-Whitney with a two-sample bootstrap, which is the right shape for different speaker populations. Audit logic is sound: one lineage rule fixed before screening, fixed-order beacon draw, per-repo review cap fixed a priori (removes the C218 problem), Y_any primary / Y_test secondary, kappa rule with a prespecified demotion path, partial-identification plus exact hypergeometric envelope retained. Verifier-first synthetic dry run with a mutation battery is the single best process fix in any proposal. Weak points: the audit one-sided test at alpha 0.025 is unexplained (conservative but arbitrary); the 60-review-hour truncation is an outcome-correlated stopping rule; CTRL-2 uses a single partition so its CI covers speaker variation only; replicate = draw+seed confounded, so the reported SD cannot be decomposed; SUBESCO as released bundles take leakage with speaker leakage (disclosed). Novelty is deliberately low, and cutting LOSO/mechanism arms leaves the paper mostly a replication plus audit, but from a preregistration standpoint it is the program most likely to be run exactly once as written.

scores.angle: Reviewer-proof generality: 7-9 corpora, three regimes, dose, structure, replay, cross-corpus; 76 GPU-h
scores.comments: Strong individual designs: DOSE holds training size and label counts constant and uses Page's L with speakers as blocks (correct ordered test on matched blocks); PROBE averages over draws within speaker so pairing holds; FACT fixes A's unequal fit/val sizes and seed streams; REPLAY has a clean estimand (our fixed pipeline on their realized split vs size-matched counterfactuals) with no prevalence-times-effect multiplication; IEMOCAP validity anchor as an implementation-audit trigger rather than an exclusion is good practice. But multiplicity is only family-wise across roughly ten families (~40-50 confirmatory tests) with no program-wise control and seven headline claims, which is exactly the setting where post-hoc narrative selection creeps in even with fixed routing. Several 'tests' are not tests: H4 equivalence ('|diff| < 2 pp in >= 2/3 of corpora') is a descriptor; H3 sign test over corpus x encoder cells treats non-independent cells as independent; STRUCT invokes Page's L with panels as blocks although panels differ across levels (JT is the appropriate one), and uses one seed per panel, repeating B's training-noise/panel-noise confound. FACT 'reuses' SCRATCH/FT RR and GG cells while asserting a shared-init seed key that SCRATCH never states, so the reuse may not preserve the pairing property claimed. Audit: author both tie-breaks adjudication and blind-codes 25 units, and blinding order is unspecified. Feasibility is the main problem for a run-once program: 31 GPU-h of extrapolated fine-tuning across nine corpora, two license-gated corpora with a day-14 rule, ~36k SSL utterances, n=100 audit with 25 human-coded, all on one author and one 12 GB GPU; the fixed truncation order protects validity but makes it likely that late arms ship incomplete.

scores.angle: Mechanism-first channel decomposition (speaker / sentence / sibling / model-selection); 52 GPU-h
scores.comments: The core idea (identical speaker x sentence disjoint test blocks, size-matched training pools, five exposure levels) is a genuinely paired design and M2's exposed-vs-unexposed-within-fold contrast with rotation and a TOST on spillover is the cleanest identity-specificity test proposed anywhere. But the decomposition is not coherent as a decomposition: D_spk = L1-L0, D_sent = L2-L0, D_lex = L3-L2, D_sib = L4-L3 do not sum to T = L4-L0 (they sum to L1+L4-2L0), L1 and L2 are non-nested, and L3's membership relative to L1 is unspecified, so the headline claim that the RAVDESS-CREMA-D gap 'is accounted for by the sibling and sentence channels' has no arithmetic behind it. H2's TOST that |D_sib| < 1 pp in corpora without sibling takes is tautological (L3 and L4 are the same pool by construction when no siblings exist). M6's hypothesis that sibling removal explains >50% of the S0-vs-S2 discrepancy is malformed: sibling handling is not a difference between S0 and S2 (both Random arms include siblings); head and split family are. M3-HPO compares a leaky validation number to an exclusive test number (bundles ordinary val-test optimism with leakage) using n=5 blocks. Multiplicity: per-corpus Holm families of 8 in M1, 4 in M2, 6 in M5, plus M3/M6/M7 families, with no program-wise control, and many hypotheses are threshold or ratio statements (A_spk > 0.5 D_spk) with no stated error control. Feasibility is under-costed: M1b alone is ~2,200 fits (300 per corpus x4 + 500 x2), and CREMA-D and SUBESCO-full at 60-65 s/fit are ~5 GPU-h each, so the '4 GPU-h' estimate is off by roughly 3x; total fits approach 5,400 and the 70 GPU-h cap would be hit, with the preregistered drop order removing precisely the mechanism arms that carry the thesis. EmoDB test blocks (2 speakers x 2 sentences) give per-speaker UARs on ~10 items over 7 classes, and the ESD/MSP-Podcast licenses are calendar-conditional. Audit design is sound (n=80, pre-fixed rule, two human coders on 20, boundary_type).

scores.angle: One-shot pipeline engineer: unified caches, seed table, split table, closed families F1-F8; 42 GPU-h
scores.comments: The most complete preregistration apparatus: run_plan.csv with SHA unit ids, seed table strings, split table with hard assertions before any fit, OSF + git tag + OpenTimestamps, closed and named families F1-F8 with sizes, SESOI of 2 pp and a +/-1 pp equivalence band, missingness propagated as p=1 placeholders, fixed manuscript slot per arm, append-only deviation file, independent re-implementation to 1e-9 and 2% bitwise replay. CORE preserves pairing correctly (per-speaker OOF UAR averaged over draws and models within speaker, identical train_seed across the four cells). LADDER correctly uses Jonckheere-Terpstra with independent panel x draw units and nested hash subsets (unlike proposal 1); DOSE uses Page's trend with the same speakers as blocks on a fixed prompt-disjoint half test set, which is the correct matched-block test. SSLPROBE E4 (LOSO vs Group5 vs size-matched LOSO on identical Ridge features with no early stopping, TOST band) is the cheapest valid resolution of the LOSO>GroupKFold puzzle in any proposal. Weaknesses: the audit carries no confirmatory test at all ('directional expectation, not a test'), which is defensible but leaves claim 1 as pure estimation; ~65 confirmatory tests across eight families (F5c alone has 21) with no program-wise control, though F5c is labelled supplement-grade; draw index doubles as training seed so partition and seed variance remain confounded; EmoDB/ESD/IEMOCAP give n=10 speakers and 2 test speakers per fold; ESD and IEMOCAP are license-conditional; 3,330 GPU fits plus 200 CPU-review hours plus a human coder for 25 units is heavy for one author, and bf16 FINETUNE is non-deterministic (disclosed). The HPO comparator (fixed CORE config not necessarily in the grid) is a minor estimand ambiguity. Close second to proposal 0; more persuasive, slightly more surface for deviation.

scores.angle: Audit-to-practice bridge: re-execute audited repos under native vs speaker-exclusive splits; stratified two-rater audit; 59 GPU-h
scores.comments: BRIDGE is the only arm in any proposal that measures inflation in the audited code itself, with a clearly bounded estimand (runnable Y_test repos, native minus minimal-edit exclusive split, repo's own metric), a construct check (static Y with realized overlap 0 = recorded false positive), full accounting of non-runnable cases, and a prespecified fallback to descriptive reporting if n<10. AUDIT-R fixes the dedup rule and strata before the draw, separates Y_test from Y_val, uses two blinded raters plus a third-human adjudicator, and states power (0.85 at n=60, p=0.70, 12% U). P1-T preserves pairing (replicate r shares draw and training seed across models and cells), closes a 9-test Holm family, and turns the corpus interaction into a SESOI-based bootstrap hypothesis. DOSE uses per-speaker slopes with cluster bootstrap on a fixed half test set. Validity deductions: SSL-U tests (2) and (4) run Wilcoxon over the 20 partition draws as if draws were independent sampling units, which is exactly the inference the frozen program's own S2 registry forbade ('draws are not n'), and pairing SUBESCO-full with SUBESCO-980 'by draw' is not a meaningful pairing; the layer-effect Spearman over layer index is a descriptor dressed as H1. Stratified sampling with 30 per stratum but pooled Wilson intervals on n=60 ignores the stratum weights (a weighted point estimate is given without an interval). MOD's mixed 'paired where sharing speakers, independent otherwise' bootstrap is ad hoc, and the fixed 3-sentence subset includes IEO, the only CREMA-D sentence with intensity variants, which confounds sentence count with repeated takes. BRIDGE inherently requires per-repo engineering judgment (which split site is decisive, environment edits) that cannot be fully prespecified, only logged, so 'run once without post-hoc changes' holds less strongly here than elsewhere; it also needs ~100 engineering hours, three humans (two raters and an adjudicator), and an IEMOCAP license, on a program whose history shows one author.

graft_ideas: [3] SSLPROBE E4: LOSO vs Group5 vs training-size-matched LOSO on identical frozen Ridge features (no early stopping) with a +/-1 pp TOST band, CPU-only; lets proposal 0 keep a defensible LOSO statement instead of cutting it entirely.
[3] Zero-GPU layer factor: cache all 13 hidden states once and add layer {final, mid, mean} to the probe level; answers the S4 question inside the existing family at no fit cost.

[3] Process apparatus: run_plan.csv with SHA unit ids, OpenTimestamps anchor on the git tag, per-unit DONE checkpoints with prediction SHA, 2% hash-selected bitwise replay, number-checked LaTeX insert generated from one results.json.
[3] LADDER design pattern: nested hash subsets with Jonckheere-Terpstra over independent panel x draw units (not Page's L), if a moderator arm is ever added.

[4] Audit stratification on paper-linked vs other with a regex fixed at freeze, plus a third-human adjudicator and publication of all rater records; and the construct check that a static Y_test with realized overlap 0 is recorded as a false positive.
[4] BRIDGE as a small descriptive arm (e.g. 6-8 runnable repos, sign counts only, no test) to give the prevalence claim a practice anchor without adding a family member.

[1] REPLAY variant: execute audited repos' split code on the real manifest and train OUR fixed pipeline on the realized split vs size-matched GroupShuffleSplit counterfactuals; cheaper and better controlled than re-running their code, and the estimand stays inside proposal 0's pipeline.

[1] Preregistered validity anchor (expected speaker-independent UAR range on a reference corpus) that triggers an implementation audit, not exclusion, plus a draw-vs-seed variance decomposition on the two anchor corpora (seeds 1-2 crossed with draws 0-2).
[1] DOSE with training size and label counts held constant and Page's L over speakers as matched blocks, if a dose arm is wanted; it is the correctly matched-block version of the dose idea.

[2] M2 identity-specificity test: within the same grouped fold, expose a rotated subset of test speakers cross-prompt and test exposed-speaker gain (Wilcoxon) against unexposed-speaker spillover (TOST); each speaker exposed in exactly one partial dose.
[2] Speaker x sentence disjoint test blocks as the L0 comparator, which makes 'speaker-exclusive' also 'text-exclusive' and removes the prompt-overlap axis that every other proposal leaves untested.

[2]/[4] SUBESCO full (5 takes) vs repetition-clean 980 panel as a paired-by-speaker contrast on identical speaker folds to isolate near-duplicate-take leakage from speaker leakage (proposal 0 currently bundles them).
universal_objections: Every audit uses a review-time cap (60/48/200 CPU-hours or per-repo caps that produce U) as part of the stopping or classification rule; cumulative review time is correlated with repository difficulty and therefore with outcome, so the achieved n is an outcome-dependent stopping point. A design-based estimate needs a fixed n with time-outs coded as U, not a prefix truncated by elapsed hours.

All controlled-study inference conditions on speakers only: per-speaker deltas are averaged over replicates/draws/models and then bootstrapped and Wilcoxon-tested, so partition-draw and training-seed variance never enter any CI or p-value. Replicate SDs are reported as descriptors, and in proposals 0 and 3 draw and seed are deliberately confounded. None proposes a variance model (speaker x draw mixed model or two-way cluster bootstrap) that would let the interval cover the stated 'not a split artifact' claim.

Every proposal keeps a RAVDESS-vs-CREMA-D 'corpus interaction' hypothesis that compares two different speaker populations differing in speaker count, sentence count, class count and recording design; it is an unpaired comparison of marginals, not an interaction in any factorial sense, and all proposals concede this in limitations while still labelling it a preregistered hypothesis.

Human-vs-AI agreement is checked on 20-25 repositories in every proposal, and a kappa >= 0.6 threshold decides whether the audit is confirmatory; with n=20-25 and ~4 categories the kappa CI half-width is roughly 0.25-0.35, so the demotion rule will frequently be decided by sampling noise. None powers or widens the reliability subsample, and none pre-specifies what happens when the CI straddles 0.6.

Multiplicity is controlled only within families; the number of families ranges from 2 (proposal 0) to ~10 (proposals 1, 2, 3), and no proposal states a program-wise or claim-wise error rate, nor a rule for how many family-level rejections a headline claim requires. In a 4-page ICASSP format, which cannot carry 40-65 tests, this reintroduces post-hoc claim selection at the writing stage even with fixed routing.

All proposals keep the small-speaker corpora (EmoDB 10, ESD 10, IEMOCAP 10, SUBESCO 20, RAVDESS 24) under per-corpus Wilcoxon tests; with 2 test speakers per grouped fold and n=10 paired units the minimum attainable two-sided p is ~0.002 and power for 1-3 pp premia is negligible, so 'positive in every corpus' families are structurally likely to fail on exactly the corpora added for generality. Only proposal 0 avoids this by cutting them.

Fine-tuning arms are accepted as non-deterministic (fp16/bf16), use a single partition or 2-3 replicates, and enter the same Holm families as deterministic arms; a scorer/verifier equality gate at 1e-12 cannot apply to them, and none specifies what replay tolerance a verifier must meet for those units.

Adjudication remains LLM-assisted in every proposal, with blinding between the AI pass and the human coder asserted rather than mechanised; in a single-author program where the same person runs the AI tooling, prepares the frame, and codes 'blind', the independence claimed for kappa is not enforceable by the stated procedures.

The audit endpoint everywhere is 'a path permits same-speaker membership'; none proposes execution on the real corpus to record realized overlap for the whole sample (proposal 1 does it only for AST-isolable fragments, proposal 4 only for the runnable BRIDGE subset), so the prevalence estimand remains 'permits', not 'used', and the frame remains GitHub-discoverable code with unquantified coverage.

Unknowns (U) are treated as a bound-only nuisance in all proposals; none models informativeness of U (size, notebook vs script, external data) or reports a sensitivity in which U are assigned by a prespecified covariate model, so the partial-identification interval's realism is asserted rather than examined.

judgements.lens: Feasibility on one RTX 5070 (12 GB), a solo author with limited months, already burned by governance churn (post-outcome verifier fixes, withdrawn prereg, ten S3 release retries). Judged on: GPU-hour realism against the recorded manifests (A: ~40 s/fit on RAVDESS+CREMA-D 5-fold; B: ~13 s/fit at 1-2k utterances; base-SSL fine-tune ~10-30 GPU-min per fold), engineering surface (new loaders, new training code, new samplers), dataset licensing risk for a gmail-address solo author, human review hours, and the probability the whole program finishes without another round of outcome-visible re-routing.

scores.angle: Confirmatory minimalist: one preregistered audit + one outer x inner factorial on 3 in-hand corpora x 4 representation levels + one partial fine-tune row, single 16-test Holm family, ~22 GPU-h
scores.comments: GPU arithmetic checks out against the manifests: 600 scratch fits (RAVDESS ~20 s, CREMA-D/SUBESCO-full ~60 s) is ~8 h, 600 probe units ~1 h, 30 partial-fine-tune fits (top-4 layers unfrozen, so no backward through the lower stack) ~5-8 h; 22 h target with 30 h cap is the only proposal where the cap is comfortably above a pessimistic estimate. Zero licensing exposure: every corpus (RAVDESS, CREMA-D, SUBESCO) is already on disk with an existing loader from P1/B/S3. Engineering reuses the P1 engine unchanged; the only new code is StratifiedGroupKFold draws crossed with seeds and a partial-freeze fine-tune loop. The verifier-first synthetic dry run and mutation battery in PREREG-0 is the exact fix for the A/B/C verifier-timing failures. Governance surface is the smallest of the five (one family, one prereg, one routing rule). Weaknesses: the author blind-coding 20 repos after having seen ~90 audit outcomes is a thin reliability check; cutting LOSO entirely forfeits any statement about a protocol many reviewers equate with speaker-independence (cheap to keep as a CPU Ridge sensitivity, see graft); the paper it yields is modest (replication + audit + decomposition + one fine-tune row) and still collides with Ibrahim 2026 on the effect half. Probability of a clean finish is the highest here.

scores.angle: Reviewer-proof generality: 7-9 corpora, 5 encoders all layers, full WavLM fine-tune across the panel, dose, structure ladders, realized-split replay, cross-corpus ladder; 76 GPU-h target, 100 h cap
scores.comments: The FT line (31 GPU-h) is under-estimated: full fine-tuning WavLM-base+ (whole transformer trainable) on CREMA-D at batch 8x2, 4 s crops is ~20 min per fit at early-stop epochs on this card, so 30 fits is ~10 h, not 6; SUBESCO-full and the 6,000-segment MSP-Podcast panel scale the same way, putting FT alone at 45-60 h and the program at 90-110 h against the 100 h cap, so late corpora are near-certain to be reported incomplete. Licensing is the worst of the five: MSP-Podcast needs an institutional signatory, IEMOCAP a USC academic agreement, ESD an emailed form, and emotion2vec+ has a model license and possible training-data contamination the proposal itself flags. The engineering surface repeats the P4 failure (8 corpora promised, 1 delivered): 6-8 new loaders, REPLAY requires executing foreign split code on real manifests and adapting our pipeline to arbitrary index sets, XCORP needs a cross-corpus label map, DOSE has two E/T rules, PROBE has a 3-head x 3-layer-policy x 5-encoder grid. Eleven arms with ten Holm families is a governance surface several times larger than the one that already produced 13 plan revisions in 9 days. Scientifically it is the most complete program and the most persuasive if delivered, but for this author on this card it is the least likely to finish.

scores.angle: Mechanism-first: five-level exposure factorial on size-matched identical test blocks across 6 corpora, dose, inner-selection, gradient-reversal/per-speaker-normalisation interventions, representational probes, SUBESCO structure ladders; 52 GPU-h, 70 h cap
scores.comments: Per-fit costs are cited from the manifests and the 52 h total is credible (M1 ~10 h by my arithmetic, nothing fine-tuned), so compute is not the problem. The problems are engineering and dependencies. The test-block generator (speaker folds x sentence folds) and the five level samplers with exact size matching are subtle new code whose bugs surface only after fits; RAVDESS with two statements leaves ~570 training items per block, so the headline corpus is also the most fragile cell. M5 adds gradient-reversal training at a fixed lambda, a known-unstable recipe that the proposal admits may under- or over-remove speaker information; that is new training code with no fallback. The central discriminating hypothesis H4 depends on ESD (both languages) arriving via emailed license, and the naturalistic check depends on MSP-Podcast (institutional signatory); losing ESD collapses the 'many sentences, few speakers, no siblings' corner that the sibling-density story needs. The audit needs two human coders. Nine mechanism arms with per-corpus Holm families, TOST margins and SESOI classes reproduce the governance load that burned the author. The sibling-take hypothesis is the single best scientific idea across all five proposals and the SUBESCO full-vs-980 pair tests it almost for free; that piece should be grafted.

scores.angle: One-shot pipeline engineer: content-addressed caches, one seed table, one split table, resumable per-fit checkpoints; CORE 2x2 x 3 models x 7 corpora, HPO, SSL probe factorial with size-matched LOSO, ladders, dose, wav2vec2 fine-tune; 42 GPU-h, 60 h cap
scores.comments: GPU estimates are the most carefully derived of the five and match the manifests (CORE ~14 h, FINETUNE 30 RAVDESS fits at ~6 min + 20 CREMA-D fits at ~25 min = ~11 h, consistent with the 10-30 min/fold fact), and the 60 h cap with a preregistered per-arm drop order is realistic. The infrastructure design (content-addressed caches keyed on manifest+weight+code SHA, per-fit DONE markers so an OS shutdown never ghost-bills again, one seed table shared across cells, OpenTimestamps anchor, append-only deviation file) is the direct engineering answer to the D1 ghost-billing, S0 v1->v2 and S3 v1-v10 churn, and is the best thing in any proposal. Feasibility is dragged down by scope: 7 corpora means 5 new loaders (EmoDB, ESD-EN, ESD-ZH, IEMOCAP, plus ESD subsetting), two of them license-conditional (ESD email form, IEMOCAP USC form), which is the P4 pattern again even with the not_run rule; 3,330 GPU fits + 15,750 CPU Ridge fits + an n=80 audit with a 200-review-hour cap is many months of solo human time; 63 named tests across F1-F8 and a 7-claim paper do not fit a 4-page venue. Strip it to 3-4 corpora and it becomes the strongest design; as written the probability of a clean end-to-end finish is moderate.

scores.angle: Audit-to-practice bridge: re-execute 12 audited risk-positive repos under native vs speaker-exclusive splits; stratified two-rater audit with Wilson CIs; trimmed 2x2 on 3 corpora; CREMA-D moderator factorial; dose; unified SSL arm with partial fine-tune; 59 GPU-h, 70 h cap
scores.comments: Compute is fine (P1-T ~4.5 h by my arithmetic, MOD 3, DOSE 4, SSL-U ~13 incl. 90 partial-fine-tune fits, BRIDGE 32 h at a 1.0 h/run cap) and licensing is low-risk (EmoDB CC0, SUBESCO in hand, IEMOCAP only conditional for BRIDGE).
