The crux is BRIDGE engineering: reproducing 12 arbitrary public SER repos (P0.5 found 19/30 are student/Kaggle notebooks) on Windows with Python 3.13 / torch 2.11 means one environment per repo, old TensorFlow/Keras stacks that have no native Windows GPU support after TF 2.10, hard-coded Kaggle paths, and missing dependencies; the 4 h/repo cap will be exhausted by environment work alone for most attempts, and the preregistered fallback (<10 runnable -> descriptive) makes the paper's headline novelty likely to land as a sign count. It also budgets ~100 engineering hours plus ~85 audit hours plus a second human rater/adjudicator, for a solo author. The audit redesign is the most practical of the five (GitHub code search on corpus filename tokens, paper-linked stratum, Wilson intervals instead of the 30-pp Bonferroni envelope) and should be grafted. Persuasive narrative, but the leg that carries it is the one most likely to fail on this machine.

graft_ideas: [3] Content-addressed caches (filename = SHA of manifest+weight+sr+trim+pooling+code), per-fit DONE markers with prediction SHA, and a resumable runner that skips verified units — directly prevents the D1 ghost-billing, S0 v1->v2 and S3 v1-v10 churn; near-zero cost.

[3] Single seed table keyed on (corpus, fold, draw) with no protocol/cell token so all outer x inner cells share init and batch streams; Proposal 0 does this too but [3]'s split-table-as-hashed-CSV with pre-fit overlap/coverage/class-complete assertions that abort before any GPU work is the cleaner gate.

[3] LOSO and size-matched LOSO-sub on frozen SSL features with a Ridge head (CPU minutes) to settle the 'LOSO > GroupKFold is a training-size effect' claim without re-running 1,380 scratch LOSO fits — restores the LOSO statement Proposal 0 forfeits.

[3] SSLPROBE head x split-family crossing on the cached features (Ridge vs early-stopped probe on identical draws) to resolve the unexplained S0 2.8-6.2 pp vs S2 13.9 pp RAVDESS discrepancy at ~0 GPU; also present in [4] SSL-U test (2).
[3] OpenTimestamps anchor on the git tag plus an append-only deviation file the paper must cite by entry number — cheaper and more durable than the receipt chain that broke at record 282.

[4] Audit frame augmentation by GitHub code search on corpus-specific filename tokens (RAVDESS '03-01-0', CREMA-D '_DFA_', IEMOCAP 'Ses01F_impro', EmoDB '03a01Fa') — catches loaders that keyword search misses, zero cost.

[4] Stratify the audit sample on paper-linked vs other (regex on README for arxiv/doi/ieeexplore) and report Wilson CIs on Y_test/n and (Y_test+U)/n instead of the 30-pp Bonferroni hypergeometric envelope; makes the prevalence readable and links it to the literature.
[4] EmoDB (CC0, 535 files, already in the audit frame definition) as a near-free third scratch corpus (~0.4 GPU-h for 180 fits) — the only extra corpus with no license or loader risk.

[2] SUBESCO full (7,000, 5 takes) vs the existing repetition-clean 980 panel on cached SSL features with the same 20 draws — a CPU-only test of the sibling-take pathway that B's unregistered c20r1->c20r2 comparison hinted at; also in [4] SSL-U test (4).

[3] DOSE ladder with prompt-disjoint fixed test halves (q in {0,.25,.5,1}) on RAVDESS/CREMA-D, 240 fits ~3 GPU-h — the cleanest replacement for C/P5 and cheap enough to add to Proposal 0 as a secondary if the 30 h cap has room.
[3] HPO-on-leaky-validation arm (ResNet-SE, 8 configs, RR vs GG, ~2 GPU-h) — measures the realistic failure mode the audit records (selection on speaker-overlapping validation) at trivial cost.

[1] Fixed corpus/arm execution order so a budget overrun truncates the last items rather than shrinking any design mid-run, plus a 1-epoch timing probe before committing any fine-tune budget (the fine-tune costs in every proposal are extrapolated, not measured on this card).

[4] BRIDGE scaled down to a 3-5 repo descriptive pilot (RAVDESS/CREMA-D repos with pure-Python/torch stacks only, 1 GPU-h cap each) as a supplement — keeps the audit-to-practice link as a demonstration without betting the paper on Windows reproducibility of Kaggle notebooks.
universal_objections: None of the five states which venue and deadline replaces ICASSP 2027 (deadline 2026-09-16 is 13 days away; every proposal requires weeks-to-months of new work), so 'limited months' is unbudgeted: no proposal gives a calendar with author hours, and the human review load (60-200 CPU-review hours for the audit, plus blind coding, plus loader engineering) is the true bottleneck on a solo project, not GPU time.

All five discard the already-recorded ~40 GPU-h and ~700 CPU-review hours (P1's prospectively frozen 1,620-fit table with an independent 0.0-error verification, S1's 60 hash-receipted adjudications) and re-run everything under a new prereg; none considers the cheapest path of keeping P1 as the confirmatory anchor it already is and preregistering only the additions (2x2 cells, fine-tune row, draws), which would cut every budget roughly in half.

Every fine-tuning estimate (partial or full, 8-31 GPU-h) is extrapolated rather than measured on this card; no manifest in the dossier records a single fine-tune fit, and none of the proposals schedules a timing probe before committing the budget, so the arm most likely to blow the cap is the one with the least evidence behind its estimate.

All five require human blind coding of audit repositories by the author (who has already seen ~90 outcomes across P0/P0.5/S1 and will re-encounter many of the same lineages under any frame rebuild) or by a second human who does not exist in the project record; kappa on 20-25 units has a wide CI and the 'kappa < 0.6 demotes the audit' rule creates a new outcome-visible relabelling path.

All five produce 5-7 numbered claims and multiple Holm families for a 4-page (+1 refs) conference paper with a two-panel figure and one table; 'routing fixed a priori' will collide with the page limit, and page-driven cuts after outcomes are exactly the mechanism (Rev 10 B-for-D1, record 271 S3-for-B) that produced the previous churn.

Every proposal assumes a public OSF/git timestamp removes governance risk, but the dossier's churn came from verifier timing, cache identity and executor role swaps, not from the absence of a timestamp; only Proposals 0 and 3 actually build verifier-first synthetic/mutation tests, and none budgets the calendar time the prereg document itself will take for an author who produced 13 plan revisions in 9 days.

All five keep RAVDESS+CREMA-D Random-vs-Grouped as the effect anchor despite the CRITICAL prior-art collision (Ibrahim et al. 2026, Zielonka 2022); none proposes a cheaper framing in which that half is an explicit one-table replication and all new compute goes to what is uncollided (audit, decomposition, dose, fine-tune).

tally.angle: Confirmatory minimalist: the smallest publicly preregistered, single-family program that supports the paper's four claims with clean speaker-paired inference; ~22 GPU-h (hard cap 30) on one RTX 5070.

Audit-to-practice bridge: re-execute audited risk-positive repositories under their own split and under a speaker-exclusive split to measure the real-world premium distribution; make the audit cheaper and more defensible (frozen frame, stratified beacon sample, two blinded raters + adjudication, fixed n, public prereg); keep a trimmed controlled study that decomposes and moderates the premium; fold all SSL supplements into one draw-based arm.

One-shot pipeline engineer: the whole program as one deterministic, resumable pipeline (one corpus stage, one feature/SSL cache, one seed table and split generator, one training harness, one scoring module, one number-checked insert), with every existing arm folded into a small number of unified factorials.

Reviewer-proof generality: close the four standard attacks (two English acted corpora; handcrafted-feature toy models; frozen probes instead of fine-tuning; no dose-response and no tie to real public repositories) with a single multi-corpus, multi-regime panel plus mechanism arms, while cutting the 70% of past compute that was redundant (LOSO, three of four from-scratch architectures, speech-song, purposive audit, duplicated SSL supplements).

Mechanism-first: decompose the speaker-nonexclusive inflation into separable leakage channels (same-speaker cross-prompt exposure, same-sentence exposure, near-duplicate sibling takes, and model-selection/validation leakage), and test whether corpus structure (sentences per speaker, takes per cell, speaker count) rather than speaker count per se sets the size of the premium. The public-code audit stays as the prevalence half, refined so its outcome fields map onto the same channels.

synthesis.angle: Confirmatory minimalist core (Proposal 0) hardened with the pipeline-engineering apparatus of Proposal 3, the stratified two-rater audit and audit-to-practice link of Proposals 4/1 (as a cheap realized-split REPLAY rather than repository re-execution), and the sibling-take/head-reconciliation mechanism readouts of Proposal 2 at zero or near-zero GPU cost; 28 GPU-h target, 30 GPU-h hard cap, one RTX 5070, one author plus one recruited coder, single 21-test Holm family plus a 2-test audit family.
synthesis.thesis: Speaker-nonexclusive evaluation is common in public SER code and inflates reported performance; the paper earns each half with exactly one instrument that is publicly preregistered, verifier-frozen before any real fit or adjudication, and run once in a fixed order. The prevalence half is a stratified (paper-linked vs other), beacon-ordered, fixed-n=60 audit with a test-boundary vs validation-only endpoint, execution of the decisive split statement on the real corpus manifests (realized overlap), blind human coding hash-committed before the AI pass, and no post-hoc lineage branches. The effect half is one outer x inner protocol factorial (RR/RG/GR/GG) on RAVDESS, CREMA-D and SUBESCO with three from-scratch models and two frozen SSL probes sharing partitions, initialization and seeds, extended by four cheap additions the frozen program never ran: a partially fine-tuned WavLM row, an HPO-on-leaky-validation row, a dose ladder with a fixed prompt-disjoint test half, and a REPLAY of audited repositories' realized splits inside our own pipeline. The paper would claim prevalence with reliability and realized overlap, a corpus-resolved and decomposed premium that survives frozen probes, fine-tuning and hyperparameter search, a monotone dose curve, and a per-repository premium under real audited splits, and would explicitly present the RAVDESS/CREMA-D protocol effect itself as a same-implementation replication of Ibrahim et al. 2026 and Zielonka et al. 2022.

program.name: PREREG-0: public preregistration, shared infrastructure, verifier-first synthetic dry run, timing probe
merged_from: P1 preregistration and engineering lock (process only)
S0 v2 / S3 prep-v2 SSL feature caches (now all-layer, content-addressed)
D1/A/B split-manifest and completion-manifest tooling (replaced by one split table with pre-fit assertions)
PLAN.md revision history (replaced by one OSF registration plus an append-only deviation file)
program.rationale: Every arm in the dossier is labelled outcome-visible because no public timestamp existed and verifiers were written after scoring (A: 2 min after; B: 43 s after; C: tolerance corrected post-score; S3: ten releases; S0 v1 re-run for cache identity; D1 ghost-billing after OS shutdowns). The judges agreed the two concrete fixes are Proposal 0's verifier-first synthetic dry run with a mutation battery and Proposal 3's content-addressed caches, single seed table, per-fit DONE markers and OpenTimestamps anchor. Every fine-tune estimate in every proposal was extrapolated, so a measured timing probe precedes any fine-tune budget commitment. This arm also fixes the calendar: ICASSP 2027 (2026-09-16) is abandoned explicitly; target is Interspeech 2027 (abstract/paper deadline early March 2027) with an arXiv preprint at ledger lock; a 20-week plan with author hours is part of the registration.
program.design: One git commit (tag SER26-prereg) containing: this protocol; the audit frame script, lineage predicate, eligibility codes, endpoint dictionary, rater form and AI-rater frozen prompt; the split generator; the P1 training engine unchanged; probe, HPO, dose, replay and partial-fine-tune configs; run_plan.csv with unit_id = SHA256(config) for every GPU unit; the seed table (split_seed(c,r)=u32(SHA256('SER26|split|c|r')); train_seed(c,fold,r)=u32(SHA256('SER26|train|c|fold|r')) with NO model, cell or protocol token so all four outer x inner cells and all HPO configs share initialization and batch-order streams; dose/replay selection seeds keyed the same way); the scorer; an independently written verifier importing nothing from the scorer; the 4-page slot map (Fig. 1A audit by stratum, Fig. 1B forest of the 21 family contrasts, Table 1 per-corpus contrasts incl. FT and HPO rows, Fig. 2 dose curves + REPLAY per-repo premia; everything else supplement). Infrastructure: byte manifests (path, bytes, SHA-256, speaker, label, sentence id, take, intensity, sex) for RAVDESS speech (1,440/24/8), CREMA-D (7,442/91/6), SUBESCO-full as released (7,000/20/7, CC BY 4.0) plus the in-hand SUBESCO-980 repetition-clean panel, EmoDB (535/10/7, CC0 via Zenodo/audb); preregistered hygiene: exact-byte duplicate groups collapsed to lexically first path, label-conflicting groups dropped, zero-variance audio dropped (CREMA-D 1076_MTI_SAD_XX), stereo downmixed, all logged; log-mel cache exactly P1 (22.05 kHz, trim 30 dB, 64 mel, FFT 1024, hop 512, 128 frames, per-utterance z-score, train-only SpecAugment); SSL cache: torchaudio HUBERT_BASE and WAVLM_BASE_PLUS, weights SHA-pinned, 16 kHz, trim 30 dB, all 13 hidden states time-mean pooled, float16 [N,13,768], filename = SHA of (manifest SHA, bundle SHA, sr, trim, pooling, code SHA) (~16.4k utterances, ~1 GPU-h). Split table (one hashed CSV per corpus): replicates r=0,1,2; outer Random = StratifiedKFold(5, shuffle, split_seed) ignoring speaker; outer Grouped = StratifiedGroupKFold(5, shuffle, split_seed, groups=speaker); inner (25% of outer train): random stratified train_test_split allowing speaker overlap vs GroupShuffleSplit(0.25) by speaker; 20 Ridge draws d=0..19 for PROBE-CPU (S2 seed rule); LOSO by speaker id; dose and replay index sets. Assertions before any fit: zero speaker overlap in every grouped path, exactly-once OOF coverage, every class present in every fold; failure aborts. Dry run: synthetic audio manifests with the real speaker/class cardinalities through the whole pipeline (1 replicate x 4 cells x 5 folds x 3 models + 2 probe units + 2 partial-fine-tune fits + 8 HPO configs + 1 dose ladder + 1 replay unit); scorer and verifier must agree to 1e-12 on all synthetic outputs including rounded-field fixtures; 20-case mutation battery (row drop, label swap, fold overlap injection, seed drift, duplicated prediction rows, missing cell propagation) must be rejected 20/20. Timing probe: one partial-fine-tune fold on each of RAVDESS, CREMA-D, SUBESCO-full (3 fits, ~0.5 GPU-h) recorded before the tag; CTRL-2 budget in the registration is set from the measured value. Then OSF registration of the protocol PDF with the tag hash, OpenTimestamps anchor of the tag, and the NIST Randomness Beacon pulse for the audit draw fixed as the first pulse after the OSF timestamp. Per-fit DONE markers holding the predictions SHA; the runner skips verified DONE units on restart so an OS shutdown never ghost-bills. Append-only deviation file that the paper must cite by entry number.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: No scientific estimand. Gates: (i) verifier == scorer to 1e-12 on synthetic outputs; (ii) 20/20 mutation cases rejected; (iii) split-table assertions pass; (iv) measured fine-tune fold time recorded; if any gate fails the tag is not created and no real unit runs. Registration timestamp must precede the first real cache write (verified by ledger).

program.name: AUDIT-1: stratified, fixed-n probability audit of public SER code with realized-overlap execution and blind human coding
merged_from: P0 candidate-frame search protocol and E1-E8 exclusion codes
P0.5 random sample and execution-validation tier (AST-isolated split execution, now on the real manifests)
S1 beacon-seeded priority order, endpoint dictionary, hash-bound evidence receipts, exact hypergeometric envelope
S1 D2 executable-blob lineage predicate (fixed a priori, no branches)
P0's six non-speaker outcomes (cut, except two descriptive columns)
program.rationale: The audit is the paper's only non-collided contribution (prior-art matrix: none of 10 collision papers did probability sampling), yet its headline is labelled exploratory: lineage rule chosen after outcomes, five branches moving the envelope <=0.3 pp but consuming text three times, no human ever coded a repo, Y conflating validation-only with test-boundary leakage, 56/60 units with unknown paper linkage, and a resource cap adopted after seeing repo size. All three judges converged on Proposal 4's audit redesign (paper-linked stratum, test-vs-validation endpoint, human rater blinded from the AI rater, GitHub code search on corpus filename tokens) and on the statistician's objections that (a) elapsed-review-hour stopping is outcome-correlated, so n must be fixed with time-outs coded U, and (b) a kappa>=0.6 gate on 20-25 units is decided by noise, so kappa is reported with a CI and not used as a gate. Proposal 1's realized-overlap execution on the real manifest replaces P0.5's synthetic tier, makes the construct 'permits' partly 'realizes', supplies the construct check (static Y with realized overlap 0 = recorded false positive) and feeds REPLAY. Two search channels give a capture-recapture coverage estimate at zero cost.
program.design: FRAME (frozen at OSF date T0, one pass): channel A = P0 GitHub repository search (2 query families x 4 corpora RAVDESS/CREMA-D/IEMOCAP/EmoDB, top-100 best match) + arXiv API top-100 per corpus + one-hop snowball; channel B = GitHub code search on loader-only filename tokens ('03-01-0' RAVDESS, '_DFA_'/'_IEO_' CREMA-D, 'Ses01F_impro' IEMOCAP, '03a01Fa' EmoDB); union with the existing 383-URL log; canonicalize; snapshot default-branch commit SHA per candidate on T0. Lineage rule fixed before any screening: explicit fork/parent, identical top-level tree SHA, identical content-blob set, executable-blob containment >=0.90 (closed suffix list, notebook = one blob, dedup by blob SHA) with corroborator (same project name, identical root README blob, or owner lineage); keeper = unique upstream > earliest created_at > URL order; merge count reported once, no branches. Eligibility E1-E5 applied to the full list before the draw (10-min screening cap; unscreenable = ineligible with code). Stratum by regex on snapshot README/description: paper-linked (arxiv.org, doi.org, ieeexplore, aclanthology, isca-archive, or 'ICASSP'/'Interspeech' + title string) vs other; stratum sizes N_1, N_2 recorded. Coverage: Lincoln-Petersen estimate of the eligible frame from channel A/B overlap (descriptive). SAMPLE: beacon pulse (first after OSF timestamp); order = SHA256(pulse || canonical_id) within stratum; first 30 eligible per stratum, n=60 fixed; if a stratum has <30 eligible, take all and report. No extension, no replacement. RATING per unit, pinned commit, static plus fragment execution: Rater H = human (author, or the recruited coder if available) blind-codes ALL 60 units first? No: H codes a hash-selected 30 of the 60 (15 per stratum) BEFORE the AI rater runs on them, mechanised: the AI rater tool refuses a unit until human_code_<id>.json is in the hashed ledger; Rater AI = frozen prompt + evidence template (path:Lstart-Lend at pinned commit for the decisive split statement and its calling entry point; per-line fragment SHA-256). Per-unit cap 1.5 review-hours per rater, fixed a priori, exceeded -> U for that rater. Endpoint: Y_test (an active train->test/eval path permits same-speaker membership on both sides), Y_val (only a train->validation/model-selection path permits it), N (all active paths verified speaker-exclusive and enumeration closed), U (undecidable, cap, or no applicable split); descriptive columns: test set used for checkpoint/hyperparameter selection (Y/N/U), single split with no variance reported (Y/N/U), corpus set, notebook vs script, year, framework, reported top-line metric on RAVDESS/CREMA-D if any, and prior lineage membership in P0/P0.5/S1 samples with the historical verdict. Execution tier for every Y/N whose decisive split statement is AST-isolable: execute the fragment in an isolated namespace on the REAL RAVDESS/CREMA-D/EmoDB manifests (IEMOCAP: synthetic manifest only, no license), record realized train/test speaker-overlap fraction, test size and the index sets (feeds REPLAY); a static Y_test with realized overlap 0 is recorded as a false positive and the adjudicated verdict becomes N. Adjudication: H vs AI disagreements on the 30 double-coded units resolved by a written rule (evidence-chain completeness wins; unresolved -> U) applied by the author with both records published; the remaining 30 units get the AI verdict plus author review under the same rule. Reliability: Cohen's kappa (4-level and Y_test-vs-not) on the 30 units with 2,000-rep bootstrap CI; reported, not a gate; the human-only verdicts on the 30 are reported as a sensitivity estimate. STATISTICS: primary = stratum-weighted frame proportion of Y_test with a stratified Wilson-type (linearized, FPC) 95% interval; per-stratum Wilson intervals on Y_test/n_s and (Y_test+U)/n_s; partial-identification interval and the S1 exact hypergeometric joint >=95% envelope retained as a secondary frame-level bound; U-informativeness sensitivity: U units imputed by a preregistered logistic model on (stratum, notebook, corpus, has external data) fitted on Y/N units, reported once. Human budget ~110 h; 0 GPU.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Estimand: proportion of eligible public GitHub/arXiv-discoverable SER repository lineages (frame at T0, four corpora) whose active train->test boundary permits same-speaker membership (Y_test), overall (stratum-weighted) and per stratum. H_A1: Y_test/n_1 > 0.5 in the paper-linked stratum; H_A2: Y_test/n_2 > 0.5 in the other stratum; one-sided exact binomial tests with U counted as non-positive, alpha 0.05, Holm over the two (audit family, separate from the controlled-study family because the estimand differs). Power at n_s=30, true 0.70, 12% U: ~0.6 per stratum, ~0.85 pooled; the pooled test is reported as a secondary. Secondary estimates (CIs, no tests): Y_val-only fraction; realized-overlap distribution among executed Y_test units; false-positive count; kappa with CI; agreement with historical P0/P0.5/S1 verdicts on re-sampled lineages; U-imputation sensitivity; Lincoln-Petersen frame coverage. Forbidden: prevalence x effect multiplication.

program.name: CTRL-1: unified outer x inner protocol factorial (RR/RG/GR/GG) x 3 corpora x 5 representation levels x 3 draw+seed replicates
merged_from: P1 (RR and GG cells, engine, features, speaker-paired inference; LOSO and FNO cut)
A (RG and GR cells; O_G/I_G decomposition, now with shared init across cells and matched inner sizes)
S0 (HuBERT-base and WavLM-base+ early-stopped linear probes as model levels on the same splits)
S2 (partition draws crossed with seeds inside the main design)
S3 (SUBESCO as a full-protocol corpus level; 980 panel as a secondary level)
D1 (cut; RAVDESS structure handled by MECH-0 and PROBE-CPU)
P4 multi-corpus queue (cut; EmoDB only, descriptive)
program.rationale: P1 spent 85% of its 1,620 fits on LOSO, whose only message (LOSO > GroupKFold in 8/8 cells) is a training-size confound now closed on CPU by PROBE-CPU; FNO never changed a sign or a decision and needed a justification sentence. A is the one arm that decomposes the pipeline premium the paper flags four times (RAVDESS O_G +9.99, I_G +5.13) and never entered the paper; folding RG/GR into the main design with a protocol-free seed key removes A's seed-stream and allocation-size confounds. S0's six contrasts were all Holm-significant on P1's splits, so probes belong as model levels in one family, not a separate 6-test family. S3 becomes a corpus level under the full protocol (never done: SUBESCO was tested only with Ridge probes and the allocation design). The AC's objection that cutting Transformer leaves two convolutional levels is met by keeping Transformer at 3 replicates instead of 5. Statistician objections met: draw-vs-seed variance decomposed on RAVDESS CNN; a two-way cluster bootstrap (speaker x replicate) reported as a secondary interval so 'not a split artifact' is covered; the RAVDESS-CREMA-D difference is an estimate, not a test. EmoDB (10 speakers) is included as a descriptive level only, because n=10 paired units has negligible power.
program.design: Corpora in the family: RAVDESS speech, CREMA-D, SUBESCO-full as released; descriptive only: EmoDB; secondary level: SUBESCO-980 repetition-clean panel on identical speaker folds (paired-by-speaker contrast with SUBESCO-full isolates near-duplicate-take leakage). Model levels: CNN, ResNet-SE, Transformer (P1 frozen configs; class count per corpus) on log-mel; HuBERT-base and WavLM-base+ final-layer time-mean 768-d early-stopped linear probes (S0 contract). Engine (all levels): class-balanced CE, AdamW (lr 1e-3, wd 1e-4; Transformer 3e-4), batch 64, <=100 epochs, cosine T_max 100, early stop patience 15 on inner weighted CE, strict-min checkpoint, restore best, float32 deterministic, test touched once. Cells: RR, RG, GR, GG (outer letter first); inner fit/val sizes fixed at exactly 75/25 of outer train in both inner arms. Replicates r=0,1,2 (draw + training seed, shared across models and cells within corpus, so cells are speaker-paired on identical outer test folds). Draw-vs-seed decomposition: RAVDESS CNN additionally runs seeds {0,1,2} x draws {0,1,2} off-diagonal (6 extra combinations x 4 cells x 5 folds = 120 fits, ~0.7 GPU-h). Fits: 3 models x 4 cells x 5 folds x 3 r = 180 per corpus: RAVDESS ~1.0 h, CREMA-D ~3.0 h, SUBESCO-full ~3.0 h, EmoDB ~0.4 h, SUBESCO-980 ~0.6 h, seed-crossing 0.7 h, Transformer overhead ~0.8 h -> ~9.5 GPU-h scratch; probe units 2 encoders x 5 corpus levels x 4 cells x 5 folds x 3 r = 600 at ~3 s = ~0.5 GPU-h. Fixed run order corpus -> model -> r -> fold -> cell; one retry for failures before outer-test access; a missing outer fold voids the (corpus, model, cell, r) cell and dependent contrasts (p=1 placeholder, family size unchanged). Outputs per fit: predictions.csv with all logits for every OOF utterance, penultimate embeddings for test and training-pool utterances (for MECH-0), history, config, hashes. Per-speaker OOF UAR on each speaker's own utterances per (corpus, level, cell, r); accuracy/macro-F1 released, no inference, no text.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: All estimands are speaker-paired UAR differences (unit = speaker; n = 24 / 91 / 20), averaged within speaker over the 3 replicates and over the named model levels before differencing; 10,000-replicate whole-speaker percentile bootstrap 95% CIs (fixed seed) and two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank (zero_method wilcox). Per corpus c in {RAVDESS, CREMA-D, SUBESCO-full}: (1) Delta_pipe^scratch(c) = mean over CNN, ResNet-SE, Transformer of [UAR(RR) - UAR(GG)] > 0; (2) Delta_pipe^probe(c) = mean over HuBERT, WavLM probes of [UAR(RR) - UAR(GG)] > 0; (3) Delta_outer(c) = mean over all 5 levels of [UAR(RG) - UAR(GG)] > 0; (4) Delta_inner(c) = mean over all 5 levels of [UAR(GR) - UAR(GG)] > 0. These 12 tests are members of the single 21-test program family (Holm, alpha 0.05). Power note: SUBESCO n=20 with per-speaker delta SD ~5 pp gives ~0.75 power for a 3 pp mean and >0.95 for >=6 pp; RAVDESS n=24 similar; CREMA-D n=91 detects ~1 pp. Secondary estimates with CIs and no tests: per-level cells (15 corpus x level pipeline deltas); interaction (RR-RG)-(GR-GG) per corpus; RAVDESS-minus-CREMA-D pipeline delta with two-sample speaker bootstrap CI (explicitly a marginal comparison of different speaker populations, not an interaction); SUBESCO-full minus SUBESCO-980 pipeline delta paired by speaker (take-leakage increment); EmoDB deltas; two-way (speaker x replicate) cluster-bootstrap intervals for every family contrast; draw-vs-seed variance components on RAVDESS CNN; replicate sign counts (x/3).

program.name: PROBE-CPU: frozen-feature Ridge factorial on cached all-layer features (head x split family x layer x 20 draws; LOSO vs Group5 vs size-matched LOSO; SUBESCO full vs 980)
merged_from: S4 WavLM layer weighting (NO-GO, now a zero-GPU layer factor)
P1 LOSO arm (1,380 fits; replaced by CPU LOSO / LOSO-sub on frozen features)
S0 (trained-probe head, reused from CTRL-1 for the head contrast)
program.rationale: S0 (early-stopped probe, P1 split) and S2 (Ridge, 20 draws) disagree 2-5x on RAVDESS (2.8-6.2 vs 13.9 pp) on identical features and no run in the artifact crosses head with split family; a reviewer will ask which drives the premium. S4's layer question never ran although all layers cost nothing once cached. P1's LOSO > GroupKFold finding is the one open puzzle a bare cut would forfeit; Proposal 3's size-matched LOSO on frozen features with a head that has no early stopping closes it for CPU minutes and was flagged by both the statistician and the feasibility judge as the cheapest valid resolution. The statistician's objection that Wilcoxon over draws treats draws as n is met by making the head contrast speaker-paired (per-speaker delta averaged over draws) and keeping all draw-level summaries as descriptors.
program.design: Features: HuBERT-base and WavLM-base+ all 13 layers from PREREG-0 cache; corpora RAVDESS, CREMA-D, SUBESCO-full, SUBESCO-980, EmoDB. Head A: StandardScaler(train fold) + RidgeClassifier(alpha 1, cholesky, class_weight balanced), no inner validation. Splits: 20 draws d=0..19 of StratifiedKFold(5) vs StratifiedGroupKFold(5) by speaker (S2 seed rule), plus the CTRL-1 replicate partitions r=0..2 so head A is speaker-paired with the CTRL-1 early-stopped probe (head B) on identical folds. Layer factor: final (12), mid (6), mean of 1-12. Fold count on head A, final layer, all corpora: Group5 (draw 0), LOSO (deterministic), LOSO-sub (each LOSO training set subsampled by hash order to the mean Group5 training-speaker fraction, 80%). SUBESCO-full vs SUBESCO-980 on identical speaker folds (draws 0-19). Fits: 5 corpus levels x 2 encoders x 3 layers x 2 protocols x 20 draws x 5 folds = 6,000 Ridge fits (~0.1 s each) + LOSO/LOSO-sub 5 x 2 x (24+91+20+20+10) x 2 = ~3,300; all CPU (~2 CPU-h). Outputs: per-draw speaker-equal OOF UAR contrasts and per-speaker OOF UAR.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Family member (1 test): H_head(RAVDESS): per-speaker [Delta_RG(Ridge) - Delta_RG(early-stopped probe)] on the CTRL-1 r=0..2 partitions, averaged over encoders and replicates within speaker, two-sided Wilcoxon over 24 speakers + whole-speaker bootstrap CI; a rejection with positive sign attributes the S0/S2 discrepancy to head choice, a non-rejection with a preregistered <2 pp point estimate attributes it to split family (the 20-draw Ridge vs P1-style partition contrast is reported as the companion descriptor). Prespecified equivalence (separate from the family, TOST alpha 0.05): UAR(LOSO-sub) - UAR(Group5) within +/-1 pp on RAVDESS and CREMA-D (speaker-paired), together with the descriptor UAR(LOSO) - UAR(Group5) > 0; joint reading 'LOSO's advantage is a training-set-size effect'. Descriptors only: per-corpus 3-encoder Ridge direction stability (>=18/20 positive and q05 > 0, S2 rule); layer-wise Delta_RG per encoder x corpus with Spearman over layer index; SUBESCO-full minus SUBESCO-980 Delta_RG paired by speaker with whole-speaker bootstrap CI (near-duplicate-take increment on frozen features).

program.name: CTRL-2: partially fine-tuned WavLM-base+ pipeline contrast (RR vs GG) on 3 corpora, r=0 partitions
merged_from: S0/S2/S3 claim registries' forbidden extrapolation to fine-tuned models (the gap this arm fills)
program.rationale: Every controlled number in the frozen program comes from small from-scratch models (RAVDESS grouped UAR 39-46%) or frozen probes whose RAVDESS premium shrank to 2.8-6.2 pp, and the registries forbid extrapolation to fine-tuning, which is the regime the audited code mostly uses. Kept from Proposal 0 at one replicate on shared folds so the fine-tuned row is speaker-paired with all five CTRL-1 levels. Feasibility judges warned every fine-tune cost is extrapolated: the budget is set from the PREREG-0 timing probe, capped at 10 GPU-h, with a preregistered drop order (SUBESCO first, then CREMA-D) and p=1 placeholders. Proposal 1's validity anchor is adopted: a grouped-UAR range triggers an implementation audit, not exclusion.
program.design: WavLM-base+ (pinned weights); CNN feature encoder and transformer layers 1-8 frozen; top 4 transformer layers + mean-pool + linear head trainable; fp16 autocast, batch 16, random 3 s crops for training, full utterance capped at 10 s at evaluation, AdamW (encoder 5e-5, head 1e-3, wd 1e-2), <=15 epochs, early stop patience 3 on inner weighted CE (inner mirrors outer: ungrouped under RR, grouped under GG), strict-min checkpoint, per-epoch checkpoints for resume. Splits: CTRL-1 replicate r=0 outer/inner partitions, cells RR and GG only. Fits: 3 corpora x 2 cells x 5 folds = 30 (timing-probe-based estimate ~1.5 h RAVDESS, ~3.5 h CREMA-D, ~3 h SUBESCO-full). Hard cap 10 GPU-h checked at fold boundaries; if hit, remaining corpus reported incomplete with p=1. fp16 non-determinism disclosed: verifier equality applies to scoring from committed predictions (exact); no bitwise retrain claim for this arm. Validity anchor (not a hypothesis): GG UAR on CREMA-D within 55-70% (literature range for frozen/partially fine-tuned base SSL); a miss triggers a logged implementation audit before scoring is unlocked.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Per corpus: Delta_pipe^ft(c) = speaker-mean of [UAR(RR) - UAR(GG)] for the fine-tuned level (r=0) > 0; two-sided Wilcoxon on speaker-level differences (n = 24/91/20) and 10,000-replicate whole-speaker bootstrap CI. Three family members. Secondary estimate (no test): Delta_pipe^ft(c) minus Delta_pipe^probe(c) on the same speakers and folds with paired CI (whether fine-tuning re-exposes speaker information that frozen final-layer features attenuate).

program.name: HPO: hyperparameter search on leaky vs grouped inner validation (ResNet-SE, RAVDESS + CREMA-D)
merged_from: P0/P0.5 outcome 'test set / validation used for selection' (36.7% in P0.5), now an audit descriptive column linked to a measured effect
program.rationale: The dossier flags 'premium under hyperparameter search on leaky validation' as the realistic failure mode found in public code and never measured (P1 used fixed configs). All three judges flagged Proposal 3's HPO arm as a cheap (~2 GPU-h) graft that ties the audit's Y_val units to a measured quantity. Same harness, one model, small preregistered grid, selection by inner validation.
program.design: ResNet-SE only; RAVDESS and CREMA-D; cells RR and GG; replicate r=0 partitions; grid of 8 configs (lr {3e-4, 1e-3} x weight decay {1e-4, 1e-3} x dropout {0.1, 0.3}); each config trained on each of the 5 outer folds with the cell's inner split (train_seed shared across configs); per fold the config with the highest inner-validation UAR is selected and its outer-test predictions used (no refit). 2 corpora x 2 cells x 8 configs x 5 folds = 160 fits (~0.4 h RAVDESS, ~1.3 h CREMA-D); cap 3 GPU-h. Comparator = the CTRL-1 r=0 ResNet-SE cell (lr 1e-3, wd 1e-4, dropout 0.1, which is a member of the grid).
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Per corpus (2 family members): Delta_HPO(c) = [UAR(RR,hpo) - UAR(GG,hpo)] - [UAR(RR,fixed) - UAR(GG,fixed)] on speaker-paired UAR; H: > 0 (tuning on a speaker-overlapping validation set enlarges the premium); two-sided Wilcoxon + whole-speaker bootstrap CI. Descriptive: distribution of selected configs under RR vs GG; selected-config inner-validation UAR minus its outer-test UAR under RR (the reported-number optimism a Y_val repository would show).

program.name: DOSE: leakage dose-response with a fixed prompt-disjoint test half (RAVDESS, CREMA-D)
merged_from: C/P5 mechanism-exposure salvage (144 checkpoints; its q=1 cross-prompt case is one rung of this ladder)
P1 untested gap 'dose-response' (only 0% and 100% overlap measured)
program.rationale: P1 measured only 0% and 100% speaker overlap; C/P5 measured a single 22-utterance cross-prompt exposure with no admissible inference, a key-exposure incident and a review waiver, ending at +4.57 pp below its own threshold. AUDIT-1's realized-overlap distribution will show intermediate overlap in the wild, so the paper needs a within-pipeline dose curve to interpret it. Proposal 3's ladder (fixed prompt-disjoint half test set, grouped inner validation, nested doses, Page's L with speakers as matched blocks) was judged the correct matched-block design; the statistician's TOST margin for 'no spillover' is added via a rotated partial-exposure contrast.
program.design: RAVDESS and CREMA-D; CNN and ResNet-SE; outer StratifiedGroupKFold(5) by speaker for replicates r=0..2. Each speaker's utterances are split into prompt-disjoint halves (RAVDESS statement 01/02; CREMA-D the P5 sentence sets A/B); fixed test = half B of the test-fold speakers at every dose. Dose q in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0} = fraction of test-fold speakers (hash-ordered, nested, rotated across replicates so each speaker is exposed in exactly one partial dose) whose half A is added to training; training-speaker utterances with matching labels removed by hash so training size and label counts are constant; inner validation grouped, drawn from train-fold speakers only, identical across doses; class weights recomputed. 2 corpora x 4 doses x 5 folds x 3 r x 2 models = 240 fits (~0.7 h RAVDESS, ~2 h CREMA-D); cap 4 GPU-h. If the program cap is threatened, DOSE is reduced to RAVDESS only (preregistered).
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Per speaker: UAR on its half-B test items at each dose, averaged over models and replicates. Family members (2): per corpus, Page's L trend test across the four doses with speakers as blocks; H: UAR increases monotonically with q. Prespecified equivalence (separate, TOST alpha 0.05, margin +/-1.5 pp): at q=0.5, unexposed test-fold speakers' UAR minus their own q=0 UAR is equivalent to zero (no spillover), while exposed speakers' gain is reported with CI. Descriptors: slope from per-speaker OLS over doses with cluster-bootstrap CI; fraction of the q=1 premium reached at q=0.25; RAVDESS vs CREMA-D slope difference (two-sample bootstrap, no test); q=1 minus q=0 alongside C's historical +6.42/+1.85 pp.

program.name: REPLAY: our fixed pipeline trained on the realized splits of audited Y_test repositories vs size-matched speaker-exclusive counterfactuals
merged_from: P0.5 execution-validation tier (AST-isolated split execution, now on real manifests via AUDIT-1)
P2/Theta scenario-burden analysis (replaced by an empirical per-repository quantity)
BRIDGE (Proposal 4's repository re-execution; not adopted, see cut entry)
program.rationale: The frozen manuscript forbids multiplying prevalence by effect size and therefore never connects its two halves; the AC ranked Proposal 4's bridge as the most citable idea but the feasibility judge and statistician found repository re-execution on Windows/torch 2.11 of Kaggle-path notebooks (~100 engineering hours, per-repo environments, non-prespecifiable edits) the leg most likely to fail. All three judges flagged Proposal 1's REPLAY as the de-risked alternative: execute the repo's own split code on the real manifest (already done in AUDIT-1), then train OUR fixed pipeline on the realized partition versus size-matched speaker-exclusive counterfactuals. The estimand stays inside our pipeline, needs no foreign environment, costs ~2 GPU-h, and gives a per-repository premium without multiplication.
program.design: Units: every AUDIT-1 Y_test lineage whose decisive split fragment executed on the real RAVDESS or CREMA-D manifest with realized overlap > 0 (expected 12-25), taken in beacon order up to 16. For each: realized train/test index sets (single split as the repo does it, or its k folds; validation carved as the repo does, else grouped 25%); counterfactual: 2 StratifiedGroupKFold-style speaker-disjoint partitions matched on test-utterance count and class proportions (hash-seeded). Model: ResNet-SE at CTRL-1 config, 2 training seeds; probe level (WavLM Ridge, final layer) on the same index sets on CPU. Fits: up to 16 repos x (1 realized + 2 counterfactual) x 2 seeds = 96 fits, RAVDESS-heavy (~1.5-2 GPU-h); reserved budget 2 GPU-h that other arms may not consume; cap 2.5. If fewer than 8 qualifying repos exist, the arm is reported descriptively (sign counts) and its family test enters as p=1 (rule fixed now).
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Delta_repo = UAR(realized split) - mean UAR(counterfactual splits), per repository, seed-averaged, per level. Family member (1): exact sign test across repositories on the ResNet-SE Delta_repo; H: majority positive. Descriptors: median Delta_repo with repository-level bootstrap CI, per corpus; Spearman of Delta_repo with realized overlap fraction and with test size; Ridge-probe Delta_repo alongside; each Delta_repo plotted against the CTRL-1 premium of the same corpus (Fig. 2). Reported next to, never multiplied with, the AUDIT-1 prevalence.

program.name: MECH-0: inference-only mechanism readouts on saved CTRL-1 embeddings (sibling nearest-neighbour, speaker-ID probe, layer-wise speaker vs premium)
merged_from: B SUBESCO allocation (its unregistered c20r1 -> c20r2 take-density hint, now a readout on SUBESCO-full vs 980)
C/P5 gap 'no representational test of speaker identity'
D1 speech-song (cut; the RAVDESS sibling structure it depended on is read out here)
program.rationale: Proposal 2's sibling-take hypothesis was judged the best scientific idea in the panel, and its nearest-neighbour readout costs only inference on embeddings CTRL-1 already saves; it explains the SUBESCO-full vs 980 contrast the program measures and gives the paper a bounded mechanism sentence in place of the forbidden 'uses voiceprint' claim. Zero training, no family tests, one supplement table and one sentence.
program.design: From CTRL-1 RR and GG checkpoints (CNN, ResNet-SE; RAVDESS, CREMA-D, SUBESCO-full, SUBESCO-980; r=0): penultimate embeddings for all training-pool and outer-test utterances (extraction ~0.3 GPU-h). (a) Sibling-NN: for each RR test utterance, cosine nearest neighbour in its training fold, categorised as sibling (same speaker x sentence x emotion, different take/intensity) / same speaker non-sibling / same sentence other speaker / other; conditional accuracy per category with whole-speaker bootstrap CI; share of test items with a sibling NN per corpus. (b) Speaker-ID linear probe on embeddings (sentence-disjoint halves within training speakers) vs chance, RR vs GG checkpoints. (c) On the PREREG-0 SSL caches: per-layer speaker-ID probe accuracy and per-layer PROBE-CPU Delta_RG; Spearman across 13 layers x 2 encoders x 3 corpora. CPU except (a) extraction.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: No family tests. Prespecified descriptive readouts with CIs: P(correct | NN sibling) - P(correct | NN other) per corpus (expected large in RAVDESS/SUBESCO-full, undefined or near zero in CREMA-D/SUBESCO-980); speaker-ID probe accuracy relative to chance for RR vs GG checkpoints; layer-wise correlation between speaker-probe accuracy and premium. Reported in the supplement with one bounded sentence in the main text; forbidden wording: 'the SER model uses speaker identity', mediation shares.

program.name: STAT-1: one-shot scoring under one 21-test program family + 2-test audit family, independent verifier replay, 2% bitwise retrain check, number-checked insert
merged_from: P1 summarizer + independent statistics verification (the pattern that achieved 0.0 error)
A/B/C/D1 scoring contracts and post-outcome verifiers (replaced)
S0/S2/S3 claim registries and S3 600 replay refits / 78-case mutation battery (replaced by the PREREG-0 battery and a 2% retrain check)
Paper numeric-insert manifest and 107 KB number checker (replaced by one results.json -> numeric_insert.tex)
program.rationale: The frozen program ran separate families (P1 24, S0 6, A 4) and descriptive readouts with routing decided after outcomes (Rev 10, record 271), and seven per-arm verifiers, several written after scoring. The statistician's universal objection was that no proposal stated a program-wise error rate or a rule for how many rejections a headline claim needs. One family with Holm gives strong FWER control across the whole controlled program; the claim-to-rejection map is fixed here; routing is fixed by the PREREG-0 slot map regardless of sign.
program.design: Executed once after the ledgers of CTRL-1, PROBE-CPU, CTRL-2, HPO, DOSE, REPLAY and AUDIT-1 are locked and hashed. Scorer produces: per-speaker cell tables; the 21 family contrasts with CIs, raw and Holm-adjusted p (family = 12 CTRL-1 + 3 CTRL-2 + 2 HPO + 2 DOSE + 1 REPLAY + 1 PROBE head); the 2-test audit family; TOST results (LOSO-sub, no-spillover); all secondary estimates; audit fractions, intervals, envelope, kappa, coverage; results.json, numeric_insert.tex, figure data JSON. Verifier (frozen in PREREG-0, no shared modules, reads only run_plan, split tables, manifests, predictions and the adjudication CSV) reproduces every reported number to 1e-12 (fp16 CTRL-2 units are scored from committed predictions, so exactness applies); any mismatch is reported verbatim, never patched. 2% hash-selected float32 fits retrained and compared bitwise. Claim-to-rejection map (fixed): Claim 1 requires H_A1 or H_A2 (stated per stratum); Claim 2 requires all three scratch RR-GG rejections and at least two probe RR-GG rejections; Claim 3 requires RG-GG and GR-GG rejections on at least two corpora; Claim 4 requires the CTRL-2 rejection on RAVDESS and at least one other corpus, and the HPO rejection on at least one corpus; Claim 5 requires both Page's L rejections; Claim 6 requires the REPLAY sign-test rejection with n>=8; any claim whose requirements fail is written as 'not supported' in the main text, not moved to the supplement.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: No new estimand. Gates: verifier replay exact; 2% retrain bitwise identical for float32 arms; number checker red = 0 before the manuscript is frozen. Holm within the 21-test program family and within the 2-test audit family, alpha 0.05; equivalence tests at alpha 0.05 outside the families.

program.name: P1 LOSO from-scratch arm (1,380 of 1,620 fits) and D1 LOSO folds (552 of 792)
program.rationale: 85% of P1's fits (~21 GPU-h) and 70% of D1's for a contrast confounded with training-set size (LOSO trains on 23/24 or 90/91 speakers vs 19-20/24 or 72-73/91), 3 of 4 CREMA-D Random-LOSO non-rejections, and D1's four LOSO secondaries not conclusive. program.rationale: FNO tracked CNN in sign and magnitude in every P1 cell (RAVDESS 15.39 vs 17.71; CREMA-D 1.82 vs 2.80), was the only architecture needing a probe-choice justification, and produced B's only negative c20r1 cells. program.name: P0 purposive 32-repo audit, six non-speaker P0 outcomes, purposive-vs-random comparison, P0.5 separate n=30 sample, S1 lineage sensitivity branches (D1/D3/291/N282), P2/Theta
program.rationale: The purposive layer was self-classified as a working-model diagnostic with no design-based inference; six of seven outcomes and the Newcombe/Fisher/Holm battery reached no paper lineage; P0.5 and S1 estimated the same construct on overlapping frames with 2 shared repos and were never reconciled; the four lineage branches all yield 44/9/7 with envelopes within 0.3 pp. AUDIT-1 fixes one lineage rule before screening, keeps two of the P0 columns as descriptors (test-set selection, no-variance reporting), and records historical-verdict agreement for any re-sampled lineage as a free cross-lineage check. All four are absorbed: S0's probes are CTRL-1 model levels; S2's draws, S3's SUBESCO-980 panel and S4's layer question are PROBE-CPU factors on one all-layer cache; content-addressed cache identity and the PREREG-0 mutation battery replace the release ladder.

pipeline_order: Week 0-2 PREREG-0: freeze code, run_plan.csv, seed table, split generator, scorer and independent verifier; build manifests, hygiene log, log-mel cache (CPU) and all-layer SSL cache (~1 GPU-h); run split-table assertions; synthetic dry run + 20-case mutation battery (~1 GPU-h); fine-tune timing probe (3 folds, ~0.5 GPU-h) and set CTRL-2 budget; OSF registration + git tag + OpenTimestamps; record NIST beacon pulse; recruit and declare the second coder (or declare none)

Week 2 onward AUDIT-1 (CPU + human, runs in parallel with all GPU stages): frame rebuild via channels A and B -> lineage rule + E1-E5 on the full candidate list -> stratum regex -> beacon-ordered draw of 30 + 30 -> human blind coding of the hash-selected 30 units (hash-committed before the AI rater is allowed to run on them) -> AI rating of all 60 -> fragment execution on real manifests (realized overlap, index sets) -> adjudication by written rule -> kappa, coverage, U-imputation sensitivity

Week 2-5 GPU-1 CTRL-1: fixed order corpus (RAVDESS, CREMA-D, SUBESCO-full, SUBESCO-980, EmoDB) -> model -> replicate -> fold -> cell, then RAVDESS CNN seed-crossing, then 600 probe units on cached features (~10 GPU-h; per-fit DONE markers, resumable)
Week 3-5 PROBE-CPU in parallel on CPU: 6,000 Ridge draw fits + LOSO/LOSO-sub + head crossing on CTRL-1 partitions + SUBESCO full vs 980
Week 5-6 GPU-2 CTRL-2: partial WavLM fine-tune, r=0 RR/GG x 5 folds, corpus order RAVDESS, CREMA-D, SUBESCO-full (~8 GPU-h, cap 10, preregistered drop order SUBESCO then CREMA-D)
Week 6 GPU-3 HPO: 160 ResNet-SE fits (~2 GPU-h, cap 3)
Week 6-7 GPU-4 DOSE: 240 fits (~3 GPU-h, cap 4; reduced to RAVDESS-only if the 30 GPU-h program cap is projected to be exceeded)
Week 7-8 GPU-5 REPLAY (after AUDIT-1 execution tier closes): up to 16 repos x 3 partitions x 2 seeds ResNet-SE (~2 GPU-h reserved, cap 2.5) + Ridge on CPU
Week 8 GPU-6 MECH-0 embedding extraction and inference-only readouts (~0.3 GPU-h); 2% hash-selected bitwise retrain check (~0.3 GPU-h)

Week 8-9 ledger lock and hash of all predictions, embeddings, audit records and adjudication CSV; STAT-1 one-shot scoring (21-test family, 2-test audit family, TOSTs) and independent verifier replay; number checker red = 0

Week 9-12 manuscript fill-in under the fixed slot map and claim-to-rejection map; arXiv preprint; code, split tables, predictions and audit receipts released with the tag; Interspeech 2027 submission (target early March 2027); total author hours ~320 (prereg 60, audit 110, engineering/monitoring 90, writing 60) plus ~20 h from the second coder
synthesis.preregistration_notes: Registered on OSF with the git tag hash and an OpenTimestamps anchor before any real cache write, adjudication or fit. Fixed and not revisable: (1) Venue and calendar: ICASSP 2027 (2026-09-16) is abandoned; target Interspeech 2027 with an arXiv preprint at ledger lock; a 12-week execution plan with author hours is part of the registration. (2) Families: one 21-test controlled-program family (12 CTRL-1 + 3 CTRL-2 + 2 HPO + 2 DOSE + 1 REPLAY + 1 PROBE head), Holm alpha 0.05, missing tests enter as p=1 with the family size unchanged; one 2-test audit family (per-stratum one-sided exact binomial vs 0.5, U as non-positive, Holm); two equivalence tests (LOSO-sub +/-1 pp; no-spillover +/-1.5 pp) at alpha 0.05 outside the families; everything else is an estimate with a CI and no test. Claim-to-rejection map is fixed in STAT-1; a claim whose requirements fail is written as 'not supported' in the main text. (3) Unit of inference = speaker; per-speaker OOF UAR; averaging over replicates and named model levels precedes differencing; whole-speaker percentile bootstrap (10,000, fixed seed) and two-sided Wilcoxon; two-way (speaker x replicate) cluster-bootstrap intervals reported as secondary for every family contrast; replicate sign counts and draw/seed variance components are descriptors. (4) The RAVDESS-minus-CREMA-D difference is a marginal comparison of different speaker populations and is registered as an estimate, not a hypothesis; the corpus-dependence direction is cited as published (Ibrahim et al. 2026; Zielonka et al. 2022). (5) Hygiene exclusions, the SUBESCO-full/980 pairing, EmoDB as descriptive-only, and no LOSO training, no accuracy/macro-F1 inference, no per-level tests, no additional encoders, corpora, heads or arms after the tag. (6) Audit: lineage rule, stratum regex, n=60 fixed (30+30), 1.5 review-hour per-rater per-unit cap coded as U (elapsed hours are never a stopping rule), endpoint dictionary, the human-before-AI mechanised ordering on 30 hash-selected units, kappa reported with CI and not used as a gate, the adjudication rule, the U-imputation covariate model, the Lincoln-Petersen coverage estimate, and the false-positive rule (static Y_test with realized overlap 0 -> N). (7) Budget: program hard cap 30 GPU-h; per-arm caps CTRL-1 12, CTRL-2 10 (set from the measured timing probe), HPO 3, DOSE 4, REPLAY 2.5 reserved, MECH-0 0.5; truncation order if the program cap is projected to be exceeded: DOSE reduced to RAVDESS-only, then HPO CREMA-D dropped, then CTRL-2 by its own drop order; no design is shrunk mid-run in any other way; every started unit enters the public ledger. (8) Verifier and scorer are frozen before outcomes and exercised on synthetic fixtures including rounded fields and fp16-scored units; any post-run scorer/verifier disagreement is reported verbatim; fp16 CTRL-2 units are declared non-bitwise-reproducible and are verified from committed predictions only. (9) Routing: the 4-page slot map (Fig. 1A audit by stratum; Fig. 1B forest of the 21 family contrasts; Table 1 per-corpus RR-GG scratch / RR-GG probe / RG-GG / GR-GG / FT / HPO rows; Fig. 2 dose curves and REPLAY per-repository premia) is fixed regardless of sign; supplement carries PROBE-CPU tables, MECH-0, EmoDB, secondary estimates. (10) Prior-art paragraph, drafted now for Related Work: 'The Random-versus-speaker-independent gap on RAVDESS and CREMA-D is established (Ibrahim, Ghoraba and Ghoraba 2026 report 95.8% vs 48.1% and 73.5% vs 53.1%; Zielonka et al. 2022 report the same direction). Those gaps compare different papers, models and pipelines. We contribute a same-implementation, same-partition, speaker-paired estimate of the gap and of its outer-test and inner-selection components, which the published numbers cannot give, and we treat the direction and ordering of the anchor-corpus effects as a replication rather than a finding.' (11) Forbidden claims: prevalence x effect multiplication, universal correction factor, 'speaker identity alone' or 'uses voiceprint', mediation shares, extrapolation beyond the six representation levels, language-causal statements for SUBESCO, and any reuse of 2026 P1/S0/S2/S3 numbers as updates (estimands changed: hygiene, fold family, model set); the 2026 P1 table is cited once as an independent prior replication. (12) Any deviation is written to the append-only deviation file and cited in the paper by entry number.
risks: CTRL-2 cost: the partial fine-tune estimate is set from a 3-fold timing probe, not from a full run; a 2x overrun consumes the program slack and triggers the preregistered truncation (SUBESCO fine-tune row incomplete with p=1), removing the fine-tune claim for the non-English corpus.

REPLAY depends on AUDIT-1 producing >=8 Y_test lineages whose split fragment executes on the real RAVDESS/CREMA-D manifests; IEMOCAP-only and external-data repositories cannot be executed, so the replay set is biased toward simple RAVDESS/CREMA-D loaders and, if <8 qualify, the bridge claim degrades to sign counts (rule fixed in advance).

Human reliability: the human coder may be the author, who has seen ~90 prior audit outcomes; the mechanised human-before-AI ordering and hash commitment enforce sequence but not independence of judgment, and a 30-unit kappa CI is roughly +/-0.25; the audit is therefore labelled AI-assisted with a single-human reliability check unless a second coder is recruited and declared before the tag.

Frame coverage remains a bounded GitHub/arXiv-discoverable frame; the Lincoln-Petersen estimate from two search channels assumes channel independence, which is violated when a repository is both keyword- and filename-discoverable, so coverage will be over-estimated and is reported as such.

SUBESCO-full as released bundles near-duplicate-take leakage with speaker leakage; the family test on SUBESCO-full measures the as-released practice premium, and the speaker-only interpretation rests on the secondary full-vs-980 contrast and MECH-0, which have no family test.

SUBESCO (20 speakers) and RAVDESS (24) give ~0.75 power for 3 pp probe-level premia after Holm over 21 tests; a probe RR-GG non-rejection on SUBESCO is plausible and would leave Claim 2 resting on the 'at least two probe rejections' rule.

Speaker-paired primary inference conditions on the three partitions; the two-way cluster bootstrap is a secondary descriptor, so a reviewer who insists on partition-level inference will find only three replicates per corpus.

Prior-art collision persists for the effect half; the paper's distinctiveness rests on the audit with realized overlap, the decomposition, HPO, dose and REPLAY. If a probability audit or a realized-split study of public SER code appears before March 2027, the contribution narrows to the execution-verified endpoint and the decomposition.

Governance: the plan removes result-dependent routing by rule, but the author produced 13 plan revisions in 9 days last time; the only enforcement is the OSF timestamp, the frozen verifier, the fixed slot map and the deviation file, which make deviations visible rather than impossible.

Windows/torch 2.11 determinism is verified only by the 2% retrain check on float32 arms; the fp16 fine-tune arm and any driver update mid-run could break exact replay for those units, which is disclosed but not recoverable.

Calendar: ~320 author hours over 12 weeks alongside a recruited coder is realistic only if the audit starts in week 2 and runs in parallel; audit review hours, not GPU time, are the binding constraint.
resulting_paper_claims: Claim 1 (audit, confirmatory): in a publicly preregistered, beacon-ordered, stratified probability sample of 60 eligible public GitHub/arXiv SER repository lineages (frame rule and endpoint fixed before screening), the fraction whose active train-test boundary permits same-speaker membership exceeds one half in the paper-linked stratum and/or in the other stratum (per-stratum exact tests, stratum-weighted frame estimate with interval, partial-identification interval and frame envelope), with validation-only leakage, realized train/test speaker overlap from executing the repositories' own split code on the real corpora, false-positive count, human-AI agreement (kappa with CI on 30 units) and frame coverage reported.

Claim 2 (controlled, confirmatory): under one implementation, one feature cache, shared initialization and identical speaker-paired partitions, speaker-nonexclusive splitting at both boundaries (RR vs GG) inflates UAR on RAVDESS, CREMA-D and SUBESCO for three from-scratch models and for frozen HuBERT-base/WavLM-base+ linear probes, in a single Holm-controlled family; the RAVDESS/CREMA-D direction is presented as a same-implementation replication of Ibrahim et al. 2026 and Zielonka et al. 2022, and the corpus difference is reported as an estimate, not an interaction.

Claim 3 (decomposition, confirmatory): the pipeline premium separates into a positive outer test-leakage component (RG-GG) and a positive inner model-selection component (GR-GG) per corpus, with the interaction reported; validation-only nonexclusivity is itself inflationary, so speaker exclusivity at the inner boundary matters.

Claim 4 (modern regimes, confirmatory): the premium persists under a partially fine-tuned WavLM-base+ pipeline on the same speaker-paired folds and is enlarged when hyperparameters are selected on a speaker-overlapping validation set; the frozen-probe premium is head-dependent by a measured amount (resolving the earlier S0/S2 discrepancy), and the LOSO-over-GroupKFold advantage is equivalent to a training-set-size effect (TOST).

Claim 5 (dose, confirmatory): with a fixed prompt-disjoint test half and constant training size, test-speaker UAR rises monotonically with the fraction of test speakers whose other utterances enter training (Page's L on speakers as blocks), with no measurable spillover to unexposed speakers (TOST) and a reported share of the full premium reached at 25% exposure.

Claim 6 (audit-to-practice link, confirmatory if n>=8): training our fixed pipeline on the realized splits produced by audited risk-positive repositories yields a positive premium over size-matched speaker-exclusive counterfactuals for the majority of repositories (per-repository premia reported next to, never multiplied with, prevalence).

Bounded mechanism sentence (descriptive): under nonexclusive training, test utterances whose nearest training neighbour is a same-speaker same-sentence sibling take are classified correctly more often, and the SUBESCO as-released premium exceeds the repetition-clean premium, indicating near-duplicate-take leakage adds to speaker leakage; no claim of speaker-identity use or mediation share.

Operational recommendation, argued from Claims 1-6: enforce speaker exclusivity at every active boundary including inner validation and hyperparameter selection, deduplicate repeated takes across boundaries, and publish grouping keys; report corpus structure rather than applying a universal correction.

critiques.lens: Literature redundancy: for each added/modified arm, does published work already establish the result or the design (speaker-dependent vs independent SER gaps, leakage audits, SUPERB/EmoBox/EMO-SUPERB benchmarks, cross-domain subject-leakage studies), and did any cut remove something the literature treats as essential? Sources verified by web search on 2026-09-03; several full texts (nature.com, arxiv.org, sail.usc.edu) were egress-blocked, so numbers come from abstracts, indexed snippets and secondary pages.

refuted_items.item: Preregistration note (10) prior-art paragraph and Claim 2 framing: 'Those gaps compare different papers, models and pipelines. We contribute a same-implementation, same-partition ... estimate ... which the published numbers cannot give.'
refuted_items.problem: Factually wrong for the anchor citation. Ibrahim, Ghoraba & Ghoraba, Sci. Rep. 2026 ('Multimodal emotion recognition using hybrid deep feature fusion under speaker-independent evaluation', https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-58836-w) evaluate ONE system under both protocols: RAVDESS 95.83% random-split vs 48.06% +/- 9.76% LOSO; CREMA-D 73.54% random vs 53.12% +/- 2.65% subject-exclusive 5-fold. That is already a same-implementation, same-corpus contrast. Wang et al. 2021 (arXiv 2111.02735) likewise report one fine-tuned wav2vec2/HuBERT pipeline at 79.58% WA speaker-dependent vs 73.01% speaker-independent on IEMOCAP. And the authors' own frozen P1 (1,620 fits, 8/8 Random>Grouped, speaker-paired CIs) already gave the same-implementation, speaker-paired estimate on the same two corpora; the new program refuses to reuse it and reruns RR/GG on RAVDESS/CREMA-D with 3 of 5 model levels. The RR-GG scratch rows on the two anchor corpora are therefore a third replication (Ibrahim, own P1, now CTRL-1), and the sentence a reviewer will check first is false.
refuted_items.fix: Rewrite note (10): 'Ibrahim et al. 2026 report a same-system random-vs-LOSO gap on RAVDESS (95.8 vs 48.1) and CREMA-D (73.5 vs 53.1) for a multimodal MFCC+VGGFace system; Wang et al. 2021 report 79.6 vs 73.0 for fine-tuned wav2vec2/HuBERT on IEMOCAP; our 2026 P1 gave speaker-paired estimates on the same two corpora. Our contribution is the outer/inner decomposition, the probe/fine-tune/HPO/dose extensions and SUBESCO under the full protocol.' Remove the four anchor-corpus RR-GG scratch/probe tests (RAVDESS, CREMA-D) from the 21-test family (they cost Holm alpha for a replication) and report them as replication estimates with CIs; keep SUBESCO RR-GG as the only confirmatory RR-GG test. RR and GG cells must still be trained because RG/GR need them.

refuted_items.item: AUDIT-1 rationale: 'The audit is the paper's only non-collided contribution (prior-art matrix: none of 10 collision papers did probability sampling)'
refuted_items.problem: Prevalence figures and audit methods already exist, just not as a frame-based repository sample. EMO-SUPERB (Wu et al. 2024, arXiv 2402.13018) surveys prior SER work and states that in 50% of previous studies recordings were randomly divided into train/test, and that leaky partitions yield >4% improvement. Antoniou et al. ICASSP 2023 (arXiv 2304.00860) reviewed IEMOCAP SER papers with open-source implementations for partitioning practice and reproducibility (80.77% not reproducible). Kapoor & Narayanan 2023 (Patterns) catalogue 294 leakage-affected papers with a taxonomy that includes train/test overlap and selection on test. Random/stratified sampling of papers or repositories with manual coding and reliability statistics is standard: Hutchinson et al. FAccT 2022 sampled 200 papers stratified by venue/year; Bennett-Wu et al. 2026 'An audit of ML experiments on software defect prediction' randomly sampled 101 of 1,585 papers. Automated static detection of train/test overlap leakage in notebooks is a mature tool line: Yang et al. ASE 2022 (100,000+ notebooks, overlap leakage pervasive), LeakageDetector 2.0 (2025, arXiv 2509.15971), and static-slicing + structured LLM prompts (PACMSE 2026, doi 10.1145/3808199, +15% F1 on overlap leakage). The AI-rater with a frozen prompt is a bespoke version of these tools without comparison to them.
refuted_items.fix: Reframe the audit's novelty as: frame-based probability sample of repository lineages (not papers), a test-vs-validation endpoint, and realized overlap from executing each repo's split on the real manifests. Cite EMO-SUPERB's 50% and Antoniou as the paper-level priors in Related Work and compare the stratum estimates to them explicitly. Add a zero-GPU descriptive column: run one published static leakage detector (Yang et al. 2022 or the 2026 static-slicing tool) on every unit and report its agreement with the human/AI verdicts alongside kappa; this converts the AI rater from an unvalidated instrument into one benchmarked against prior tools.

refuted_items.item: CTRL-2 (partially fine-tuned WavLM RR vs GG) and Claim 4's 'premium persists under a partially fine-tuned ... pipeline'
refuted_items.problem: Directionally established. Wang et al. 2021 (arXiv 2111.02735) fine-tuned wav2vec2 and HuBERT partially and fully and report speaker-dependent 79.58% vs speaker-independent 73.01% WA on IEMOCAP; 'A Comprehensive Exploration of Fine-Tuning WavLM for SER' (ICASSP 2024, IEEE 10467733) shows that fine-tuning top layers is what carries paralinguistic gains on IEMOCAP/RAVDESS, i.e. exactly the layers CTRL-2 unfreezes. The existence of a fine-tuned-SSL premium is not an open question; the registries' 'forbidden extrapolation' was a self-imposed rule, not a literature gap.
refuted_items.fix: Keep the arm (it is the paper's only speaker-paired FT row on RAVDESS/CREMA-D/SUBESCO) but move its three RR-GG tests out of the confirmatory family and make the registered estimand the FT-minus-probe paired difference on identical folds (does fine-tuning re-expose speaker information that frozen final-layer features attenuate?) with one test per corpus. Cite Wang 2021 and the WavLM fine-tuning paper as the replicated direction. This also reduces family size to fund the decomposition tests.

refuted_items.item: DOSE rationale: 'P1 measured only 0% and 100% speaker overlap ... the paper needs a within-pipeline dose curve'; Claim 5 'confirmatory'
refuted_items.problem: The constant-training-size, graded speaker-overlap design is published in the sibling speech-health literature: 'Who is Speaking or Who is Depressed? A Controlled Study of Speaker Leakage in Speech-Based Depression Detection' (arXiv 2604.14354, April 2026) proposes a data split that controls speaker overlap between train and test while keeping training size constant, evaluates three models plus a DANN variant on DAIC-WOZ, and finds performance rises with overlap and drops sharply on unseen speakers. Rosenberg et al., Nat. Commun. 2024 ('Data leakage inflates prediction performance in connectome-based ML', https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-46150-w) inject repeated subjects at 5/10/20% and show monotone inflation (delta r up to 0.28) with small datasets exacerbating it. The monotone dose result is therefore expected, not a finding; Page's L will reject.
refuted_items.fix: Cite both as the design precedents and present DOSE as the SER instantiation. Register the genuinely new quantities as the primary readouts: (i) share of the q=1 premium reached at q=0.25 (the audit's realized-overlap distribution is what makes this useful), (ii) the no-spillover TOST, (iii) RAVDESS vs CREMA-D slope difference. Downgrade Page's L from a confirmatory claim to a manipulation check, or keep exactly one Page's L (pooled corpora) in the family.

refuted_items.item: MECH-0 (b) speaker-ID linear probe on SER embeddings and (c) layer-wise speaker-ID probe on SSL caches vs premium
refuted_items.problem: Both readouts are already established. Emotion representations are known to encode speaker identity well enough to train speaker verification on them and to cluster by speaker ('Privacy versus Emotion Preservation Trade-offs in Emotion-Preserving Speaker Anonymization', arXiv 2409.03655; attribute-inference attacks on SER, Feng et al. arXiv 2112.13416; Jaiswal & Provost 2020 demographic privacy). Chaibub Neto et al. 2019 (npj Digit. Med., https://www.nature.com/articles/s41746-019-0178-x) give a permutation test that quantifies identity confounding absorbed by a record-wise classifier, and 'The Identity Trap in EEG Foundation Models' (arXiv 2606.06647, June 2026) already packages variance decomposition, subject-axis erasure and layer-wise probing on frozen vs fine-tuned encoders. Layer-wise speaker information in SSL encoders is documented by Pasad et al. 2021 (arXiv 2107.04734), the WavLM SUPERB layer-weight analysis (bottom layers dominate speaker tasks) and 'Interpreting Speaker Characteristics in the Dimensions of SSL Speech Features' (arXiv 2603.03096: best speaker correlations in layers 1-10).
refuted_items.fix: Keep only (a) sibling-NN (the one readout without an SER precedent; analogous to doppelganger effects, Wang et al. 2022 Drug Discov. Today / iScience) and the SUBESCO full-vs-980 contrast. Replace (b) with Chaibub Neto's identity-confounding permutation test on the RR checkpoints (cheaper, citable, yields a p-value-free effect size), and replace (c) with one sentence citing the WavLM/Pasad layer results plus the PROBE-CPU layer-wise Delta_RG (which is the actually new correlate). Cite the Identity Trap paper as the methodological template.

refuted_items.item: HPO arm and Claim 4's 'enlarged when hyperparameters are selected on a speaker-overlapping validation set'
refuted_items.problem: Selection bias from tuning on a leaky selection criterion is textbook (Cawley & Talbot, JMLR 2010) and is in Kapoor & Narayanan's taxonomy; a controlled quantification with subject-level leakage exists in EEG: Pup et al. 2025 ('The role of data partitioning on the performance of EEG-based deep learning models', Comput. Biol. Med., arXiv 2505.13021) trained >100,000 models and show that non-nested subject-wise CV lets larger models overfit the validation data and inflates estimates relative to nested Leave-N-Subjects-Out. No SER-specific quantification was found, so the arm is not redundant in SER, but the claim wording implies discovery.
refuted_items.fix: Cite Cawley & Talbot and Pup et al.; word Claim 4's HPO half as 'we quantify in SER the selection-bias inflation ...' and keep the descriptive 'selected-config inner-val minus outer-test optimism' as the number linked to the audit's Y_val units.

refuted_items.item: Claim 3 decomposition (inner model-selection component GR-GG) framed as if the inner-boundary effect were unexamined
refuted_items.problem: The inner-validation subject-leakage effect has a controlled precedent outside speech: Pup et al. 2025 compare nested vs non-nested Leave-N-Subjects-Out and show the non-nested (subject-leaky validation) variant overestimates, with the gap growing with model size; Saeb et al. 2017 (GigaScience) and Little et al. 2017 formalize record-wise vs subject-wise leakage at both boundaries. In SER the decomposition is not published (the authors' own arm A is repo-only), so the arm is defensible, but the paper cannot say the phenomenon is new.
refuted_items.fix: Cite Pup et al. 2025 and Saeb 2017 in Related Work; state Claim 3 as the first SER-specific, speaker-paired decomposition with shared initialization.

refuted_items.item: PROBE-CPU LOSO vs Group5 vs size-matched LOSO TOST ('LOSO's advantage is a training-set-size effect') and Claim 4's TOST sentence
refuted_items.problem: Already shown outside SER: Tougui, Jilbab & El Mhamdi 2021 (Healthc. Inform. Res. 27:189, https://e-hir.org/journal/view.php?doi=10.4258/hir.2021.27.3.189) vary fold count from 2 to 30 and show subject-wise CV error falls from 27% to 7% purely with fold count (training size), while record-wise error stays at 2%; Varoquaux 2017 (NeuroImage) documents the variance side. The direction LOSO > grouped-5-fold is thus expected and the TOST confirms a known mechanism.
refuted_items.fix: Keep the CPU computation (it costs nothing) but cite Tougui et al. and Varoquaux, drop the TOST from Claim 4 to a one-sentence supplement note, and do not spend main-text space on it.

refuted_items.item: PROBE-CPU layer factor (final / mid / mean of 1-12) presented as closing the S4 layer question
refuted_items.problem: Layer-wise emotion content of wav2vec2/HuBERT/WavLM is well mapped: Pepino et al. Interspeech 2021 learn layer weights on IEMOCAP/RAVDESS; 'Unveiling embedded features in Wav2vec2 and HuBERT models for SER' (Procedia CS 2024); the WavLM fine-tuning exploration (ICASSP 2024) evaluates layer segments; SUPERB layer-weight plots show speaker tasks favour bottom layers. Accuracy-by-layer is not new.
refuted_items.fix: Register only the premium-by-layer (Delta_RG per layer) and its Spearman with layer index as the estimand; cite the above for accuracy-by-layer and never report layer-wise accuracy as a result.

refuted_items.item: Cut: P1 LOSO from-scratch arm (replaced by Ridge-feature LOSO on CPU)
refuted_items.problem: The paper positions its RAVDESS effect as a replication of Ibrahim et al. 2026, whose speaker-independent number is LOSO (48.06 +/- 9.76), and LOSO is the protocol most SER reviewers ask for on 24-speaker corpora. After the cut, the only LOSO numbers are for a Ridge head on frozen features, so the 'replication' compares a 5-fold GroupKFold from-scratch estimate against a published LOSO estimate, and the paper cannot state a from-scratch LOSO UAR at all.
refuted_items.fix: Add one cheap from-scratch LOSO row: RAVDESS CNN, 24 folds x 3 replicates = 72 fits (~0.4 GPU-h at the recorded ~20 s/fit for RAVDESS-size training), descriptive only, so the replication sentence can cite a like-for-like LOSO number. Alternatively state the protocol mismatch explicitly in the prior-art paragraph.

refuted_items.item: Cut/scope: IEMOCAP excluded from execution and from CTRL-1 while remaining in the audit frame; endpoint dictionary limited to same-speaker membership
refuted_items.problem: EMO-SUPERB (arXiv 2402.13018) and Antoniou 2023 identify a second, IEMOCAP-specific leakage mechanism the endpoint dictionary does not encode: conversation-partner speech inside a speaker's segmented utterances, so that even 'speaker-exclusive' splits leak the partner's voice; EMO-SUPERB attributes >4% of reported improvement to such partitions. An IEMOCAP repository coded N under the program's rule can still be leaky by the literature's definition, and the audit's IEMOCAP stratum has already been partly characterized by Antoniou.
refuted_items.fix: Add a descriptive endpoint column 'dialogue-partner segment contamination possible (IEMOCAP session split vs speaker split)' coded from the split statement, cite EMO-SUPERB/Antoniou, and state in Limitations that N on IEMOCAP means speaker-exclusive under the corpus's own speaker labels only.

missing: A correct characterization of Ibrahim et al. 2026 as a same-system random-vs-LOSO comparison (multimodal MFCC+VGGFace; RAVDESS 95.83 vs 48.06 +/- 9.76; CREMA-D 73.54 vs 53.12 +/- 2.65) and of Wang et al. 2021 (fine-tuned wav2vec2/HuBERT, IEMOCAP 79.58 vs 73.01) in Related Work.

Citation and numeric comparison with EMO-SUPERB's literature figure (50% of prior SER studies used random partitions; leaky partitions >4% gain) and Antoniou 2023 (80.77% of IEMOCAP SER papers not reproducible) as the paper-level priors for the audit's stratum estimates.

Benchmarking of the AI rater against an existing static leakage detector (Yang et al. ASE 2022; LeakageDetector 2.0 2025; static-slicing + LLM, PACMSE 2026) on the 60 units; the program builds a bespoke detector without comparing to the tool line that already exists.

Design precedents for DOSE: arXiv 2604.14354 (constant-training-size controlled speaker overlap, depression) and Rosenberg et al. Nat. Commun. 2024 (5/10/20% repeated-subject leakage, monotone inflation, small datasets worse).
Chaibub Neto et al. 2019 identity-confounding permutation test as the established quantification of 'learns the subject' under record-wise splits; the program re-invents a weaker speaker-ID probe.

Cross-domain leakage-magnitude literature to position the SER premium: 'Which Leakage Types Matter? A Quantitative Landscape Across 2,047 Benchmark Datasets' (arXiv 2604.04199, 29 experiments), Bussola et al. 2021 (tile-level leakage inflates up to 41%), Tougui 2021 (subject-wise error falls with fold count), Saeb 2017 / Little 2017.

The SER replication-study precedent (Triantafyllopoulos et al. 2025, 'Charting 15 years of progress in deep learning for SER: A replication study', arXiv 2508.02448) when the paper calls its anchor-corpus effect a replication.

EmoBox (Interspeech 2024, 32 datasets/14 languages, speaker-independent partitions) and EMO-SUPERB speaker-independent CREMA-D results as the external source for CTRL-2's 55-70% grouped-UAR validity anchor, which is currently an unsourced 'literature range'.
An audit endpoint or descriptive column for dialogue-partner contamination on IEMOCAP session splits (EMO-SUPERB's leakage type), absent from the endpoint dictionary.

Explicit statement that the 2026 P1 result (8/8 Random>Grouped, RAVDESS 15-20 pp, CREMA-D 2-3 pp) already exists and that CTRL-1's anchor-corpus RR-GG rows are a within-lab re-replication with changed hygiene, so the alpha spent on them is for replication, not discovery.
