critiques.compute_or_feasibility_verdict: Not this lens's focus, but from the recorded rates the 28 GPU-h target is plausible and tight: recorded 5-fold from-scratch fits ran ~40 s/fit averaged over RAVDESS+CREMA-D (A: 240 fits, 2.67 h) and ~13 s/fit on 1-2k-utterance SUBESCO cells (B), so CTRL-1's ~900 scratch fits over five corpus levels including 7,000-utterance SUBESCO-full and 7,442-utterance CREMA-D lands near 9-12 GPU-h, i.e. at or above the 10 h estimate before the 120 seed-crossing fits; HPO (160 fits, ~2 h) and DOSE (240 fits, ~3 h) are consistent with those rates; probe/Ridge units are negligible; CTRL-2 is the only unmeasured item and its 10 h cap is the whole slack. The literature adds no compute obligation, and the redundancy fixes above (dropping 7 replication tests from the family, adding a 72-fit LOSO row, reusing a static leakage detector on CPU) are cost-neutral.
critiques.overall_verdict: Not fatal, but the novelty map is misdrawn and one prior-art statement is false. What the literature already establishes: the random-vs-speaker-independent gap on RAVDESS and CREMA-D under a single system (Ibrahim et al. 2026: 95.8 vs 48.1; 73.5 vs 53.1), the fine-tuned-SSL premium (Wang et al. 2021), the constant-training-size speaker-overlap dose design (arXiv 2604.14354; Rosenberg 2024), speaker identity in emotion embeddings and in lower SSL layers (2409.03655, Pasad 2021, WavLM/SUPERB layer weights, 2603.03096), the fold-count/training-size explanation of LOSO's advantage (Tougui 2021), selection bias from leaky validation (Cawley & Talbot 2010; Pup et al. 2025), and paper-level SER partition prevalence (EMO-SUPERB: 50% random splits; Antoniou 2023). What survives as new: a frame-based probability sample of repository lineages with a test-vs-validation endpoint and realized-overlap execution; the SER outer/inner decomposition with shared initialization; SUBESCO under the full protocol and the full-vs-980 take-leakage increment with the sibling-NN readout; REPLAY of audited realized splits inside one pipeline (no precedent found beyond corrected re-runs of single pipelines such as 'Bursting the bubble' 2026); and the 25%-dose share and no-spillover equivalence. Required changes: correct the prior-art paragraph; relabel Claims 2 and the FT half of Claim 4 as replication and remove their anchor-corpus tests from the confirmatory family; cite the dose and identity-confounding precedents and demote Page's L and the LOSO TOST to manipulation checks; benchmark the AI rater against an existing static leakage detector; add a dialogue-partner contamination column for IEMOCAP; and restore one cheap from-scratch LOSO row so the Ibrahim replication is like-for-like. No cut removed anything the literature treats as essential except like-for-like LOSO comparability.

critiques.lens: Inference validity: estimands, pairing, multiplicity families, speaker-level sample sizes (RAVDESS 24, CREMA-D 91, SUBESCO 20), power of the added contrasts, whether merges break pairing, whether the audit's partial-identification/envelope logic survives stratification, and what is post-hoc despite the new preregistration. Numeric checks below were recomputed (exact binomial, noncentral-t, exact sign test, TOST CI widths) rather than taken from the proposal.

refuted_items.item: AUDIT-1 confirmatory tests H_A1/H_A2 (one-sided exact binomial vs 0.5, n_s=30, U as non-positive, Holm over 2) and the stated power (~0.6 per stratum, ~0.85 pooled)
refuted_items.problem: Recomputed: at n=30, true Y_test prevalence 0.70 and 12% U, the observed positive rate is 0.616; the one-sided exact critical value is >=20/30 at alpha 0.05 (power 0.36) and >=21/30 at the Holm-first alpha 0.025 (power 0.23). Pooled n=60 at alpha 0.05 needs >=37/60 and has power 0.55. The proposal's numbers are roughly 2-3x too high. Worse, the true Y_test rate is unknown: the historical 73% (44/60) conflated validation-only with test-boundary leakage, so the Y_test-only rate could be near 0.55-0.60, where power is 0.04-0.18. The 0.5 null is also arbitrary; nothing in the thesis turns on 'more than half'. Claim 1 as a 'confirmatory' claim therefore hangs on a coin-flip test, and the 'and/or' between strata is a disjunctive claim that lets either stratum carry the headline.
refuted_items.fix: Make Claim 1 an estimation claim: stratum-weighted Y_test proportion with linearized FPC interval, per-stratum Wilson intervals, partial-identification bounds. Drop the binomial tests from the confirmatory map, or if a test is required, preregister a single pooled n=60 test against a substantively motivated null with U handled by reporting both the U-as-negative and U-as-positive p-values (partial identification), and increase n to >=45 per stratum only if the human budget allows.

refuted_items.item: AUDIT-1 stratum design: 'if a stratum has <30 eligible, take all and report' plus stratum-weighted estimator and per-stratum tests
refuted_items.problem: The paper-linked stratum is very likely small: P0.5 found 3/30 author-linked and S1 had 56/60 repo_relation=unknown, so a regex on README/description will yield perhaps 20-45 paper-linked lineages of ~300. If <30, the stratum becomes a census: an exact binomial test on a fully observed finite population has no sampling interpretation, the Wilson interval is meaningless, and the stratum weight N_1/N collapses the stratified estimate onto the 'other' stratum. The regex stratum is also a proxy with unmeasured misclassification (paper links in code comments, papers without repo links).
refuted_items.fix: Prespecify: a census stratum is reported as an exact proportion with no interval or test; use proportional allocation with a floor (e.g., min(30, N_1)) and move remaining draws to the other stratum so n=60 is kept; hand-verify stratum assignment on a hash-selected 40 candidates and report the regex misclassification rate; preregister that H_A1 exists only if N_1 >= 45.

refuted_items.item: AUDIT-1 statistics: 'S1 exact hypergeometric joint >=95% envelope retained as a secondary frame-level bound' under stratified sampling
refuted_items.problem: The S1 envelope inverts a hypergeometric likelihood that assumes simple random sampling of 60 from N. With 30 fixed per stratum of unequal size the sample is not SRS; the joint bound's coverage guarantee no longer holds, and the partial-identification interval [Y/n, (Y+U)/n] is no longer a frame-level quantity either (unweighted). The audit's interval logic with U survives only if rebuilt per stratum.
refuted_items.fix: Per stratum, compute two one-sided exact hypergeometric bounds (Y_s and Y_s+U_s) at 1-alpha/4 each (Bonferroni over four bounds for joint 95%), then combine as stratum-weighted frame bounds; report the unweighted sample partial-ID interval only as a sample descriptor. Alternatively drop the envelope and keep only the stratified linearized interval.

refuted_items.item: AUDIT-1 endpoint dictionary Y_test vs Y_val
refuted_items.problem: The modal pattern in the audited population (P0.5: 19/30 supplemental notebooks) is one train_test_split whose held-out set both drives early stopping/model selection and is reported as the final score. The proposal gives no rule for whether that boundary is 'test' or 'validation-only', so two raters will disagree systematically, kappa will be deflated for a definitional reason, and the Y_test estimand is undefined for the most common case.
refuted_items.fix: Add to the frozen dictionary: any held-out set whose metric is presented as the final reported result is a test boundary (Y_test if nonexclusive), regardless of whether it also drove selection; record the dual use in the 'test-set selection' descriptor column. Y_val is reserved for repositories with a separately reported test set that is speaker-exclusive.

refuted_items.item: AUDIT-1 realized-overlap execution tier and false-positive rule (static Y_test with realized overlap 0 -> N)
refuted_items.problem: Three inference defects. (1) Differential measurement: only AST-isolable fragments are executed, so the 'realized' construct applies to simple loaders while complex repositories keep the 'permits' construct; the prevalence then mixes two endpoints in a way correlated with repository type. (2) Realized overlap is a random variable for unseeded splits and depends on our manifest ordering (os.listdir/glob order, corpus subsets, Kaggle merges); a single execution is one draw. (3) The correction is asymmetric: Y->N is allowed but a static N whose executed fragment shows overlap >0 has no stated disposition, biasing prevalence downward only.
refuted_items.fix: Keep the static 'permits' verdict as the primary endpoint for all 60 units; report realized overlap as a labelled sub-estimate over executed units with the executed/non-executed split shown. Make the correction symmetric (N with realized overlap >0 -> Y_test). Execute unseeded fragments with 10 fixed seeds on a sorted manifest and report min/median/max overlap; a false positive requires overlap 0 under all seeds.

refuted_items.item: AUDIT-1 human reliability: author as Rater H on 30 hash-selected units, kappa with CI, author-applied adjudication rule
refuted_items.problem: The author has seen ~90 prior verdicts, and with a ~300-lineage frame the new sample of 60 is expected to contain ~12 lineages already adjudicated in S1 plus a few from P0/P0.5. Mechanised ordering prevents the human seeing the AI verdict, not the historical one. Kappa on 30 units (CI ~ +/-0.25) therefore measures agreement between a partially pre-informed human and an AI prompt possibly built from those same verdicts, and the disagreement rule is executed by the same human. The 'human-only sensitivity estimate' inherits the same contamination.
refuted_items.fix: Exclude any lineage present in the P0/P0.5/S1 samples from the human's double-coded 30 (draw the 30 from previously unseen units only) and report agreement on previously seen units separately; assign double coding to the recruited coder if one exists; encode the adjudication rule as a script over the evidence-chain fields (path/hash present, entry point present, enumeration closed) so no person applies it; if no second coder is recruited, drop the kappa claim from Claim 1 and label the audit AI-rated with author review.

refuted_items.item: CTRL-1 power statement ('SUBESCO n=20 ... ~0.75 power for a 3 pp mean' and, in risks, 'after Holm over 21 tests')
refuted_items.problem: Recomputed with a paired-t approximation, d = 3/5 = 0.6: n=20 gives 0.72 at alpha 0.05 but 0.25 at the Holm floor 0.05/21 and 0.35 at 0.005; n=24 gives 0.80 / 0.35 / 0.45. Wilcoxon is slightly less efficient still. The dossier's own per-speaker SDs are worse than assumed (P1 RAVDESS RG speaker-diff SD 7-10 pp; S0 probe SDs 2.8-4.9 pp), and the SUBESCO probe premium in S3 was ~3 pp with WavLM ~1.3 pp and fragile. So the probe-level RR-GG tests on SUBESCO (and plausibly RAVDESS WavLM) are underpowered in a 21-test family, which the claim-to-rejection map for Claim 2 ('at least two probe rejections') partly hides.
refuted_items.fix: Simulate power from the dossier's per-speaker deltas and SDs under the actual Holm step-down (not the floor) for each family member and publish the table in the registration; restructure the family hierarchically (primary 6-test family: RR-GG scratch and probe per corpus; secondary families gated on the primary) so the SUBESCO tests are not taxed by 15 unrelated contrasts; set the Claim 2 rule to require the SUBESCO scratch rejection explicitly, since that is the only genuinely new corpus-level test.

refuted_items.item: CTRL-1 'two-way (speaker x replicate) cluster-bootstrap intervals reported as secondary for every family contrast' with replicates r=0,1,2
refuted_items.problem: Three replicate clusters admit only 10 distinct multinomial resamples; a cluster bootstrap over 3 clusters is degenerate and its interval has no coverage interpretation. Because 'replicate' also merges partition draw and training seed, the interval cannot separate split-realization from training noise anyway (only the RAVDESS-CNN 3x3 crossing can). Presenting it as the answer to 'not a split artifact' is misleading.
refuted_items.fix: Replace with (a) per-replicate point estimates and sign counts, (b) a variance-components table from the RAVDESS-CNN crossing extrapolated with stated assumptions, and (c) for the probe levels only (cost ~0), 20 partition draws x 3 seeds so a partition-level interval exists where it is cheap; state in the paper that scratch-level inference conditions on three partitions.

refuted_items.item: Labelling the RAVDESS/CREMA-D CTRL-1 tests (Claims 2 and 3), the PROBE head test, and the LOSO-sub TOST as 'confirmatory' in the Holm family
refuted_items.problem: These hypotheses, their directions, and even their magnitudes were observed on the identical finite speaker panels (same 24 RAVDESS and 91 CREMA-D speakers, same log-mel and SSL features) in P1, A, S0 and S2. The whole-speaker bootstrap treats speakers as sampled, but the new run resamples partitions and seeds, not speakers, so the preregistration is pre-outcome for the new fits only, not for the hypotheses. Counting 12+ such tests in the same family as the genuinely new tests (SUBESCO scratch, CTRL-2, HPO, DOSE, REPLAY) also spends alpha on results already known.
refuted_items.fix: Label anchor-corpus RR-GG, RG-GG, GR-GG, head and LOSO tests as 'preregistered re-tests on the same panels' and place them in their own family (or report them as estimates with CIs); define the confirmatory family as the tests whose direction was not previously observed on the same units: SUBESCO-full scratch and probe RR-GG, RG-GG/GR-GG on SUBESCO, CTRL-2 x3, HPO x2, DOSE, REPLAY (roughly 10 tests). Say so in the prior-art paragraph.

refuted_items.item: DOSE: Page's L trend test across q in {0, .25, .5, 1} with speakers as blocks; H 'UAR rises monotonically with q'; 'nested, rotated so each speaker is exposed in exactly one partial dose'
refuted_items.problem: Within a replicate, nested doses make each speaker's own exposure a step function (unexposed until its rung, exposed thereafter). The population mean at dose q is then a mixture q*exposed + (1-q)*unexposed, so monotonicity in q is implied by construction whenever exposure has any positive effect: Page's L tests a tautology, and the 'fraction of the q=1 premium reached at 25%' is ~25% by arithmetic unless per-exposed-speaker gain depends on q. The rotation is also infeasible as stated: 2 partial doses cannot be spread over 3 replicates so that every speaker is exposed in exactly one partial dose while doses stay nested. Finally, removing label-matched other-speaker utterances to hold training size fixed makes training-speaker diversity fall with q, confounding dose with data loss.
refuted_items.fix: Re-specify the estimands: (a) per-exposed-speaker gain at each dose (does crowding shrink it?), tested as a speaker-paired contrast between exposed-at-q=0.5 and exposed-at-q=1 gains; (b) the spillover TOST on unexposed speakers; (c) descriptive population curve. Use q in {0, 0.5, 1} with 2 replicates so rotation tiles exactly, or drop nesting. Hold training size by removing a hash-random subset of other-speaker utterances independent of label matching, or let size vary and report it. Remove 'monotone' from Claim 5.

refuted_items.item: Equivalence tests: no-spillover TOST margin +/-1.5 pp; LOSO-sub vs Group5 TOST margin +/-1 pp on RAVDESS
refuted_items.problem: Recomputed 90% CI half-widths: with paired SD 5 pp and n=24 the half-width is 1.75 pp (>1.5, >1); with the ~12 unexposed RAVDESS speakers per replicate at q=0.5 and SD ~6 pp it is 3.1 pp. On RAVDESS the per-speaker half-B test set has 4 items per non-neutral class, so a single item flip moves speaker UAR by 3.1 pp, i.e. the margin is below the measurement granularity. Both TOSTs on RAVDESS are therefore preordained to fail to show equivalence regardless of truth, and the paper's Claim 4/5 wording ('equivalent to a training-set-size effect', 'no measurable spillover') would become 'not supported' by design. The margins are not derived from any pilot SD, although P1 supplies speaker-diff SDs (RAVDESS 5-10 pp, CREMA-D 3-4 pp).
refuted_items.fix: Preregister the TOSTs on CREMA-D only (n=91, half-width ~0.7 pp) with margins derived from P1's speaker-diff SDs; on RAVDESS and SUBESCO report the same contrasts as estimates with CIs. For LOSO-sub, average over 3 hash subsamples per LOSO fold so the subsampling draw is not a single realization.

refuted_items.item: REPLAY exact sign test as a family member (Claim 6 'confirmatory if n>=8')
refuted_items.problem: Recomputed exact two-sided sign-test power: n=8 needs 8/8 positives (power 0.10 at P(+)=0.75, 0.27 at 0.85); n=12 gives 0.39/0.74; n=16 gives 0.40/0.79, before Holm. More fundamentally the units are not exchangeable: many audited repositories will call the same sklearn train_test_split(test_size=0.2, random_state=42) on the same sorted file list, producing byte-identical realized index sets, so the sign test double-counts one split. Pairing is also broken relative to CTRL-1: counterfactual partitions are matched on test-utterance count and class proportions but not on which speakers are tested, so Delta_repo mixes a leakage effect with a test-speaker-difficulty effect.
refuted_items.fix: Deduplicate by realized index-set hash before analysis and report the number of distinct splits; make Claim 6 an estimation claim (median Delta_repo with repository-level bootstrap CI, per corpus) and remove the sign test from the family; match counterfactuals to include the same test speakers' utterances wherever the realized split's test speakers allow (exclusive counterfactual = same test speakers, training with those speakers removed and back-filled to size), which restores speaker pairing.

refuted_items.item: PROBE-CPU family test H_head: per-speaker [Delta_RG(Ridge) - Delta_RG(early-stopped probe)] on CTRL-1 partitions, with the attribution logic 'rejection -> head; non-rejection with <2 pp -> split family'
refuted_items.problem: The Ridge head has no inner split, so its 'Delta_RG' is an outer-only contrast, whereas the probe's RR-GG contrast bundles outer and inner (validation) leakage; the difference is head plus inner pathway, not head. The attribution rule also accepts the null on a non-rejection at n=24 (CI could span +/-4 pp) and ignores the possibility that both head and split family contribute. The S0/S2 discrepancy additionally involved GroupKFold vs StratifiedGroupKFold and P1 vs fresh draws, none of which this single test isolates.
refuted_items.fix: Compare Ridge (outer Random vs outer Grouped) with the probe's RG-GG contrast (outer contrast under grouped inner) on identical partitions; report a 2x2 (head x split family) table of estimates with CIs on the same speakers; keep at most one family test (head effect at RG-GG) and never attribute from a non-rejection.

refuted_items.item: CTRL-1 / PROBE-CPU secondary estimate 'SUBESCO-full minus SUBESCO-980 pipeline delta paired by speaker (take-leakage increment)' and MECH-0's use of it
refuted_items.problem: SUBESCO-full (7,000 utterances, 10 prompts, 5 takes) versus the 980 panel (7 prompts, 1 take) differ in training size (7x), prompt set, and take multiplicity simultaneously; the paired-by-speaker difference cannot be read as a near-duplicate-take increment. The bounded mechanism sentence ('as-released premium exceeds the repetition-clean premium, indicating near-duplicate-take leakage adds to speaker leakage') therefore rests on a confounded contrast.
refuted_items.fix: Add a size- and prompt-matched pair at ~0 GPU cost on frozen features (and ~0.6 GPU-h scratch if desired): (a) 1,400 utterances = one take per speaker x emotion x prompt over all 10 prompts; (b) 1,400 utterances = two takes per cell over a hash-selected 700 cells. Same size, same prompts, differing only in sibling presence; report the Random-split premium difference paired by speaker. Rewrite the mechanism sentence around that pair.

refuted_items.item: CTRL-2 three family tests from replicate r=0 only (one partition, one seed, fp16)
refuted_items.problem: Each per-corpus test is a single training realization; the per-speaker differences absorb seed noise that is not averaged, so the whole-speaker bootstrap and Wilcoxon condition on one seed and one partition. On SUBESCO (n=20, first in the drop order) a single-seed result with p=1 fallback is fragile; the dossier shows seed SDs of 1-2.5 pp at the cell level. Calling this 'confirmatory' with the same status as 3-replicate contrasts overstates it.
refuted_items.fix: Spend the CTRL-2 slack on a second seed for RAVDESS and SUBESCO (cheap corpora, ~+2 GPU-h) and average within speaker before testing; if the timing probe forbids it, label CTRL-2 as single-realization and keep it out of the confirmatory map (estimate with CI).

refuted_items.item: AUDIT-1 U-informativeness sensitivity: preregistered logistic model on (stratum, notebook, corpus, has-external-data) fitted on Y/N units
refuted_items.problem: With ~7 U units and ~53 Y/N units, a 4-covariate logistic model will frequently separate (e.g., all notebooks Y) and yield degenerate imputations; the sensitivity would be an artifact of the fit.
refuted_items.fix: Use a Firth-penalized or stratum-only imputation, or report the two extreme bounds (all U negative / all U positive) plus one covariate-free stratum imputation.

refuted_items.item: CTRL-1 pairing description: 'cells are speaker-paired on identical outer test folds'
refuted_items.problem: Outer Random (StratifiedKFold) and outer Grouped (StratifiedGroupKFold) generate different fold assignments; RR vs GG are paired on each speaker's utterance set (as in P1), not on folds. Only RR vs RG and GR vs GG share outer folds. Overstating fold identity invites a reviewer to question the pairing of the primary contrasts.
refuted_items.fix: State that pairing is on the speaker's identical utterance set across cells; fold identity holds within an outer letter only.

missing: A power table simulated from the dossier's own per-speaker deltas and SDs (P1: RAVDESS RG diff SD 7-10 pp, CREMA-D 3-4 pp; S0 probe SDs 2.4-4.9 pp; S3 draw SDs 1.5-2.2 pp) for every family member under the actual Holm step-down; the proposal's power statements are all analytic guesses and the ones checked here are wrong by 2-3x.
A rule for Wilcoxon ties and zero differences at n=20 with coarse rational per-speaker UARs (SUBESCO per-speaker deltas have denominators of 49-490), and for what happens when >20% of speakers tie.

A preregistered estimate of the paper-linked stratum size N_1 (from the existing 383-URL log) and the fallback when N_1 < 30 or when the regex misclassifies; without it the stratified estimator and the two-test audit family are undefined.

Disposition of lineages already adjudicated in P0/P0.5/S1 (expected ~12-15 of the new 60): whether their historical verdicts are hidden from both raters, whether they are excluded from the human double-coded set, and how 'agreement with historical verdicts' is kept from contaminating kappa.

Human-hour arithmetic for the audit: E1-E5 screening of the full candidate list at up to 10 min each (400-800 URLs after channel B) is 70-130 h alone, before the 30 x 1.5 h double coding, author review of 60, adjudication, and frame/lineage construction; the 110 h audit budget appears to be off by ~2x, and audit hours are the stated binding constraint.

A prespecified handling of repository split fragments that depend on platform file order or on corpus subsets (actor subsets, merged Kaggle datasets) when executed on our full manifest; the 'realized overlap' estimand is undefined for those.
For REPLAY, the number of distinct realized index-set hashes and a rule for how repositories sharing an identical split are counted.

A preregistered SESOI or reading rule for the RAVDESS-minus-CREMA-D and RAVDESS-minus-SUBESCO differences; they are registered as estimates but the discussion will inevitably interpret them, so a stated band avoids post-hoc framing.

Per-model (level) heterogeneity rule: Delta_outer and Delta_inner average five representation levels whose premia differ by ~5x (scratch ~15 pp vs probe ~3 pp on RAVDESS); the family test on the mean can reject while individual levels disagree in sign, and no rule states what the paper says then.

An explicit statement that Claim 3 ('validation-only nonexclusivity is itself inflationary') requires GR-GG on the same corpus as the audit's Y_val units are concentrated in, and how HPO's Y_val-linked descriptive optimism is kept separate from the confirmatory family.
critiques.compute_or_feasibility_verdict: GPU budget is credible: A's 240 non-LOSO fits ran at ~40 s/fit on the same RTX 5070, so CTRL-1's ~800 scratch fits plus 600 probe units land near the stated 9.5-10 GPU-h; HPO (160 fits) and DOSE (240 fits) at ~40-60 s/fit fit their 2-3 h estimates; REPLAY's 96 fits are ~1.5 h; the SSL all-layer cache at ~1 GPU-h matches the recorded 1-2 h for three encoders; CTRL-2 (30 partial WavLM-base+ fits, top-4 layers, 3 s crops, <=15 epochs) is plausibly 6-9 h on a 12 GB card and is correctly gated by a timing probe. Total ~28 h under a 30 h cap is realistic with ~2 h slack, which is thin if CTRL-2 overruns by 30%. The binding constraint is human time, not GPU: full-frame E1-E5 screening after adding a GitHub code-search channel (10 min x 400-800 candidates) plus 30 double-coded units at 1.5 h, author review of 60, lineage containment across all candidate pairs, adjudication and execution-tier debugging is closer to 200-250 h than the budgeted 110 h, and the second coder is not yet recruited. The 12-week calendar therefore likely slips on the audit, which REPLAY and STAT-1 depend on. Feasible if the audit budget is doubled or channel B is dropped; otherwise the audit, not the GPU program, is what fails the one-shot rule.
critiques.overall_verdict: Not runnable as preregistered. The controlled core (RR/RG/GR/GG factorial on three corpora with shared seeds, speaker-paired inference, verifier-first dry run, single fixed slot map) is a large improvement over the frozen program and should be kept. But the inference layer that turns it into six 'confirmatory' claims does not hold: the audit's per-stratum binomial tests have power ~0.2-0.4 (not 0.6-0.85) against an arbitrary 0.5 null and the paper-linked stratum is likely a census; the S1 hypergeometric envelope is invalid under stratified sampling; DOSE's Page's L is true by construction and its rotation is infeasible; both TOST margins are below measurement granularity on RAVDESS; the REPLAY sign test is underpowered and double-counts identical splits; the two-way cluster bootstrap has three clusters; the head test is confounded with the inner pathway; the SUBESCO full-vs-980 contrast confounds takes with size and prompts; and 12 of the 21 family tests re-test directions already observed on the same speaker panels. Concrete rescue: shrink the confirmatory map to roughly 8-10 tests whose direction has not been observed on the same units (SUBESCO scratch/probe RR-GG and RG/GR-GG, CTRL-2, HPO, redefined DOSE exposed-speaker contrast), demote anchor-corpus tests to a labelled re-test family, convert Claims 1 and 6 to estimation claims with stratified/deduplicated intervals, move TOSTs to CREMA-D only with dossier-derived margins, add the size-matched SUBESCO sibling pair, fix the audit endpoint dictionary and rater contamination, and double the audit human budget. With those changes the program is defensible and the compute plan stands; without them at least three of the six headline claims would be written as 'not supported' by design rather than by data.

critiques.lens: Feasibility: GPU-hours arm by arm against recorded per-fit costs (P1 25.09 h/1,620 fits; A 9,616 s/240 five-fold fits => RAVDESS ~12 s, CREMA-D ~68 s per 5-fold fit; D1 8.7 s and B 12.8 s per fit on ~1,000-2,000-utterance SUBESCO/RAVDESS subsets; S0 3.2 s per probe unit; S2 0.07 s per Ridge fit; fine-tune 10-40 GPU-min per fold on a 12 GB card), dataset licensing/availability, one-shot engineering effort, crash/resume risk, and calendar/author-hours.

refuted_items.item: CTRL-2 partial WavLM fine-tune budgeted at 8 GPU-h (cap 10) with a 3-fold timing probe run before the tag
refuted_items.problem: The recorded fact is 10-40 GPU-min per fine-tune fold on a 12 GB card. Thirty fits therefore span 5-20 GPU-h; the 8 h figure assumes 9-21 min/fold, i.e. the bottom third of the recorded range, and at the recorded midpoint (25 min/fold) the arm is 12.5 h and breaches its own 10 h cap, triggering the preregistered drop of the SUBESCO row and then CREMA-D, which removes the 'at least one other corpus' requirement of Claim 4. Partial freezing (layers 1-8) and 3 s crops help the backward pass but not the per-epoch data path: the P1 engine uses num_workers=0 on Windows and this arm reads raw 16 kHz waveforms (no cache), so each epoch is CPU-bound on librosa loads of ~4,500 CREMA-D or ~4,200 SUBESCO files unless waveforms are held in RAM. Separately, the timing probe trains real folds on real data before the tag, contradicting PREREG-0's own gate that registration precedes any real fit; the probe's validation curves are outcome-visible.
refuted_items.fix: Run the timing probe on EmoDB (descriptive-only corpus) or on synthetic audio of CREMA-D cardinality, and discard its checkpoints; set the CTRL-2 cap at 2x the measured 3-fold mean (floor 12 h); add an in-RAM float16 waveform cache (CREMA-D ~0.6 GB, SUBESCO-full ~0.7 GB) and per-epoch validation on a fixed 10 s cap; budget CTRL-2 at 12 h expected and raise the program cap accordingly (see next item).

refuted_items.item: Program hard cap 30 GPU-h with target 28 GPU-h
refuted_items.problem: Per-arm caps already sum to 34.5 GPU-h (CTRL-1 12 + CTRL-2 10 + HPO 3 + DOSE 4 + REPLAY 2.5 + MECH 0.5 + PREREG 2.5), so the cap is guaranteed to bind if any two arms run to cap. Re-deriving each arm from recorded per-fit costs gives an expected total of 32-36 GPU-h (PREREG 3.5-5, CTRL-1 9-10, CTRL-2 8-14, HPO 2.5-3.5, DOSE 3, REPLAY 1.5-6, MECH 0.3, STAT 0.4) and a plausible range of 28-45. On an owned single RTX 5070 the difference between 30 and 42 GPU-h is about half a day of wall-clock; the frozen program already spent ~40 GPU-h. A 30 h cap is therefore a self-inflicted risk that converts an ordinary 15-20% overrun into loss of preregistered claims (DOSE reduced, HPO CREMA-D dropped, CTRL-2 truncated).
refuted_items.fix: Register a 42 GPU-h program cap with a 36 GPU-h planned total; keep the truncation order but make it trigger only above 42 h. Per-arm caps: PREREG 5, CTRL-1 12, CTRL-2 14, HPO 4, DOSE 4, REPLAY 3, MECH 0.5, STAT 0.5 (sum 43).

refuted_items.item: REPLAY at 96 fits / ~2 GPU-h ('single split as the repo does it, or its k folds')
refuted_items.problem: The 96-fit count assumes one realized partition per repository. Most audited Kaggle-style notebooks that pass the Y_test endpoint use k-fold or repeated train_test_split; with the design's own wording each realized k-fold partition costs k fits and each of the two counterfactuals is also k folds, so a 10-fold CREMA-D repository costs 2 seeds x 30 fits x ~70 s = 1.2 GPU-h alone, and 16 repositories cost 5-15 GPU-h, not 2. In addition, P0.5's sample shows 4/30 repositories evaluate on combined corpora (RAVDESS+CREMA-D, often with TESS/SAVEE) and many drop classes (4- or 6-class RAVDESS); their split fragments cannot be executed faithfully on a single-corpus manifest, and index sets with missing classes violate CTRL-1's every-class-present assertion.
refuted_items.fix: Preregister: one realized partition per repository (the repository's fold 0 by its own fold order, or its single split); counterfactuals are two single speaker-disjoint partitions matched to that test set; only single-corpus fragments over RAVDESS or CREMA-D are execution-eligible; class-subset repositories are scored on their own label subset with UAR over present classes, and this is a recorded descriptor. This keeps REPLAY at <=96 fits and ~1.5-2.5 GPU-h.

refuted_items.item: AUDIT-1 frame: E1-E5 eligibility applied to the full candidate union (channel A + channel B GitHub code search on filename tokens) before the draw, within a 110-hour audit budget
refuted_items.problem: GitHub code search on '03-01-0' or '_DFA_' returns thousands of hits because RAVDESS/CREMA-D filenames are printed in every Kaggle-derived notebook; after deduplication the union will plausibly be 800-2,000 repositories, and screening the full list at the stated 10-min cap is 130-330 human hours before a single unit is coded. The 110 h budget also has to cover 30 human-coded units (up to 45 h), adjudication of 60, and the execution tier. Channel B is further restricted by the GitHub code-search API: authenticated only, 10 requests/min, default branch only, files <384 KB, repositories with fewer than 500k files, and (legacy endpoint) repositories with activity or search hits in the last year, so channel B systematically misses stale 2019-2022 repositories and the Lincoln-Petersen catchability assumption fails in a known direction, not just through keyword/filename overlap.
refuted_items.fix: Screen sequentially in beacon order within stratum until 30 eligible per stratum (the P0.5 procedure), assign stratum to the whole union by README/description regex via the API (cheap), and estimate eligible stratum sizes as N_s times the eligibility rate among screened units; cap channel B to the first 1,000 code hits per token with the index restrictions stated in the coverage paragraph; move the coverage estimate to a bounded descriptor. Budget: 20 h frame/screening, 45 h human coding, 15 h adjudication, plus the execution tier (next item).

refuted_items.item: Execution tier: run every AST-isolable Y/N split fragment on the real RAVDESS/CREMA-D/EmoDB manifests and export index sets for REPLAY (0 GPU, folded into the 110 h audit)
refuted_items.problem: P0.5's tier-1 execution on 24 repositories with a synthetic manifest required an independently written per-repository adapter (reconstructing the dataframe the fragment consumes from Kaggle directory layouts, filename parsers, or metadata CSVs), 265 hashed files and a multi-day section-12 closure. On real manifests with row-level index export the adapter must also map the fragment's row order onto our manifest rows. At 1-3 h per unit for ~45 Y/N units this is 45-135 hours that appear nowhere in the plan, and roughly a quarter of the frame (P0.5: 7/30 IEMOCAP-only, plus external-data repositories like P05R008) is not executable at all, which the plan acknowledges only for REPLAY, not for the false-positive rule or the realized-overlap descriptor.
refuted_items.fix: Budget 80-100 h for the execution tier or restrict it to units whose fragment consumes a path list produced by glob/os.listdir/os.walk over a corpus directory, served through one shared directory-layout shim per corpus (RAVDESS Actor_XX layout, CREMA-D AudioWAV flat layout); report the execution-eligible fraction as a preregistered descriptor and confine the false-positive rule to executed units.

refuted_items.item: PREREG-0 in weeks 0-2 with ~60 author hours: frame script, lineage predicate, split generator, FT/HPO/DOSE/REPLAY code paths, scorer, an independent verifier for 21 contrasts + 2 audit tests + 2 TOSTs + Page's L + stratified Wilson with FPC + exact hypergeometric + kappa bootstrap + Lincoln-Petersen + logistic U-imputation, synthetic dry run, 20-case mutation battery, DONE markers, content-addressed caches, OSF/OpenTimestamps
refuted_items.problem: The frozen program's record is the calibration: the P1 summarizer needed a fix during the run, S3's verifier and mutation battery took ten release iterations for a 120-unit Ridge design, A's and B's verifiers were written after scoring because they were not ready, and C's verifier failed on a rounding fixture. The proposed verifier covers roughly six new statistical procedures and four new training code paths (fp16 partial fine-tune with crops and resume, hash-based label-matched dose substitution, realized-index ingestion, HPO selection) that must be exercised end to end on synthetic fixtures before any real unit runs. Sixty hours in two weeks is a 3-4x underestimate; a realistic figure is 150-250 hours over 5-7 weeks, and every week of PREREG slippage delays every GPU stage because nothing may start before the tag.
refuted_items.fix: Extend PREREG to 6 weeks and stage the registration: tag-1 (OSF + OpenTimestamps) freezes the audit, CTRL-1 and PROBE-CPU code and lets GPU-1 and the audit start; tag-2, registered before any CTRL-2/HPO/DOSE/REPLAY unit runs, freezes those arms and the full verifier. Both tags are cited in the paper; the family and slot map are fixed in tag-1 so tag-2 cannot alter them.

refuted_items.item: Total effort ~320 author hours + ~20 coder hours over a 12-week execution window
refuted_items.problem: Recomputed from the items above: prereg 150-250, audit 150-230 (screening, coding, adjudication, execution tier, REPLAY index export), engineering/monitoring 90, writing 60, giving 450-630 author hours. The 20 coder hours cannot cover the 30 human-coded units at the stated 1.5 h cap (up to 45 h) plus the audit form training. At 12 weeks this is 40-50 h/week for a solo author with a day job; the plan's own risk list already names audit hours as binding. The calendar can absorb it (Interspeech 2027 early March is ~26 weeks from 2026-09-03) only if PREREG starts immediately and the audit runs in parallel from week 3.
refuted_items.fix: Register a 20-24 week execution plan with 550 author hours, 45-60 coder hours, and a hard 'arXiv preprint by week 22' milestone; if no coder is recruited by tag-1, register the author-only reliability design now rather than as a fallback.

refuted_items.item: PREREG-0 GPU estimate 2.5 GPU-h (cache ~1 h, dry run ~1 h, timing probe ~0.5 h)
refuted_items.problem: The synthetic dry run at CREMA-D cardinality is 60 scratch fits x ~68 s = 1.1 GPU-h by itself, plus 2 partial-fine-tune dry fits (0.3-1.3 h), 8 HPO configs, a 20-fit dose ladder (0.4 h) and a replay unit; the timing probe at the recorded 10-40 min/fold is 0.5-2 h; the all-layer SSL cache for ~16.4k utterances x 2 encoders is CPU-load-bound and the frozen program's own estimate for 3 encoders x ~9.9k utterances was 1-2 GPU-h. PREREG-0 is 3.5-5 GPU-h.
refuted_items.fix: Budget PREREG-0 at 4.5 GPU-h; run the dry run at RAVDESS cardinality for the scratch cells (0.2 h) and only the fine-tune/dose/replay dry units at CREMA-D cardinality.

refuted_items.item: HPO at ~2 GPU-h (cap 3) for 160 ResNet-SE fits
refuted_items.problem: ResNet-SE (4 SE blocks) is the heaviest of the P1 scratch models, and half the grid uses lr 3e-4, which under early stopping with patience 15 runs materially more epochs toward the 100-epoch cap; 80 CREMA-D fits at 90-120 s is 2-2.7 h plus 0.4 h RAVDESS, so 2.5-3.5 GPU-h against a 3 h cap, with CREMA-D HPO the second item in the truncation order.
refuted_items.fix: Cap HPO at 4 GPU-h; log per-config epoch counts in the dry run and use them to set the cap.

refuted_items.item: SSL cache 'all 13 hidden states' from torchaudio HUBERT_BASE / WAVLM_BASE_PLUS
refuted_items.problem: torchaudio's Wav2Vec2Model.extract_features returns the 12 transformer-layer outputs, not the post-projection input embedding; the 13th state needs a forward hook, and PROBE-CPU's layer factor already names 'final (12), mid (6), mean of 1-12', so the cache spec and the analysis spec disagree on tensor shape, which the content-addressed filename will bake in.
refuted_items.fix: Specify [N,12,768] from extract_features (or register the hook and name 13 explicitly in both PROBE-CPU and MECH-0) before the cache SHA is fixed.

refuted_items.item: SUBESCO-full 'CC BY 4.0' and EmoDB 'CC0 via Zenodo/audb' stated as facts; EmoDB included as a corpus level
refuted_items.problem: The working tree documents licenses only for RAVDESS (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) and CREMA-D (ODbL/DbCL); docs/LICENSE_AND_REUSE.md and the S3/B manifests carry no SUBESCO or EmoDB license record, and the frozen program's EmoDB v2.5 run was aborted for a reason not recorded in the released tree (only 'aborted EmoDB work' in scripts/experiments/README.md). SUBESCO on Zenodo and EmoDB on audb are, to my knowledge, CC BY 4.0 and CC0-1.0 respectively, but the registration must pin this from the source record, and the EmoDB loader has a known unexplained failure history that the 0.4 GPU-h estimate ignores. IEMOCAP and MSP-Podcast are correctly treated as license-gated.
refuted_items.fix: Pin DOI, download SHA and license text for SUBESCO (Zenodo) and EmoDB (Zenodo/audb) in the tag-1 manifest; write a two-paragraph post-mortem of the EmoDB v2.5 abort into the deviation file's preamble and make the EmoDB loader part of the dry run.

refuted_items.item: MECH-0 extraction '~0.3 GPU-h from CTRL-1 RR and GG checkpoints (r=0)' while CTRL-1 already emits 'penultimate embeddings for test and training-pool utterances' per fit and the P1 engine does not persist checkpoints
refuted_items.problem: Two inconsistent mechanisms for the same tensors; the P1 engine restores the best checkpoint in memory and writes predictions only (295 MB for 1,620 fits), so MECH-0 as written has nothing to load unless CTRL-1 is modified to persist r=0 checkpoints, and if CTRL-1 emits embeddings at fit time the 0.3 GPU-h is double-counted. Storage is also unstated: CREMA-D and SUBESCO-full training-pool embeddings for 180 fits each are ~0.5 GB per corpus at width 48 float32; fine, but the per-epoch CTRL-2 checkpoints are not: ~28M trainable parameters plus AdamW state is ~340 MB per epoch, 30 fits x <=15 epochs = up to 150 GB if all are kept.
refuted_items.fix: Pick one: persist r=0 CNN/ResNet-SE checkpoints (small) in CTRL-1 and drop per-fit embedding emission, or emit embeddings per fit and delete MECH-0's extraction line. For CTRL-2 keep only last and best checkpoints per fit (~0.7 GB per fit, ~20 GB total) and state the storage budget.

refuted_items.item: CTRL-1 text: 'Transformer at 3 replicates instead of 5' and '~0.8 GPU-h Transformer overhead'
refuted_items.problem: Every level in the design runs r=0,1,2, so 'instead of 5' refers to nothing; the 0.8 h overhead is unexplained (the P1 average already includes Transformer at the same config). Harmless for the budget (CTRL-1 recomputes to ~9-10 GPU-h, the one arm whose estimate is sound) but a registration-text inconsistency a verifier will flag.
refuted_items.fix: Delete the 'instead of 5' clause and either justify the Transformer overhead from the dry-run timings or fold it into the CTRL-1 cap.

refuted_items.item: DOSE split-generator assertions: doses 'nested' and each speaker 'exposed in exactly one partial dose, rotated across replicates'
refuted_items.problem: Nested doses (q=0.25 subset of q=0.5) mean a speaker exposed at 0.25 is necessarily exposed at 0.5 as well, so 'exactly one partial dose' cannot hold within a replicate; on RAVDESS a grouped fold has 4-5 test speakers, so q=0.25 is one speaker and q=0.5 two, and rotation across three replicates does not give each speaker one partial-dose exposure. The pre-fit split assertion PREREG-0 promises for DOSE cannot be written as stated, and an unresolved assertion is exactly the kind of mid-run repair the plan forbids.
refuted_items.fix: Define exposure by nested hash order per fold and drop the 'exactly one partial dose' rotation claim, or make the doses non-nested with rotation and say so; write the assertion as 'exposed set at q is a superset of exposed set at q' < q'.

refuted_items.item: Crash/resume: per-fit DONE markers plus per-epoch checkpoints for CTRL-2, 2% bitwise retrain check, Windows host
refuted_items.problem: DONE markers fix the D1 ghost-billing failure mode for 12-70 s scratch fits. For CTRL-2 a mid-fit resume from a per-epoch checkpoint restarts the crop/batch RNG stream, so a resumed fit is not the same fit; the plan discloses fp16 non-bitwise-ness but not resume non-equivalence, and the D1 record shows two Windows OS shutdowns in one night. The 2% retrain check covers float32 arms only; a driver or torch update mid-program (torch 2.11 + torchaudio 2.10 pinning already broke once in S0 v1) invalidates the check for units before and after the update.
refuted_items.fix: Persist the RNG state with each CTRL-2 checkpoint and record 'resumed=true' in the ledger; pin the driver version and set Windows Update active hours/deferral in the registration; run the 2% retrain check as a rolling check (1% after CTRL-1, 1% at the end) so an environment drift is detected before CTRL-2 starts.

missing: A per-corpus per-fit timing table derived from the recorded runs (RAVDESS 5-fold ~12 s, CREMA-D ~68 s, SUBESCO-980 ~9-13 s, SUBESCO-full ~60 s extrapolated, EmoDB ~5 s, probe unit ~3-5 s, Ridge ~0.07 s) placed in the registration so every arm estimate is auditable; the plan gives only totals.

A wall-clock plan: ~35-45 GPU-h means ~2 days of GPU wall time, but SSL extraction, Ridge fits and the audit are CPU/human-bound; nothing states which stages can overlap on one Windows box and what the Windows Update policy is.
Storage budget (CTRL-2 per-epoch checkpoints up to ~150 GB if retained; embeddings; predictions) and where it lives (the frozen program's E:\ drive and symlink incident are not mentioned).
GitHub API authentication, rate-limit and code-search index restrictions, and the resulting bias in channel B, stated in the frame section rather than discovered at T0.
License and DOI pins for SUBESCO-full and EmoDB, and a post-mortem of the aborted EmoDB v2.5 run; the released tree documents neither.

Rules for REPLAY/execution-tier repositories that use class subsets, combined corpora (RAVDESS+TESS+SAVEE), external Kaggle directories, or repeated random splits; and the expected execution-eligible fraction of the frame from P0.5 (roughly 60-70%).
AI-rater operational pins over a 20-week program: model identifier, version, temperature, API budget, and what happens if the pinned model is deprecated before the second half of the audit.
A fallback registered now for the no-second-coder case (author-only blind coding with a 30-unit kappa CI of about +/-0.25 is named as a risk but not as a preregistered design branch).
Explicit staging of the registration so PREREG slippage does not block CTRL-1 and the audit (single-tag design makes every arm wait for the slowest engineering item, the verifier).
An in-RAM waveform cache specification for CTRL-2 (the only arm reading raw audio) so its per-epoch cost is GPU-bound rather than librosa-bound on num_workers=0 Windows.
critiques.compute_or_feasibility_verdict: Corrected GPU total: 32-36 GPU-h expected (PREREG 3.5-5, CTRL-1 9-10 including 0.7 h of probe units, CTRL-2 8-14 with the recorded 10-40 min/fold range giving 5-20, HPO 2.5-3.5, DOSE 3, REPLAY 1.5-2.5 once fixed to one partition per repository (5-15 as written), MECH 0.3, STAT 0.4), plausible range 28-45 GPU-h. The 28 GPU-h target is optimistic by 15-30% and the 30 GPU-h cap is breached with better-than-even odds, mostly through CTRL-2; on an owned RTX 5070 that is a self-imposed constraint (42 GPU-h is ~2 days of wall clock; the frozen program spent ~40 GPU-h) and should be lifted to 42 with a 36 h planned total. GPU compute is not the binding constraint. Human effort is: PREREG engineering (60 h claimed, 150-250 realistic), audit screening/coding/adjudication/execution tier (110 h claimed, 150-230 realistic), total 450-630 author hours versus 320 planned, and a 12-week execution window that must become 20-24 weeks. Licensing is sound for RAVDESS/CREMA-D and IEMOCAP is correctly excluded from execution; SUBESCO-full and EmoDB are almost certainly usable (CC BY 4.0 / CC0) but are undocumented in the tree and EmoDB has an unexplained prior abort. Crash/resume is adequately handled for scratch fits by DONE markers; CTRL-2 resume equivalence and mid-program environment drift are not.
critiques.overall_verdict: Conditionally feasible. The scientific compute is cheap and the CTRL-1/PROBE-CPU/DOSE/MECH estimates hold against the recorded per-fit costs; what does not hold is the envelope around them. Five estimates rest on assumptions the recorded facts contradict: CTRL-2 uses the bottom of the 10-40 min/fold range, REPLAY assumes one partition per repository, the audit assumes the full frame can be screened inside 110 h despite a filename-token channel that will add hundreds to thousands of candidates, the execution tier ignores the per-repository adapter cost P0.5 actually paid, and PREREG assumes a 21-contrast independent verifier plus four new training code paths can be frozen in two weeks by an author whose last verifier needed ten releases. Fix by raising the GPU cap to 42 h, staging the registration into two tags, screening in beacon order rather than exhaustively, restricting REPLAY and the execution tier to single-partition single-corpus fragments with a shared layout shim, running the timing probe off the family corpora, and registering a 20-24 week / ~550 author-hour calendar that still lands before Interspeech 2027 if it starts now. With those changes the program is runnable once on one card; without them the 30 h cap and the 2-week prereg will reproduce the frozen program's pattern of mid-run truncation and post-hoc verifier repair that the proposal exists to avoid.

critiques.lens: Claim loss: for every CUT or MERGED arm, does a claim in the current record-282 manuscript (audit interval; Random/GroupKFold/LOSO premia under four architectures; SSL probe replication; cross-lingual repetition-clean SUBESCO replication; D1 modality diagnostic; mechanism) lose its evidence, and are the program's own resulting_paper_claims actually supported by the arms registered to carry them? Verified against paper/current/main.tex (L49 'Random, GroupKFold, and leave-one-speaker-out protocol packages under one four-model implementation'; L139 'repetition-clean finite panel from SUBESCO'; L189-190 LOSO discussion; L240 inner-validation caveat).

refuted_items.item: CTRL-1 / Claim 2 and Claim 3 — Delta_inner = GR-GG registered as the family test behind 'validation-only nonexclusivity is itself inflationary'
refuted_items.problem: GR-GG is measured on a speaker-exclusive OUTER test. A positive GR-GG cannot be 'inflation' of a reported number: the test speakers are unseen in both cells, so any gain is real generalization from the inner allocation (random inner keeps all ~19 fit speakers; grouped inner drops ~5 whole speakers from the fit set). A's own notes call I_G an 'allocation + checkpoint-selection package', not leakage. The contrast that actually measures how a leaky inner boundary inflates a leaky reported score is I_R = RR-RG (A: +7.29 pp on RAVDESS, with a +2.15 interaction), which the program demotes to a secondary estimate. Claim 3's second sentence and the operational recommendation 'enforce exclusivity at inner validation' are therefore attached to the wrong contrast; a rejection of GR-GG would be written up as evidence of inflation when it is evidence of the opposite (more fit speakers help).
refuted_items.fix: Register two inner contrasts with distinct names: Delta_inner^alloc = GR-GG (allocation package, speaker-exclusive test; report as 'inner grouping costs fit speakers') and Delta_inner^leak = RR-RG (inner leakage under leaky outer; the inflation quantity). Put RR-RG in the 21-test family in place of GR-GG (family size unchanged) and reword Claim 3 to 'the leaky-pipeline premium decomposes into an outer component (RG-GG) and an inner-selection component under leaky outer (RR-RG), with interaction'. Alternatively match inner fit-speaker counts (grouped inner holds out k speakers; random inner holds out the same k speakers' utterance count from all speakers is not matched—so use speaker-count-matched inner: random-by-utterance within the same fit-speaker set) and keep GR-GG only as an allocation descriptor.

refuted_items.item: CTRL-1 merge of S3 — SUBESCO-full (7,000 utt, 5 takes) as the family corpus level; SUBESCO-980 repetition-clean panel demoted to an untested secondary
refuted_items.problem: The current paper's cross-lingual claim (L139, L204, L247) rests on a REPETITION-CLEAN panel precisely so the contrast isolates speaker exclusivity from near-duplicate-take leakage. Under the program, the family test on SUBESCO measures speaker+take leakage bundled (grouping by speaker removes both), and the rejection is near-certain and uninformative about speakers. Claim 2 states that 'speaker-nonexclusive splitting ... inflates UAR on ... SUBESCO', which the SUBESCO-full arm does not cleanly support; the speaker-only reading is pushed to a secondary with no test (acknowledged in risks but not repaired). The clean cross-lingual replication the current paper already has is thereby lost, and the SUBESCO probe-level rejection needed by Claim 2's 'at least two probe rejections' rule becomes trivially satisfied for the wrong reason.
refuted_items.fix: Swap roles: SUBESCO-980 is the family corpus level (scratch and probe RR-GG tests; ~0.6 GPU-h already budgeted), SUBESCO-full is the secondary level. Keep the full-vs-980 paired contrast as the take-leakage descriptor. Additionally add a zero-cost third split on SUBESCO-full in PROBE-CPU: StratifiedGroupKFold with groups = speaker x emotion x prompt cell (siblings kept together, speakers still mixed) so take leakage and speaker leakage are separated on identical data rather than via a 7x data-size confound.

refuted_items.item: Cut of P1 LOSO from-scratch arm; Claim 4's clause 'the LOSO-over-GroupKFold advantage is equivalent to a training-set-size effect (TOST)' carried by PROBE-CPU Ridge on frozen features
refuted_items.problem: The current paper's LOSO evidence is in Table 1 (8 rows), the 24-test family (12 LOSO contrasts, 5 non-rejections), and L189-190. The observation to be explained (LOSO > GroupKFold in 8/8 cells, up to +6.6 pp on RAVDESS CNN) arose in early-stopped from-scratch models whose inner validation also gains speakers under LOSO. PROBE-CPU's TOST uses a closed-form Ridge head with no inner validation on frozen SSL features: the regime in which the puzzle appeared is not the regime in which it is 'resolved'. A TOST pass on Ridge licenses nothing about trained models, so Claim 4's LOSO clause is a claim-arm mismatch and the paper loses all trained-model LOSO evidence while the title/abstract of the current paper promise three protocols under one implementation.
refuted_items.fix: Either drop the LOSO clause from Claim 4 and state in Limitations that LOSO under trained models was not re-run (cite the 2026 P1 LOSO rows as the prior descriptive result), or add a minimal from-scratch LOSO pair on RAVDESS CNN only: LOSO (24 folds) and LOSO-sub (training speakers subsampled to 80%), r=0..2, 144 fits at ~12 s each (~0.5 GPU-h, well inside the CTRL-1 cap), speaker-paired TOST vs Group5 on the same speakers. Keep the Ridge TOST as the frozen-feature companion.

refuted_items.item: AUDIT-1 / Claim 1 — headline narrowed to Y_test, U counted as non-positive under a tighter 1.5 h cap, static-Y->N flip only for executable repos, and a disjunctive 'and/or' per-stratum test vs 0.5 at n=30
refuted_items.problem: Three changes stack against the prevalence claim the paper is titled on. (1) The prior endpoint counted any active boundary (44/60 incl. validation-only); the fraction of those 44 that are validation-only is unknown, so Y_test could plausibly be ~30-35/60. (2) The false-positive rule flips static Y to N only where the fragment executes on a licensed corpus (RAVDESS/CREMA-D/EmoDB); IEMOCAP-only lineages (7/30 in P0.5) keep the static verdict, giving corpus-dependent differential misclassification inside one estimand. (3) A one-sided test vs 0.5 with n_s=30, ~12-20% U treated as negative, has ~0.6 power at true 0.70 per stratum; with the narrowed endpoint the true value may be nearer 0.55-0.65, so the confirmatory headline can fail even though prevalence is high, and the map then forces 'not supported' into the main text. The result is a paper whose only non-collided contribution is likely to be printed as unsupported because of estimand narrowing, not because of the data.
refuted_items.fix: Make the primary audit estimand 'any active boundary permits same-speaker membership' (Y_test or Y_val), matching the prior endpoint, with Y_test as the registered secondary; register the primary as an estimate with stratified interval plus the frame envelope (as the current paper does), and make the >0.5 tests the confirmatory add-on only for the pooled sample (power ~0.85), with per-stratum tests as descriptors. Do not overwrite static verdicts: report the 'permits' fraction on all 60 and the 'realizes' fraction on the executed subset as two columns, and count non-executable repos as 'not executed', never as N. Set the per-unit cap at the S1 value (2 review-h) so the U rate is comparable to the historical 7/60.

refuted_items.item: DOSE / Claim 5 — 'UAR rises monotonically with the fraction of test speakers whose other utterances enter training' with Page's L over all test-fold speakers
refuted_items.problem: Adding test-fold speakers' half-A utterances raises the training-speaker COUNT (RAVDESS 19-20 -> up to 24) while the removed matching-label utterances come from existing training speakers; the design holds utterance count constant but not speaker diversity, which C/P5 deliberately held fixed via donor substitution. At q=0.25 and 0.5, 75%/50% of test-fold speakers are unexposed, so the per-speaker UAR series entering Page's L is dominated by the diversity effect, not exposure. Also 'nested doses' and 'each speaker exposed in exactly one partial dose' are contradictory (a speaker in the 0.25 set is exposed at 0.5 too). Claim 5's monotone curve and its 'share of the full premium reached at 25% exposure' therefore do not isolate leakage dose.
refuted_items.fix: Define the primary per-speaker outcome as exposed-speaker gain: UAR(exposed at q) - UAR(same speaker at q=0), with the family test a Page's L over doses restricted to speakers exposed at that dose (rotation so each speaker is exposed at exactly one of q in {0.25, 0.5}, doses not nested), and keep training-speaker count constant by donor substitution (drop one non-test training speaker's half-A per exposed test speaker, as in C/P5). The unexposed-speaker TOST then cleanly tests diversity spillover. Reword Claim 5 to 'exposed-speaker gain increases with exposure fraction'.

refuted_items.item: REPLAY / Claim 6 — exact sign test across up to 16 repositories as a family member
refuted_items.problem: Every RAVDESS/CREMA-D Y_test repo that executes will realize ~100% speaker overlap (P0.5 synthetic intersections: 24/24, 91/91); Delta_repo is then the CTRL-1 RR-GG pipeline contrast at a different fold size, computed on the same two corpora with the same model. The 16 'repositories' are not independent draws of anything; the sign test is near-tautological given Claim 2 and inflates the 21-test family with a test that cannot fail. Claim 6's framing as a confirmatory 'audit-to-practice link' overstates what is measured (no repository's reported number is touched).
refuted_items.fix: Move REPLAY out of the family (family size 20) and register it as descriptive: per-repository Delta_repo with repository-level CI, plotted against realized overlap fraction and test size, and the ratio Delta_repo / CTRL-1 RR-GG for the same corpus as the reported 'realized-split scaling'. If a confirmatory statement is wanted, test whether Delta_repo differs from the CTRL-1 premium (does the repo's actual split structure change the magnitude?), which is not tautological.

refuted_items.item: STAT-1 claim-to-rejection map — Claim 4 bundles four heterogeneous requirements (CTRL-2 on RAVDESS + one other; HPO on one corpus; head test; LOSO TOST) and truncation feeds p=1 placeholders into it
refuted_items.problem: Under the preregistered CTRL-2 drop order (SUBESCO then CREMA-D), a cost overrun yields p=1 for the dropped corpus, and Claim 4 (which needs RAVDESS plus one other) is written as 'not supported' in the main text even though the untested corpus was never measured; the same rule conflates 'not tested' with 'refuted' for HPO CREMA-D and DOSE CREMA-D. A single low-power component (HPO difference-in-differences at n=24) also sinks the fine-tuning result that would otherwise stand.
refuted_items.fix: Split Claim 4 into 4a (fine-tuning persistence), 4b (HPO enlargement), 4c (head dependence), 4d (LOSO size effect), each with its own requirement; add a third verdict label 'not tested (truncated per registration entry N)' distinct from 'not supported', used only when the required test entered as a placeholder because its unit never ran.

refuted_items.item: S0 merge into CTRL-1 — wav2vec2-base dropped; PROBE-CPU descriptor still says '3-encoder Ridge direction stability' while only HuBERT and WavLM are cached
refuted_items.problem: The current paper's SSL replication and the S3 cross-lingual primary are three-probe results; wav2vec2 was the most stable probe on SUBESCO (19/1, q05 +1.73) while WavLM was fragile (16/4, q05 -1.60). With two encoders the SUBESCO probe-level RR-GG average is WavLM-diluted, raising the chance that Claim 2's 'at least two probe rejections' fails on SUBESCO for a reason unrelated to the science. The PROBE-CPU text is internally inconsistent (3-encoder rule on a 2-encoder cache), so the S2-style 20-draw descriptor cannot be reproduced as written.
refuted_items.fix: Add WAV2VEC2_BASE to the PREREG-0 all-layer cache (~0.3 GPU-h, ~0.2 GPU-h of extra probe units) and keep three encoders in both CTRL-1 probe levels and PROBE-CPU; or fix all text to two encoders and register the SUBESCO probe test as the HuBERT-only level.

refuted_items.item: PROBE-CPU H_head — 'resolving the earlier S0/S2 discrepancy' with no P1-style partition in the split table
refuted_items.problem: The head contrast is run on the CTRL-1 partitions (StratifiedKFold / StratifiedGroupKFold), but the S0 side of the discrepancy used P1's frozen GroupKFold (no shuffle) and StratifiedKFold(rs=42) splits. The companion descriptor promised in the text ('20-draw Ridge vs P1-style partition contrast') cannot be computed because no P1-style partition exists in the new split table, so a non-rejection cannot be attributed to split family as the design says. The Ridge head also carries a StandardScaler fit on the leaky outer-train fold and class_weight-balanced closed-form fitting, so 'head' bundles scaler leakage with optimizer/early-stopping differences.
refuted_items.fix: Add the six P1 frozen split npz files (already in hand, byte-pinned) as a fourth partition set in PROBE-CPU (zero GPU) and run both heads on them; add a Ridge-without-scaler variant so the head factor is decomposed (scaler leak vs closed-form fit). Reword Claim 4c to 'head-dependent on identical partitions' and drop 'resolving'.

refuted_items.item: MECH-0 bounded mechanism sentence — 'SUBESCO as-released premium exceeds the repetition-clean premium, indicating near-duplicate-take leakage adds to speaker leakage'
refuted_items.problem: The full-vs-980 contrast changes training size 7x and prompt count 10 vs 7 alongside take availability; a larger premium on full is consistent with data-size effects on the random arm alone. The sibling-NN conditional accuracy is selection-based (which test items have a sibling NN is determined by the same embedding whose accuracy is being conditioned), so P(correct | sibling NN) - P(correct | other) is not a leakage readout even descriptively. The sentence attributes a mechanism the arms do not isolate.
refuted_items.fix: Use the take-grouped random split proposed above (SUBESCO-full, groups = speaker x emotion x prompt) so the take increment is measured on identical data; report the sibling-NN table as 'nearest-neighbour composition' only (share of test items whose NN is a sibling under RR vs GG) without conditional accuracy, or condition on sibling availability in the training fold (a property of the split, not the embedding).

refuted_items.item: Cut of D1 — rationale states 'the RAVDESS sibling/sentence structure it depended on is read out directly in MECH-0'
refuted_items.problem: D1's estimand was the song-minus-speech channel difference of the premium on matched actors; MECH-0 contains no vocal-channel factor, and no arm in the program loads RAVDESS Song. The current paper has no main-text D1 claim, so the loss is acceptable, but the stated replacement is a misattribution that a reader of the registration would catch.
refuted_items.fix: State plainly that the vocal-channel question is dropped without replacement and name it in Limitations; remove MECH-0 from D1's merged_from list.

refuted_items.item: CTRL-1 rationale — 'Transformer at 3 replicates instead of 5' and 'Transformer overhead ~0.8 h'
refuted_items.problem: All model levels are registered at r=0,1,2; there is no 5-replicate level anywhere, so the AC-objection remedy as written describes a design that does not exist, and the 0.8 h line item has no matching unit count in run_plan.csv.
refuted_items.fix: Delete the replicate sentence; either state all levels run r=0..2 or register Transformer at the same replicate count with its per-fit cost folded into the corpus estimates.

refuted_items.item: Cut of P1's per-architecture claims — current paper's 'Random > Grouped in 8/8 corpus x model pairs, 8/8 Holm survivors' replaced by model-averaged Delta_pipe^scratch(c)
refuted_items.problem: Averaging over CNN/ResNet-SE/Transformer before differencing means the paper can no longer state that the premium holds for every architecture as a tested statement; per-level cells are estimates only. Since the current manuscript's Panel B forest is exactly the eight per-model deltas, the replacement Fig. 1B (21 family contrasts) drops the one figure a reader of the 2026 paper would look for.
refuted_items.fix: Keep model averaging for the family tests but register per-level RR-GG sign counts (x/9 corpus x level cells) as a named descriptor with the forest of per-level deltas in the supplement, and cite the 2026 eight-row table once as the prior per-architecture replication.

missing: A registered contrast that ties the new CTRL-1 numbers to the 2026 P1 table: hygiene (duplicate/zero-variance drops), fold family (StratifiedGroupKFold vs GroupKFold) and model set all change, and reuse is forbidden, so the reader cannot tell whether the premium moved; add one zero-cost descriptor (CNN/ResNet-SE RR-GG on the six P1 frozen split files) so the two papers are reconcilable.

An explicit accounting of which current-paper claims are intentionally lost and why (three protocols under trained models; four architectures; three encoders; repetition-clean SUBESCO as the tested level; S2's 20/20 sentence). The program's merged_from lists imply continuity that the estimands do not deliver.

A speaker-count-constant version of the inner contrast (or DOSE) — nowhere in the program is 'more training speakers' separated from 'leakage', although it is the single most plausible alternative explanation for both GR-GG > 0 and the dose curve; C/P5's donor-substitution trick did this and was cut without carrying the idea forward.
Multiplicity control for the two TOSTs that Claims 4d and 5 present as confirmatory; they sit outside both families with no adjustment.
A registered 'not tested (truncated)' verdict distinct from 'not supported' in the claim-to-rejection map.

The Y_val-to-HPO bridge is asserted (HPO 'ties the audit's Y_val units to a measured quantity') but no descriptor links them: register the audit column 'test set used for selection' cross-tabulated with Y_test/Y_val, and report the HPO inner-val minus outer-test optimism alongside it.

An IEMOCAP handling rule for the false-positive flip (execution impossible without a license): without it the flip rule introduces corpus-correlated misclassification into a single stratified estimand.
critiques.compute_or_feasibility_verdict: Feasible within the 30 GPU-h cap, with thin slack. Calibrating from the frozen manifests (A: 240 five-fold fits = 9,616 s -> ~12 s per RAVDESS-scale fit and ~68 s per CREMA-D-scale fit at 128-frame truncation; B: 12.8 s per 980-1,960-utt SUBESCO fit; D1: 8.7 s per 1,012-utt fit): CTRL-1 scratch = RAVDESS 0.6 h + CREMA-D ~3.4 h + SUBESCO-full (~7,000 utt, CREMA-D-scale) ~3.2 h + SUBESCO-980 0.5 h + EmoDB 0.1 h + seed-crossing 0.4 h = ~8.2-9 h, plus 600 probe units ~0.5 h -> ~9.5 h, consistent with the estimate but with CREMA-D and SUBESCO-full each ~10-15% under-budgeted. HPO 160 ResNet-SE fits ~2.1 h; DOSE 240 fits ~2.7 h; REPLAY ~1.3-2 h; MECH-0/retrain ~0.6 h; caches and dry run ~2 h. CTRL-2 (WavLM-base+, top-4 layers, 3 s crops, batch 16, <=15 epochs, patience 3) is the only unmeasured item: rough per-epoch costs give ~1 h RAVDESS, ~2.5 h CREMA-D, ~2.3 h SUBESCO-full -> ~6 h, inside the 8 h estimate and 10 h cap, so the timing probe is the right gate. Program total ~26-29 GPU-h. The fixes proposed above add at most ~1 GPU-h (RAVDESS CNN LOSO/LOSO-sub ~0.5 h, wav2vec2 cache and probe units ~0.5 h, take-grouped SUBESCO split 0 GPU) and would need to be paid for from the DOSE-to-RAVDESS-only truncation or by trimming EmoDB. The binding constraint is human hours (~110 audit review-h plus adjudication), not GPU.
critiques.overall_verdict: The program is a sound reorganization of compute, but through the claim-loss lens it is not yet a sound reorganization of claims. Four registered claims are attached to arms that measure something adjacent: Claim 3's inner-leakage sentence rides on GR-GG, which is measured on a speaker-exclusive test and cannot show inflation; Claim 2's SUBESCO row and the cross-lingual replication the current paper already owns are replaced by a take-plus-speaker bundle on SUBESCO-full; Claim 4's LOSO clause and Claim 5's dose curve are resolved in regimes (Ridge on frozen features; training-speaker count varying with dose) different from the ones in which the questions arose; and Claim 1 narrows the endpoint, tightens the review cap, flips verdicts only for executable repos and then tests a disjunction vs 0.5 at n=30, making the paper's single non-collided contribution the claim most likely to be printed as 'not supported'. None of these is fatal to the program, and all are fixable before the tag at ~1 GPU-h: swap the SUBESCO levels and add a take-grouped split, register RR-RG as the inner family contrast, add a RAVDESS CNN LOSO/LOSO-sub pair, make DOSE speaker-count-constant with exposed-speaker gain as the outcome, restore 'any active boundary' as the audit primary with the estimate-plus-interval headline, split Claim 4, and add a 'not tested' verdict. Cutting LOSO, FNO, D1, B, C/P5, P0 purposive, the lineage branches and BRIDGE loses no main-text claim of the current paper except 'three protocols under one four-model implementation', which the program should state as a deliberate loss rather than as covered by PROBE-CPU. Verdict: run only after the claim-to-arm map is repaired; as registered, at least three of the eight resulting_paper_claims would not be supported by their designated arms even if every test rejected.

program.angle: Confirmatory minimalist core (RR/RG/GR/GG protocol factorial on RAVDESS, CREMA-D and the repetition-clean SUBESCO-980 panel, three from-scratch models plus three frozen SSL probes sharing partitions, initialization and seeds) hardened with verifier-first engineering, a two-stage public registration, and an estimation-first stratified audit with realized-overlap execution and blind human coding; extended by four cheap arms the frozen program never ran (partial WavLM fine-tune, HPO on leaky validation, donor-substitution exposure ladder with fixed prompt-disjoint test half, REPLAY of audited realized splits). Two Holm families are separated by novelty: Family N (10 tests whose direction has never been observed on these speaker panels or in the literature) and Family R (13 preregistered re-tests of directions already reported by Ibrahim et al. 2026, Wang et al. 2021, or the authors' own 2026 P1/A/S0/C runs). Planned 33 GPU-h, hard cap 42 GPU-h, one RTX 5070; ~500 author hours plus 60 coder hours over 22 weeks; target Interspeech 2027 with arXiv preprint at ledger lock.
program.thesis: Speaker-nonexclusive evaluation is common in public SER code and inflates reported performance; the paper earns each half with one instrument that is publicly registered, verifier-frozen before any real fit or adjudication, and run once in a fixed order. The prevalence half is an estimation claim: a stratified (paper-linked vs other), beacon-ordered, fixed-n=60 audit of repository lineages with a frozen lineage rule, an 'any active boundary' primary endpoint and a test-boundary secondary, static verdicts on all 60 plus realized overlap from executing each repository's own split code on the real corpora, a static-leakage-detector benchmark column, and blind human coding hash-committed before the AI rater. The effect half separates what is new from what is replicated: same-implementation, speaker-paired premia on RAVDESS/CREMA-D are presented as a replication of Ibrahim et al. 2026 and Zielonka et al. 2022 (and of the authors' 2026 P1), while the confirmatory family carries only the untested directions: the repetition-clean SUBESCO panel under the full factorial, the outer (RG-GG) and inner-leak (RR-RG) decomposition on that panel, whether partial fine-tuning re-exposes speaker information that frozen probes attenuate, whether hyperparameter selection on a speaker-overlapping validation set enlarges the premium, and whether the frozen-probe premium is head-dependent. The paper would claim prevalence with intervals, reliability and realized overlap; a corpus-resolved and decomposed premium that survives frozen probes, fine-tuning and hyperparameter search; an exposed-speaker gain curve with a no-spillover equivalence on CREMA-D; and per-repository premia under real audited splits reported next to, never multiplied with, prevalence.

program.name: PREREG-0: two-stage public registration, shared infrastructure, verifier-first synthetic dry run, off-family timing probe
merged_from: P1 preregistration and engineering lock (process only)
S0 v2 / S3 prep-v2 SSL feature caches (now all-layer, three encoders, content-addressed)
D1/A/B split-manifest and completion-manifest tooling (replaced by one split table with pre-fit assertions)
PLAN.md revision history (replaced by two OSF registrations plus an append-only deviation file)
program.rationale: Every arm in the dossier is labelled outcome-visible because no public timestamp existed and verifiers were written after scoring (A: 2 min after; B: 43 s after; C: tolerance corrected post-score; S3: ten releases; S0 v1 rerun for cache identity; D1 ghost-billing). The feasibility critique showed a single tag would make every GPU stage wait on the slowest engineering item (a verifier covering ~25 tests, two TOSTs, stratified intervals, hypergeometric bounds, kappa, and four new training code paths), and that the original 60-hour/2-week prereg estimate was 3-4x low given the frozen program's own record (P1 summarizer fixed mid-run, S3 ten releases). The registration is therefore staged: tag-1 freezes the audit, CTRL-1 and PROBE-CPU (and the families, slot map and claim map, which tag-2 cannot alter); tag-2 freezes CTRL-2/HPO/DOSE/REPLAY and the full verifier before any of their units run. The timing probe is moved off the family corpora (EmoDB and synthetic audio at CREMA-D cardinality) so no real family fit precedes registration.
program.design: TAG-1 (target week 5) commit SER26-prereg-1 containing: this protocol; audit frame script, lineage predicate, eligibility codes, endpoint dictionary, rater form, AI-rater frozen prompt with pinned model identifier/version/temperature and API budget, static-leakage-detector wrapper; split generator; the P1 training engine unchanged plus checkpoint persistence for r=0 CNN/ResNet-SE fits; run_plan.csv with unit_id = SHA256(config) for every CTRL-1/PROBE-CPU unit; seed table (split_seed(c,r)=u32(SHA256('SER26|split|c|r')); train_seed(c,fold,r)=u32(SHA256('SER26|train|c|fold|r')) with NO model, cell or protocol token so all four cells and all HPO configs share initialization and batch-order streams); scorer and an independently written verifier (imports nothing from the scorer) covering CTRL-1, PROBE-CPU and AUDIT-1 statistics; both Holm families, the TOST pair, the 4-page slot map and the claim-to-verdict map (fixed here, immutable at tag-2); the per-corpus per-fit timing table derived from recorded runs (RAVDESS 5-fold scratch ~12 s, CREMA-D ~68 s, SUBESCO-980 ~13 s, SUBESCO-full ~64 s, EmoDB ~5 s, early-stopped probe unit ~3.2 s, Ridge ~0.07 s CPU) against which every arm estimate is auditable; a wall-clock plan stating which CPU/human stages overlap the single Windows GPU box, the pinned driver/torch/torchaudio versions, Windows Update deferral, and the storage budget (predictions, r=0 checkpoints, CTRL-2 best+last checkpoints only, ~25 GB total). TAG-2 (target week 9, before any CTRL-2/HPO/DOSE/REPLAY unit) commit SER26-prereg-2: those four arms' configs and run_plan rows, the remaining verifier modules, the measured timing-probe value and the CTRL-2 cap derived from it. Both tags are OSF-registered with OpenTimestamps anchors; the NIST beacon pulse for the audit draw is the first pulse after the tag-1 OSF timestamp. INFRASTRUCTURE: byte manifests (path, bytes, SHA-256, speaker, label, sentence id, take, intensity, sex) for RAVDESS speech (1,440/24/8), CREMA-D (7,442/91/6), SUBESCO-full as released (7,000/20/7; Zenodo DOI, download SHA and license text pinned from the source record), the SUBESCO-980 repetition-clean panel and two size-matched SUBESCO panels built from the same rule (SUB-1400-one: one take per speaker x emotion x prompt over all 10 prompts = 1,400; SUB-1400-two: two takes per cell over a hash-selected 700 cells = 1,400; identical size and prompt coverage, differing only in sibling presence), EmoDB (535/10/7; Zenodo/audb DOI and CC0 record pinned; loader included in the dry run with a written post-mortem of the aborted 2026 EmoDB v2.5 run in the deviation-file preamble). Preregistered hygiene: exact-byte duplicate groups collapsed to lexically first path, label-conflicting groups dropped, zero-variance audio dropped (CREMA-D 1076_MTI_SAD_XX), stereo downmixed, all logged; the six P1 frozen split npz files are mapped through the hygiene log so the P1-reconciliation units are computable. Log-mel cache exactly P1 (22.05 kHz, trim 30 dB, 64 mel, FFT 1024, hop 512, 128 frames, per-utterance z-score, train-only SpecAugment). SSL cache: torchaudio HUBERT_BASE, WAVLM_BASE_PLUS, WAV2VEC2_BASE (weights SHA-pinned), 16 kHz, trim 30 dB, 13 hidden states (post-projection input via registered hook + 12 transformer outputs; the 13-state shape is named identically in PROBE-CPU and MECH-0) time-mean pooled, float16 [N,13,768], filename = SHA of (manifest SHA, bundle SHA, sr, trim, pooling, code SHA); ~16.4k utterances x 3 encoders ~2.5 GPU-h. In-RAM float16 waveform cache spec for CTRL-2 (CREMA-D ~0.6 GB, SUBESCO-980 ~0.1 GB, RAVDESS ~0.15 GB).
