SPLIT TABLE (one hashed CSV per corpus level): replicates r=0,1,2; outer Random = StratifiedKFold(5, shuffle, split_seed) ignoring speaker; outer Grouped = StratifiedGroupKFold(5, shuffle, split_seed, groups=speaker); inner (exactly 25% of outer train in both arms): random stratified train_test_split allowing speaker overlap vs GroupShuffleSplit(0.25) by speaker; 20 Ridge draws d=0..19 (S2 seed rule); 10 probe draws x 2 seeds for the HuBERT partition-level interval; LOSO by speaker id and LOSO-sub (3 hash subsamples of training speakers to 80%); SUBESCO-full take-grouped split (StratifiedGroupKFold with groups = speaker x emotion x prompt cell, speakers mixed across folds); DOSE rotation halves and donor pairings; REPLAY size-matched partitions. Assertions before any fit: zero speaker overlap in every grouped path, exactly-once OOF coverage, every class present in every fold, DOSE donor/target cell-count identity; failure aborts. DRY RUN: synthetic audio manifests with real speaker/class cardinalities; scratch cells at RAVDESS cardinality (60 fits, ~0.2 GPU-h); fine-tune, HPO, dose and replay dry units at CREMA-D cardinality (~1 GPU-h); scorer and verifier must agree to 1e-12 on all synthetic outputs including rounded-field and fp16-scored fixtures; 24-case mutation battery (row drop, label swap, fold overlap injection, seed drift, duplicated prediction rows, missing-cell propagation, DOSE cell-count violation, realized-index misalignment, stratum weight error, kappa bootstrap seed drift) must be rejected 24/24. TIMING PROBE (before tag-2, after tag-1): three partial-fine-tune folds on EmoDB and on synthetic audio at CREMA-D cardinality (~1.5 GPU-h), checkpoints discarded; CTRL-2 cap = 2x the measured per-fold mean scaled to each corpus, floor 12 GPU-h. Per-fit DONE markers holding the predictions SHA; runner skips verified DONE units on restart; CTRL-2 checkpoints persist RNG state and mark resumed=true in the ledger. Append-only deviation file cited by entry number.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: No scientific estimand. Gates: (i) verifier == scorer to 1e-12 on synthetic outputs; (ii) 24/24 mutation cases rejected; (iii) split-table assertions pass; (iv) tag-1 OSF timestamp precedes the first real cache write and the first audit screening action (ledger-verified); (v) tag-2 OSF timestamp precedes the first CTRL-2/HPO/DOSE/REPLAY unit and records the measured timing-probe value. Any failed gate blocks the corresponding tag.

program.name: AUDIT-1: stratified, fixed-n=60 probability audit of public SER repository lineages; estimation-only headline with 'any active boundary' primary and test-boundary secondary; realized-overlap execution; blind human coding; static-detector benchmark
merged_from: P0 candidate-frame search protocol and E1-E8 exclusion codes
P0.5 random sample and sequential beacon-order screening; execution-validation tier (AST-isolated split execution, now on real manifests with a shared layout shim)
S1 beacon-seeded priority order, endpoint dictionary, hash-bound evidence receipts, exact hypergeometric bounds (now per stratum)
S1 D2 executable-blob lineage predicate (fixed a priori, no branches)
P0's 'test set used for selection' and 'single split no variance' outcomes (kept as descriptor columns)
program.rationale: The audit remains the paper's distinctive contribution, but the literature critique showed its novelty is narrower than claimed (EMO-SUPERB reports 50% random partitions in prior SER studies; Antoniou 2023 reviewed IEMOCAP code; static leakage detectors exist) and the inference critique showed the confirmatory per-stratum binomial tests had power ~0.2-0.4 against an arbitrary 0.5 null, the paper-linked stratum is probably a census, the SRS hypergeometric envelope is invalid under stratification, the Y_test/Y_val dictionary was undefined for the modal single-split notebook, and the author-as-rater design was contaminated by ~90 prior verdicts. The claim-loss critique showed that narrowing to Y_test with a tighter review cap and an asymmetric executable-only flip rule would make the paper's only non-collided contribution the one most likely printed as 'not supported'. The audit is therefore an estimation instrument: 'any active boundary' primary (comparable to the 2026 endpoint), Y_test secondary, static verdicts never overwritten, stratified intervals, and reliability measured on lineages no rater has seen before. The feasibility critique's screening arithmetic (a filename-token channel can add hundreds to thousands of candidates) is met by sequential beacon-order screening to quota and a capped channel B.
program.design: FRAME (frozen at tag-1 date T0): channel A = P0 GitHub repository search (2 query families x 4 corpora RAVDESS/CREMA-D/IEMOCAP/EmoDB, top-100 best match) + arXiv API top-100 per corpus + one-hop snowball; channel B = authenticated GitHub code search on loader-only filename tokens ('03-01-0' RAVDESS, '_DFA_'/'_IEO_' CREMA-D, 'Ses01F_impro' IEMOCAP, '03a01Fa' EmoDB), capped at the first 1,000 code hits per token, with the index restrictions (default branch, <384 KB files, recent-activity bias) stated in the coverage paragraph; union with the existing 383-URL log; canonicalize; snapshot default-branch commit SHA per candidate at T0. Lineage rule fixed before any screening: explicit fork/parent, identical top-level tree SHA, identical content-blob set, executable-blob containment >=0.90 (closed suffix list, notebook = one blob, dedup by blob SHA) with corroborator (same project name, identical root README blob, or owner lineage); keeper = unique upstream > earliest created_at > URL order; merge count reported once, no branches. STRATUM assigned to every candidate lineage before screening by API regex on README/description (arxiv.org, doi.org, ieeexplore, aclanthology, isca-archive, or 'ICASSP'/'Interspeech' + title string) = paper-linked vs other; N_1, N_2 (candidate counts) recorded; regex misclassification rate estimated by hand-verifying a hash-selected 40 candidates and reported; an estimate of N_1 from the existing 383-URL log is recorded in tag-1. SAMPLE: beacon pulse; order = SHA256(pulse || canonical_id) within stratum; E1-E5 eligibility applied sequentially in that order (10-min screening cap; unscreenable = ineligible with code) until quota; allocation n_1 = min(30, eligible paper-linked), n_2 = 60 - n_1; if the paper-linked stratum is exhausted before 30 it is a census, reported as an exact proportion with no interval; eligible stratum sizes estimated as candidate N_s times the screened eligibility rate (variance carried into the stratified interval). RATING per unit at pinned commit: Rater H (recruited coder; the author only if no coder is declared at tag-1, in which case the audit is labelled AI-rated with author review and the agreement statistic is labelled author-AI agreement) codes a hash-selected 30 units (15 per stratum where possible) drawn ONLY from lineages absent from the P0/P0.5/S1 samples, BEFORE the AI rater runs on them (mechanised: the AI tool refuses a unit until human_code_<id>.json is in the hashed ledger); Rater AI = frozen prompt + evidence template (path:Lstart-Lend at pinned commit for the decisive split statement and its calling entry point; per-line fragment SHA-256); per-unit cap 2 review-hours per rater (S1 value, so the U rate is comparable to 7/60), exceeded -> U for that rater. ENDPOINT DICTIONARY: Y_test = an active train->held-out path whose metric is presented as the final reported result permits same-speaker membership on both sides, regardless of whether that set also drove selection (dual use recorded in the descriptor column); Y_val = only a train->validation/model-selection path permits it AND a separately reported test set is verified speaker-exclusive; N = all active paths verified speaker-exclusive and enumeration closed; U = undecidable, cap, or no applicable split; primary Y_any = Y_test or Y_val. Descriptor columns: test set used for checkpoint/hyperparameter selection (Y/N/U), single split with no variance reported (Y/N/U), dialogue-partner contamination possible (IEMOCAP session vs speaker split; per EMO-SUPERB/Antoniou), corpus set, single-corpus vs combined-corpus loader, class subset, notebook vs script, framework, year, reported top-line metric on RAVDESS/CREMA-D, execution-eligible (Y/N), and prior lineage membership with historical verdict (filled from the ledger only after adjudication; hidden from both raters). STATIC-DETECTOR COLUMN: one published static train/test-overlap leakage detector (the Yang et al. ASE 2022 notebook analysis or LeakageDetector 2.0, pinned version) run on every unit; its verdict and tool coverage (unit parseable or not) recorded; agreement with the adjudicated verdict reported alongside kappa. EXECUTION TIER for every Y/N unit whose decisive split fragment is AST-isolable AND consumes a path list produced by glob/os.listdir/os.walk over a single corpus directory, served through one shared layout shim per corpus (RAVDESS Actor_XX layout; CREMA-D AudioWAV flat layout; EmoDB flat): execute in an isolated namespace on the REAL manifest, sorted file order; unseeded fragments run with 10 fixed seeds; record min/median/max realized train/test speaker-overlap fraction, test size, class subset used, and the index sets (feeds REPLAY). IEMOCAP-only, combined-corpus, external-data and non-glob loaders are recorded as 'not executed'. Static verdicts are NEVER overwritten: a discordance table reports static Y_any with realized overlap 0 under all seeds and static N with realized overlap >0 under any seed. ADJUDICATION: H vs AI disagreements resolved by a script over evidence-chain fields (path/hash present, entry point present, enumeration closed; unresolved -> U) with both records published; the 30 single-rated units get the AI verdict plus author review under the same script. RELIABILITY: Cohen's kappa (4-level and Y_any-vs-not) on the double-coded 30 with 2,000-rep bootstrap CI; agreement on re-sampled historical lineages reported separately; reported, never a gate. STATISTICS: primary = stratum-weighted frame proportion of Y_any with linearized FPC 95% interval; secondary = same for Y_test; per-stratum Wilson intervals on Y/n_s and (Y+U)/n_s; per-stratum partial-identification intervals; per-stratum two one-sided exact hypergeometric bounds (Y_s and Y_s+U_s) at 1-alpha/4 combined into stratum-weighted frame bounds (joint >=95%); U handling: all-U-negative and all-U-positive bounds plus one stratum-only imputation (no covariate logistic model); Lincoln-Petersen frame-coverage estimate from channel A/B overlap reported as a bounded descriptor with its known failure directions; realized-overlap distribution among executed units and the executed fraction; comparison sentence to EMO-SUPERB's 50% and Antoniou 2023. Human budget ~165 h (screening ~20, human coding <=60, AI rating + author review ~30, execution tier ~40, adjudication/detector ~15); 0 GPU.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Estimand (estimation only, no confirmatory test; the audit family is removed): proportion of eligible public GitHub/arXiv-discoverable SER repository lineages (frame at T0, four corpora) in which at least one active train->held-out boundary permits same-speaker membership (Y_any), stratum-weighted and per stratum, with the test-boundary proportion (Y_test) as the registered secondary. Reported quantities with intervals: Y_any and Y_test stratified estimates; per-stratum Wilson and partial-identification intervals; stratum-weighted hypergeometric frame bounds; U-bound sensitivity; Y_val-only fraction; discordance counts from the execution tier; realized-overlap distribution; static-detector agreement; kappa with CI; regex misclassification rate; Lincoln-Petersen coverage. Prespecified reading rule: the headline is the stratified Y_any point estimate with its interval; no 'more than half' or other threshold statement is made. Forbidden: prevalence x effect multiplication; any verdict overwrite by execution results.

program.name: CTRL-1: unified outer x inner protocol factorial (RR/RG/GR/GG) on RAVDESS, CREMA-D and SUBESCO-980 with three scratch models and three frozen probes; secondary levels SUBESCO-full, SUB-1400 matched pair, EmoDB; RAVDESS CNN seed-crossing, LOSO/LOSO-sub pair and P1-split reconciliation
merged_from: P1 (RR and GG cells, engine, features, speaker-paired inference; LOSO reduced to one RAVDESS CNN pair; FNO cut)
A (RG and GR cells; O_G and I_R decomposition with shared init across cells and matched inner sizes)
S0 (HuBERT-base, WavLM-base+ and wav2vec2-base early-stopped linear probes as model levels on the same splits)
S2 (partition draws crossed with seeds inside the main design; 10x2 draw/seed grid for the HuBERT probe level)
S3 (SUBESCO-980 repetition-clean panel as the family corpus level under the full protocol; SUBESCO-full as secondary)
B SUBESCO allocation (its take-density hint becomes the SUB-1400-one vs SUB-1400-two matched pair and the take-grouped split)
D1 (cut without replacement; see cut entry)
P4 multi-corpus queue (cut; EmoDB descriptive only)
program.rationale: The claim-loss critique showed two claim-to-arm mismatches: GR-GG is measured on a speaker-exclusive outer test and cannot show inflation (A called I_G an allocation package); the inflation quantity is RR-RG (A: +7.29 pp on RAVDESS), so RR-RG enters the families and GR-GG becomes an allocation descriptor. Second, SUBESCO-full bundles take leakage with speaker leakage, so the repetition-clean 980 panel (the current paper's cross-lingual instrument) is the family level and SUBESCO-full a secondary; the full-vs-980 contrast confounds size and prompts with takes, so a size- and prompt-matched pair (SUB-1400-one vs SUB-1400-two) and a take-grouped split on SUBESCO-full isolate sibling presence on identical data. The inference and literature critiques showed that RAVDESS/CREMA-D directions were already observed on these exact speaker panels (P1, A, S0) and by Ibrahim et al. 2026, so those tests move to Family R; the three-cluster two-way bootstrap is replaced by per-replicate estimates, a variance-components table from the RAVDESS CNN crossing, and a 10-draw x 2-seed grid on the HuBERT probe level where it is cheap (~0.5 GPU-h, not ~0 as the critique assumed). wav2vec2-base is restored (it was the most stable SUBESCO probe). A RAVDESS CNN LOSO/LOSO-sub pair (~0.5 GPU-h) restores a like-for-like from-scratch LOSO number for the Ibrahim replication, and a CNN run on the six P1 frozen split files (~0.7 GPU-h) reconciles the new numbers with the 2026 table under changed hygiene.
program.design: Corpus levels: family = RAVDESS speech (24 spk), CREMA-D (91), SUBESCO-980 (20 spk, 7 emotions, 7 prompts, one take per cell); secondary (RR/GG cells only, estimates) = SUBESCO-full (7,000), SUB-1400-one, SUB-1400-two, EmoDB (10 spk); all SUBESCO levels share speaker folds by split_seed so contrasts between levels are speaker-paired. Model levels: CNN, ResNet-SE, Transformer (P1 frozen configs, class count per corpus, all at r=0,1,2) on log-mel; HuBERT-base, WavLM-base+, wav2vec2-base final-layer (state 12) time-mean 768-d early-stopped linear probes (S0 contract). Engine (all levels): class-balanced CE, AdamW (lr 1e-3, wd 1e-4; Transformer 3e-4), batch 64, <=100 epochs, cosine T_max 100, early stop patience 15 on inner weighted CE, strict-min checkpoint, restore best, float32 deterministic, test touched once; r=0 CNN and ResNet-SE best checkpoints persisted for MECH-0 (no per-fit embedding emission). Cells: RR, RG, GR, GG (outer letter first); inner fit/val sizes exactly 75/25 of outer train in both inner arms. Replicates r=0,1,2 (draw + training seed, shared across models and cells within corpus; pairing is on each speaker's identical utterance set across cells; fold identity holds within an outer letter only). Fits: family levels 3 models x 4 cells x 5 folds x 3 r = 180 each (RAVDESS 0.6 h, CREMA-D 3.4 h, SUBESCO-980 0.65 h); secondary levels 3 models x 2 cells x 5 x 3 = 90 each (SUBESCO-full 1.6 h, SUB-1400-one 0.4 h, SUB-1400-two 0.4 h, EmoDB 0.13 h); SUBESCO-full take-grouped split, CNN, 15 fits (0.27 h); RAVDESS CNN seed-crossing seeds {0,1,2} x draws {0,1,2} off-diagonal (120 fits, 0.4 h); RAVDESS CNN LOSO (24 folds) and LOSO-sub (24 folds, one hash subsample per replicate) x 3 r = 144 fits (0.5 h); P1 reconciliation: CNN RR and GG on the six P1 frozen split files mapped through hygiene, 3 seeds, RAVDESS + CREMA-D = 60 fits (0.67 h); probe units 3 encoders x (3 family levels x 4 cells + 4 secondary levels x 2 cells) x 5 folds x 3 r = 900 (~0.8 h); HuBERT probe partition grid on the three family levels, RR/GG, 10 draws x 2 seeds x 5 folds = 600 units (~0.5 h). Total ~10.4 GPU-h; cap 13. Fixed run order corpus -> model -> r -> fold -> cell, then crossing, LOSO pair, reconciliation, probes; one retry for failures before outer-test access; a missing outer fold voids the (corpus, model, cell, r) cell and dependent contrasts (p=1 placeholder, family size unchanged, verdict 'not tested'). Outputs per fit: predictions.csv with all logits for every OOF utterance, history, config, hashes. Per-speaker OOF UAR per (corpus, level, cell, r); accuracy/macro-F1 released without inference or text.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: All estimands are speaker-paired UAR differences (unit = speaker; n = 24 / 91 / 20), averaged within speaker over 3 replicates and over the named model levels before differencing; 10,000-replicate whole-speaker percentile bootstrap 95% CIs (fixed seed) and two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank (zero_method wilcox; n_nonzero reported; exact sign test added whenever >20% of speakers tie at zero). Per corpus c: (1) Delta_pipe^scratch(c) = mean over CNN, ResNet-SE, Transformer of [UAR(RR) - UAR(GG)] > 0; (2) Delta_pipe^probe(c) = mean over the three probes of [UAR(RR) - UAR(GG)] > 0; (3) Delta_outer(c) = mean over all 6 levels of [UAR(RG) - UAR(GG)] > 0; (4) Delta_inner^leak(c) = mean over all 6 levels of [UAR(RR) - UAR(RG)] > 0. FAMILY N (Holm, alpha 0.05, 10 tests program-wide): tests 1-4 on SUBESCO-980 (direction never observed on this panel under trained models or the factorial). FAMILY R (Holm, alpha 0.05, 13 tests program-wide, labelled 'preregistered re-tests on the same speaker panels'): tests 1-4 on RAVDESS and on CREMA-D (8 tests). Power table simulated from dossier per-speaker deltas and SDs (P1 RAVDESS RG diff SD 7-10 pp, CREMA-D 3-4 pp; S0 probe SDs 2.4-4.9 pp; S3 draw SDs 1.5-2.2 pp) under the actual Holm step-down is published in tag-1; expected: SUBESCO-980 scratch test >0.95 for >=6 pp, probe test ~0.45-0.6 for 3 pp at the Family-N step-down (stated as the weakest confirmatory test). Descriptors with CIs and no tests: Delta_inner^alloc(c) = GR-GG (allocation package on a speaker-exclusive test; stated as costing fit speakers, not inflation); per-level cells and per-level RR-GG sign counts (x/9 scratch, x/9 probe); interaction (RR-RG)-(GR-GG); RAVDESS-minus-CREMA-D and RAVDESS-minus-SUBESCO-980 pipeline deltas with two-sample speaker bootstrap CIs, read against a preregistered +/-3 pp band ('larger' only if the CI lies wholly outside the band); SUB-1400-two minus SUB-1400-one RR-GG paired by speaker (sibling-presence increment at matched size and prompts); SUBESCO-full random minus take-grouped random UAR (take-leakage increment on identical data); SUBESCO-full minus SUBESCO-980 (reported with the size/prompt confound stated); EmoDB deltas; per-replicate estimates and sign counts (x/3); variance components (draw vs seed) from the RAVDESS CNN crossing; HuBERT probe partition-level interval from the 10x2 grid; RAVDESS CNN LOSO, LOSO-sub and Group5 UARs (descriptive; like-for-like with Ibrahim et al. 2026 LOSO); CNN RR-GG on the six P1 frozen splits next to the 2026 P1 CNN rows (reconciliation, no test). Heterogeneity rule: if any level's sign disagrees with the tested mean's direction, the paper states it beside the test.

program.name: PROBE-CPU: frozen-feature Ridge factorial on cached 13-state features (head x partition family x layer x 20 draws; P1 frozen splits; LOSO vs Group5 vs size-matched LOSO; SUBESCO take-grouped split and matched pair)
merged_from: S4 WavLM layer weighting (NO-GO, now a zero-GPU layer factor registered as premium-by-layer only)
P1 LOSO arm (1,380 fits; replaced by CPU LOSO / LOSO-sub on frozen features plus the RAVDESS CNN pair in CTRL-1)
S0 (trained-probe head, reused from CTRL-1 for the head contrast)
program.rationale: S0 and S2 disagree 2-5x on RAVDESS on identical features; the inference critique showed the original head test confounded head with the inner pathway (Ridge has no inner split, the probe's RR-GG bundles both) and could not attribute from a non-rejection, and the claim-loss critique noted no P1-style partition existed to reproduce the S0 side. The head contrast is now Ridge (outer Random - outer Grouped) versus the probe's RG-GG (outer contrast under grouped inner) on identical partitions, with a 2x2 head x partition-family table and a no-scaler Ridge variant so scaler leakage is separated from closed-form fitting. Layer-wise accuracy is well mapped (Pepino 2021, Pasad 2021, SUPERB layer weights), so only premium-by-layer is registered. Tougui et al. 2021 already show subject-wise CV error falls with fold count, so the LOSO-sub equivalence is a one-line supplement note on CREMA-D only (RAVDESS margins are below measurement granularity).
program.design: Features: HuBERT-base, WavLM-base+, wav2vec2-base, all 13 states from the PREREG-0 cache; corpus levels RAVDESS, CREMA-D, SUBESCO-980, SUBESCO-full, SUB-1400-one, SUB-1400-two, EmoDB. Heads: A1 = StandardScaler(train fold) + RidgeClassifier(alpha 1, cholesky, class_weight balanced); A2 = RidgeClassifier without scaler; head B = the CTRL-1 early-stopped probe (reused predictions). Partition sets: (i) 20 draws d=0..19 of StratifiedKFold(5) vs StratifiedGroupKFold(5) by speaker (S2 seed rule); (ii) CTRL-1 replicate partitions r=0..2 (Ridge on outer Random / outer Grouped; probe B on all four cells); (iii) the six P1 frozen split files (GroupKFold no-shuffle, StratifiedKFold rs=42) mapped through hygiene, RAVDESS and CREMA-D, both heads; (iv) Group5 (draw 0), LOSO, LOSO-sub (3 hash subsamples averaged) on the final state; (v) SUBESCO-full take-grouped split (groups = speaker x emotion x prompt) alongside its random and speaker-grouped splits, and the SUB-1400 pair on identical speaker folds. Layer factor on head A1, draws 0-19: Delta_RG per state s=0..12. Fits: ~7 levels x 3 encoders x 13 states x 2 protocols x 20 draws x 5 folds ~ 55,000 Ridge fits at ~0.07 s (~1.1 CPU-h) plus head A2, LOSO/LOSO-sub and P1-split units (~0.5 CPU-h); all CPU. Outputs: per-draw speaker-equal OOF UAR contrasts and per-speaker OOF UAR.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: FAMILY N member (1 test): H_head(RAVDESS): per-speaker [Ridge-A1 outer contrast (Random - Grouped) minus probe-B (RG - GG)] on the CTRL-1 r=0..2 partitions, averaged over encoders and replicates within speaker; two-sided Wilcoxon over 24 speakers + whole-speaker bootstrap CI; a rejection is reported as a head effect at the outer boundary; a non-rejection is reported as an estimate with CI and never used to attribute the discrepancy elsewhere. Descriptor 2x2 table (head A1/A2/B x partition family 20-draw/CTRL-1/P1-frozen) of outer-boundary premia with CIs on the same speakers, RAVDESS and CREMA-D. EQUIVALENCE (TOST family, Holm over 2 with the DOSE spillover TOST, alpha 0.05): UAR(LOSO-sub) - UAR(Group5) within +/-1 pp on CREMA-D, head A1, speaker-paired (margin from P1 CREMA-D speaker-diff SD 3-4 pp, n=91, 90% CI half-width ~0.7 pp), together with the descriptor UAR(LOSO) - UAR(Group5); RAVDESS and SUBESCO-980 reported as estimates. Descriptors only: per-corpus 3-encoder Ridge direction stability (>=18/20 positive and q05 > 0); premium-by-state Delta_RG per encoder x corpus with Spearman over state index (no layer-wise accuracy reported; cite Pepino 2021, Pasad 2021, SUPERB); SUB-1400-two minus SUB-1400-one Delta_RG paired by speaker; SUBESCO-full random minus take-grouped premium; CNN and Ridge RR-GG on the P1 frozen splits next to the 2026 P1 and S0 values.

program.name: CTRL-2: partially fine-tuned WavLM-base+ pipeline contrast (RR vs GG) on RAVDESS, CREMA-D and SUBESCO-980; r=0 partitions, second seed on SUBESCO-980
merged_from: S0/S2/S3 claim registries' forbidden extrapolation to fine-tuned models (the gap this arm fills on speaker-paired folds)
program.rationale: The direction of a fine-tuned-SSL premium is literature-established (Wang et al. 2021: 79.6 vs 73.0 on IEMOCAP; ICASSP 2024 WavLM fine-tuning), so the FT RR-GG tests move to Family R; the genuinely untested quantity, and the Family-N estimand, is whether fine-tuning re-exposes speaker information that frozen final-layer probes attenuate (FT minus probe premium on identical speakers and folds). The feasibility critique showed the 8 GPU-h estimate used the bottom of the recorded 10-40 min/fold range and that the timing probe on family corpora contradicted the registration gate; the probe is now off-family, the cap is 2x measured (floor 12), SUBESCO-980 replaces SUBESCO-full (cutting the largest fine-tune corpus), an in-RAM waveform cache removes the librosa bottleneck, and a second seed is added only where cheap. A 'not tested' verdict protects truncated corpora from being written as refuted.
program.design: WavLM-base+ (pinned weights); CNN feature encoder and transformer layers 1-8 frozen; top 4 transformer layers + mean-pool + linear head trainable; fp16 autocast, batch 16, random 3 s crops for training from the in-RAM float16 waveform cache, full utterance capped at 10 s at evaluation, AdamW (encoder 5e-5, head 1e-3, wd 1e-2), <=15 epochs, early stop patience 3 on inner weighted CE (inner mirrors outer: ungrouped under RR, grouped under GG), strict-min checkpoint, best+last checkpoints only with RNG state persisted (resumed=true logged). Splits: CTRL-1 r=0 outer/inner partitions, cells RR and GG. Fits: RAVDESS 10 (seed 0), CREMA-D 10 (seed 0), SUBESCO-980 20 (seeds 0,1) = 40; planning estimate from the recorded range scaled by corpus size ~2 h RAVDESS, ~6 h CREMA-D, ~3 h SUBESCO-980 (both seeds) = ~11 GPU-h; cap = 2x measured timing-probe mean per corpus, floor 12, ceiling 14, checked at fold boundaries. Preregistered drop order if the cap is hit: SUBESCO-980 seed 1, then CREMA-D; RAVDESS and SUBESCO-980 seed 0 are never dropped; dropped units enter as p=1 with verdict 'not tested (truncated, deviation entry N)'. fp16 non-determinism disclosed; verifier equality applies to scoring from committed predictions. Validity anchor (not a hypothesis): GG UAR on CREMA-D within 55-70%, sourced from EmoBox (Interspeech 2024) and EMO-SUPERB speaker-independent CREMA-D results; a miss triggers a logged implementation audit before scoring is unlocked.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Per corpus c: Delta_pipe^ft(c) = speaker-mean of [UAR(RR) - UAR(GG)] at the fine-tuned level (r=0; SUBESCO-980 averaged over 2 seeds within speaker) > 0; two-sided Wilcoxon (n = 24/91/20) and whole-speaker bootstrap CI; three FAMILY R members (replication of Wang et al. 2021 direction on speaker-paired folds). FAMILY N members (3): Delta_reexpose(c) = Delta_pipe^ft(c) - Delta_pipe^probe(c) on the same speakers and folds (probe level from CTRL-1 r=0, three-encoder mean, and WavLM-only as descriptor) > 0; speaker-paired Wilcoxon + bootstrap CI. Single-realization caveat stated for RAVDESS and CREMA-D.

program.name: HPO: hyperparameter search on leaky vs grouped inner validation (ResNet-SE, RAVDESS + CREMA-D)
merged_from: P0/P0.5 outcome 'test set / validation used for selection' (36.7% in P0.5), now an audit descriptor column cross-tabulated with Y_test/Y_val and linked to a measured optimism
program.rationale: Selection bias from a leaky selection criterion is textbook (Cawley & Talbot 2010) and quantified for subject-level leakage in EEG (Pup et al. 2025), but not in SER; the arm is kept as the SER quantification with the claim reworded accordingly. The feasibility critique's cost correction (ResNet-SE heavier; lr 3e-4 runs more epochs) raises the estimate to ~2.6 GPU-h and the cap to 4. The Y_val-to-HPO bridge is made explicit by a registered cross-tabulation in AUDIT-1 and the optimism descriptor here.
program.design: ResNet-SE only; RAVDESS and CREMA-D; cells RR and GG; replicate r=0 partitions; grid of 8 configs (lr {3e-4, 1e-3} x weight decay {1e-4, 1e-3} x dropout {0.1, 0.3}); each config trained on each of the 5 outer folds with the cell's inner split (train_seed shared across configs); per fold the config with the highest inner-validation UAR is selected and its outer-test predictions used (no refit). 2 corpora x 2 cells x 8 configs x 5 folds = 160 fits (~0.35 h RAVDESS, ~2.2 h CREMA-D); cap 4 GPU-h; per-config epoch counts logged in the dry run. Comparator = the CTRL-1 r=0 ResNet-SE cell (a grid member).
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Per corpus (2 FAMILY N members): Delta_HPO(c) = [UAR(RR,hpo) - UAR(GG,hpo)] - [UAR(RR,fixed) - UAR(GG,fixed)] on speaker-paired UAR; H: > 0; two-sided Wilcoxon + whole-speaker bootstrap CI (power at n=24 stated as low in the registered table; CREMA-D is the better-powered member). Descriptors: distribution of selected configs under RR vs GG; selected-config inner-validation UAR minus its outer-test UAR under RR (the reported-number optimism a repository with a dual-use held-out set would show), reported next to the AUDIT-1 cross-tabulation of 'test set used for selection' with Y_test/Y_val.

program.name: DOSE: donor-substitution exposure ladder with a fixed prompt-disjoint test half (RAVDESS, CREMA-D); exposed-speaker gain, crowding contrast and no-spillover equivalence
merged_from: C/P5 mechanism-exposure salvage (its cross-prompt donor substitution is the constant-size, constant-speaker-count mechanism; its q=1 case is the top rung)
program.rationale: The inference critique showed the original nested-dose Page's L was true by construction (population mean at q is a mixture of exposed and unexposed speakers) and its rotation infeasible; the claim-loss critique showed that adding test speakers' utterances raised training-speaker count, confounding dose with diversity, which C/P5 had avoided by donor substitution; the literature critique showed the constant-size graded-overlap design is published (arXiv 2604.14354; Rosenberg et al. 2024), so the primary readouts are the new quantities: per-exposed-speaker gain and whether it shrinks when more test speakers are co-exposed, the no-spillover equivalence on CREMA-D, and the corpus difference. Exposed-speaker gain at full exposure was already observed on these panels in C/P5 (+6.42/+1.85 pp without valid inference), so it is a Family R re-test.
program.design: RAVDESS and CREMA-D; CNN and ResNet-SE; outer StratifiedGroupKFold(5) by speaker, the CTRL-1 r=0 partition. Each speaker's utterances are split into prompt-disjoint halves (RAVDESS statement 01/02; CREMA-D the P5 sentence sets A/B); fixed test = half B of the test-fold speakers at every condition. Each test-fold speaker is hash-paired with a same-sex donor training speaker of the same fold; at baseline the donor's half A is in training and the target's is not; exposure of a target replaces the donor's half-A cells with the target's half-A cells (identical label x prompt-cell counts), so training utterance count, label counts and the number of speakers contributing to training are constant (one half-represented donor is swapped for one half-represented target); inner validation grouped, drawn from non-donor training speakers only, identical across conditions; class weights recomputed. Conditions: q=0 (no exposure), q=1 (all test-fold speakers exposed), q=0.5 in two rotations (hash halves H1/H2 of each fold's test speakers, so every speaker is exposed at q=0.5 in exactly one rotation and unexposed-with-co-exposed-neighbours in the other); doses are not nested; the pre-fit assertion checks cell-count identity across conditions. Fits: per corpus per model 5 folds x (q0 + q1 + 2 rotations) = 20 x 2 seeds = 40; x 2 models x 2 corpora = 160 fits (~0.3 h RAVDESS, ~1.5 h CREMA-D); cap 3 GPU-h. Truncation (only if the 42 GPU-h program cap is projected to be exceeded): CREMA-D seed 1 dropped, then RAVDESS seed 1.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: Per speaker (averaged over models and seeds): G1 = UAR(half B | exposed at q=1) - UAR(half B | q=0); G05 = UAR(half B | exposed at q=0.5, own rotation) - UAR(half B | q=0); S05 = UAR(half B | unexposed at q=0.5, other rotation) - UAR(half B | q=0). FAMILY R (2 tests): G1 > 0 per corpus (speaker-paired Wilcoxon + whole-speaker bootstrap CI; re-test of the C/P5 direction with valid inference). TOST family member (with the LOSO-sub TOST, Holm over 2, alpha 0.05): CREMA-D S05 equivalent to zero within +/-1.5 pp (n=91, SD ~4 pp, 90% CI half-width ~0.7 pp); RAVDESS S05 reported as an estimate (granularity: one item flip = 3.1 pp per speaker). Descriptors with CIs: crowding contrast G1 - G05 per corpus (does per-speaker gain change when all rather than half of the test speakers are exposed); share G05/G1; RAVDESS-minus-CREMA-D G1 difference (two-sample bootstrap, +/-3 pp reading band); G1 next to C's historical +6.42/+1.85 pp. Cited precedents: arXiv 2604.14354, Rosenberg et al. 2024. Claim wording: 'exposed-speaker gain', never 'monotone dose curve'.

program.name: REPLAY: our fixed pipeline trained on the realized single splits of audited risk-positive repositories vs same-utterance speaker-exclusive OOF and size-matched counterfactuals (descriptive)
merged_from: P0.5 execution-validation tier (AST-isolated split execution, now on real manifests via AUDIT-1 with the shared layout shim)
P2/Theta scenario-burden analysis (replaced by an empirical per-repository quantity)
BRIDGE (Proposal 4's repository re-execution; not adopted, see cut entry)
program.rationale: All three GPU-bearing critiques converged: the sign test was underpowered (n=8 needs 8/8), repositories sharing sklearn train_test_split(random_state=42) on a sorted list produce byte-identical splits, k-fold repositories would cost k-fold fits, combined-corpus and class-subset loaders cannot be executed faithfully, and since RAVDESS/CREMA-D random splits realize ~100% overlap the quantity is near-tautological with CTRL-1 RR-GG. REPLAY is therefore descriptive, one realized partition per repository, deduplicated by index-set hash, with a same-utterance speaker-paired counterfactual taken for free from the CTRL-1 GG r=0 ResNet-SE OOF predictions and a size-matched grouped partition as a second descriptor.
program.design: Units: AUDIT-1 Y_any lineages whose decisive fragment executed on the real RAVDESS or CREMA-D manifest (single-corpus glob/listdir loaders only) with realized overlap > 0, deduplicated by realized index-set hash (distinct-split count reported), taken in beacon order up to 16. For each: the repository's fold 0 by its own fold order or its single split (one realized partition; validation carved as the repo does, else grouped 25%); class-subset repositories scored on their own label subset with UAR over present classes (descriptor recorded). Counterfactual 1 (primary, speaker-paired, zero cost): CTRL-1 GG r=0 ResNet-SE OOF predictions restricted to the realized test utterances (every test utterance predicted by a model that never saw its speaker). Counterfactual 2 (descriptor): one speaker-disjoint partition matched on train fraction and class proportions (hash-seeded), trained with the same model. Model: ResNet-SE at CTRL-1 config, 2 training seeds; WavLM Ridge (final state) on the same index sets on CPU. Fits: up to 16 x (1 realized + 1 size-matched) x 2 seeds = 64 fits (~0.7-1 GPU-h); planned 1, cap 2, reserved. If fewer than 8 distinct qualifying splits exist the arm is reported with sign counts only (rule fixed now).
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: No family test. Delta_repo = per-speaker UAR on the realized test utterances under the realized split minus per-speaker UAR on the same utterances from the speaker-exclusive OOF, seed-averaged, speaker-paired within repository; reported per repository with whole-speaker bootstrap CI, and as a per-corpus median with repository-level bootstrap CI. Descriptors: Delta_repo vs realized overlap fraction and test size (Spearman); ratio Delta_repo / CTRL-1 RR-GG for the same corpus ('realized-split scaling'); size-matched counterfactual difference; Ridge-probe Delta_repo. Reported next to, never multiplied with, the AUDIT-1 prevalence; Claim 6 is an estimation claim.

program.name: MECH-0: inference-only nearest-neighbour composition readout on persisted CTRL-1 r=0 checkpoints; premium-by-layer correlate from PROBE-CPU
merged_from: B SUBESCO allocation (take-density hint, now the SUB-1400 pair and take-grouped split measured in CTRL-1/PROBE-CPU)
C/P5 gap 'no representational test of speaker identity' (dropped as a readout; cited literature instead)
S4 layer question (probe side; premium-by-layer only)
program.rationale: The literature critique showed speaker identity in emotion embeddings and in lower SSL layers is documented (arXiv 2409.03655, Feng et al. 2021, Pasad 2021, SUPERB/WavLM layer weights, arXiv 2603.03096) and Chaibub Neto et al. 2019 give the established identity-confounding test; the claim-loss critique showed the sibling conditional-accuracy readout was selection-based and the full-vs-980 sentence confounded. MECH-0 therefore keeps only the nearest-neighbour composition (a split property, not an accuracy conditioned on the embedding), points the mechanism sentence at the SUB-1400 matched pair and the take-grouped split, and cites rather than re-runs the speaker-probe results. The feasibility critique's inconsistency (no checkpoints persisted) is resolved by persisting r=0 CNN/ResNet-SE checkpoints in CTRL-1.
program.design: From persisted CTRL-1 r=0 RR and GG checkpoints (CNN, ResNet-SE; RAVDESS, CREMA-D, SUBESCO-980, SUBESCO-full, SUB-1400-one, SUB-1400-two): penultimate embeddings for training-pool and outer-test utterances (inference ~0.3 GPU-h). (a) NN composition: for each RR and GG test utterance, cosine nearest neighbour in its training fold, categorised as sibling (same speaker x sentence x emotion, different take/intensity) / same speaker non-sibling / same sentence other speaker / other; share per category per corpus level; sibling availability in the training fold (a split property) reported alongside. (b) Premium-by-state Spearman from PROBE-CPU (already computed) cited as the layer correlate, with the literature's speaker-information-by-layer results cited rather than re-measured. No speaker-ID probe is trained.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: No family tests. Prespecified descriptive readouts with CIs: share of test items whose training-fold NN is a sibling under RR vs GG per corpus level (expected non-zero on SUB-1400-two and SUBESCO-full, zero by construction on SUBESCO-980 and SUB-1400-one); SUB-1400-two minus SUB-1400-one RR-GG increment (from CTRL-1/PROBE-CPU) as the bounded mechanism number. Supplement table plus one bounded main-text sentence: 'on size- and prompt-matched SUBESCO panels, the random-split premium is larger when sibling takes are present, and under nonexclusive training a share of test items have a sibling take as nearest training neighbour'; forbidden wording: 'uses speaker identity', mediation shares, any causal claim from the full-vs-980 contrast.

program.name: STAT-1: one-shot scoring under Family N (10 tests), Family R (13 tests) and the 2-test TOST family; independent verifier replay; rolling 2% bitwise retrain check; number-checked insert; three-valued claim verdicts
merged_from: P1 summarizer + independent statistics verification (the pattern that achieved 0.0 error)
A/B/C/D1 scoring contracts and post-outcome verifiers (replaced)
S0/S2/S3 claim registries and S3 replay refits / mutation battery (replaced by the PREREG-0 battery and the rolling retrain check)
S1 exact hypergeometric envelope code (now per stratum)
Paper numeric-insert manifest and number checker (replaced by one results.json -> numeric_insert.tex)
program.rationale: The inference critique showed 12 of the original 21 family tests re-tested directions already observed on the same speaker panels and that the audit binomial tests and REPLAY sign test were underpowered or non-exchangeable; the claim-loss critique showed truncation placeholders would print 'not supported' for claims that were never tested and that Claim 4 bundled four heterogeneous requirements. The families are split by novelty, the audit and REPLAY become estimation claims, the two TOSTs get their own Holm pair, Claim 4 is split into 4a-4d, and a third verdict 'not tested (truncated, deviation entry N)' is added. The retrain check is rolling so environment drift is detected before CTRL-2.
program.design: Executed once after the ledgers of CTRL-1, PROBE-CPU, CTRL-2, HPO, DOSE, REPLAY, MECH-0 and AUDIT-1 are locked and hashed. Scorer produces: per-speaker cell tables; Family N (SUBESCO-980 scratch RR-GG, probe RR-GG, RG-GG, RR-RG; Delta_reexpose x3; Delta_HPO x2; H_head) and Family R (RAVDESS and CREMA-D scratch RR-GG, probe RR-GG, RG-GG, RR-RG = 8; FT RR-GG x3; DOSE G1 x2) with CIs, raw and Holm-adjusted p; TOST family (CREMA-D LOSO-sub; CREMA-D S05) with Holm; all descriptors; audit stratified estimates, intervals, per-stratum bounds, kappa, detector agreement, discordance table, coverage; results.json, numeric_insert.tex, figure data JSON. Verifier (frozen at tag-1/tag-2, no shared modules, reads only run_plan, split tables, manifests, predictions, adjudication CSV and audit ledger) reproduces every reported number to 1e-12; any mismatch reported verbatim, never patched. Rolling retrain check: 1% hash-selected float32 fits retrained bitwise after CTRL-1 (before CTRL-2 starts) and 1% at the end (~0.4 GPU-h). CLAIM-TO-VERDICT MAP (verdicts: supported / not supported / not tested (truncated, entry N)): Claim 1 = estimation claim, always reported with intervals (no verdict). Claim 2 requires Family N SUBESCO-980 scratch and probe RR-GG rejections; RAVDESS/CREMA-D Family R results reported as replication. Claim 3 requires Family N SUBESCO-980 RG-GG and RR-RG rejections plus Family R RG-GG and RR-RG rejections on at least one anchor corpus. Claim 4a (FT persistence, replication) requires Family R FT RR-GG on RAVDESS and at least one other corpus; 4a' (re-exposure) requires at least 2 of 3 Delta_reexpose rejections; 4b (HPO) requires at least one Delta_HPO rejection (the corpus is named); 4c (head) requires H_head; 4d (LOSO size effect) is a supplement note requiring the CREMA-D LOSO-sub TOST. Claim 5 requires both Family R G1 rejections and reports the crowding contrast, share and the CREMA-D spillover TOST. Claim 6 = estimation claim, always reported. Any claim whose required test entered as a truncation placeholder receives 'not tested'; any claim whose test ran and did not reject receives 'not supported' in the main text.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: No new estimand. Gates: verifier replay exact; rolling retrain bitwise identical for float32 arms; number checker red = 0 before the manuscript is frozen. Holm within Family N (10), within Family R (13), and within the TOST pair, alpha 0.05; missing tests enter as p=1 with family size unchanged and verdict 'not tested'.

program.name: P1 LOSO from-scratch arm (1,380 of 1,620 fits) and D1 LOSO folds (552 of 792)
program.rationale: 85% of P1's fits (~21 GPU-h) for a contrast confounded with training-set size, whose mechanism is already published (Tougui et al. 2021: subject-wise CV error falls with fold count). Retained in reduced form only: a RAVDESS CNN LOSO/LOSO-sub pair (144 fits, ~0.5 GPU-h, descriptive) inside CTRL-1 so the Ibrahim et al. 2026 LOSO number has a like-for-like from-scratch comparator, and the CPU Ridge LOSO/LOSO-sub TOST on CREMA-D in PROBE-CPU. The paper states as a deliberate loss that trained-model LOSO under all architectures and both corpora is not re-run and cites the 2026 P1 LOSO rows as the prior descriptive result.
program.design: Not run except the RAVDESS CNN pair in CTRL-1.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None; see CTRL-1 descriptor and PROBE-CPU TOST.

program.name: FNO architecture (P1/A/B/D1 cells)
program.rationale: FNO tracked CNN in sign and magnitude in every P1 cell (RAVDESS 15.39 vs 17.71; CREMA-D 1.82 vs 2.80), was the only architecture needing a probe-choice justification, and produced B's only negative cells. CNN, ResNet-SE and Transformer (all at r=0,1,2) span convolutional and attention families. The paper states as a deliberate loss that the per-architecture 8/8 statement of the 2026 paper is replaced by model-averaged tests plus per-level sign counts, and cites the 2026 eight-row table once as the prior per-architecture replication.
program.design: Not run.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

program.name: D1 RAVDESS speech-song matched panel (792 fits)
program.rationale: Its speech half re-ran P1 on a 23-actor / 6-class subset; the song-minus-speech contrast was not conclusive for CNN and all four Random-LOSO secondaries were not conclusive; it appears in no current manuscript claim. The vocal-channel question is dropped WITHOUT replacement (the earlier statement that MECH-0 reads it out was a misattribution: no arm loads RAVDESS Song) and is named in Limitations.

program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

program.name: B SUBESCO fixed-budget allocation diagnostic (2,880 fits, 10.25 GPU-h)
program.rationale: Largest compute item in the frozen program; its fixed-budget design binds speaker count to repeat density, one seed per block confounds training noise with block noise, and it ended as a routing sentence. Its interpretable observation (adding a second take roughly triples the premium) becomes a registered, confound-controlled descriptor: the SUB-1400-one vs SUB-1400-two matched pair (same size, same prompts, differing only in sibling presence) at scratch and Ridge levels, plus the take-grouped split on SUBESCO-full and the MECH-0 NN-composition readout. A budget-varying speaker/sentence ladder is named in Limitations as future work.
program.design: Not run.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None; routed to CTRL-1/PROBE-CPU descriptors and MECH-0.

program.name: C/P5 cross-prompt target-actor exposure substitution and its salvage machinery (144 checkpoints, 6,336 scored rows)
program.rationale: A mechanism pilot with no admissible inference, delivered after a key-exposure incident and a review waiver. Its donor-substitution mechanism (constant utterance count, label cells and contributing-speaker count) is carried forward as the DOSE design, which adds a fixed prompt-disjoint test half, two exposure fractions with rotation, valid speaker-paired inference on exposed-speaker gain (Family R re-test of C's direction), a crowding contrast and a no-spillover equivalence on CREMA-D.
program.design: Not run.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None; replaced by DOSE.

program.name: P0 purposive 32-repo audit, four non-speaker P0 outcomes, purposive-vs-random comparison, P0.5 separate n=30 sample, S1 lineage sensitivity branches (D1/D3/291/N282), P2/Theta
program.rationale: The purposive layer was a working-model diagnostic with no design-based inference; P0.5 and S1 estimated the same construct with 2 shared repos and were never reconciled; the four lineage branches all yield 44/9/7 within 0.3 pp. AUDIT-1 fixes one lineage rule before screening, keeps two P0 columns as descriptors (test-set selection, no-variance reporting), adds dialogue-partner and static-detector columns, records historical verdicts for re-sampled lineages as a post-adjudication check (hidden from raters), and replaces P2's scenario multiplication with REPLAY's empirical per-repository quantity.
program.design: Not run.
program.estimand_and_hypothesis: None.

program.name: S0 v1/v2, S2, S3 release ladder and S4 as separate arms
program.rationale: S0 v2 existed only for provenance; S2 and S3 were one Ridge design on different corpora; S3 needed ten releases for zero scientific change; S4 never ran. All four are absorbed: S0's three probes are CTRL-1 model levels; S2's draws, S3's SUBESCO-980 panel and S4's layer question are PROBE-CPU factors on one 13-state cache (premium-by-layer only); content-addressed cache identity and the PREREG-0 mutation battery replace the release ladder. pipeline_order: Weeks 0-5 PREREG-0 stage 1: freeze audit/CTRL-1/PROBE-CPU code, run_plan.csv rows, seed table, split generator, scorer and the independent verifier modules for those arms; families, slot map and claim-to-verdict map; timing table, wall-clock plan, storage budget, driver/torch pins; build manifests with pinned SUBESCO/EmoDB DOIs and licenses, hygiene log, log-mel cache (CPU) and 13-state SSL cache for three encoders (~2.5 GPU-h); run split-table assertions; synthetic dry run for CTRL-1/PROBE-CPU/AUDIT statistics + mutation battery (~0.5 GPU-h); recruit and declare the second coder or register the author-only branch; tag-1 + OSF + OpenTimestamps; record NIST beacon pulse

Weeks 5-18 AUDIT-1 (CPU + human, parallel with all GPU stages): frame union (channel A + capped channel B) -> lineage rule -> stratum regex on all candidates (+40 hand-verified) -> beacon-ordered sequential E1-E5 screening to 30/30 (or census + reallocation) -> coder blind-codes the hash-selected 30 previously unseen units (hash-committed before the AI rater) -> AI rating of all 60 -> static-detector column -> execution tier on glob/listdir single-corpus fragments via the layout shim (10 seeds, realized overlap, index sets) -> scripted adjudication -> kappa, discordance table, coverage, U bounds

Weeks 5-9 GPU-1 CTRL-1: fixed order corpus (RAVDESS, CREMA-D, SUBESCO-980, SUBESCO-full, SUB-1400-one, SUB-1400-two, EmoDB) -> model -> replicate -> fold -> cell; then take-grouped CNN units, RAVDESS CNN seed-crossing, LOSO/LOSO-sub pair, P1-split reconciliation, 900 probe units, HuBERT 10x2 grid (~10.5 GPU-h; per-fit DONE markers, resumable); first 1% rolling retrain check at close

Weeks 6-10 PROBE-CPU in parallel on CPU: ~55,000 Ridge fits over 13 states x 20 draws, A2 no-scaler variant, P1 frozen splits, LOSO/LOSO-sub (3 subsamples), SUBESCO take-grouped split and SUB-1400 pair, head crossing on CTRL-1 partitions

Weeks 7-9 PREREG-0 stage 2: off-family timing probe (EmoDB + synthetic CREMA-D cardinality, ~1.5 GPU-h, checkpoints discarded); dry units for CTRL-2/HPO/DOSE/REPLAY at CREMA-D cardinality (~1 GPU-h); remaining verifier modules; CTRL-2 cap set from the measured value; tag-2 + OSF + OpenTimestamps before any unit of those arms

Weeks 9-12 GPU-2 CTRL-2: partial WavLM fine-tune from the in-RAM waveform cache, r=0 RR/GG x 5 folds, corpus order RAVDESS (seed 0), CREMA-D (seed 0), SUBESCO-980 (seeds 0, 1) (~11 GPU-h planned, cap 12-14 from probe; drop order SUBESCO-980 seed 1, then CREMA-D)
Week 12 GPU-3 HPO: 160 ResNet-SE fits (~2.6 GPU-h, cap 4)
Weeks 12-13 GPU-4 DOSE: 160 donor-substitution fits (~1.8 GPU-h, cap 3)

Weeks 14-16 GPU-5 REPLAY (after the AUDIT-1 execution tier closes): up to 16 distinct realized splits x (realized + size-matched) x 2 seeds ResNet-SE (~1 GPU-h, cap 2) + Ridge on CPU; same-utterance counterfactual from CTRL-1 GG OOF
Week 16 GPU-6 MECH-0 embedding inference on persisted r=0 checkpoints and NN-composition readouts (~0.3 GPU-h); final 1% rolling retrain check (~0.2 GPU-h)

Weeks 17-18 ledger lock and hash of all predictions, checkpoints, audit records and adjudication CSV; STAT-1 one-shot scoring (Family N 10, Family R 13, TOST pair) and independent verifier replay; number checker red = 0

Weeks 18-22 manuscript fill-in under the fixed slot map and three-valued claim map; explicit lost-claims paragraph; arXiv preprint by week 22; code, split tables, predictions and audit receipts released with the tags; Interspeech 2027 submission (early March 2027, ~week 25); total ~500 author hours (prereg 180, audit ~105 author-side, engineering/monitoring 90, writing 70, STAT/release 55) plus ~60 coder hours
program.preregistration_notes: Two OSF registrations (tag-1: audit, CTRL-1, PROBE-CPU, families, slot map, claim map; tag-2: CTRL-2, HPO, DOSE, REPLAY, full verifier, measured timing) with OpenTimestamps anchors; tag-1 precedes any real cache write or screening action; tag-2 precedes any unit of its four arms; tag-2 cannot alter anything fixed in tag-1. Fixed and not revisable: (1) Venue and calendar: ICASSP 2027 is abandoned; target Interspeech 2027 with an arXiv preprint by week 22 of a 22-week plan registered with ~500 author hours and ~60 coder hours. (2) Families: Family N (10 tests: SUBESCO-980 scratch RR-GG, probe RR-GG, RG-GG, RR-RG; Delta_reexpose on RAVDESS/CREMA-D/SUBESCO-980; Delta_HPO on RAVDESS/CREMA-D; H_head RAVDESS) and Family R (13 preregistered re-tests: RAVDESS and CREMA-D scratch RR-GG, probe RR-GG, RG-GG, RR-RG; FT RR-GG x3; DOSE G1 x2), each Holm alpha 0.05, missing tests p=1 with family size unchanged and verdict 'not tested'; TOST pair (CREMA-D LOSO-sub +/-1 pp; CREMA-D spillover +/-1.5 pp) Holm alpha 0.05; the audit and REPLAY are estimation claims with no tests; everything else is an estimate with a CI. A simulated power table from the dossier's per-speaker deltas and SDs under the actual Holm step-down is part of tag-1, with the SUBESCO-980 probe test named as the weakest confirmatory member. (3) Unit of inference = speaker; per-speaker OOF UAR; averaging over replicates and named model levels precedes differencing; whole-speaker percentile bootstrap (10,000, fixed seed) and two-sided Wilcoxon (zero_method wilcox; n_nonzero reported; exact sign test added when >20% of speakers tie); per-replicate estimates and sign counts, RAVDESS CNN draw/seed variance components and the HuBERT 10x2 partition-level interval are the partition-uncertainty descriptors; scratch-level inference is stated to condition on three partitions. (4) Corpus differences (RAVDESS-minus-CREMA-D, RAVDESS-minus-SUBESCO-980, DOSE G1 difference) are marginal comparisons registered as estimates with a +/-3 pp reading band ('larger' only if the CI lies wholly outside the band); the anchor-corpus direction is cited as published. (5) Hygiene exclusions, the SUBESCO-980 family level with SUBESCO-full/SUB-1400 as secondary, EmoDB descriptive-only, no LOSO training beyond the RAVDESS CNN pair, no accuracy/macro-F1 inference, no per-level tests, no additional encoders, corpora, heads or arms after tag-1. (6) Audit: lineage rule; stratum regex with a 40-candidate misclassification check and a tag-1 estimate of N_1; n=60 fixed with allocation min(30, eligible paper-linked) and census rule; sequential beacon-order screening (elapsed hours never a stopping rule); 2 review-hour per-rater per-unit cap coded U; endpoint dictionary with the dual-use rule; human-before-AI mechanised ordering on 30 previously unseen units; scripted adjudication; kappa with CI never a gate; static-detector column; execution tier restricted to single-corpus glob/listdir fragments via the layout shim with 10 seeds; no verdict overwriting (discordance table); U bounds and stratum-only imputation; per-stratum hypergeometric bounds; Lincoln-Petersen as a bounded descriptor; AI-rater model/version/temperature/budget pinned with a deprecation fallback (re-rate all units with the successor model, both columns published). (7) Budget: planned 33 GPU-h; program hard cap 42 GPU-h; per-arm caps PREREG 5.5, CTRL-1 13, CTRL-2 12-14 (from the timing probe), HPO 4, DOSE 3, REPLAY 2 reserved, MECH-0 0.5, STAT 0.5; truncation order only if the program projection exceeds 42 h: DOSE seed-1 units, HPO CREMA-D, CTRL-2 by its own drop order; every started unit enters the public ledger; truncated tests receive 'not tested', never 'not supported'. (8) Verifier and scorer frozen before outcomes and exercised on synthetic fixtures including rounded fields and fp16-scored units; any post-run disagreement reported verbatim; fp16 CTRL-2 units are non-bitwise-reproducible and are verified from committed predictions; rolling 1%+1% retrain checks; driver and torch/torchaudio versions pinned; resumed fits flagged. (9) Routing: the 4-page slot map (Fig. 1A audit stratified estimates with intervals and discordance; Fig. 1B forest of Family N and Family R contrasts, visually separated; Table 1 per-corpus RR-GG scratch / RR-GG probe / RG-GG / RR-RG / FT / re-exposure / HPO rows; Fig. 2 DOSE exposed-speaker gains and REPLAY per-repository premia) is fixed regardless of sign; supplement carries PROBE-CPU tables, MECH-0, EmoDB, LOSO pair, P1 reconciliation, secondary estimates. (10) Prior-art paragraph, drafted now for Related Work: 'Ibrahim, Ghoraba and Ghoraba (2026) report a same-system random-versus-LOSO gap on RAVDESS (95.8% vs 48.1%) and CREMA-D (73.5% vs 53.1%) for a multimodal MFCC+VGGFace system; Zielonka et al. (2022) report the same direction; Wang et al. (2021) report 79.6% vs 73.0% for fine-tuned wav2vec2/HuBERT on IEMOCAP; our 2026 P1 gave speaker-paired estimates on the same two corpora; EMO-SUPERB (2024) finds random partitions in about half of prior SER studies and Antoniou et al. (2023) reviewed IEMOCAP code. We treat the anchor-corpus direction as a replication (Triantafyllopoulos et al. 2025 for the replication framing) and contribute: a frame-based probability sample of repository lineages with a test-versus-validation endpoint, realized overlap from executed split code and a static-detector benchmark; the SER outer/inner decomposition with shared initialization (precedents outside speech: Saeb et al. 2017, Pup et al. 2025); the repetition-clean SUBESCO panel under the full protocol with a size-matched sibling-take contrast; whether partial fine-tuning re-exposes speaker information; the SER quantification of leaky hyperparameter selection (Cawley and Talbot 2010); a donor-substitution exposure ladder (design precedents arXiv 2604.14354, Rosenberg et al. 2024); and replay of audited realized splits in one pipeline. The LOSO-over-grouped advantage (Tougui et al. 2021) and speaker information in emotion embeddings and lower SSL layers (Pasad et al. 2021; arXiv 2409.03655) are cited, not re-established.' (11) Lost-claims accounting, drafted now for Limitations: three protocols under trained models (LOSO only as a RAVDESS CNN pair), four architectures (FNO dropped), the S2 20/20 sentence, the D1 vocal-channel diagnostic (dropped without replacement), the speaker-count-versus-repeat allocation question (B), and a speaker-count-matched inner-validation variant (GR-GG remains an allocation descriptor confounded with fit-speaker count) are deliberate losses. (12) Forbidden claims: prevalence x effect multiplication, universal correction factor, 'more than half' audit statements, 'speaker identity alone' or 'uses voiceprint', mediation shares, 'monotone dose curve', 'resolving' the S0/S2 discrepancy, extrapolation beyond the seven representation levels, language-causal statements for SUBESCO, and any reuse of 2026 P1/S0/S2/S3 numbers as updates; the 2026 P1 table is cited once as the prior replication and reconciled through the P1-split CNN descriptor. (13) Any deviation is written to the append-only deviation file and cited in the paper by entry number.
risks: CTRL-2 cost is set from a 3-fold off-family timing probe; at the top of the recorded 10-40 min/fold range CREMA-D alone could reach 7 h and the arm 14 h, triggering the drop order (SUBESCO-980 seed 1, then CREMA-D) and 'not tested' verdicts for the CREMA-D FT and re-exposure rows.

Human time, not GPU, is the binding constraint: ~500 author hours over 22 weeks alongside a coder who is not yet recruited; if no coder is declared at tag-1 the audit is registered as AI-rated with author review and the reliability statistic is only author-AI agreement on previously unseen units.

The paper-linked stratum may be a census of 20-45 lineages, in which case its proportion has no sampling interval and the stratified headline is dominated by the 'other' stratum; the regex stratum proxy has unmeasured misclassification beyond the 40-candidate check.

The execution tier covers only single-corpus glob/listdir loaders (expected ~50-65% of Y/N units); the realized-overlap descriptor and REPLAY are therefore biased toward simple RAVDESS/CREMA-D loaders, and IEMOCAP-only units contribute only static verdicts and the dialogue-partner column.

Family N's SUBESCO-980 probe test has ~0.45-0.6 power at the Holm step-down for a 3 pp premium (S3 observed ~3 pp with WavLM fragile); a non-rejection is plausible and would print Claim 2 as 'not supported' even though the anchor-corpus replications reject.
Delta_reexpose (FT minus probe) and Delta_HPO at n=24 are low-powered single-realization contrasts; Claims 4a' and 4b may rest on CREMA-D alone.

Channel B's code-search index bias (recent activity, default branch, file size) and keyword/filename overlap violate Lincoln-Petersen independence in a known direction; coverage is reported as a bounded descriptor only.

Scratch-level inference conditions on three partitions per corpus; a reviewer insisting on partition-level inference for trained models will find only the RAVDESS CNN crossing and the HuBERT probe 10x2 grid.

Prior-art collision persists for the effect half; distinctiveness rests on the audit with realized overlap, the decomposition, the repetition-clean SUBESCO factorial, re-exposure, HPO, DOSE and REPLAY. A frame-based audit of public SER code appearing before March 2027 would narrow the contribution.

Governance: the two-tag design makes deviations visible, not impossible; the author produced 13 plan revisions in 9 days last time, and the AI-rater model may be deprecated mid-program (fallback registered but costly).

Windows/torch determinism is verified only by rolling 1%+1% float32 retrain checks; a driver update mid-run or two OS shutdowns in one night (as in D1) would be logged as resumed units and could break exact replay for CTRL-2.
resulting_paper_claims: Claim 1 (audit, estimation): in a publicly registered, beacon-ordered, stratified probability sample of 60 eligible public GitHub/arXiv SER repository lineages (frame and lineage rule fixed before screening), the stratum-weighted proportion in which at least one active train->held-out boundary permits same-speaker membership is reported with a linearized FPC interval, per-stratum Wilson and partial-identification intervals and stratum-weighted hypergeometric frame bounds; the test-boundary proportion, validation-only fraction, realized train/test speaker overlap from executing the repositories' own split code on the real corpora, static-execution discordance counts, agreement with a published static leakage detector, human-AI kappa with CI on 30 previously unseen units, and frame coverage are reported alongside, and compared with EMO-SUPERB's literature figure.

Claim 2 (controlled, confirmatory for SUBESCO-980; replication for RAVDESS/CREMA-D): under one implementation, one feature cache, shared initialization and identical speaker-paired partitions, speaker-nonexclusive splitting at both boundaries (RR vs GG) inflates UAR on the repetition-clean SUBESCO-980 panel for three from-scratch models and for frozen HuBERT/WavLM/wav2vec2 probes (Family N), and reproduces the published RAVDESS/CREMA-D direction (Family R re-tests, presented as a same-implementation replication of Ibrahim et al. 2026, Zielonka et al. 2022 and our 2026 P1); corpus differences are reported as estimates against a preregistered band.

Claim 3 (decomposition, confirmatory for SUBESCO-980; re-test for anchors): the leaky-pipeline premium separates into a positive outer test-leakage component (RG-GG) and a positive inner-selection component under a leaky outer split (RR-RG), with the interaction and the allocation descriptor (GR-GG) reported; nonexclusive validation inflates a nonexclusive reported score, so speaker exclusivity at the inner boundary matters (first SER-specific speaker-paired decomposition with shared initialization; precedents Saeb 2017, Pup 2025 cited).

Claim 4a (fine-tuning, replication): the premium persists under a partially fine-tuned WavLM-base+ pipeline on the same speaker-paired folds (Family R; direction per Wang et al. 2021). Claim 4a' (re-exposure, confirmatory): the fine-tuned premium exceeds the frozen-probe premium on the same speakers and folds, i.e. fine-tuning re-exposes speaker information that frozen final-layer features attenuate (Family N). Claim 4b (HPO, confirmatory): selecting hyperparameters on a speaker-overlapping validation set enlarges the premium (Family N; SER quantification of Cawley and Talbot 2010), with the inner-validation-minus-test optimism reported next to the audit's dual-use column. Claim 4c (head, confirmatory): the frozen-probe outer-boundary premium is head-dependent by a measured amount on identical partitions (Family N). Claim 4d (supplement): the LOSO-over-GroupKFold advantage is equivalent to a training-set-size effect on CREMA-D frozen features (TOST; Tougui et al. 2021 cited).

Claim 5 (exposure, re-test plus quantification): with a fixed prompt-disjoint test half and constant training utterance count, label cells and contributing-speaker count, exposed test speakers gain UAR when their other-prompt utterances enter training (Family R re-test of the C/P5 direction), the per-speaker gain at half exposure versus full exposure and its share are reported with CIs, and unexposed co-fold speakers show no measurable spillover on CREMA-D (TOST).

Claim 6 (audit-to-practice link, estimation): training our fixed pipeline on the realized splits produced by audited risk-positive repositories yields per-repository premia over a same-utterance speaker-exclusive counterfactual, reported per repository and as per-corpus medians with intervals, scaled against the controlled premium and never multiplied with prevalence.

Bounded mechanism sentence (descriptive): on size- and prompt-matched SUBESCO panels the random-split premium is larger when sibling takes are present, and under nonexclusive training a share of test items have a same-speaker same-sentence sibling take as nearest training neighbour; no claim of speaker-identity use or mediation share.

Operational recommendation, argued from Claims 1-6: enforce speaker exclusivity at every active boundary including inner validation and hyperparameter selection, deduplicate repeated takes across boundaries, publish grouping keys, and report corpus structure rather than applying a universal correction.

rejected_critiques: LIT-4 partial: 'keep exactly one Page's L (pooled corpora) in the family' — rejected because INF-10 shows a population-mean trend across exposure fractions is implied by construction whenever exposure has any positive effect; a pooled version is equally tautological. The exposed-speaker gain contrast and the crowding descriptor replace it.

LIT-5 partial: 'replace the speaker-ID probe with Chaibub Neto et al. 2019's identity-confounding permutation test' — rejected as a run item because that test requires training additional models under within-subject label permutations (not inference-only) and would add an unbudgeted arm; it is cited as the established framing and the speaker-ID probe is dropped rather than replaced.

INF-1 partial: 'increase n to >=45 per stratum only if the human budget allows' — rejected; the audit's confirmatory tests are removed altogether, so larger n would buy interval width only, and the feasibility critique shows human hours are already the binding constraint at n=60.

INF-7 partial: 'restructure the family hierarchically with secondary families gated on the primary' — rejected in favour of two ungated Holm families split by novelty; gatekeeping would make Family R's error rate conditional on Family N outcomes and would suppress reporting of the replication results a reviewer expects to see regardless of the SUBESCO outcome.

INF-8 partial: the claim that 20 draws x 3 seeds on the probe levels costs '~0' — rejected as stated (early-stopped probe units cost ~3.2 s each; 20x3 on three encoders and three corpora is ~4.8 GPU-h); accepted in reduced form (10 draws x 2 seeds, HuBERT only, ~0.5 GPU-h).

INF-12 partial: 'exclusive counterfactual = same test speakers with those speakers removed from training and back-filled' — rejected because realized RAVDESS/CREMA-D random splits contain all speakers in the test set, so removing them leaves no training data; replaced by the same-utterance speaker-exclusive OOF counterfactual taken from CTRL-1 GG predictions, which restores speaker pairing at zero cost.

INF-15 partial: 'second seed for RAVDESS and SUBESCO (~+2 GPU-h)' — accepted only for SUBESCO-980; the RAVDESS second seed (~2 GPU-h at the planning rate) is declined to keep CTRL-2 inside a cap set at 2x the measured probe; RAVDESS and CREMA-D are labelled single-realization instead.

FEAS-5 partial: 'budget 80-100 h for the execution tier' — rejected in favour of the critique's own alternative (restrict execution to glob/listdir single-corpus fragments through one layout shim per corpus, report the eligible fraction), budgeted at 40 h; the 80-100 h option would exceed the total human budget the same critique deems realistic.

CL-1 alternative: 'speaker-count-matched inner variant (random-by-utterance within the same fit-speaker set) so GR-GG can be kept as a clean allocation contrast' — rejected as an added cell set because it changes the definition of the inner random arm away from what public code does and adds fits without serving any registered claim; GR-GG is kept only as a descriptor explicitly labelled as confounded with fit-speaker count, and the confound is carried into the lost-claims paragraph.

CL-6 alternative: 'test whether Delta_repo differs from the CTRL-1 premium as a confirmatory statement' — rejected as a test because repositories sharing sklearn defaults produce non-exchangeable, partly identical splits and the quantity is a ratio of two estimates on the same corpus; it is reported as the 'realized-split scaling' descriptor with CIs.

missing_questions: Speaker-count / panel-size moderator: the thesis' 'report corpus structure' recommendation and the ~6x RAVDESS-vs-CREMA-D gap rest on speaker count (24 vs 91) as the suspected driver, yet no arm subsamples CREMA-D to 24 speakers (or matches utterances-per-speaker) under the RR/GG factorial. B was cut and its replacement (SUB-1400 pair) isolates sibling takes only. A CREMA-D-24 level is ~0.75 GPU-h (180 scratch fits at ~15 s) and is the only cheap direct test of the moderator.

Coherence between the audit primary and the effect half: Y_any counts Y_val-only lineages (leaky validation, verified-exclusive test) as risk, but the program's own decomposition treats GR-GG as an allocation effect, not inflation, so no arm shows that Y_val-only configurations inflate any reported number unless the validation score itself is reported (dual-use). The Y_val-only fraction is reported but its inflation relevance is never measured (e.g., inner-validation UAR under random vs grouped inner from CTRL-1 histories, or a GR-HPO cell).

Code risk vs repositories' own reported numbers: AUDIT-1 collects 'reported top-line metric on RAVDESS/CREMA-D' and, for the paper-linked stratum, could record whether the paper text claims speaker-independence while the code does not (P0's paper_code_discrepancy field), but no arm analyses either. REPLAY measures our pipeline under their splits, not the inflation of what they actually reported.

IEMOCAP, the modal corpus in the audited code (7/30 IEMOCAP-only in P0.5) and the only one with session/dialogue-partner leakage, has no effect arm; the dialogue-partner column is a descriptor with no measured magnitude. The thesis' 'inflates reported performance' is untested on the corpus most public SER code uses (acknowledged as a licence limitation, but still a gap).

Same-prompt sibling vs cross-prompt speaker exposure on the anchor corpora: DOSE is cross-prompt only, SUB-1400 isolates siblings only on SUBESCO, and the per-speaker utterance fraction (dose) is never varied. On RAVDESS (2 statements x 2 reps x 2 intensities) the sibling share of the RR premium, and how the premium scales with fraction of a test speaker's utterances seen, remain unmeasured; CTRL-1 RR-GG minus DOSE G1 cannot be read as that share because training compositions differ.

Partition-level inference for trained models on the Family N corpus: SUBESCO-980 (n=20, 4 test speakers per grouped fold) has no draw x seed crossing; only the RAVDESS CNN crossing and the HuBERT 10x2 probe grid exist, so every confirmatory SUBESCO-980 test conditions on three partitions.
unverified_claims: Claim 4a' ('fine-tuning re-exposes speaker information that frozen final-layer features attenuate'): a representational attribution with no representational measurement (speaker-ID probe explicitly dropped). The arm measures only FT premium minus probe premium, which also bundles capacity, 3 s crop augmentation, fp16, 15-epoch/patience-3 regime and trainable-layer differences; and the Family N comparator is the three-encoder probe mean while FT is WavLM-only (WavLM had the smallest, fragile probe premium), so the test does not compare like with like.

Claim 3's inference 'speaker exclusivity at the inner boundary matters' and the recommendation 'enforce exclusivity at every active boundary including inner validation': supported only under a leaky outer split (RR-RG). Under an exclusive outer test the program's own descriptor (GR-GG, A: +5.1 pp RAVDESS) shows inner exclusivity lowers the honestly measured score without removing inflation; no arm shows inner nonexclusivity inflates a speaker-exclusive reported number.

Claim 1's 'realized train/test speaker overlap from executing the repositories' own split code on the real corpora': applies only to single-corpus glob/listdir loaders served through a layout shim (program's own estimate 50-65% of Y/N units; IEMOCAP, combined-corpus, external-data and many notebooks excluded), so realized overlap is a biased-subset descriptor, not a property of the sample.

Claim 4d ('LOSO-over-GroupKFold advantage is equivalent to a training-set-size effect'): the TOST on Ridge frozen features shows LOSO-sub ~ Group5 only; attributing the trained-model LOSO advantage observed in P1 (all 8 cells) to size has no arm because from-scratch LOSO was cut except one RAVDESS CNN pair (descriptive, n=24, margins below granularity).

Claim 6 (REPLAY per-repository premia): conditional on >=8 distinct realized splits after index-set dedup; the program itself notes shared sklearn rs=42 splits and ~100% realized overlap on RAVDESS/CREMA-D, so the quantity is likely to collapse to a sign count near-identical to CTRL-1 RR-GG rather than a per-repository distribution.

Operational recommendation 'deduplicate repeated takes across boundaries': supported only by SUBESCO descriptors (SUB-1400 pair, take-grouped split, NN composition) with no test and no anchor-corpus counterpart; RAVDESS repeats/intensities are never isolated.

Claim 2's 'shared initialization ... identical speaker-paired partitions' for probes vs scratch models: the probe levels are early-stopped linear heads on cached features and the scratch models are trained on log-mel; 'identical partitions' holds, but the model-averaged Family N test can reject with one of three levels disagreeing (heterogeneity rule reports it, the claim wording does not).
over_engineering: EmoDB carried through PREREG-0 (DOI/licence pinning, loader, v2.5 post-mortem), CTRL-1 (90 scratch fits + probe units) and PROBE-CPU, for a level the program itself calls 'negligible paired power, descriptive only' with 2 test speakers per fold; cut it and run the timing probe on synthetic audio alone.

Static-leakage-detector benchmark column (Yang et al. ASE 2022 / LeakageDetector 2.0): these tools target preprocessing and row-overlap leakage, not group/speaker leakage; expected applicable coverage near zero, ~15 h for a mostly 'not parseable / not applicable' agreement table.

PROBE-CPU full crossing (7 corpus levels x 3 encoders x 13 states x 20 draws x 2 protocols ~55k fits, plus the A2 no-scaler head, P1-frozen-split units and 3-subsample LOSO-sub) for supplement-only descriptors; the only registered readout is a premium-by-state Spearman and one H_head test on RAVDESS. Restrict the layer factor to the three family levels and drop A2.

SUBESCO-full under three scratch models x RR/GG (90 fits, 1.6 GPU-h, largest secondary level) for the full-vs-980 contrast the program disclaims as size/prompt-confounded; CNN-only (30 fits) suffices for the take-grouped increment and MECH-0.

P1-split reconciliation (60 scratch fits + Ridge) and the RAVDESS CNN LOSO/LOSO-sub pair (144 fits): ~1.2 GPU-h for supplement descriptors; 'like-for-like with Ibrahim et al. 2026' is not like-for-like (their system is multimodal MFCC+VGGFace), and the paper forbids reusing 2026 numbers as updates anyway.
Lincoln-Petersen frame-coverage estimate from channel A/B overlap: the program concedes independence is violated in a known direction; a bounded descriptor with known bias adds text, not information.
Family R Holm over 13 replication re-tests: Holm machinery on already-established directions produces no claim; CIs and sign counts would serve the replication framing.
REPLAY's second (size-matched) counterfactual and WavLM-Ridge replay on top of a descriptive arm whose unit count is likely below the 8-split floor.

Rolling 1%+1% bitwise retrain checks and the 24-case mutation battery are proportionate given the program's history, but CTRL-2 (the largest arm, fp16) is exempt from bitwise verification, so the retrain check protects only the cheap arms; keep, but do not present as verifying the FT results.
completeness.final_verdict: Every one of Claims 1-6 has at least one arm behind it and the program is far tighter than the frozen one, but three thesis-level questions remain unaddressed: the speaker-count moderator (a ~0.75 GPU-h CREMA-D-24 level would close it), the coherence of the 'any active boundary' audit primary with an effect half that treats validation-only leakage as allocation rather than inflation, and any link from code verdicts to the numbers repositories actually report. The wording most exposed is Claim 4a' ('re-exposes speaker information', a representational claim with no representational measurement and a mismatched comparator) and the inner-boundary recommendation (supported only under a leaky outer split). Roughly 4 GPU-h and ~20 human hours of descriptor work (EmoDB, SUBESCO-full x3 models, detector column, P1 reconciliation/LOSO pair, the full PROBE-CPU crossing) touch no claim and could be cut or redirected to the CREMA-D-24 level.
